chapters.title: Chapter 451: Provoking Brida Goes Wrong...
paragraphs: The women weren’t glaring because their Lord had received a larger portion of food.
As the Lord of Blessed Land, Silas was entitled to the finest feasts in the cosmos.
They were glaring because a single woman was completely hogging him!
Sitting directly in the center of the large mat, Silas was comfortably cross-legged, leaning back with an amused affectionate smile.
And seated directly upon his lap, nestled securely between his thighs with his left arm wrapped snugly around her waist, was Tasmin.

The agile commander had completely stripped off her sky-iron armor plates, leather pauldrons, and harnesses, leaving her clad only in a lightweight form-fitting black sleeveless singlet and a pair of snug training shorts that exposed her toned athletic shoulders and long smooth legs.
Her usually sharp aloof demeanor was completely dismantled.
Her sharp amber eyes were wide, her porcelain cheeks were flushed a brilliant radiant pink, and her body was practically melting against Silas’s broad chest as he held her close.
"Come on, open up," Silas coaxed gently.
Silas reached into a wooden platter resting beside them, picking up a thick succulent piece of roasted venison that had been thoroughly dipped into a savory sweet-garlic herb sauce.
Holding the glazed meat delicately between his fingers, Silas lifted it right to Tasmin’s lips.
Tasmin’s throat bobbed as she swallowed hard.
Her heart was beating so violently against her ribs that she was terrified Silas could feel the vibration through his chest.
"Ah..." Tasmin parted her lips obediently, taking the tender meat into her mouth and chewing slowly.
The rich savory flavors exploded across her palate, perfectly seasoned and cooked to melt-in-the-mouth perfection.
"Well? How is it?" Silas asked, his blue eyes crinkling with warmth.
"It’s... it’s exceptionally good, my Lord," Tasmin murmured softly, her raspy voice carrying a rare vulnerable sweetness as she ducked her head slightly.
"Oh? Is that so?" Silas grinned.
Without breaking eye contact, Silas smoothly brought his thumb and index finger which had lightly brushed against the inside of Tasmin’s lips and were coated in the savory sauce up to his own mouth.
Silas casually licked the sauce clean from his fingertips, letting out a satisfied hum.
Tasmin’s entire face instantly erupted into a volcanic crimson blush that reached all the way to the roots of her hair.
Her toes curled against the linen mat and her hands clutched the fabric of his trousers as steam practically rose from the top of her head.

’Why is my Lord doing all this... in front of the entire army...?!’ Tasmin screamed internally, her mind completely short-circuiting as she buried her burning face against the crook of his neck. ’All because of dark circles under my eyes...?!’
Silas continued licking his finger as Tasmin sighed.

’I’ve been training...’ Tasmin thought, her amber eyes shimmering with a mixture of overwhelming bashfulness and deep quiet satisfaction. ’Every single night, while the rest of the barracks slept, I stayed awake refining my shadow manipulation... I pushed through the exhaustion, ran perimeter sweeps across the jagged ridges, and drilled until my muscles tore... all just to prove my worth. All just to impress my Lord.’
Silas reached down toward the wooden platter once more, his fingers deftly selecting another thick succulent morsel of slow-roasted venison.
The meat glistened beneath a rich, dark glaze of honeyed herbs and crushed garlic.
"Come on, Tas," Silas murmured softly, his voice low and rich near her ear. "You didn’t eat nearly enough before we marched out this morning. Take another bite."
He brought the piece to her lips, and Tasmin obediently parted them, letting him place the tender morsel onto her tongue.
As she chewed, savoring the explosion of savory, melt-in-your-mouth flavor, a tiny drop of sauce lingered at the corner of her lower lip.
Subconsciously, Tasmin extended the pink tip of her tongue, delicately and cutely licking the stray drop of glaze from her lips.
Silas let out a genuine laugh, his chest vibrating against her back.
"Look at you," he chuckled fondly, reaching into his pocket with his free hand and pulling out a clean linen napkin.
Gently, with the careful touch of someone handling fragile porcelain, he brought the cloth to her chin, softly dabbing away the remaining sheen.
Tasmin’s breath hitched. Her heart hammered wildly against her ribs, her toes curling involuntarily against the fabric of her training shorts.
She absolutely loved being treated like this.
To be held, spoiled, and cared for like a delicate, cherished princess... it made every drop of sweat, every sleepless night of training, and every aching muscle entirely worth it.
’It feels like... like we’re already married...’
FLUMP!
The blissful romantic illusion shattered instantly as an armored figure violently planted herself directly onto the edge of the woven mat.
"Oh, come on! This is blatant favoritism and I demand an official review from the high command!"
Brida sat cross-legged right beside them, her heavy iron gauntlets resting on her armored knees as her large fierce amber eyes locked onto Silas with an exaggerated pout.
’This bitch...’
Her broad shoulders slumped forward, and she puffed out her cheeks like a giant disgruntled mastiff.

"My Lord!" Brida whined, gesturing wildly with her thick calloused hands. "Look at this! Tasmin gets the royal cushion while I’m over here withering away from lack of physical affection! Move over, Tasmin... it’s my turn to sit on the Lord’s lap!"
Silas looked at the towering six-foot-four woman, whose broad muscle-dense frame weighed easily twice as much as the agile Shadow commander currently in his arms.
Silas let out a dry deadpan chuckle, raising an eyebrow at her.
"Brida, if you sit on my lap in full plate armor, you’re going to snap my femur into three distinct pieces. You’re far too heavy for this seat..."

"Heavy?! I am built of pure territorial defense capability!" Brida protested loudly, placing a hand dramatically over her heart. "Fine! If I can’t have the throne, then I demand the royal feeding service! My soul is crying for protein, Captain!"
Silas shook his head with an amused sigh. "Alright, alright. Open up."
He picked up a prime-cut piece of roasted boar rib from the platter, generously swirling it through the sweet-garlic dipping sauce before extending it toward the pouting woman.
Brida’s face lit up with instant triumphant glee. "Aaaaah—"
She lunged forward, snapping her jaws around the meat with eager ferocity but she didn’t just take the boar rib.

As Silas tried to pull his hand back, Brida deliberately closed her lips tight around his thumb and index finger, sucking the savory sauce and his fingertips into her mouth with an audible lingering sound.
SLURP! SLURP!
Silas blinked in mild surprise, finally pulling his glistening hand free with a soft wet pop.
"Thank you..."
Brida swallowed the meat in a single gulp, a wild wicked grin spreading across her broad face.
She tilted her chin down, catching Tasmin’s glaring gaze, and slowly mouthed six silent mocking words across the mat.
’You can taste my saliva next.’
TWITCH!
A visible vein instantly ruptured in the corner of Tasmin’s forehead.
The romantic warmth that had filled the commander’s chest evaporated in a second, replaced by a roaring volcanic eruption of outrage.

’That shameless, thick-skulled, muscle-brained barbarian...!’ Tasmin fumed internally, her amber eyes flashing with dangerous malice. ’She really thinks she can mock me on my Lord’s mat?! Let’s see how smug you look when you’re stripped bare in front of the entire vanguard!’
VUUUUUUM.
Without making a sound, Tasmin subtly flicked her slender fingers beneath Silas’s thigh.
The pitch-black shadow stretching beneath the woven linen mat violently surged.
In less than a fraction of a millisecond, five needle-thin tendrils of condensed shadow mana erupted beneath Brida’s seat like invisible guillotines!
SNIP-SHRED!
The sharp shadow blades didn’t cut flesh... they were aimed with spiteful precision.

In a single, seamless, instantaneous shredding motion, the tendrils ripped straight through the seams of Brida’s leather breeches, tore through her undergarments, and completely disintegrated her boxers and trousers into microscopic threads of useless fabric, leaving her lower half entirely naked to the open air.
Tasmin leaned back into Silas’s chest, a smug, satisfied smirk curving her lips.
’Hah! Enjoy the humiliation, you overgrown bruiser! Let’s see you try to flirt while desperately covering yourself in front of thirty recruits—’
Tasmin froze.
Sitting on the mat, Brida didn’t shriek and she didn’t gasp either.
She didn’t make a frantic scramble to pull down her tunic or hide behind her tower shield.
’O... oh... I fucked up.’
Instead, a wide unhinged grin spread slowly across Brida’s face.
Tasmin’s stomach instantly dropped through the floorboards of reality.
A cold bead of sweat trickled down the scout’s neck as a horrifying realization slammed into her brain.
’...Oh gods. I forgot... I forgot what she acts like.’
Without a single microsecond of hesitation, Brida pushed off the ground and stood straight up to her full towering height.
"HEY! LOOK AT WHAT THE SNEAKY WOMAN JUST DID!" Brida’s booming thunderous voice roared across the peaceful encampment, cutting through the chatter of all four squads like an artillery blast.
Every single recruit in the clearing instantly stopped eating and turned their heads toward the Lord’s mat.
Brida stood tall in the midday sunlight, unbothered by the cool mountain breeze brushing against her bare lower half.
She turned around slowly, proudly presenting her rock-hard and fully exposed rear end to the entire expeditionary force.
"Captain! Look at this treacherous act of sabotage!" Brida shouted, grabbing both cheeks of her massive muscular ass with her iron-plated gauntlets.𝘧𝓇𝑒𝑒𝑤ℯ𝑏𝓃𝘰𝑣ℯ𝘭.𝘤ℴ𝘮
CLAP! SLAP!
She gave her rear two heavy reverberating smacks that echoed loudly across the quiet clearing, vigorously shaking her hips back and forth in a wild unrestrained dance.

"Look at this immaculate form!" Brida praised herself loudly, completely shameless as she flexed her powerful glutes. "Toned through hundreds of hours of heavy shield-bashing! Perfect curves forged in the fires of siege warfare! And Tasmin just tore away my armor out of pure jealousy because she knows she can’t match this mass!"
Across the encampment, the reaction was immediate and catastrophic.
"PFFFFFT—!" Helen choked on a mouthful of spiced tuber stew, spraying a cloud of broth across the grass as she hacked violently.
"BY THE GODS! MY EYES!" Sarah screamed, toppling backward off her woven mat in breathless hysterics.
"COMMANDER BRIDA! PLEASE! WE ARE IN THE MIDDLE OF A MILITARY EXPEDITION!" Catelyn yelled, covering her blushing face with both hands while peeking widely through her fingers.
Several younger recruit maidens simply fell sideways into the soft black grass, clutching their stomachs as they laughed so hard tears streamed down their cheeks.
Silas sat frozen on the mat, his wooden platter still in hand, staring at the towering Commander with an expression that perfectly balanced deadpan exhaustion and genuine amusement.
He slowly rubbed the bridge of his nose, his lips twitching as he struggled not to burst into laughter.
Brida wasn’t finished.
Seeing Silas looking at her, Brida’s grin widened with provocative audacity... That was what she was known for after all.
’If I don’t take advantage of this chance, when else will I be able to take advantage of it?’

She took a heavy step forward, plant-pivoting her boots into the turf, and bent deeply at the waist, sticking her bare rear end directly toward Silas’s face, barely two feet away from the edge of the mat.
She looked back over her broad shoulder, winking with wild flirtatiousness.
"Well, Captain? SinceTasmin was kind enough to clear away the obstacles... why don’t you take a break from feeding and rail me right here on the grass? I promise I won’t break the mat!"
POOOOOOF!
Tasmin’s entire body went rigid.
A volcanic crimson blush exploded across Tasmin’s face, turning her cheeks, neck, and ears a brilliant shade of scarlet.
Steam practically whistled from the top of her head as she violently buried her face straight into Silas’s chest, groaning in agonizing mortification.
’...She doesn’t know the meaning of shame,’ Tasmin whimpered into Silas’s tunic, wishing the earth would open up and swallow her whole. ’She truly does not know what shame is!’
[Author’s Note]
See you all next month.

chapters.title: Chapter 452: Break Period [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The wide velvet-black clearing under the weeping willow was momentarily suspended in stunned breathless silence.

Every single recruit was still staring wide-eyed at the towering six-foot-four frame of Brida, who remained bent deeply at the waist with her fully exposed rear end aimed right at the edge of the Lord’s mat.
Tasmin was still burying her flushed face straight into Silas’s chest, her fists clutching his dark tunic as if she could pull the fabric over her head and vanish from the mortal plane entirely.
Silas looked at the provocative display, his blue eyes gleaming with an amused effortless spark.
"Sure."
A collective synchronized blink rippled across the entire encampment.
"Eh?" Helen let out a squeak.
"Wait, what—?" Sarah gasped, her jaw dropping open.

Before Brida could even register the words, Silas smoothly shifted Tasmin off his thighs onto the cushioned linen, planted his boots onto the soft black turf, and rose to his full height in a single fluid motion.
He didn’t draw back with mana or channel the divine aura of his Gold Core.
He simply stepped up directly behind the bent-over Titan, squared his shoulders, cocked his right arm, and swung his broad, calloused palm in a clean horizontal arc.
THWACK!
The concussive flesh-on-flesh impact cracked through the quiet clearing with the acoustic force of a dry thunderclap.
The heavy blow struck dead-center across the dense, muscular curve of Brida’s left cheek.

The force set off a visible hypnotic ripple across the golden-bronze skin of her rear, vibrating through muscle and tendon in a mesmerizing shockwave that left behind a bright fiery-red handprint perfectly contoured against her flesh.
"Aaaaaaahhn~!"
A loud moan tore from Brida’s throat, echoing across the shaded willow branches.
Her knees instantly buckled beneath her frame.
With a dramatic trembling shudder, the towering woman collapsed forward onto the grass, tumbling from her knees flat onto her stomach.

Her heavy iron-plated boots kicked up into the air in a fit of wild, giddy ecstasy, her heels drumming against the turf as she buried her flushed grinning face in the cool black blades of grass as her broad shoulders shook with breathless euphoric giggles.
"Hehehehe... ahaha... that’s the stuff..." Brida wheezed happily, her fingers clawing at the dirt. "That’s that true authority right there..."
Silas let out a dry exasperated sigh, shaking his head as a small smirk tugged at the corner of his mouth.
With a casual flick of his wrist, a dimensional ripple opened in the air beside him.
Silas reached into his inventory, pulled out a thick folded woolen traveling mat, and tossed it down directly over Brida’s exposed lower half, draping the heavy fabric over her hips like a blanket.
"Stop causing trouble for the recruits and behaving like a wild beast in the middle of lunch," Silas scolded lightly, though his tone was layered with fond amusement.
Brida rolled onto her side beneath the mat, looking up at him with a remarkably obedient, dopey grin spreading across her face.
"Put some clothes on before you catch a cold," Silas added, crossing his arms.
"Sure, sure, my Lord!" Brida replied cheerfully, giving him a mock salute from the ground.
She didn’t argue.
With practiced ease, Brida reached into a concealed magnetic storage compartment built into the inner lining of her heavy chestplate.
She fished out a pair of snug dark-gray athletic boxers alongside a set of clean reinforced leather trousers.

Gathering the woolen mat tightly around her waist like a makeshift skirt, the woman scurried on her hands and knees toward a dense thicket of blackberry bushes at the edge of the clearing, humming a bawdy marching tune as she went to dress.
Silas watched her disappear into the foliage before turning back to the central mat.
Tasmin was still curled up in a tight, embarrassed ball on the linen, her face hidden behind her knees.
Silas knelt down beside her, slid his arms beneath her slender waist and thighs, and gently lifted the agile woman back onto his lap, pulling her securely against his chest once more.
"Come on now, Tas," Silas murmured softly, his voice low and warm against her ear. "The spectacle is over so eat a little more."
He reached for the wooden platter, picking up a tender skewer of mountain fowl dipped in a light honey-soy marinade, and held it to her lips.
Tasmin peeked out from between her bangs, her cheeks still dusted with a soft lingering crimson blush.
She looked up at Silas’s calm reassuring smile, her heart fluttering before she obediently parted her lips to take another bite.
She chewed slowly, leaning the back of her head against his broad shoulder, letting the steady thump of his heartbeat soothe the lingering adrenaline in her veins.

"You’ve been pushing yourself too hard on the night patrols and training too," Silas said gently, brushing a stray lock of dark hair behind her ear. "Once you finish this skewer, lay down and get some rest. You have the entire break period to sleep."
Tasmin blinked her amber eyes, looking down at his chest with a soft, fluttering warmth swelling inside her. "My Lord... but the perimeter—"
"The perimeter is secure. Aurelia, Lupina, and the recruits are watching the borders," Silas cut in with a firm comforting finality. "Rest."
Tasmin let out a tiny contented sigh.
She finished the meat, wiped her lips with the napkin Silas offered, and gently shifted off his lap onto the thick woven cushion beside him.

Curling her legs toward her chest, she rested her head upon a rolled cloak, and within less than two minutes, the exhausted commander had drifted into a deep tranquil sleep as her breathing began evening out into a soft steady rhythm.
Silas looked down at her peaceful face, a tender smile touching his lips.

’I knew you were exhausted,’ Silas thought, reaching down to pull the edge of a light linen blanket over her shoulders. ’Trying to train for your Shadow Heart constantly while scouting as well... you carried more than your share of the weight for a long time.’
"Lord Silas?"
A soft melodic voice broke through his thoughts from the opposite corner of the Lord’s mat.
Silas turned his head to see the Princess sitting primly on her knees.
Her lightweight sky-iron cuirass sat neatly propped against a wooden crate behind her, leaving her in a pristine white embroidered blouse that accentuated her delicate royal posture.
In her lap, she held an open compartmentalized wooden bento box lined with polished lacquer.

Resting inside the main ceramic bowl was a steaming, fragrant serving of rich, golden-brown bone broth, packed with hand-pulled wheat noodles, tender slices of braised mountain boar belly, a soft-boiled spirit-fowl egg halved to reveal a molten golden yolk, and a vibrant garnish of chopped scallions and crisp bamboo shoots.
The Princess was staring into the bowl with deep bewilderment, holding a pair of polished ebony chopsticks in her right hand as if they were complex magical artifacts.

"Lord Silas... how does one consume this dish?" the Princess asked, her azure eyes wide with genuine curiosity as she tilted the box toward him. "And what is the proper name of this culinary creation? In the Capital, our banquet chefs only serve roasted whole drakes, pureed vegetable creams, and silver-plated pastry crusts. I have never observed broth paired directly with long, elastic grain strands in this fashion."
A few paces away, sitting gracefully at the edge of the vanguard circle, Aurelia was holding an identical wooden lunchbox.
The former Saintess was eating in complete tranquil silence.
She held the chopsticks with effortless poise, lifting a neat bundle of noodles and broth to her lips with quiet grace.
As the rich savory broth... steeped with concentrated spirit herbs and roasted marrow washed over her palate, Aurelia’s golden-amber eyes subtly widened.

’The depth of this flavor...’ Aurelia mused internally, a blissful warmth spreading through her chest. ’The holy kitchens of the Meolion High Church served only bland purified mana-bread and cold ceremonial wine to ensure ascetic discipline but this dish possesses a complex, hearty soul that revitalizes both physical meridians and spiritual reserves. Once we conclude this basin campaign and return to the inner sanctum of Blessed Land, I must formally request an audience with the territory’s Chef to offer my sincere commendations.’
Silas chuckled softly at the Princess’s wide-eyed confusion, shifting his position to sit closer to her.

"This is Kaelia’s latest culinary experiment," Silas explained with an amused grin, pointing toward the steaming bowl. "It’s called Blessed Ramen... Back on Earth, it was one of the most beloved comfort foods in the world. Kaelia spent the last three days refining the broth using high-tier monster bones, roasted garlic, and soy-fermented mountain beans to get the umami balance just right."
"Ra... men?" the Princess repeated the unfamiliar word carefully, testing the syllables on her tongue. "And the long strands?"
"Hand-pulled wheat noodles," Silas said. "Here, let me show you."
Silas picked up his own pair of chopsticks, deftly demonstrating the motion.

He slid the wooden tips into the broth, pinched a neat portion of noodles, twirled his wrist in a smooth circular arc to secure the strands, and lifted them out of the steam. "You twirl them slightly to keep them from slipping, blow gently to cool the broth, and then take a bite..."
The Princess nodded with intense concentration, mimicking his grip.
She drove the ebony sticks into the bowl, attempted to squeeze the noodles, and tried to twist her wrist.
FLUMP!
The slippery broth-slicked noodles instantly slid free of the wood, splashing a tiny droplet of golden broth back into the bowl.
The Princess tried a second time, her brow furrowing in royal frustration.
She pinched harder, but the wooden sticks crossed awkwardly in her small fingers, sending another bundle of noodles tumbling back into the ceramic basin.
A soft frustrated pout formed on her lips with a light pink flush dusting her cheeks as she looked up at Silas with embarrassed pleading eyes.

"I... I do not possess the necessary manual dexterity to twirl these wooden rods, Lord Silas," she admitted in a tiny sheepish whisper, her pride slightly wounded. "Imperial etiquette tutors only instructed me in the use of seven distinct types of silver forks and jeweled bone-spoons."
Silas let out a warm laugh. "Don’t worry about it. It takes practice."
Without a second thought, Silas took the ebony chopsticks gently from her hand.
He deftly dipped them into her bowl, expertly gathering a perfect, bite-sized swirl of steaming noodles topped with a tender sliver of braised boar belly.
He lifted the portion smoothly, brought it close to his lips, blew two gentle breaths over the steam to cool the broth, and then extended the chopsticks directly toward the Princess’s lips.
"Say ah," Silas smiled playfully.
The Princess’s heart skipped a heavy beat.
Her azure eyes widened, staring at the food offered directly before her face.
She looked around nervously, noticing several recruits giggling behind their wooden cups, before looking back at Silas’s bright, encouraging expression.
Slowly, delicately, she parted her soft pink lips.
Silas guided the noodles into her mouth.
The moment the rich savory broth and melting boar belly touched her tongue, the Princess’s eyes lit up with delight.

The chewy texture of the hand-pulled noodles combined with the deep layered warmth of the garlic-infused marrow broth was unlike anything she had ever tasted within the cold gilded halls of the Palace.
"Mmmph...!" she hummed, chewing eagerly with her hand cupped delicately under her chin to catch any stray drops.
Once she swallowed, she looked up at him with sparkling eyes, entirely dropping her guarded royal veneer.
"It is magnificent, Lord Silas! The flavors are rich, comforting, and remarkably invigorating! Please... another bite?"
"Coming right up," Silas chuckled, happily twirling another bundle of noodles and feeding the royal maiden until the bowl was completely empty.
Roughly twenty minutes later, the brass hands on the timers chimed softly, signaling the end of the midday rest period.

Across the clearing, the fifty-plus recruit maidens, scouts, and vanguard champions stood up, rolling their shoulders, securing their leather harnesses, and latching their weapon sheaths with sharp metallic clicks.
Silas gently adjusted the sleeping Tasmin, sliding her off his side and settling her comfortably onto the thick woolen mat beneath the shade, making sure she remained undisturbed.
He stood up, stretching his broad shoulders until his joints popped with a satisfying crack.
’It’s time...’
Silas stepped to the front of the Lord’s mat, looking across the assembled ranks of Squad One, Squad Two, and Squad Three.
His blue eyes swept across the clearing, his brow furrowing slightly in sharp appraisal.

’Wait a minute...’ Silas thought, his gaze tracking the missing colors among the formations. ’Where are the northern perimeter units? Eluned’s women aren’t here... and neither is Eluned herself. Weren’t they scheduled to rendezvous at the central clearing minutes ago?’
Before Silas could extend his mana perception into the northern tree line—
FWHOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
A blinding emerald-green blur tore out from the dense foliage on the right flank at supersonic speed.
The sudden displaced air shrieked like a falling mortar shell.
BOOM!
The green blur slammed dead-center into Silas’s chest with the concussive force of a runaway siege engine, completely knocking the breath from his lungs.
"OOF—!"

Silas grunted as the overwhelming momentum forced his boots to skid fifteen feet backward across the turf, carving two deep smoking trenches through the black grass before his Gold Core mana anchored him firmly into the earth.
Wrapped entirely around his torso like a living vine of divine jade was Eluned.

sentences.text: The wide velvet-black clearing under the weeping willow was momentarily suspended in stunned breathless silence.

Every single recruit was still staring wide-eyed at the towering six-foot-four frame of Brida, who remained bent deeply at the waist with her fully exposed rear end aimed right at the edge of the Lord’s mat.
Tasmin was still burying her flushed face straight into Silas’s chest, her fists clutching his dark tunic as if she could pull the fabric over her head and vanish from the mortal plane entirely.
Silas looked at the provocative display, his blue eyes gleaming with an amused effortless spark.
"Sure."
A collective synchronized blink rippled across the entire encampment.
"Eh?" Helen let out a squeak.
"Wait, what—?" Sarah gasped, her jaw dropping open.

He didn’t draw back with mana or channel the divine aura of his Gold Core.
He simply stepped up directly behind the bent-over Titan, squared his shoulders, cocked his right arm, and swung his broad, calloused palm in a clean horizontal arc.
THWACK!
The concussive flesh-on-flesh impact cracked through the quiet clearing with the acoustic force of a dry thunderclap.
The heavy blow struck dead-center across the dense, muscular curve of Brida’s left cheek.

The force set off a visible hypnotic ripple across the golden-bronze skin of her rear, vibrating through muscle and tendon in a mesmerizing shockwave that left behind a bright fiery-red handprint perfectly contoured against her flesh.
"Aaaaaaahhn~!"
A loud moan tore from Brida’s throat, echoing across the shaded willow branches.
Her knees instantly buckled beneath her frame.
With a dramatic trembling shudder, the towering woman collapsed forward onto the grass, tumbling from her knees flat onto her stomach.

Her heavy iron-plated boots kicked up into the air in a fit of wild, giddy ecstasy, her heels drumming against the turf as she buried her flushed grinning face in the cool black blades of grass as her broad shoulders shook with breathless euphoric giggles.
"Hehehehe... ahaha... that’s the stuff..." Brida wheezed happily, her fingers clawing at the dirt.
"That’s that true authority right there..."
Silas let out a dry exasperated sigh, shaking his head as a small smirk tugged at the corner of his mouth.
With a casual flick of his wrist, a dimensional ripple opened in the air beside him.
Silas reached into his inventory, pulled out a thick folded woolen traveling mat, and tossed it down directly over Brida’s exposed lower half, draping the heavy fabric over her hips like a blanket.
"Stop causing trouble for the recruits and behaving like a wild beast in the middle of lunch," Silas scolded lightly, though his tone was layered with fond amusement.
Brida rolled onto her side beneath the mat, looking up at him with a remarkably obedient, dopey grin spreading across her face.
"Put some clothes on before you catch a cold," Silas added, crossing his arms.
"Sure, sure, my Lord!" Brida replied cheerfully, giving him a mock salute from the ground.
She didn’t argue.
With practiced ease, Brida reached into a concealed magnetic storage compartment built into the inner lining of her heavy chestplate.
She fished out a pair of snug dark-gray athletic boxers alongside a set of clean reinforced leather trousers.

Gathering the woolen mat tightly around her waist like a makeshift skirt, the woman scurried on her hands and knees toward a dense thicket of blackberry bushes at the edge of the clearing, humming a bawdy marching tune as she went to dress.
Silas watched her disappear into the foliage before turning back to the central mat.
Tasmin was still curled up in a tight, embarrassed ball on the linen, her face hidden behind her knees.
Silas knelt down beside her, slid his arms beneath her slender waist and thighs, and gently lifted the agile woman back onto his lap, pulling her securely against his chest once more.
"Come on now, Tas," Silas murmured softly, his voice low and warm against her ear.
"The spectacle is over so eat a little more."
He reached for the wooden platter, picking up a tender skewer of mountain fowl dipped in a light honey-soy marinade, and held it to her lips.
Tasmin peeked out from between her bangs, her cheeks still dusted with a soft lingering crimson blush.
She looked up at Silas’s calm reassuring smile, her heart fluttering before she obediently parted her lips to take another bite.
She chewed slowly, leaning the back of her head against his broad shoulder, letting the steady thump of his heartbeat soothe the lingering adrenaline in her veins.
"You’ve been pushing yourself too hard on the night patrols and training too," Silas said gently, brushing a stray lock of dark hair behind her ear.
"Once you finish this skewer, lay down and get some rest.
You have the entire break period to sleep."
Tasmin blinked her amber eyes, looking down at his chest with a soft, fluttering warmth swelling inside her.
"My Lord... but the perimeter—"
"The perimeter is secure.
Aurelia, Lupina, and the recruits are watching the borders," Silas cut in with a firm comforting finality.
"Rest."
Tasmin let out a tiny contented sigh.
She finished the meat, wiped her lips with the napkin Silas offered, and gently shifted off his lap onto the thick woven cushion beside him.

Curling her legs toward her chest, she rested her head upon a rolled cloak, and within less than two minutes, the exhausted commander had drifted into a deep tranquil sleep as her breathing began evening out into a soft steady rhythm.
Silas looked down at her peaceful face, a tender smile touching his lips.

’I knew you were exhausted,’ Silas thought, reaching down to pull the edge of a light linen blanket over her shoulders. ’Trying to train for your Shadow Heart constantly while scouting as well... you carried more than your share of the weight for a long time.’
"Lord Silas?"
A soft melodic voice broke through his thoughts from the opposite corner of the Lord’s mat.
Silas turned his head to see the Princess sitting primly on her knees.
Her lightweight sky-iron cuirass sat neatly propped against a wooden crate behind her, leaving her in a pristine white embroidered blouse that accentuated her delicate royal posture.

chapters.title: Chapter 453: UP And Maps [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The Goddess had her long slender legs locked tightly around Silas’s waist, her soft porcelain arms wrapped securely around his neck, and her radiant emerald-tinged blonde hair cascading wildly over his shoulders.
Her golden-green eyes sparkled with mischievous, breathless affection as she buried her face against the crook of his neck, inhaling his familiar scent with a happy musical giggle.
"My Lord! My darling Lord!" Eluned chimed, nuzzling her soft cheek against his jawline. "I missed you terribly during the morning march!"
STEP! STEP! CLANG!
Moments later, emerging from the northern tree line in crisp synchronized military order, came the twenty recruit maidens assigned to Eluned’s northern detachment.
Unlike the slightly fatigued units of the other squads, Eluned’s girls marched into the clearing practically glowing with excessive physical energy.

Several of the warrior maidens were flexing their toned, unblemished biceps, their ash-wood spears held proudly across their shoulders, their sky-iron cuirasses completely free of a single speck of dirt or monster blood.

"Squad Four reporting for midday assembly!" the lead recruit maiden called out, offering a respectful salute while bowing deeply. "We sincerely apologize to our Lord for our delayed arrival! An unexpected purge held up our return march!"
Silas stood in the center of the clearing, his arms instinctively supporting Eluned’s thighs to keep her from tumbling, though he looked at the Goddess with a raised eyebrow and a deadpan expression.
"Eluned," Silas said, looking directly into her sparkling golden-green eyes. "Why on earth is your squad late? You were only assigned to sweep the low-tier shrublands along the northern creek."
Eluned pulled her face back slightly, offering him a serene innocent smile that looked as pure as fresh morning dew.

"Oh, it was nothing of great consequence, my love," Eluned replied smoothly, her melodic voice floating through the clearing. "While my lovely girls were surveying the creek beds, we simply crossed paths with a rather rude collection of vulgar shapeshifting parasites... creatures who possessed the brazen audacity to mimic your divine handsome countenance."
Silas’s eyes narrowed slightly, a cold chill running down the back of his neck as he recalled Tasmin’s earlier report about the bipedal wolf-mimics.
’What did you do to them...?’ Silas thought, dreading the answer.
Eluned gently closed her eyes, resting her forehead against Silas’s temple.
A quiet radiant stillness settled over her expression as a vivid detailed recollection of the morning’s encounter unfolded in the depths of her consciousness.
(Flashback — Forty-Five Minutes Ago, Northern Creek Sector)
The northern sector of the Umbral Basin was bathed in the cool dappled sunlight filtering through towering willow-oak trees.
The recruits of Squad Four were moving in a loose, comfortable search formation along the pebble-strewn banks of a crystal-clear mountain creek.
The water bubbled merrily over smooth stones, the gentle breeze rustling through the ferns.
Suddenly, the brush on the opposite bank rustled violently.
RUSTLE! SNAP!
Stepping out from the shadowed thickets were seven figures.
Every single one of them possessed the exact height, broad muscular shoulders, sharp jawline, short midnight-black hair, and piercing blue eyes of Silas Graves.
They wore identical dark tactical tunics and held glowing golden longswords in their right hands.

"Halt, Squad Four!" the central Silas-mimic called out, its voice an uncanny pitch-perfect imitation of Silas’s tone. "The northern sweep is cancelled... Drop your weapons and approach me for individual mana replenishment."
The recruits immediately froze, their eyes widening in sudden confused hesitation.
"Lord... Lord Silas?" a young spear-maiden whispered, taking half a step forward. "Why are there seven of you...?"
Standing at the front of the formation, Eluned did not blink.
She slowly tilted her head to the side, her golden-green eyes narrowing into two vertical slits of divinity.

Her divine perception sliced straight through the visual illusions... the creatures beneath the skin possessed no golden souls, no Genesis Runes upon their knuckles, and their shadows on the pebbles... they didn’t have any.
"How crude," Eluned whispered.
The air around the creek bank did not simply grow cold... it completely ceased to move.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
A primordial domain of sovereignty erupted from Eluned’s slender frame as the tranquil creek waters instantly parted, and the earth beneath the opposite bank groaned violently.
Massive arm-thick roots of ironwood tore upward from the bedrock like the skeletal claws of a submerged titan.
"W-Wait—!" the lead Silas-mimic shrieked, its human vocal chords instantly distorting into the terrified guttural yowl of a feral beast as it tried to leap backward.
CRACK-CRUNCH!
It was far too late.

Dozens of razor-sharp ironwood roots erupted beneath all seven shapeshifters, wrapping around their ankles, wrists, and throats in an unbreakable, vice-like grip that pinned them horizontally in mid-air.

The seven monsters panicked, their human illusions melting away like hot wax to reveal their true forms... grotesque eight-foot-tall bipedal wolf-aberrations covered in patchy gray fur, with rows of needle-like fangs and bloodshot crimson eyes.
"SCREE!"
"SCRAAAAAAA!"
Eluned walked across the surface of the bubbling creek, her bare feet gliding over the water without disturbing a single ripple.
Her face was completely devoid of anger as instead, a bright melodic hum danced past her pink lips.
"Roots in the soil, seeds in the ground... Little pests make a wonderful sound..."
Eluned raised her right hand, her slender fingers curling into a slow, delicate fist.
"Grind~ Grind~ Grind~" Eluned incanted softly.
KRRRRRRRRRRRRRR-CRUNCH!
The ironwood roots did not merely crush the seven beasts... that would have been too easy.
Thousands of tiny barbed thorns... harder than diamond and humming with acidic digestive enzymes sprouted along the surface of the wood.
The roots began rotating in opposing, high-speed helical spirals, transforming into a massive meat-grinder that dragged the screaming shapeshifters into the center of the wooden vortex.
SPLAT! SQUELCH! CRACK! CRUNCH!
The sounds of fracturing monster bones, popping organs, and pulverized muscle tissue echoed through the serene forest clearing like a gruesome orchestral symphony.
The seven eight-foot wolf-monsters were crushed, stripped, and ground into microscopic, nutrient-dense biological powder in less than ten seconds.
The terrifying superheated friction of the divine grinding process flash-dried the organic matter, reducing the entire pack of Tier-2 anomalies into a mountain of fine dark-brown mineral dust.
POP.
With a wave of her left hand, a hollowed-out, two-foot-tall wooden storage jar carved from living spirit-oak materialized in the air before her.
Eluned swirled her index finger in a graceful circle.
FWHOOSH.
A gentle gust of wind mana gathered the entirety of the nutrient-rich bone-and-flesh powder, funneling the dark dust neatly through the air and straight into the open mouth of the wooden jar.
CLACK!
The spirit-oak lid snapped shut, sealing the jar with an airtight rune.
Eluned picked up the heavy wooden jar, hugging it affectionately against her chest with a bright, radiant smile, resuming her cheerful song.
"Rich in the bone, sweet in the marrow... My garden will bloom so brightly tomorrow..."

She turned back to the recruits, who were standing on the creek bank with their jaws hanging slack, their faces completely drained of color as they stared at the spot where seven monsters had existed moments prior.
"Come along, girls!" Eluned called out with boundless, sunny enthusiasm, waving her free hand. "We must hurry! We cannot keep our darling Lord waiting for his midday meal!"
(Present Clearing — Under the Willow Tree)
Eluned opened her golden-green eyes, her tranquil affectionate smile returning in full force as she looked up at Silas from where she hung wrapped around his waist.
She patted his cheek softly with her warm hand, her voice sweet and dripping with honeyed innocence.
"You truly don’t have to worry about those nasty little shapeshifters anymore, my darling," Eluned chirped happily, her eyes curving into soft crescents. "They are in a much, much better place now."
Silas stared at her, feeling a bead of sweat trickle down the nape of his neck.
He didn’t ask another question as he didn’t need to.
He simply wrapped his arm securely around her waist, letting out a long slow breath as he looked out over his assembled, formidable army.
"Alright," Silas smiled wryly. "Let’s finish lunch and prepare for the afternoon march."
The soft rustle of the weeping willow leaves provided a rhythmic, soothing canopy above the Lord’s woven linen mat.
Beside Silas, Tasmin remained curled in a peaceful exhausted ball beneath her light woolen blanket, her lips parted slightly as tiny adorable snores escaped her throat.
Her dark hair was splayed across the rolled-up traveling cloak serving as her pillow, the deep dark circles under her eyes finally softening under the influence of rest and full nourishment.
Sitting squarely on Silas’s lap now was Eluned.
The Goddess had made herself completely at home, her slender arms resting comfortably across his shoulders as her porcelain thighs bracketed his hips.

Her golden-green eyes fluttered with sunny delight as Silas lifted a steaming wooden bowl of buttered tuber mash mixed with shredded spirit-fowl, scooping up a generous spoonful and extending it toward her lips.
"Ah~" Eluned chimed, parting her soft rosy lips obediently.
She took the bite, humming a melodious harmonic note of culinary bliss as she leaned her cheek against his jawline.
While Silas kept a steady comforting rhythm of feeding the Goddess, his mind began to drift toward the administrative part of the territory.
’Now... let’s check the UP haul,’ Silas thought, his blue eyes narrowing with quiet anticipation.
Throughout the entire morning campaign, his senses had been subtly bombarded by a continuous stream of system notifications.

Because his expeditionary force had split into distinct operational squads... sweeping through jagged gorges, incinerating subterranean arachnid nests, butchering wolf-shapeshifters, and much more... The tabs had been rolling in like high tide.
Multiple recruits had broken through levels and Vala herself seemed to be one of them.
’That woman... She sure is strong.’
Silas had deliberately muted the active system chimes to avoid distraction during combat but now, with the camp secure and lunch underway, he willed the interface to manifest.
VUUUUUUM.
A sleek translucent blue holographic ledger materialized before his line of sight, invisible to everyone except himself.
[UP Balance: 3,020 UP]
Silas stared at the glowing golden digits, his fingers tapping rhythmically against Eluned’s hip.

’3,020 Upgrade Points,’ Silas mused, a satisfied smirk touching his lips. ’Not bad at all for a single morning’s run in addition to what we had left... It’s a solid haul that gives us plenty of breathing room for our next infrastructure leap.’
Still, his boundless greedy ambition hummed beneath the surface.

’It’s good, but I’d still like to harvest significantly more before we pack up for the Keep. We’ve got an entire operational afternoon ahead of us, and Thora’s foundry needs every scrap of high-grade raw ore and reinforcement we can provide.’
"My darling Lord?" Eluned’s sweet voice interrupted his inner calculations.
She gently reached out, placing her soft, fragrant fingers over his hand holding the wooden spoon.
"You seem lost in territorial strategies. Please, do not trouble yourself with feeding me every mouthful... I can happily feed myself so you may attend to your thoughts."
Silas chuckled warmly, giving her head an affectionate pat that smoothed her green locks.
"Alright, eat up."
With a flick of his wrist, Silas opened his inventory.
A roll of thick enchanted paper materialized in his grasp, and he laid it flat across the unoccupied edge of the mat, weighing the corners down with small river stones.
He looked at the marked quadrant where they had just cleared out the Broodmother Spider Queen.

On the original cartographic survey of the Umbral Basin, that particular cavern had been stamped with a faded red X... indicating an unchecked geographic anomaly suspected of containing mineral-rich veins.
With a charcoal stylus, Silas drew a firm dark circle around the red X.

’That spider den wasn’t just a monster nest... it was sitting on top of an unrefined underground stratum,’ Silas thought, his eyes gleaming with satisfaction. ’Which means we didn’t just clear out an arachnid menace... we officially secured a brand-new mining cavern for the territory.’
Silas traced his stylus across the map, scanning the adjacent terrain.
Roughly three miles to the northeast of their current encampment, another prominent red X was marked near a jagged limestone cliffside, designated in Thora’s dwarven handwriting as Sector KB-22.
TAP! TAP!
Silas brought the tip of his stylus down firmly on the mark.

’This is the way to go,’ Silas decided, his strategic layout snapping into place. ’We’ll march out, raid the interior, and exterminate every beast nesting inside... That way, when we begin mining tomorrow morning, the entire sector will be completely sanitized and ready for excavation.’

sentences.text: The Goddess had her long slender legs locked tightly around Silas’s waist, her soft porcelain arms wrapped securely around his neck, and her radiant emerald-tinged blonde hair cascading wildly over his shoulders.
Her golden-green eyes sparkled with mischievous, breathless affection as she buried her face against the crook of his neck, inhaling his familiar scent with a happy musical giggle.
"My Lord!
My darling Lord!" Eluned chimed, nuzzling her soft cheek against his jawline.
"I missed you terribly during the morning march!"
STEP!
STEP!
CLANG!
Moments later, emerging from the northern tree line in crisp synchronized military order, came the twenty recruit maidens assigned to Eluned’s northern detachment.
Unlike the slightly fatigued units of the other squads, Eluned’s girls marched into the clearing practically glowing with excessive physical energy.

Several of the warrior maidens were flexing their toned, unblemished biceps, their ash-wood spears held proudly across their shoulders, their sky-iron cuirasses completely free of a single speck of dirt or monster blood.
"Squad Four reporting for midday assembly!" the lead recruit maiden called out, offering a respectful salute while bowing deeply.
"We sincerely apologize to our Lord for our delayed arrival!
An unexpected purge held up our return march!"
Silas stood in the center of the clearing, his arms instinctively supporting Eluned’s thighs to keep her from tumbling, though he looked at the Goddess with a raised eyebrow and a deadpan expression.
"Eluned," Silas said, looking directly into her sparkling golden-green eyes.
"Why on earth is your squad late?
You were only assigned to sweep the low-tier shrublands along the northern creek."
Eluned pulled her face back slightly, offering him a serene innocent smile that looked as pure as fresh morning dew.
"Oh, it was nothing of great consequence, my love," Eluned replied smoothly, her melodic voice floating through the clearing.

"While my lovely girls were surveying the creek beds, we simply crossed paths with a rather rude collection of vulgar shapeshifting parasites... creatures who possessed the brazen audacity to mimic your divine handsome countenance."
Silas’s eyes narrowed slightly, a cold chill running down the back of his neck as he recalled Tasmin’s earlier report about the bipedal wolf-mimics.
’What did you do to them...?’ Silas thought, dreading the answer.
Eluned gently closed her eyes, resting her forehead against Silas’s temple.
A quiet radiant stillness settled over her expression as a vivid detailed recollection of the morning’s encounter unfolded in the depths of her consciousness.
(Flashback — Forty-Five Minutes Ago, Northern Creek Sector)
The northern sector of the Umbral Basin was bathed in the cool dappled sunlight filtering through towering willow-oak trees.
The recruits of Squad Four were moving in a loose, comfortable search formation along the pebble-strewn banks of a crystal-clear mountain creek.
The water bubbled merrily over smooth stones, the gentle breeze rustling through the ferns.
Suddenly, the brush on the opposite bank rustled violently.
RUSTLE!
SNAP!
Stepping out from the shadowed thickets were seven figures.
Every single one of them possessed the exact height, broad muscular shoulders, sharp jawline, short midnight-black hair, and piercing blue eyes of Silas Graves.
They wore identical dark tactical tunics and held glowing golden longswords in their right hands.
"Halt, Squad Four!" the central Silas-mimic called out, its voice an uncanny pitch-perfect imitation of Silas’s tone.
"The northern sweep is cancelled...
Drop your weapons and approach me for individual mana replenishment."
The recruits immediately froze, their eyes widening in sudden confused hesitation.
"Lord...
Lord Silas?" a young spear-maiden whispered, taking half a step forward.
"Why are there seven of you...?"
Standing at the front of the formation, Eluned did not blink.
She slowly tilted her head to the side, her golden-green eyes narrowing into two vertical slits of divinity.

Her divine perception sliced straight through the visual illusions... the creatures beneath the skin possessed no golden souls, no Genesis Runes upon their knuckles, and their shadows on the pebbles... they didn’t have any.
"How crude," Eluned whispered.
The air around the creek bank did not simply grow cold... it completely ceased to move.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
A primordial domain of sovereignty erupted from Eluned’s slender frame as the tranquil creek waters instantly parted, and the earth beneath the opposite bank groaned violently.
Massive arm-thick roots of ironwood tore upward from the bedrock like the skeletal claws of a submerged titan.
"W-Wait—!" the lead Silas-mimic shrieked, its human vocal chords instantly distorting into the terrified guttural yowl of a feral beast as it tried to leap backward.
CRACK-CRUNCH!
It was far too late.

Dozens of razor-sharp ironwood roots erupted beneath all seven shapeshifters, wrapping around their ankles, wrists, and throats in an unbreakable, vice-like grip that pinned them horizontally in mid-air.

The seven monsters panicked, their human illusions melting away like hot wax to reveal their true forms... grotesque eight-foot-tall bipedal wolf-aberrations covered in patchy gray fur, with rows of needle-like fangs and bloodshot crimson eyes.
"SCREE!"
"SCRAAAAAAA!"
Eluned walked across the surface of the bubbling creek, her bare feet gliding over the water without disturbing a single ripple.
Her face was completely devoid of anger as instead, a bright melodic hum danced past her pink lips.
"Roots in the soil, seeds in the ground...
Little pests make a wonderful sound..."
Eluned raised her right hand, her slender fingers curling into a slow, delicate fist.
"Grind~ Grind~ Grind~" Eluned incanted softly.
KRRRRRRRRRRRRRR-CRUNCH!
The ironwood roots did not merely crush the seven beasts... that would have been too easy.
Thousands of tiny barbed thorns... harder than diamond and humming with acidic digestive enzymes sprouted along the surface of the wood.
The roots began rotating in opposing, high-speed helical spirals, transforming into a massive meat-grinder that dragged the screaming shapeshifters into the center of the wooden vortex.
SPLAT!
SQUELCH!
CRACK!
CRUNCH!
The sounds of fracturing monster bones, popping organs, and pulverized muscle tissue echoed through the serene forest clearing like a gruesome orchestral symphony.
The seven eight-foot wolf-monsters were crushed, stripped, and ground into microscopic, nutrient-dense biological powder in less than ten seconds.
The terrifying superheated friction of the divine grinding process flash-dried the organic matter, reducing the entire pack of Tier-2 anomalies into a mountain of fine dark-brown mineral dust.
POP.
With a wave of her left hand, a hollowed-out, two-foot-tall wooden storage jar carved from living spirit-oak materialized in the air before her.
Eluned swirled her index finger in a graceful circle.
FWHOOSH.
A gentle gust of wind mana gathered the entirety of the nutrient-rich bone-and-flesh powder, funneling the dark dust neatly through the air and straight into the open mouth of the wooden jar.
CLACK!
The spirit-oak lid snapped shut, sealing the jar with an airtight rune.
Eluned picked up the heavy wooden jar, hugging it affectionately against her chest with a bright, radiant smile, resuming her cheerful song.
"Rich in the bone, sweet in the marrow...
My garden will bloom so brightly tomorrow..."

She turned back to the recruits, who were standing on the creek bank with their jaws hanging slack, their faces completely drained of color as they stared at the spot where seven monsters had existed moments prior.
"Come along, girls!" Eluned called out with boundless, sunny enthusiasm, waving her free hand.
"We must hurry!
We cannot keep our darling Lord waiting for his midday meal!"
(Present Clearing — Under the Willow Tree)
Eluned opened her golden-green eyes, her tranquil affectionate smile returning in full force as she looked up at Silas from where she hung wrapped around his waist.
She patted his cheek softly with her warm hand, her voice sweet and dripping with honeyed innocence.
"You truly don’t have to worry about those nasty little shapeshifters anymore, my darling," Eluned chirped happily, her eyes curving into soft crescents.
"They are in a much, much better place now."
Silas stared at her, feeling a bead of sweat trickle down the nape of his neck.
He didn’t ask another question as he didn’t need to.
He simply wrapped his arm securely around her waist, letting out a long slow breath as he looked out over his assembled, formidable army.
"Alright," Silas smiled wryly.
"Let’s finish lunch and prepare for the afternoon march."
The soft rustle of the weeping willow leaves provided a rhythmic, soothing canopy above the Lord’s woven linen mat.
Beside Silas, Tasmin remained curled in a peaceful exhausted ball beneath her light woolen blanket, her lips parted slightly as tiny adorable snores escaped her throat.
Her dark hair was splayed across the rolled-up traveling cloak serving as her pillow, the deep dark circles under her eyes finally softening under the influence of rest and full nourishment.
Sitting squarely on Silas’s lap now was Eluned.
The Goddess had made herself completely at home, her slender arms resting comfortably across his shoulders as her porcelain thighs bracketed his hips.

Her golden-green eyes fluttered with sunny delight as Silas lifted a steaming wooden bowl of buttered tuber mash mixed with shredded spirit-fowl, scooping up a generous spoonful and extending it toward her lips.
"Ah~" Eluned chimed, parting her soft rosy lips obediently.
She took the bite, humming a melodious harmonic note of culinary bliss as she leaned her cheek against his jawline.
While Silas kept a steady comforting rhythm of feeding the Goddess, his mind began to drift toward the administrative part of the territory.
’Now... let’s check the UP haul,’ Silas thought, his blue eyes narrowing with quiet anticipation.
Throughout the entire morning campaign, his senses had been subtly bombarded by a continuous stream of system notifications.
Because his expeditionary force had split into distinct operational squads... sweeping through jagged gorges, incinerating subterranean arachnid nests, butchering wolf-shapeshifters, and much more...
The tabs had been rolling in like high tide.
Multiple recruits had broken through levels and Vala herself seemed to be one of them.
’That woman...
She sure is strong.’
Silas had deliberately muted the active system chimes to avoid distraction during combat but now, with the camp secure and lunch underway, he willed the interface to manifest.
VUUUUUUM.
A sleek translucent blue holographic ledger materialized before his line of sight, invisible to everyone except himself.
[UP Balance: 3,020 UP]
Silas stared at the glowing golden digits, his fingers tapping rhythmically against Eluned’s hip.
’3,020 Upgrade Points,’ Silas mused, a satisfied smirk touching his lips. ’Not bad at all for a single morning’s run in addition to what we had left...
It’s a solid haul that gives us plenty of breathing room for our next infrastructure leap.’
Still, his boundless greedy ambition hummed beneath the surface.
’It’s good, but I’d still like to harvest significantly more before we pack up for the Keep.
We’ve got an entire operational afternoon ahead of us, and Thora’s foundry needs every scrap of high-grade raw ore and reinforcement we can provide.’
"My darling Lord?" Eluned’s sweet voice interrupted his inner calculations.
She gently reached out, placing her soft, fragrant fingers over his hand holding the wooden spoon.
"You seem lost in territorial strategies.
Please, do not trouble yourself with feeding me every mouthful...
I can happily feed myself so you may attend to your thoughts."
Silas chuckled warmly, giving her head an affectionate pat that smoothed her green locks.
"Alright, eat up."

chapters.title: Chapter 454: Mine KB-22 [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Around the clearing, the fifty-plus warrior maidens were finishing the last of their rations, stowing away their lunchboxes, and stretching their limbs.
Silas stood up from the mat, gently letting Eluned slide down onto her feet, and rolled his shoulders until his spine gave a crisp satisfying pop.
He stepped to the front of the Lord’s mat, his presence commanding immediate effortless silence across the fifty-yard clearing.
All four squads instantly snapped to attention, their eyes turning toward him with bright devotion.
Silas looked out over his assembled army, a proud radiant smile breaking across his handsome face.

"Listen up, girls!" Silas called out, his voice carrying effortlessly on the mountain breeze. "You’ve fought exceptionally well all morning... You held your formations, adapted to unexpected ambush tactics, and cleared out multiple high-threat anomaly pockets without a single casualty. I am immensely proud of every single one of you."
A collective murmur of joyous pride rippled through the ranks, several recruits clasping their hands over their chests as their cheeks flushed with happy color.

"And for our recruits," Silas continued, his gaze sweeping over the fifteen maidens who had followed him into the spider den, "if you maintain this level of discipline, focus, and execution through the rest of the afternoon march... the recruit tag comes off today. When we cross the threshold back into Blessed Land tonight, you will officially be inducted as recognized Warriors of our territory!"
"YEAAAAAH!"
A thunderous, unified cheer erupted from the recruit maidens, their ash-wood spears thrusting into the sky with triumphant vigor.

For these women, their past service within the rigid suffocating ranks of the Unmovable Wall had been defined by cold dismissals, disposable assignments, and riding on the borrowed glory of haughty commanders.

Not that it was bad because Lord Evelyn or rather Lord Sky treated them very well but in Blessed Land, their sweat was acknowledged, their meals were lavish, and their Lord personally watched over their growth.
The thought of earning their full warrior crest filled their hearts with a burning fire.
Across the clearing, the Blessed Wolves were brought forward.
Each squad mounted up with crisp synchronization.
Even Eluned strode over to the Blessed wolf that had quietly been padding behind her squad all morning, hopping onto the leather saddle with an effortless, graceful vault.
"We shall see you at the territory, my darling!" Eluned called out, blowing Silas a radiant kiss from atop her mount.
Tasmin, now fully awake and visibly refreshed, stood beside her dire wolf, stretching her toned arms over her head with a long feline arch of her back.
She adjusted the leather harnesses of her singlet, casting a lingering affectionate look back toward Silas.
"Stay safe, my Lord," Tasmin murmured, a soft smirk gracing her lips before she vaulted into her saddle. "Don’t let the recruits steal all your attention."
"Move out!" Brida bellowed, now fully clad in clean trousers and leading the vanguard detachment forward in a thunderous gallop.
Silas turned toward Helen, who was securing the brass-rimmed chronomancy timer to her wrist armor.
"Helen, what’s our operational window before the afternoon recall?" Silas asked.
Helen tapped the glass face of the device, checking the alignment of the enchanted brass gears.
"We have a little over two hours, Lord Silas, before we have to begin making our return march!"
Silas turned toward Valkyrie, who was already waiting at his side with an eager tail-thumping pant.
He swung his leg smoothly over the saddle, reached down with both hands, and scooped the Princess up by her waist, settling the royal maiden securely between his arms.
Silas drew his golden-runed longsword from its scabbard with a sharp ringing chime that echoed across the clearing.
"Two hours is plenty of time," Silas grinned, his blue eyes flashing with sovereign excitement. "Squad One! Why don’t we raid another cavern?!"
"HOO-AH!" the squad roared in unison.
With a powerful kick from Valkyrie’s hind legs, the wolf exploded into a full gallop, leading the column northeast across the undulating black grass.
Roughly twenty-five minutes later, the squad arrived at the foot of a towering limestone ridge.
The terrain here was barren and rugged, choked with gray shale, calcified stalagmites, and twisted deadwood shrubs.

Carved directly into the face of the limestone cliff was a wide, yawning cavern entrance spanning nearly thirty feet across as chiseled into a weather-worn survey marker near the entrance was the territorial designation... KB-22.
’I think the scouts said that it had monsters or something.’
Silas pulled Valkyrie to a halt, leaning forward against the saddle pommel as he looked at the dark opening.
Beside the map marker, Thora had etched a distinct dwarven rune representing Mana Diamonds... an exceptionally rare crystalline mineral that naturally formed under immense underground mana pressure.

’Mana Diamonds...’ Silas mused, his merchant-like greed stirring pleasantly within his chest. ’Those things are ridiculously valuable. In the LAB markets, a single raw carat sells for enough gold to buy a whole lot of things but more importantly, when refined through Thora’s forge, Mana Diamonds serve as the ultimate conductivity cores for high-tier magical weapons and defensive jewelry.’
Not to mention he could upgrade them too before selling, there were too many gains in mining for Silas to not love it.
The cavern entrance was dark and barely illuminated by the ambient light filtering through the limestone fissures.
Aurelia stepped forward on foot, her slender hand raised before her.
"Allow me, Lord Silas," Aurelia murmured softly.
VUUUUUM!
A small perfectly spherical orb of pure white Argent Flame ignited above Aurelia’s open palm.

With a gentle flick of her wrist, she pushed the floating orb forward. The radiant sphere drifted twenty paces into the yawning cavern mouth, casting a daylight glow across the damp stone walls, illuminating smooth limestone tunnels, cascading mineral stalactites, and dead silence.
There were no webbing traps, no acidic pools, and not a single visible mana signature lingering within the immediate fifty-yard threshold.
"The entrance appears completely clear of hostiles, my Lord," Aurelia reported, glancing back.

"Dismount and form standard search-and-clear lines," Silas commanded, lifting the Princess down onto the gravel before vaulting off Valkyrie’s back. "Spears in the front rank, blades on the flanks, mages holding the center."
The fifteen recruit maidens moved with disciplined speed.

Ash-wood spears were brought to low-ready, void-iron arming swords cleared their sheaths with crisp metallic clicks, and the squad crossed the threshold into Cavern KB-22 in a tight overlapping wedge formation.
For the first forty paces, the only sound was the synchronized crunch of leather boots against gravel.
Then, from the deep, pitch-black labyrinthine tunnels branching off the main cavern hall—
SKITTER! RATTLE! CHATTER!
A chorus of high-pitched guttural shrieks erupted from the darkness!
"GAK-GAK-GAK!"
Surging out from five separate subterranean side tunnels came an entire chaotic horde of over sixty Cavern Goblins.
These were not the frail, starving green runts of the surface forests.
These beasts stood nearly four feet tall, their leathery slate-gray skin covered in thick warts and scar tissue.
Their bloodshot yellow eyes blazed with feral hunger, and they brandished rusted iron cleavers, jagged bone clubs, and crude flint-tipped short spears.
And towering behind them, leading the charge with earth-shaking, heavy footsteps, were four massive Hobgoblins.
Standing nearly eight feet tall with broad, slab-like torsos of dense, corded muscle, the Hobgoblins wore crude chestplates hammered from scrap iron.
In their clawed hands, they wielded six-foot spiked morningstars and jagged broadswords that scraped violently against the stone floor.
They looked poorly made though.
’How do they even get weapons?’
CLANG! SCRAPE! KRRRR-SH!
"Hostiles inbound!" Helen barked. "Front rank, BRACE! Lock your spear butts into the stone!"
"Shields up! Overlap edges!" Sarah shouted from the right flank.
BOOM!
The fifteen recruits dropped into a rock-solid phalanx formation.

The front six spear-maidens planted the iron butts of their ash-wood shafts deep into the gravel fissures, angling their glowing void-iron tips outward at forty-five degrees to form an impenetrable wall of steel points.
CRUNCH! SQUELCH!
The forward wave of manic goblins slammed directly into the spear wall at reckless mindless speed.

Three goblins were instantly impaled through their chests, their leathery green-gray bodies lifting off their feet under their own forward momentum dark blood spraying across the limestone floorboards.
"GAK—!"
"HOLD THE LINE!" Helen grunted, planting her shoulder against the spear shaft and absorbing the kinetic with a sharp flex of her core mana. "Thrust and rotate! DON’T LET THEM GATHER AT THE BASE!"
THWACK-SHIK!
The recruit maidens worked with textbook efficiency.

As the front rank held the brace, the second rank drove their void-iron blades over the spear shoulders, stabbing downward in rapid piston strikes that severed goblin necks and split craniums with sickening wet crunches.
SPLAT! CRACK! THUD!
"Two trying to flank around the left stalagmite!" a young sword-maiden called out, parrying a jagged bone club with a sharp upward deflection.
CLANG!
"I see them!" another recruit shouted, pivoting smoothly on her left heel and driving her blade straight through the flanking goblin’s eye socket with frictionless velocity.
SQUELCH.
Standing ten paces back in the center of the cavern, Silas leaned casually against a massive limestone pillar, his golden sword resting loosely across his shoulder.
He raised his left hand to his mouth, letting out a long, relaxed, and thoroughly bored yawn:
’Haaaaaaan...’
Silas didn’t move a single muscle.
He didn’t draw upon his Gold Core, nor did he cast a single spark of flame.
He simply watched the skirmish unfold with the relaxed, critical eye of an instructor watching an elementary sparring drill.

’Good footwork on the left flank,’ Silas evaluated in his mind, his blue eyes tracking the recruits’ micro-movements. ’Sarah adjusted her weight perfectly during that parry... Helen’s commands are sharp, she could be a Captain too... These simple gray-skin goblins can’t even scratch their armor plates.’
BOOM! BOOM!
The ground shook as the lead eight-foot Hobgoblin shoved past its smaller kin, raising a massive two-hundred-pound spiked iron morningstar high above its head!
"CRAAAAA!" the Hobgoblin roared, bringing the spiked weapon down in a violent whistling arc aimed straight at Helen’s shield.
WHOOOOOOSH!
"Argent Barrier." Aurelia’s serene voice whispered from the backline.
VUUUUUUM... CLANG!
A pristine glowing shield of translucent white holy fire manifested half an inch above Helen’s iron pauldron.
The Hobgoblin’s massive iron morningstar struck the celestial barrier with the deafening force of a siege catapult yet the holy shield didn’t even ripple.
Instead, the concussive force violently rebounded straight back into the Hobgoblin’s thick wrists, fracturing its carpals with a loud sickening snap.
"GRAAAAAAH!" the giant brute howled in agonizing shock, dropping the morningstar to the floor.
"NOW! TAKE ITS LEGS!" Helen screamed, seizing the opening.
SLASH-CRUNCH!
Two recruit sword-maidens blurred forward beneath the beast’s guard, their void-iron blades executing synchronized hamstring slices that severed the Hobgoblin’s Achilles tendons like snapping ropes.

The eight-foot titan crashed heavily onto its knees with a booming thud, where Helen stepped forward and drove her spear straight through its throat, ending its life in a single pressurized geyser of black blood!
While the main phalanx systematically butchered the remaining three Hobgoblins and their chaotic retinue, a lone cowardly Cavern Goblin broke away from the main skirmish.
Crouching low on all fours, the three-foot-tall gray runt scrambled around the shadows of a limestone stalagmite, clutching a jagged bone dagger between its filthy claws.
Its yellow eyes locked onto the blue-haired royal maiden standing near Silas.
"Squeeee!" the goblin hissed, lunging out from the shadows directly toward the Princess.
The Princess gasped, her azure eyes widening as the snarling, wart-covered face leaped through the air.
Her instincts screamed at her to retreat, but her mind instantly recalled Silas’s steady words as he guided her to fight while they rode here.
’Plant your foot... Find your balance and drive through the core.’
SHIK!
The Princess drew her six-inch void-iron dagger from its thigh sheath with a crisp trembling ring of steel.
’Haah... Calm down...’
She did not tumble backward onto her rear.
She gritted her teeth, stepped firmly into the gravel with her left boot, and lowered her center of gravity.
As the goblin lunged with its bone dagger, the Princess pivoted her torso to the right, letting the rusted bone weapon scrape harmlessly past her white blouse.
SWISH.
"Begone, foul creature of the dark!" the Princess shouted, channeling every ounce of her royal resolve.
She drove the void-iron dagger upward with both hands, plunging the sharp blade straight beneath the goblin’s chin, driving the steel through its palate and clean into its brain.
CRUNCH-SQUELCH!
The goblin’s yellow eyes rolled back into its skull, its body stiffening mid-air before collapsing limply onto the limestone floor at her feet.
"Haaah... Haah... Hahh..."
The Princess stood over the slain beast, her chest heaving as she pulled the dagger free and wiped the dark fluid clean against a patch of dry moss.
A breathless, radiant smile broke across her face. "I... I did it! Another clean strike!"
She turned around to look for Silas and Aurelia and instantly froze.
The entire cavern was dead silent.
The chaotic horde of sixty Cavern Goblins and four massive Hobgoblins had ceased to exist.
Across the wide limestone chamber, every single beast had been thoroughly slaughtered.
Severed green-gray limbs, shattered iron clubs, and neatly decapitated monster corpses lay scattered across the gravel in neat piles.

The fifteen recruits were already wiping their blades clean with dry cloths, chatting and laughing among themselves like normal young women finishing an afternoon chore, while Aurelia calmly extinguished her floating orb of holy fire.
Standing against the pillar, Silas looked over at the wide-eyed Princess, his blue eyes crinkling with warm effortless amusement as he gave her a thumbs-up.
"Not bad, Princess," Silas chuckled, pushing off the limestone wall. "Not bad at all."
