He swung his leg smoothly over the saddle, reached down with both hands, and scooped the Princess up by her waist, settling the royal maiden securely between his arms.
Silas drew his golden-runed longsword from its scabbard with a sharp ringing chime that echoed across the clearing.
"Two hours is plenty of time," Silas grinned, his blue eyes flashing with sovereign excitement.
"Squad One!
Why don’t we raid another cavern?!"
"HOO-AH!" the squad roared in unison.
With a powerful kick from Valkyrie’s hind legs, the wolf exploded into a full gallop, leading the column northeast across the undulating black grass.
Roughly twenty-five minutes later, the squad arrived at the foot of a towering limestone ridge.
The terrain here was barren and rugged, choked with gray shale, calcified stalagmites, and twisted deadwood shrubs.

Carved directly into the face of the limestone cliff was a wide, yawning cavern entrance spanning nearly thirty feet across as chiseled into a weather-worn survey marker near the entrance was the territorial designation...
’I think the scouts said that it had monsters or something.’
Silas pulled Valkyrie to a halt, leaning forward against the saddle pommel as he looked at the dark opening.
Beside the map marker, Thora had etched a distinct dwarven rune representing Mana Diamonds... an exceptionally rare crystalline mineral that naturally formed under immense underground mana pressure.
’Mana Diamonds...’ Silas mused, his merchant-like greed stirring pleasantly within his chest. ’Those things are ridiculously valuable.

In the LAB markets, a single raw carat sells for enough gold to buy a whole lot of things but more importantly, when refined through Thora’s forge, Mana Diamonds serve as the ultimate conductivity cores for high-tier magical weapons and defensive jewelry.’
Not to mention he could upgrade them too before selling, there were too many gains in mining for Silas to not love it.
The cavern entrance was dark and barely illuminated by the ambient light filtering through the limestone fissures.
Aurelia stepped forward on foot, her slender hand raised before her.
"Allow me, Lord Silas," Aurelia murmured softly.
VUUUUUM!
A small perfectly spherical orb of pure white Argent Flame ignited above Aurelia’s open palm.
With a gentle flick of her wrist, she pushed the floating orb forward.

The radiant sphere drifted twenty paces into the yawning cavern mouth, casting a daylight glow across the damp stone walls, illuminating smooth limestone tunnels, cascading mineral stalactites, and dead silence.
There were no webbing traps, no acidic pools, and not a single visible mana signature lingering within the immediate fifty-yard threshold.
"The entrance appears completely clear of hostiles, my Lord," Aurelia reported, glancing back.
"Dismount and form standard search-and-clear lines," Silas commanded, lifting the Princess down onto the gravel before vaulting off Valkyrie’s back.
"Spears in the front rank, blades on the flanks, mages holding the center."
The fifteen recruit maidens moved with disciplined speed.

Ash-wood spears were brought to low-ready, void-iron arming swords cleared their sheaths with crisp metallic clicks, and the squad crossed the threshold into Cavern KB-22 in a tight overlapping wedge formation.
For the first forty paces, the only sound was the synchronized crunch of leather boots against gravel.
Then, from the deep, pitch-black labyrinthine tunnels branching off the main cavern hall—
SKITTER!
RATTLE!
CHATTER!
A chorus of high-pitched guttural shrieks erupted from the darkness!
"GAK-GAK-GAK!"
Surging out from five separate subterranean side tunnels came an entire chaotic horde of over sixty Cavern Goblins.
These were not the frail, starving green runts of the surface forests.
These beasts stood nearly four feet tall, their leathery slate-gray skin covered in thick warts and scar tissue.
Their bloodshot yellow eyes blazed with feral hunger, and they brandished rusted iron cleavers, jagged bone clubs, and crude flint-tipped short spears.
And towering behind them, leading the charge with earth-shaking, heavy footsteps, were four massive Hobgoblins.
Standing nearly eight feet tall with broad, slab-like torsos of dense, corded muscle, the Hobgoblins wore crude chestplates hammered from scrap iron.
In their clawed hands, they wielded six-foot spiked morningstars and jagged broadswords that scraped violently against the stone floor.
They looked poorly made though.
’How do they even get weapons?’
CLANG!
SCRAPE!
KRRRR-SH!
"Hostiles inbound!" Helen barked.
"Front rank, BRACE!
Lock your spear butts into the stone!"
"Shields up!
Overlap edges!" Sarah shouted from the right flank.
BOOM!
The fifteen recruits dropped into a rock-solid phalanx formation.

The front six spear-maidens planted the iron butts of their ash-wood shafts deep into the gravel fissures, angling their glowing void-iron tips outward at forty-five degrees to form an impenetrable wall of steel points.
CRUNCH!
SQUELCH!
The forward wave of manic goblins slammed directly into the spear wall at reckless mindless speed.

Three goblins were instantly impaled through their chests, their leathery green-gray bodies lifting off their feet under their own forward momentum dark blood spraying across the limestone floorboards.
"GAK—!"
"HOLD THE LINE!" Helen grunted, planting her shoulder against the spear shaft and absorbing the kinetic with a sharp flex of her core mana.
"Thrust and rotate!
DON’T LET THEM GATHER AT THE BASE!"
THWACK-SHIK!
The recruit maidens worked with textbook efficiency.

As the front rank held the brace, the second rank drove their void-iron blades over the spear shoulders, stabbing downward in rapid piston strikes that severed goblin necks and split craniums with sickening wet crunches.
SPLAT!
CRACK!
THUD!
"Two trying to flank around the left stalagmite!" a young sword-maiden called out, parrying a jagged bone club with a sharp upward deflection.
CLANG!
"I see them!" another recruit shouted, pivoting smoothly on her left heel and driving her blade straight through the flanking goblin’s eye socket with frictionless velocity.
SQUELCH.
Standing ten paces back in the center of the cavern, Silas leaned casually against a massive limestone pillar, his golden sword resting loosely across his shoulder.
He raised his left hand to his mouth, letting out a long, relaxed, and thoroughly bored yawn:
’Haaaaaaan...’
Silas didn’t move a single muscle.
He didn’t draw upon his Gold Core, nor did he cast a single spark of flame.
He simply watched the skirmish unfold with the relaxed, critical eye of an instructor watching an elementary sparring drill.
’Good footwork on the left flank,’ Silas evaluated in his mind, his blue eyes tracking the recruits’ micro-movements. ’Sarah adjusted her weight perfectly during that parry...
Helen’s commands are sharp, she could be a Captain too...
These simple gray-skin goblins can’t even scratch their armor plates.’
BOOM!
BOOM!
The ground shook as the lead eight-foot Hobgoblin shoved past its smaller kin, raising a massive two-hundred-pound spiked iron morningstar high above its head!
"CRAAAAA!" the Hobgoblin roared, bringing the spiked weapon down in a violent whistling arc aimed straight at Helen’s shield.
WHOOOOOOSH!
"Argent Barrier." Aurelia’s serene voice whispered from the backline.
VUUUUUUM...
CLANG!
A pristine glowing shield of translucent white holy fire manifested half an inch above Helen’s iron pauldron.
The Hobgoblin’s massive iron morningstar struck the celestial barrier with the deafening force of a siege catapult yet the holy shield didn’t even ripple.
Instead, the concussive force violently rebounded straight back into the Hobgoblin’s thick wrists, fracturing its carpals with a loud sickening snap.
"GRAAAAAAH!" the giant brute howled in agonizing shock, dropping the morningstar to the floor.
"NOW!
TAKE ITS LEGS!" Helen screamed, seizing the opening.
SLASH-CRUNCH!
Two recruit sword-maidens blurred forward beneath the beast’s guard, their void-iron blades executing synchronized hamstring slices that severed the Hobgoblin’s Achilles tendons like snapping ropes.

The eight-foot titan crashed heavily onto its knees with a booming thud, where Helen stepped forward and drove her spear straight through its throat, ending its life in a single pressurized geyser of black blood!
While the main phalanx systematically butchered the remaining three Hobgoblins and their chaotic retinue, a lone cowardly Cavern Goblin broke away from the main skirmish.
Crouching low on all fours, the three-foot-tall gray runt scrambled around the shadows of a limestone stalagmite, clutching a jagged bone dagger between its filthy claws.
Its yellow eyes locked onto the blue-haired royal maiden standing near Silas.
"Squeeee!" the goblin hissed, lunging out from the shadows directly toward the Princess.
The Princess gasped, her azure eyes widening as the snarling, wart-covered face leaped through the air.
Her instincts screamed at her to retreat, but her mind instantly recalled Silas’s steady words as he guided her to fight while they rode here.
’Plant your foot...
Find your balance and drive through the core.’
SHIK!
The Princess drew her six-inch void-iron dagger from its thigh sheath with a crisp trembling ring of steel.
’Haah...
Calm down...’
She did not tumble backward onto her rear.
She gritted her teeth, stepped firmly into the gravel with her left boot, and lowered her center of gravity.
As the goblin lunged with its bone dagger, the Princess pivoted her torso to the right, letting the rusted bone weapon scrape harmlessly past her white blouse.
SWISH.
"Begone, foul creature of the dark!" the Princess shouted, channeling every ounce of her royal resolve.
She drove the void-iron dagger upward with both hands, plunging the sharp blade straight beneath the goblin’s chin, driving the steel through its palate and clean into its brain.
CRUNCH-SQUELCH!
The goblin’s yellow eyes rolled back into its skull, its body stiffening mid-air before collapsing limply onto the limestone floor at her feet.
"Haaah...
Haah...
Hahh..."
The Princess stood over the slain beast, her chest heaving as she pulled the dagger free and wiped the dark fluid clean against a patch of dry moss.
A breathless, radiant smile broke across her face.
I did it!
Another clean strike!"
She turned around to look for Silas and Aurelia and instantly froze.
The entire cavern was dead silent.
The chaotic horde of sixty Cavern Goblins and four massive Hobgoblins had ceased to exist.
Across the wide limestone chamber, every single beast had been thoroughly slaughtered.
Severed green-gray limbs, shattered iron clubs, and neatly decapitated monster corpses lay scattered across the gravel in neat piles.

The fifteen recruits were already wiping their blades clean with dry cloths, chatting and laughing among themselves like normal young women finishing an afternoon chore, while Aurelia calmly extinguished her floating orb of holy fire.
Standing against the pillar, Silas looked over at the wide-eyed Princess, his blue eyes crinkling with warm effortless amusement as he gave her a thumbs-up.
"Not bad, Princess," Silas chuckled, pushing off the limestone wall.
"Not bad at all."

chapters.title: Chapter 455: A Mine With No Diamonds? [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The chill of Cavern KB-22 clung to the jagged limestone architecture like a physical weight, carrying on its stagnant currents the coppery tang of freshly spilled monster blood and the acrid sulfurous stench of scorched bone and cartilage.
Across the wide uneven expanse of the cavern’s entrance floor, the aftermath of the brief but violent skirmish painted a gruesome picture.
Sixty dispatched Cavern Goblins and four massively mutilated Hobgoblins lay scattered across the jagged shale in broken, unmoving heaps.
Their crude flint knives, jagged bone daggers, and splintered wooden clubs lay discarded harmlessly in the gravel, slick with the dark viscous ichor of their former owners.

Silas reached down from the reinforced leather saddle of Valkyrie, wrapping his broad calloused hands gently but firmly around the Princess’s slender waist to hoist her back up onto the Blessed wolf’s saddle pommel.

The blue-haired royal maiden settled comfortably between his arms, her chest rising and falling in a steady adrenaline-laced rhythm as her porcelain cheeks retained a soft rosy flush from her recent dagger kill.
’My second kill, killing monsters is exhilarating for sure.’
She carefully drew a clean linen oilcloth from her belt pouch, wiping the dark foul-smelling fluid from the thin edge of her void-iron blade with deliberate precision.

Her small fingers trembled slightly with the lingering aftershocks of combat, but she maintained a steady grip, ensuring the metal was pristine before sliding the weapon back into its fitted thigh sheath with a crisp satisfying metallic sound.
Around them, the fifteen recruit maidens moved across the bloodstained floor with disciplined efficiency that spoke volumes of their rigorous training.

They worked in pairs, cleaning their ash-wood spears and steel-rimmed shields, checking leather harness buckles, and ensuring their weapons remained free of the corrosive monster grime that could dull a blade or rot a wooden shaft.

Near the rear rank, Brenda... a young freckled former border-wall soldier who had spent agonizing months surviving on dry, weevil-infested hardtack, bitter well water, and stale salted mutton before joining the Unmovable Wall hesitantly lowered the iron butt of her spear to the limestone bedrock.
"Uh..."𝐟𝕣𝗲𝕖𝕨𝗲𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝗲𝚕.𝗰𝚘𝐦
She looked down at the pile of thick, muscular goblin carcasses heaped before her boots, her stomach giving a phantom rumble born of old desperate habits.
She chewed nervously on her lower lip, glancing side to side before tentatively raising a single gauntleted hand toward Silas.

"Um... Lord Silas?" Brenda called out hesitantly, her voice echoing softly off the high limestone ceiling, instantly drawing the attention of her squadmates. "Are we... are we supposed to field-dress and harvest the meat from these beasts? For the territory larders?"
WHOOSH!
The entire cavern went dead silent.
The only sound was the drip-drip-drip of water falling from a stalactite in the distance.
Helen stopped mid-motion with her whetstone, her mouth parting in sheer, dumbfounded disbelief as she turned her head slowly toward Brenda, looking at the girl as if she had just grown a second head.
Sarah slowly lowered her void-iron arming sword, her eyebrows creeping upward so high they nearly vanished completely into her hairline.
Catelyn froze with a clean roll of bandages in her hands, blinking rapidly, while several other recruit maidens cast looks of soul-deep bewilderment across the chamber.
Even Aurelia, who was calmly brushing a stray speck of ash from the hem of her pristine white robe, paused mid-gesture.
The former Saintess slowly tilted her head, her serene golden eyes blinking in quiet confusion.

"Brenda..." Helen said slowly, her tone caught precariously between utter horror and dry exasperation. "Have you completely lost your mind? Who in the seven realms of creation is desperate enough to eat goblin meat?!"

"It’s rank! It’s absolutely rancid!" Sarah cried out, sticking her tongue out and miming a gag in pure revulsion. "It smells like stagnant swamp runoff mixed with wet dog, and it tastes like sulfurous bile! I would literally rather boil and chew on my own leather boots than put a strip of goblin flesh in my mouth!"
"I-I just thought... s-since we were collecting resources for Blessed Land and meat is meat—" Brenda stammered, her entire face instantly turning a brilliant shade of crimson.
She hastily pulled her hands back, dropping her gaze to her boots and ducking her head in agonizing mortification. "I apologize! Please pretend I never spoke! I’m sorry!"
Silas let out a deep, booming chuckle from atop Valkyrie, the rich warm sound bouncing off the high stone arches and instantly shattering the recruits’ tense awkward silence.

"At ease, Brenda," Silas said, offering her an easy, reassuring smile that immediately eased the tension knotting her shoulders. "There is no need to apologize. Old habits die hard, especially when you’ve been starved on the wall but you don’t have to worry about scavenging scrap meat ever again. In Blessed Land, our kitchens are stocked with wild boar, herb-crusted spirit fowl, savory root vegetables, and fresh river game... We don’t eat toxic cavern pests under my banner. You should know that."
Brenda let out a massive trembling sigh of relief, bowing her head deeply. "Thank you, my Lord... I understand."

"You’re not wrong about the scarcity, though," Silas noted, letting his gaze sweep across the jagged limestone tunnels stretching into the pitch-black subterranean depths ahead. "Aside from a few beasts, our expedition group has barely run into any monsters that can actually be eaten today. It’s been nothing but venomous spiders, parasitic worms, and underground vermin."

"A natural consequence of the deep mountain trenches, Lord Silas," Aurelia murmured gently, stepping up beside Valkyrie with tranquil, ethereal grace. "Creatures dwelling in these dark corridors feed primarily upon mana-tainted moss, cavern vermin, and toxic fungi, rendering their flesh completely unsuitable and often poisonous for mortal consumption."
VUUUUUUM!
With a subtle elegant turn of her slender wrist, Aurelia rekindled the floating orb of incandescent Argent Flame.
The pure white fire rose ten feet into the air, casting a brilliant unwavering daylight radiance that pushed back the oppressive shadows and illuminated the damp, winding tunnel ahead.
"Alright, enough chatter! Form standard search lines!" Helen commanded, clapping her gauntlet against her breastplate to refocus the squad.
She rolled her shoulders and leveled her ash-wood spear. "Keep your spacing tight! Spears front, blades flanking!"
The fifteen recruit maidens immediately fell into a tight overlapping wedge formation, advancing deeper into the winding corridors of Cavern KB-22.
The path sloped downward at a steep angle, twisting past ancient calcium deposits, dry fissure beds, and narrow rock chimneys that whistled with eerie drafts.
Along the way, the dark corners of the cave occasionally writhed with movement.
Three lone straggler goblins... scouts that had avoided the initial slaughter leapt from the rocky shadows, snapping their jagged jaws ferociously and swinging rusted daggers.
"GAK-SKREEE!"
They didn’t even make it within striking distance.
THWACK-SHIK!
Helen and Brenda thrust their spears forward in perfect, piston-like synchronization.
The void-iron tips pierced the goblins’ throats and chests before their feet even touched the ground, pinning them to the limestone walls with violent pressurized bursts of black blood.
SPLAT!
"Clear!" Helen called out, yanking her spear free.
Yet, as they pressed hundreds of yards deeper into the mountain, Silas’s brow furrowed in deep confusion.
He leaned over Valkyrie’s thick neck, his piercing blue eyes scanning the bare limestone walls, the rocky floor, and the dripping ceiling.
There was nothing.
There were no glowing crystalline veins... no rough gemstone deposits and not a single microscopic fleck of raw Mana Diamond shimmered under Aurelia’s holy light.
The walls were nothing but porous brittle gray rock.

’Why the hell is this cavern marked with an X on the map, then?’ Silas thought, his fingers drumming against his leather saddle pommel. ’Thora’s geological surveys and dwarven instincts are rarely wrong. If she noted Mana Diamonds in Sector KB-22, they should be here. Did the goblins mine them all? Did they conceal the deposits? Or is there something else buried deeper inside?’
RUMBLE...

Before his mind could ponder the geological mystery any further, the narrow winding corridor widened abruptly, the ceiling arching upward to reveal a colossal dome-shaped hollow spanning well over a hundred yards wide.
The squad came to an abrupt halt at the cavern threshold.
The sight before them explained exactly why the cavern had been so fiercely guarded at the entrance.
The entire massive chamber had been converted into an entrenched populated goblin settlement.
"CRK!"
"GHEEE!"
"PSSSSHT!"

Clustered across the uneven rock floor were dozens of crude, primitive makeshift huts constructed from stacked limestone boulders, stretched animal pelts, and splintered deadwood branches dragged in from the surface.
Smoldering bone-fires cast erratic, flickering orange shadows against the high ceiling, filling the air with a thick choking haze of smoke.
And occupying the settlement was an entire tribal horde.
Over eighty Cavern Goblins milled about the huts.

A dozen hulking muscle-bound Hobgoblins stood near the center, carrying massive spiked clubs And at the far back of the chamber, lounging atop a massive elevated throne carved from stacked granite blocks, was a Goblin King.
[Target Analyzed: Goblin King (Tier 2)]
The King was a bloated grotesque Tier-2 anomaly standing nearly ten feet tall, its corpulent flabby green-gray torso wrapped in thick, crude plates of scavenged and hammered iron.

Atop its misshapen cranium sat a tarnished brass circlet studded with cracked river stones and stacked directly beside the arms of its throne were two massive boulders weighing several hundred pounds each, clearly meant to be used as primitive artillery.
For a single, agonizingly tense second, the two groups simply stopped and blinked at each other across the vast cavern floor.
BLINK!
The goblins, mid-bite into whatever foul scavenged meat they were chewing, stared at the glowing white orb of holy fire and the armored women standing at their doorstep.
BLINK!
The recruits tightened their grips on their weapons, their eyes locking onto the overwhelming numbers.
The stillness shattered in an instant.
SKREEEEEEE!
GAK-GAK-GAK-GAK!
A cacophony of feral ear-splitting non-human shrieks, guttural roars, and rapid jaw-clicking erupted from the entire goblin horde.
The beasts dropped their food, snatching up stone cleavers, flint axes, and sharpened femurs.
Like a wave of starving locusts, the entire settlement surged forward across the cavern floor, rushing the entrance.
"They’re quite hostile!" Silas called out from the back. He sounded very calm and didn’t even draw his sword. "Squad One! You girls handle it! Sweep and clear the room!"
"UNDERSTOOD!" the girls roared in unison.
BOOM!
The recruit maidens surged forward to meet the horde, their combat boots detonating against the limestone.
Helen spearheaded the front line, her spear flashing with condensed mana.
’Let’s go!’
As the first wave of runts reached her, she executed a brutal low-angle sweep.
WHOOSH!
The heavy ash-wood shaft cracked through the shins of three charging goblins with a sharp echoing sound, shattering their legs instantly.
Before they could even hit the ground, Helen drove her void-iron point straight down through the central beast’s chest.
CRUNCH!
"Left flank, tighten up! Don’t let them surround us!" Sarah yelled.
She ducked smoothly beneath a hurled flint axe, her fluid agility a testament to her endless sparring sessions.
SHING!
Sarah’s void-iron short sword cut a clean blinding silver arc through the smoky air, cleaving a leaping goblin completely in half at the waist.
"Fuu... Exciting..."
She didn’t pause after that... pivoting sharply on her heel, she slammed her heavy iron pommel directly into the snout of another beast trying to bite her thigh.
CLACK-CRUNCH!
"Spears, cycle through! Thrust and retract!" Brenda shouted, finally finding her rhythm and confidence in the heat of battle.
She drove her spear forward in rapid succession, skewering two screeching runts with a pressurized sound before pulling back behind the shield wall.
While the recruit phalanx held the chaotic frontline, the heavy hitters of the vanguard stepped onto the battlefield.
From the center of the formation, Morrighan stepped forward.
The Demonic Caster Hero moved with imposing weight.
’More battles and battles... I don’t mind if I’m fighting for Blessed Land but can’t all these monsters just... die?’
Her long flowing crimson hair whipped behind her like a trail of liquid embers, and her deep molten-gold eyes blazed with terrifying majesty.
The two polished, obsidian-black horns curving from her pale temples began to hum and crackle with a dark violet glow.
CLANK! RATTLE-RATTLE-RATTLE!
"Bind." Morrighan’s deep voice resonated through the cavern, cutting through the screeching of the horde.
She thrust her open palm violently toward the ground.
KRA-CRACK!
The bedrock beneath two massive charging nine-foot-tall Hobgoblins violently fractured.
Four thick, heavy chains forged from pure pitch-black abyssal mana erupted from the stone, wrapping tightly around the Hobgoblins’ thick ankles in an unbreakable vice-like lock.
"GRAAAAAAH?!" the two giant brutes roared in panicked fury, stumbling forward and crashing to their knees as they struggled violently to lift their legs.
But the shadowy chains held them firmly anchored to the floor.
Morrighan didn’t just stand back and cast from afar. Despite her tall, commanding frame, she moved with shocking explosive agility.
VUUUUUUM!
"[Demon’s Resolve]!" she incanted.
Her obsidian horns blazed with blinding violet light as her physical strength, speed, and power doubled in a single instant.
BOOM!
Morrighan detonated the stone beneath her boots, closing the thirty-foot gap in a fraction of a heartbeat.
She closed her right fist, and an inferno of pitch-black suffocating brimstone fire ignited around her armored gauntlet, crackling with superheated demonic fury.
"[Brimstone Punch]!" she roared.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Morrighan drove her fiery fist straight into the chest of the left Hobgoblin.
The concussive impact generated a shockwave that blasted the surrounding goblins forty feet backward.

The Hobgoblin’s heavy scrap-iron chestplate caved inward like wet parchment, its ribs pulverized to dust as the dark brimstone flame detonated inside its torso, blowing a fist-sized crater straight through its back and instantly incinerating its internal organs.
SPLAT-CRACKLE!
Without losing a single ounce of momentum, Morrighan planted her pivot foot, gracefully twisting her slender hips through the air to carry the force of her punch into a spin.
WHOOOOOOSH!
Her heavy, scale-armored spade-tipped tail whipped through the air like a massive swinging steel mace.
THWACK-CRUNCH!

The dense armored tip of her tail smashed directly into the side of the second pinned Hobgoblin’s skull as the force snapped its thick neck at a horrifying violent ninety-degree angle, sending the giant beast crashing lifelessly to the stone in a heap of broken bone.

Brenda let out a massive trembling sigh of relief, bowing her head deeply.
"Thank you, my Lord...
I understand."
"You’re not wrong about the scarcity, though," Silas noted, letting his gaze sweep across the jagged limestone tunnels stretching into the pitch-black subterranean depths ahead.
"Aside from a few beasts, our expedition group has barely run into any monsters that can actually be eaten today.
It’s been nothing but venomous spiders, parasitic worms, and underground vermin."
"A natural consequence of the deep mountain trenches, Lord Silas," Aurelia murmured gently, stepping up beside Valkyrie with tranquil, ethereal grace.

"Creatures dwelling in these dark corridors feed primarily upon mana-tainted moss, cavern vermin, and toxic fungi, rendering their flesh completely unsuitable and often poisonous for mortal consumption."
VUUUUUUM!
With a subtle elegant turn of her slender wrist, Aurelia rekindled the floating orb of incandescent Argent Flame.
The pure white fire rose ten feet into the air, casting a brilliant unwavering daylight radiance that pushed back the oppressive shadows and illuminated the damp, winding tunnel ahead.
"Alright, enough chatter!
Form standard search lines!" Helen commanded, clapping her gauntlet against her breastplate to refocus the squad.
She rolled her shoulders and leveled her ash-wood spear.
"Keep your spacing tight!
Spears front, blades flanking!"
The fifteen recruit maidens immediately fell into a tight overlapping wedge formation, advancing deeper into the winding corridors of Cavern KB-22.
The path sloped downward at a steep angle, twisting past ancient calcium deposits, dry fissure beds, and narrow rock chimneys that whistled with eerie drafts.
Along the way, the dark corners of the cave occasionally writhed with movement.
Three lone straggler goblins... scouts that had avoided the initial slaughter leapt from the rocky shadows, snapping their jagged jaws ferociously and swinging rusted daggers.
"GAK-SKREEE!"
They didn’t even make it within striking distance.
THWACK-SHIK!
Helen and Brenda thrust their spears forward in perfect, piston-like synchronization.
The void-iron tips pierced the goblins’ throats and chests before their feet even touched the ground, pinning them to the limestone walls with violent pressurized bursts of black blood.
SPLAT!
"Clear!" Helen called out, yanking her spear free.
Yet, as they pressed hundreds of yards deeper into the mountain, Silas’s brow furrowed in deep confusion.
He leaned over Valkyrie’s thick neck, his piercing blue eyes scanning the bare limestone walls, the rocky floor, and the dripping ceiling.
There was nothing.
There were no glowing crystalline veins... no rough gemstone deposits and not a single microscopic fleck of raw Mana Diamond shimmered under Aurelia’s holy light.
The walls were nothing but porous brittle gray rock.

’Why the hell is this cavern marked with an X on the map, then?’ Silas thought, his fingers drumming against his leather saddle pommel. ’Thora’s geological surveys and dwarven instincts are rarely wrong.
If she noted Mana Diamonds in Sector KB-22, they should be here.
Did the goblins mine them all?
Did they conceal the deposits?
Or is there something else buried deeper inside?’
RUMBLE...

Before his mind could ponder the geological mystery any further, the narrow winding corridor widened abruptly, the ceiling arching upward to reveal a colossal dome-shaped hollow spanning well over a hundred yards wide.
The squad came to an abrupt halt at the cavern threshold.
The sight before them explained exactly why the cavern had been so fiercely guarded at the entrance.
The entire massive chamber had been converted into an entrenched populated goblin settlement.
"CRK!"
"GHEEE!"
"PSSSSHT!"

Clustered across the uneven rock floor were dozens of crude, primitive makeshift huts constructed from stacked limestone boulders, stretched animal pelts, and splintered deadwood branches dragged in from the surface.
Smoldering bone-fires cast erratic, flickering orange shadows against the high ceiling, filling the air with a thick choking haze of smoke.
And occupying the settlement was an entire tribal horde.
Over eighty Cavern Goblins milled about the huts.

A dozen hulking muscle-bound Hobgoblins stood near the center, carrying massive spiked clubs And at the far back of the chamber, lounging atop a massive elevated throne carved from stacked granite blocks, was a Goblin King.
[Target Analyzed: Goblin King (Tier 2)]
The King was a bloated grotesque Tier-2 anomaly standing nearly ten feet tall, its corpulent flabby green-gray torso wrapped in thick, crude plates of scavenged and hammered iron.

Atop its misshapen cranium sat a tarnished brass circlet studded with cracked river stones and stacked directly beside the arms of its throne were two massive boulders weighing several hundred pounds each, clearly meant to be used as primitive artillery.
For a single, agonizingly tense second, the two groups simply stopped and blinked at each other across the vast cavern floor.
BLINK!
The goblins, mid-bite into whatever foul scavenged meat they were chewing, stared at the glowing white orb of holy fire and the armored women standing at their doorstep.
BLINK!
The recruits tightened their grips on their weapons, their eyes locking onto the overwhelming numbers.
The stillness shattered in an instant.
SKREEEEEEE!
GAK-GAK-GAK-GAK!
A cacophony of feral ear-splitting non-human shrieks, guttural roars, and rapid jaw-clicking erupted from the entire goblin horde.
The beasts dropped their food, snatching up stone cleavers, flint axes, and sharpened femurs.
Like a wave of starving locusts, the entire settlement surged forward across the cavern floor, rushing the entrance.
"They’re quite hostile!" Silas called out from the back.
He sounded very calm and didn’t even draw his sword.
"Squad One!
You girls handle it!
Sweep and clear the room!"
"UNDERSTOOD!" the girls roared in unison.
BOOM!
The recruit maidens surged forward to meet the horde, their combat boots detonating against the limestone.
Helen spearheaded the front line, her spear flashing with condensed mana.
’Let’s go!’
As the first wave of runts reached her, she executed a brutal low-angle sweep.
WHOOSH!
The heavy ash-wood shaft cracked through the shins of three charging goblins with a sharp echoing sound, shattering their legs instantly.
Before they could even hit the ground, Helen drove her void-iron point straight down through the central beast’s chest.
CRUNCH!
"Left flank, tighten up!
Don’t let them surround us!" Sarah yelled.
She ducked smoothly beneath a hurled flint axe, her fluid agility a testament to her endless sparring sessions.
SHING!
Sarah’s void-iron short sword cut a clean blinding silver arc through the smoky air, cleaving a leaping goblin completely in half at the waist.
"Fuu...
Exciting..."
She didn’t pause after that... pivoting sharply on her heel, she slammed her heavy iron pommel directly into the snout of another beast trying to bite her thigh.
CLACK-CRUNCH!
"Spears, cycle through!
Thrust and retract!" Brenda shouted, finally finding her rhythm and confidence in the heat of battle.
She drove her spear forward in rapid succession, skewering two screeching runts with a pressurized sound before pulling back behind the shield wall.
While the recruit phalanx held the chaotic frontline, the heavy hitters of the vanguard stepped onto the battlefield.
From the center of the formation, Morrighan stepped forward.
The Demonic Caster Hero moved with imposing weight.
’More battles and battles...
I don’t mind if I’m fighting for Blessed Land but can’t all these monsters just... die?’
Her long flowing crimson hair whipped behind her like a trail of liquid embers, and her deep molten-gold eyes blazed with terrifying majesty.
The two polished, obsidian-black horns curving from her pale temples began to hum and crackle with a dark violet glow.
CLANK!
RATTLE-RATTLE-RATTLE!
"Bind." Morrighan’s deep voice resonated through the cavern, cutting through the screeching of the horde.
She thrust her open palm violently toward the ground.
KRA-CRACK!
The bedrock beneath two massive charging nine-foot-tall Hobgoblins violently fractured.
Four thick, heavy chains forged from pure pitch-black abyssal mana erupted from the stone, wrapping tightly around the Hobgoblins’ thick ankles in an unbreakable vice-like lock.
"GRAAAAAAH?!" the two giant brutes roared in panicked fury, stumbling forward and crashing to their knees as they struggled violently to lift their legs.
But the shadowy chains held them firmly anchored to the floor.
Morrighan didn’t just stand back and cast from afar.
Despite her tall, commanding frame, she moved with shocking explosive agility.
VUUUUUUM!
"[Demon’s Resolve]!" she incanted.
Her obsidian horns blazed with blinding violet light as her physical strength, speed, and power doubled in a single instant.
BOOM!
Morrighan detonated the stone beneath her boots, closing the thirty-foot gap in a fraction of a heartbeat.
She closed her right fist, and an inferno of pitch-black suffocating brimstone fire ignited around her armored gauntlet, crackling with superheated demonic fury.
"[Brimstone Punch]!" she roared.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Morrighan drove her fiery fist straight into the chest of the left Hobgoblin.
The concussive impact generated a shockwave that blasted the surrounding goblins forty feet backward.

The Hobgoblin’s heavy scrap-iron chestplate caved inward like wet parchment, its ribs pulverized to dust as the dark brimstone flame detonated inside its torso, blowing a fist-sized crater straight through its back and instantly incinerating its internal organs.
SPLAT-CRACKLE!
Without losing a single ounce of momentum, Morrighan planted her pivot foot, gracefully twisting her slender hips through the air to carry the force of her punch into a spin.
WHOOOOOOSH!
Her heavy, scale-armored spade-tipped tail whipped through the air like a massive swinging steel mace.
THWACK-CRUNCH!

The dense armored tip of her tail smashed directly into the side of the second pinned Hobgoblin’s skull as the force snapped its thick neck at a horrifying violent ninety-degree angle, sending the giant beast crashing lifelessly to the stone in a heap of broken bone.

chapters.title: Chapter 456: There’s Actually Diamonds [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: To her right, a feral silver blur detonated across the cavern floor.
WHOOSH!
Lupina had completely dropped to all fours.
The silver-haired demi-human’s wolf ears flattened tightly against her head with her bushy tail whipping wildly behind her for balance.

Her three-inch retractable steel claw gauntlets extended from her knuckles with a metallic shik as a towering ten-foot Hobgoblin armed with a massive iron-spiked tree trunk blocked her path, letting out a deafening earth-shaking roar.
"RAHHHHHHHHHHHHH!!!!"
Lupina’s amber eyes suddenly ignited with a brilliant supernatural sapphire-blue flame.
Deep within her core, her internal mana channels violently expanded, circulating a thick untamed energy through every muscle fiber in her limbs.
The air around her began to distort with raw pressure.
She bared her sharp white fangs, a low growl vibrating in her throat as she whispered a single enigmatic phrase.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Reality seemed to bend and snap around her silhouette.
Lupina did not merely accelerate... she transformed into a frictionless terrifying streak of pure gray-silver destruction.
Moving at a speed completely imperceptible to the naked eye, she shot forward like a living hurricane.
’DIE!
She shot directly through its center of mass.
SHRED-SHRED-SHRED-SHRED!
In less than a single imperceptible fraction of a second, the air shrieked as hundreds of vacuum claw slashes erupted simultaneously across the giant brute’s entire frame.
SPLAT-CRUNCH-POP!
By the time Lupina reappeared twenty feet behind the beast, skidding to a halt on all fours with smoke rising from her steel claws, the ten-foot Hobgoblin had already ceased to exist as a creature.

In an instant, its armor, flesh, and muscle were pulverized to ribbons, and its massive skeleton collapsed into a heap of delicate shattered fragments that looked like broken fish bones scattered across the bloody stone.
The mysterious terrifying surge of 10x power vanished as quickly as it had ignited, her glowing blue eyes fading back to amber as her mana channels settled.
’All of my energy is almost gone...’
Regardless, Lupina didn’t pause for even a second.
SWOOSH!
She flipped effortlessly through the air, executing a tight acrobatic triple spin before landing with both knees slammed firmly onto the shoulders of another charging Hobgoblin.
THUD!
"DIE, YOU UGLY BAG OF ROTTEN FILTH!" Lupina cursed ferociously, her steel claw gauntlets blurring into a frenzied, blinding flurry of strikes.
SLASH-HACK-RIP-TEAR!
Her three-inch steel claws repeatedly tore across the beast’s face, shredding its eyelids, blinding its yellow eyes in a spray of blood, and gouging deep chasms across its jawline.
Before the blinded, screaming beast could even raise its hands to defend itself, Lupina executed a vicious, cross-slashing cleave that severed its head entirely from its shoulders.
SPLAT-THUD!

As the recruit maidens, Morrighan, and Lupina slaughtered the remaining goblin ranks with devastating efficiency, Aurelia made a direct undisturbed beeline straight toward the stone throne at the far end of the chamber.
The ten-foot Goblin King panicked.
Seeing its entire royal guard obliterated in mere seconds, the corpulent monster let out a desperate shriek.
"SKRRRRR-GRAAAAAH!"

The King reached down with its massive flabby arms, lifting one of the three-hundred-pound limestone boulders resting beside its throne. With a violent heave of its bloated shoulders, it hurled the colossal rock through the air straight toward Aurelia’s head.
WHOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
The massive boulder whistled through the smoky air like a falling meteor, carrying enough force to crush a cavalry horse.
Aurelia didn’t even slow her serene gliding stride.
"Haah..."
She casually swayed her upper body three inches to the left, her body fluttering gracefully as she let the giant rock scream harmlessly past her shoulder.
BOOM!
The boulder smashed into the limestone wall behind her, shattering into a thousand powdery fragments that rained down on the cavern floor.
"GAAAK!" the Goblin King roared in terror, hoisting the second three-hundred-pound boulder and hurling it with even greater force.
WHOOOOOOSH!
This time, Aurelia raised her right arm, her slender hand sheathing itself in a thin razor-sharp blade of pure white Argent Flame.
SHING!
With a casual, almost lazy flick of her wrist, she swung the holy fire blade horizontally through the air.
KRA-SHAAAA!
The massive three-hundred-pound boulder was cleanly sliced in half mid-air.
The thermal intensity of the holy fire cauterized the stone as it cut, sending the two heavy halves tumbling harmlessly to her left and right as she strode effortlessly through the center gap.
Aurelia closed the remaining distance in a single fluid step.
The Goblin King desperately swung a massive, jagged iron cleaver downward in a final panicked strike.
SWISH!
Aurelia gracefully stepped inside the beast’s reach, her movement so tranquil and effortless that she appeared to dance across the stone.
She placed the palm of her left hand gently against the center of the King’s bloated iron-plated chest.
"May your corrupt soul return to the ash from whence it crawled," Aurelia murmured with serene finality.
"[Argent Inferno]."
VUUUUUUUM... BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A pillar of blinding holy fire detonated from her palm.

The terrifying heat did not leave behind a single drop of blood or bone. In less than a second, the ten-foot Goblin King, its heavy iron armor, and the very granite blocks of its throne were completely vaporized into a brilliant swirling cloud of sparkling white embers that gently drifted toward the cavern ceiling.
The chamber fell into silence as the chaotic horde of over eighty goblins and their monstrous commanders had been entirely eradicated.
Sitting atop Valkyrie at the entrance of the village, Silas watched the final sparks fade away, resting his golden sword casually over his shoulder.
Beside him, the Princess was bouncing slightly in the saddle, clapping her small hands together with breathless admiration.

"Magnificent! Truly magnificent!" the Princess cheered brightly, her blue eyes sparkling as she looked at the warrior maidens across the battlefield. "Lady Morrighan’s shadowy chains were breathtaking, and Lady Lupina’s speed was unmatched!"
"Well fought, girls," Silas called out, offering them a proud encouraging smile. "Clean, efficient execution across all ranks."
Morrighan stood tall amidst the carnage, her heavy spade-tipped tail settling calmly behind her and a touched warmth reached her molten-gold eyes at the Princess’s praise.
Lupina, standing atop a pile of goblin corpses, wiped her steel claws against her leather pants, puffing out her chest with fierce wolfish pride.
Silas looked around the wide, empty limestone chamber, his eyes sweeping over the crude stone huts and the scorched remains of the throne.

"Well," Silas remarked, stroking his chin with a slight disappointed sigh. "We weren’t able to find a single exposed crystal vein in this entire chamber, either. So this could mean that excavation and deep tunneling will need to be done to reach the actual deposits. And that means calling in Brida and the other heavy hitters, but that will have to wait until tomorrow."
While Silas spoke, the Princess casually shifted her weight, leaning her small frame against the uneven limestone wall bordering the left side of the cavern entrance.
CLICK! KRRRRRR-RUMBLE!
Beneath the delicate accidental pressure of her back, a hidden hollow section of the limestone wall suddenly gave way with an ancient grinding of stone!

"Eep!" the Princess gasped, stumbling backward and catching herself against Valkyrie’s pommel as a three-foot section of the rock face slid smoothly into the earth, revealing a concealed narrow passage tunnel leading deep into the mountain’s core.
And shining out from the depths of the hidden tunnel—
GLIMMER! SHIMMER!
A breathtaking kaleidoscope of vibrant, multi-colored light instantly illuminated the dark cavern.

Embedded densely along the walls, ceiling, and floor of the secret passage were hundreds upon hundreds of raw, uncut Mana Diamonds... glowing in brilliant pulsing hues of cerulean blue, radiant emerald and royal amethyst, radiating with rich concentrated mana.
Silas blinked, staring into the glittering tunnel as a wide, triumphant grin spread across his face.
"Well... look at that," Silas chuckled warmly, turning to look at the blue-haired royal maiden in his arms. "Looks like we found the real treasure after all."
He leaned down slightly, meeting her gaze with genuine appreciation.
"Thank you, Princess. Your keen eye just saved our mining corps three whole days of excavation work."
The Princess’s azure eyes widened, and a deep radiant crimson blush instantly swept over her delicate cheeks all the way to the tips of her ears.
She quickly looked down at her lap, her fingers shyly twisting the fabric of her leggings with a small blissful smile curling her lips as the light of the Mana Diamonds washed over them.
"You– you’re welcome."
The narrow, concealed passage connecting the goblin settlement to the hidden depths of the mountain was barely wide enough for two people to walk shoulder-to-shoulder.
The air inside the fissure was immediately different... gone was the suffocating sulfurous stench of the goblin bone-fires, replaced by a crisp coolness that smelled weird.
’Fuck.’
Silas quickly realized the logistical constraint of the tunnel.
Valkyrie, standing nearly as tall as a draft horse with her broad muscular shoulders, could not simply trot through the jagged limestone gap without scraping her sides raw.
With a smooth, fluid motion, Silas swung his leg over the saddle and dropped down to the stone floor.
He reached up, placing his hands firmly around the Princess’s slender waist, and lifted her down from the Blessed wolf’s back, setting her gently onto her boots.
"Valkyrie, you’ll have to squeeze through carefully," Silas instructed, patting the dire wolf’s snout. "Keep your head low."
The Blessed wolf let out a soft compliant chuff, lowering her broad head and carefully picking her way through the narrow opening, her claws clicking methodically against the bedrock.
Silas followed right behind her, keeping the Princess close, with Aurelia, Helen, and the rest of the recruits filing into the tunnel in a single organized column.
For the first thirty paces, the passage was completely cloaked in darkness, illuminated only by the floating orb of Aurelia’s Argent Flame.
But as they rounded a sharp, ninety-degree bend in the limestone, a breathtaking impossible radiance washed over them, completely drowning out the celestial fire.
"By the gods..." Sarah whispered, her void-iron sword drooping toward the floor.
"It’s... it’s an underground sky," Brenda breathed, her eyes wide with awe.
The tunnel opened up into a sprawling cavernous geode.
The walls, the uneven floor, and the sweeping vaulted ceiling were entirely encrusted with thousands upon thousands of raw uncut Mana Diamonds.
But what made the chamber truly spectacular was not just the sheer volume of the precious stones... it was the light.

High above, near the apex of the cavern ceiling, dozens of jagged, naturally formed fissures pierced straight through the mountain’s crust. Brilliant unfiltered shafts of midday sunlight poured down through the cracks.
As the raw sunlight struck the exposed crystalline facets of the Mana Diamonds, the light was refracted, scattering across the chamber in a prismatic kaleidoscope.
"This is where that light came from..."
Swirling beams of cerulean blue, radiant emerald, and royal amethyst danced across the girls’ armor, painting the entire cavern in a shifting, breathing tapestry of multi-colored brilliance.
The mana in the air was so dense and pure that it felt like standing in a gentle warm river.
The Princess stepped forward, completely mesmerized.
Her azure eyes reflected the swirling lights as she approached a cluster of cerulean diamonds protruding from the cavern wall.
"It is utterly beautiful," the Princess murmured, her voice filled with quiet wonder.
She reached out with her small hands, gripping a loose, fist-sized blue diamond that was only partially wedged into the brittle limestone.
With a soft grunt of effort, she wiggled the stone back and forth until...
CRACK!
It snapped free from the bedrock. She held the heavy glowing gemstone up to the sunlight, watching the internal facets shimmer with trapped mana.
She turned back to Silas, her brow furrowing in genuine, innocent confusion.

"Lord Silas... if this entire cavern is filled with such priceless, magnificent treasures, why are we not mining it all out right this very moment? Surely we can gather enough to fill our dimensional storage!"
The recruits blinked, looking between the Princess, the glowing walls, and their own empty hands.
Several of them instinctively tightened their grips on their spears, clearly entertaining the idea of chipping away at the walls.
Silas leaned against Valkyrie’s flank, crossing his arms over his chest as a warm amused chuckle rumbled in his throat.

"It’s a fair question, Princess," Silas replied, his voice carrying effortlessly through the echoing chamber. "But the answer comes down to pure logistics and the integrity of the ore. We are currently deployed as a combat unit, not an excavation one."

He pointed a finger at Helen’s spear. "If we tried to mine these diamonds right now, what would we use? Your void-iron swords? Your ash-wood spears? If you strike a raw Mana Diamond with a combat edge at the wrong angle, you won’t extract it... you’ll shatter the crystal matrix, completely destroying its internal mana conductivity and rendering it totally worthless."
The girls exchanged slightly embarrassed glances, slowly lowering their weapons.

"Furthermore," Silas continued, pushing off the wolf’s flank and pacing slowly through the prismatic light. "proper mining requires heavy specialized equipment. Thora’s runic pickaxes and structural bracing to ensure the cavern doesn’t collapse on our heads while we dig... If we wait and bring the heavy detachment tomorrow, and the day after, we’ll have the proper time to meticulously extract, catalog, and organize the ores."

And shining out from the depths of the hidden tunnel—
GLIMMER!
SHIMMER!
A breathtaking kaleidoscope of vibrant, multi-colored light instantly illuminated the dark cavern.

Embedded densely along the walls, ceiling, and floor of the secret passage were hundreds upon hundreds of raw, uncut Mana Diamonds... glowing in brilliant pulsing hues of cerulean blue, radiant emerald and royal amethyst, radiating with rich concentrated mana.
Silas blinked, staring into the glittering tunnel as a wide, triumphant grin spread across his face.
"Well... look at that," Silas chuckled warmly, turning to look at the blue-haired royal maiden in his arms.
"Looks like we found the real treasure after all."
He leaned down slightly, meeting her gaze with genuine appreciation.
"Thank you, Princess.
Your keen eye just saved our mining corps three whole days of excavation work."
The Princess’s azure eyes widened, and a deep radiant crimson blush instantly swept over her delicate cheeks all the way to the tips of her ears.
She quickly looked down at her lap, her fingers shyly twisting the fabric of her leggings with a small blissful smile curling her lips as the light of the Mana Diamonds washed over them.
"You– you’re welcome."
The narrow, concealed passage connecting the goblin settlement to the hidden depths of the mountain was barely wide enough for two people to walk shoulder-to-shoulder.
The air inside the fissure was immediately different... gone was the suffocating sulfurous stench of the goblin bone-fires, replaced by a crisp coolness that smelled weird.
’Fuck.’
Silas quickly realized the logistical constraint of the tunnel.
Valkyrie, standing nearly as tall as a draft horse with her broad muscular shoulders, could not simply trot through the jagged limestone gap without scraping her sides raw.
With a smooth, fluid motion, Silas swung his leg over the saddle and dropped down to the stone floor.
He reached up, placing his hands firmly around the Princess’s slender waist, and lifted her down from the Blessed wolf’s back, setting her gently onto her boots.
"Valkyrie, you’ll have to squeeze through carefully," Silas instructed, patting the dire wolf’s snout.
"Keep your head low."
The Blessed wolf let out a soft compliant chuff, lowering her broad head and carefully picking her way through the narrow opening, her claws clicking methodically against the bedrock.
Silas followed right behind her, keeping the Princess close, with Aurelia, Helen, and the rest of the recruits filing into the tunnel in a single organized column.
For the first thirty paces, the passage was completely cloaked in darkness, illuminated only by the floating orb of Aurelia’s Argent Flame.
But as they rounded a sharp, ninety-degree bend in the limestone, a breathtaking impossible radiance washed over them, completely drowning out the celestial fire.
"By the gods..." Sarah whispered, her void-iron sword drooping toward the floor.
"It’s... it’s an underground sky," Brenda breathed, her eyes wide with awe.
The tunnel opened up into a sprawling cavernous geode.
The walls, the uneven floor, and the sweeping vaulted ceiling were entirely encrusted with thousands upon thousands of raw uncut Mana Diamonds.
But what made the chamber truly spectacular was not just the sheer volume of the precious stones... it was the light.
High above, near the apex of the cavern ceiling, dozens of jagged, naturally formed fissures pierced straight through the mountain’s crust.
Brilliant unfiltered shafts of midday sunlight poured down through the cracks.
As the raw sunlight struck the exposed crystalline facets of the Mana Diamonds, the light was refracted, scattering across the chamber in a prismatic kaleidoscope.
"This is where that light came from..."
Swirling beams of cerulean blue, radiant emerald, and royal amethyst danced across the girls’ armor, painting the entire cavern in a shifting, breathing tapestry of multi-colored brilliance.
The mana in the air was so dense and pure that it felt like standing in a gentle warm river.
The Princess stepped forward, completely mesmerized.
Her azure eyes reflected the swirling lights as she approached a cluster of cerulean diamonds protruding from the cavern wall.
"It is utterly beautiful," the Princess murmured, her voice filled with quiet wonder.
She reached out with her small hands, gripping a loose, fist-sized blue diamond that was only partially wedged into the brittle limestone.
With a soft grunt of effort, she wiggled the stone back and forth until...
CRACK!
It snapped free from the bedrock.
She held the heavy glowing gemstone up to the sunlight, watching the internal facets shimmer with trapped mana.
She turned back to Silas, her brow furrowing in genuine, innocent confusion.
"Lord Silas... if this entire cavern is filled with such priceless, magnificent treasures, why are we not mining it all out right this very moment?
Surely we can gather enough to fill our dimensional storage!"
The recruits blinked, looking between the Princess, the glowing walls, and their own empty hands.
Several of them instinctively tightened their grips on their spears, clearly entertaining the idea of chipping away at the walls.
Silas leaned against Valkyrie’s flank, crossing his arms over his chest as a warm amused chuckle rumbled in his throat.
"It’s a fair question, Princess," Silas replied, his voice carrying effortlessly through the echoing chamber.
"But the answer comes down to pure logistics and the integrity of the ore.
We are currently deployed as a combat unit, not an excavation one."
He pointed a finger at Helen’s spear.
"If we tried to mine these diamonds right now, what would we use?
Your void-iron swords?
Your ash-wood spears?

If you strike a raw Mana Diamond with a combat edge at the wrong angle, you won’t extract it... you’ll shatter the crystal matrix, completely destroying its internal mana conductivity and rendering it totally worthless."
The girls exchanged slightly embarrassed glances, slowly lowering their weapons.
"Furthermore," Silas continued, pushing off the wolf’s flank and pacing slowly through the prismatic light.
"proper mining requires heavy specialized equipment.
Thora’s runic pickaxes and structural bracing to ensure the cavern doesn’t collapse on our heads while we dig...
If we wait and bring the heavy detachment tomorrow, and the day after, we’ll have the proper time to meticulously extract, catalog, and organize the ores."

chapters.title: Chapter 457: Help From Reina [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas paused, picking up a loose thumb-sized emerald diamond from the floor and tossing it casually into the air, catching it with a sharp clack.

"We need to carefully separate the haul," Silas explained, his newly awakened merchant-like instincts bleeding into his voice. "We have to determine which flawless diamonds we keep to power Thora’s foundry and reinforce Blessed Land’s defensive capabilities, and which slightly flawed stones we export to the markets to liquidate for raw capital which I will invest back in the Territory some more."
While he spoke, Silas’s internal thoughts shifted to the digital ledger sitting quietly in his mind.

’I may have seventy-five million sitting securely in my bank account right now...’ Silas thought, his blue eyes narrowing slightly as he looked at the sprawling wealth around him. ’To a mortal man on Earth, that’s generational wealth. You could retire to a private island and never work another day in your life but here? In a world of gods, empires, and territorial warfare? Seventy-five million is good but even back at the auction... It’s not enough. If I want to build a true unassailable empire that bends the very cosmos to its knees, I need more. I need billions. I need an economy so massive it can swallow rival countries whole.’
The Umbral Basin was going to sponsor that lifestyle...
"Spread out and explore the perimeter!" Helen ordered, snapping Silas out of his ambitious reverie. "Do not strike the walls, but report any structural anomalies or secondary tunnels!"
The women scattered through the sprawling glittering chamber, their boots crunching softly against the crystalline gravel.
The awe of the environment made them temporarily forget the exhaustion of the morning’s slaughter.
They pointed at massive geodes, marveled at the swirling colors, and traced their fingers over the smooth, glassy surfaces of the unmined wealth.
"Lord Silas! Lady Aurelia! Over here!"
The shout came from deep within the eastern alcove of the cavern.
Silas and Aurelia immediately moved toward the voice, navigating through a cluster of towering calcified stalagmites.
They found three recruits standing at the threshold of a sunken, bowl-shaped depression in the cavern floor.
This section of the cave was completely different. The chaotic, multi-colored light faded, replaced by an intense aura.
"Look at this..." Sarah whispered, pointing downward.
It was a grove, but instead of plants, it was grown entirely from crystal.
The walls and floor here were coated in a bizarre, almost organic formation of striking blood-red crystals and pure, milky-white diamonds.
The red and white formations twisted around each other like petrified vines, pulsing with a slow heartbeat-like luminescence that made the air feel heavy and metallic on the tongue.
Silas stopped at the edge of the depression, his instincts flaring sharply.
The mana density in this specific alcove was astronomically higher than the rest of the cavern.
"Step back from the edge, girls. All of you," Silas commanded, his tone dropping its previous warmth, replaced by a firm authoritative edge.
The maidens immediately complied, taking several large steps backward, their hands resting nervously on their hilts.
"Is something wrong, my Lord?" Helen asked, her eyes darting around the shadows. "Are there more monsters hiding down there?"

"Not monsters in the traditional sense," Silas explained, his blue eyes carefully studying the pulsing red and white formations. "Be careful where you step in environments like this. When elemental mana becomes this dense, this stagnant, and this crystallized over centuries... it tends to gain sentience. This is exactly the kind of breeding ground where elemental spirits manifest."
"Spirits?" Brenda echoed, shivering slightly despite her heavy armor.

"Yes," Silas nodded. "And uncontracted spirits born in isolation are notoriously volatile. If you disturb their physical anchors... these red and white crystals... they won’t fight you with iron clubs like the goblins. They will simply attempt to invert your internal mana channels, boiling your blood or freezing your lungs from the inside out."
The recruits visibly swallowed hard, their previous awe instantly evaporating into a cold respect for the dangers of the world.
Even the Princess took a cautious step closer to Silas, her small hand reaching out to lightly grip the edge of his dark tunic for reassurance.
Though they didn’t fully comprehend the complex metaphysical mechanics of spirit manifestation, Silas’s warning was enough to completely calm their adventurous urges.
Silas stood in silence for a long moment, studying the eerie pulsing red and white grove.
’These aren’t standard Mana Diamonds. The elemental affinity here is mutated. Fire and pure light, perhaps? Or blood and bone?’
He mentally marked the exact coordinates of the alcove.
"We will leave this specific grove untouched for now. When we return with the rest, I’ll bring Eluned. Her botanical and spiritual authority will be necessary to safely untangle this mess."
He turned back to the squad.
"Alright, we’ve confirmed the payload. Time to pull back. Everyone, back to the surface!"
Ten minutes later, the entire squad emerged from the jagged limestone maw of Cavern KB-22, stepping back out into the rugged gray shale terrain of the Umbral Basin.
The afternoon air had drastically shifted.
The cool mountain breeze that had accompanied their midday lunch had completely vanished, replaced by a biting, violent chill that seemed to seep directly through the seams of the girls’ armor.
Silas pulled Valkyrie forward by her reins, stopping a few dozen yards away from the cavern entrance.
He looked back at the gaping, thirty-foot-wide hole carved into the cliffside.

"Ah, we have to secure it, too," Silas muttered, running a hand through his dark hair. "We just slaughtered the predators of this sector. If we leave this entrance wide open overnight, a new pack of wandering beasts or rogue anomalies will just wander right in and make a nest out of our newly discovered diamond mine."
Aurelia stepped forward, her white robes fluttering in the bitter wind.
"Lord Silas, if you wish, I can weave a grand barrier of Argent Flame across the threshold. It will incinerate any creature foolish enough to attempt entry before tomorrow morning."

"Save your mana reserves for the march back, Aurelia," Silas smiled gently, raising a hand to stop her. "A fiery barrier acts as a beacon. In the Umbral Basin, a massive wall of holy fire might just attract Tier-3 or Tier-4 beasts curious about the light. We need something more subtle, like something that completely removes the entrance from the equation."
Silas didn’t climb onto Valkyrie. Instead, he stepped forward, planting his boots firmly onto the gray shale.
He closed his eyes for a fraction of a second, tapping into the divine reservoir of his Gold Core.
VUUUUUUM!
His aura flared as a faint golden halo illuminating his silhouette but this time, he didn’t call upon his flames.
He reached for the anchoring weight of the Earth Element.
Silas raised his right boot and stomped down against the bedrock with staggering concussive force.
KRA-BOOOOOOM!
The entire cliffside shuddered violently, as if struck by a earthquake!
The girls stumbled, dropping into low stances to keep their balance as the ground groaned in agonizing protest.
KRRRRRR-RUMBLE! KRRRR-CRACK!
From the deep bedrock beneath the cavern entrance, colossal slabs of solid dense limestone and dark granite violently erupted from the earth.
The massive stone plates slid upward with the grinding shriek of shifting tectonic plates, interlocking and weaving together like the teeth of a gargantuan gear.

In less than ten seconds, the entire thirty-foot-wide cavern entrance was completely sealed shut by an impenetrable seamless wall of solid mountain rock, blending perfectly into the surrounding cliffside.
To a passing beast, Cavern KB-22 simply no longer existed.
"Impressive as always, my Lord," Helen praised, watching the dust settle.
Silas vaulted smoothly back into Valkyrie’s saddle, lifting the Princess up in front of him.
But as he settled his grip on the reins, a tiny freezing droplet of moisture struck his cheek.
He looked up at the sky.
The perpetual hazy morning of the Umbral Basin had darkened considerably.
From the heavy, bruised gray clouds rolling rapidly over the jagged mountain peaks, the first delicate, icy flakes of snow began to fall.
"Snow?" Sarah muttered, shivering violently as a gust of freezing wind whipped past her exposed neck. "At this time? Are you joking?"

"The climate in the Umbral Basin is dictated by chaotic mana currents, not natural seasons," Silas explained calmly, though she too pulled her white robes tighter around her shoulders. "It can shift from a balmy breeze to a lethal blizzard in a matter of hours... Maybe you all didn’t notice it so much since you were so busy."
A chorus of miserable chattering complaints rippled through the ranks of the recruits.
They were dressed in lightweight sky-iron cuirasses and leather tunics meant for high-mobility combat, not sub-zero winter survival.
CHIME! CHIME! CHIME!
A sharp, metallic ringing cut through the whistling wind.
Helen raised her left arm, tapping the brass face of the timer strapped to her gauntlet.
"Lord Silas! The midday operational window has expired!" Helen reported, her breath pluming in a cloud of white mist. "We need to begin the return march to Blessed Land immediately!"

"You heard her!" Silas called out, raising his voice over the rising howl of the wind. "Double-time! Start heading back to Blessed Land! Keep your formations tight so no one gets lost in the whiteout!"
Valkyrie let out a low rumbling growl, her paws crunching into the rapidly accumulating frost as she galloped forward.
Silas held her to a moderate, loping pace, ensuring he didn’t outrun the infantry.
The snow intensified with terrifying speed.
Within ten minutes, the light dusting transformed into a swirling blinding blizzard.
The wind shrieked through the deadwood trees, driving the freezing snow laterally into the girls’ faces.
The Princess huddled tightly against Silas’s broad chest, burying her face into the warm, thick fur of Valkyrie’s mane to escape the biting wind.
Her small hands gripped his tunic with desperate strength as her body trembled slightly against the cold.
Silas looked back over his shoulder.
The fifteen recruits were trudging through the deepening snowdrifts, their heads bowed against the gale, their boots slipping on the icy shale.
They were keeping up through stubborn willpower, but the physical toll of the morning’s endless combat combined with the freezing slog was rapidly draining their stamina.

’This is inefficient,’ Silas thought, his brow furrowing as he shielded his eyes from the snow. ’Our infantry is strong, but mobility is a massive bottleneck. If only we had more mounts to transport them during these rapid weather shifts...’
HOWOOOOOOOOOOL!
A triumphant howl pierced straight through the shrieking blizzard, echoing from the snow-covered treeline to their right.
Silas pulled Valkyrie to a halt, his hand instinctively dropping to the hilt of his golden sword.
The recruits instantly formed a defensive circle, leveling their spears into the blinding whiteout.
From the swirling snow, a muscular silhouette broke through the treeline.
It was Luna.
The Blessed Wolf bounded through the snowdrifts with effortless, joyful power.

Riding securely on her broad back were Vala and Reina. Both women were covered in a light dusting of snow, their cheeks flushed red from the cold, but their eyes were shining with fierce undeniable triumph.
Vala’s dark hair whipped wildly in the wind, her hand resting confidently on her void-iron blade, while Reina held the reins with an exhausted but victorious grin plastered across her face.
"Lord Silas!" Reina called out, waving her arm enthusiastically as Luna trotted up beside Valkyrie.

"Reina. Vala," Silas smiled warmly, relief washing over him as he saw his hidden blade and scout completely unharmed. "Excellent timing. Did you manage to track down any new Umbral Wolves for the cavalry corps?"
Both women nodded vigorously.
Reina turned in the saddle, letting out a sharp, commanding whistle that cut through the gale.
From the snow-choked treeline, the shadows themselves seemed to detach and move. One by one, feral shapes padded out into the open.
There were forty-six of them.
They were Umbral Wolves... both scarred males and lethal females.
"Good work."
They were roughly the size of heavy warhorses, their fur a jagged uneven mix of midnight black and ash gray.
Their yellow eyes glowed faintly in the blizzard, and their muzzles were pulled back in low submissive pants.
They looked wild and untamed, lacking the majestic divine coats of Luna and Valkyrie.
Silas let out a genuine sigh of relief with tension bleeding out of his shoulders.
"Forty-six of them," Reina reported proudly, patting Luna’s neck. "We had to clear out a rather nasty parasitic hive-mind, but the next pack which we found is now subdued and ready for integration."
Silas looked over the feral pack.
’Well I can establish contracts with them once we get to Blessed Land.’

"Incredible work, both of you," Silas praised, his eyes shifting back to his shivering infantry squad. "Reina, ask the pack alpha if my girls behind me can ride them... They’re freezing, and we need to accelerate our march."
Silas could use the rune but he had initially planned to build their stamina this way.
Reina nodded, leaning forward and speaking a series of low clicks and chuffs to Luna.
Luna turned her massive head toward the largest heavily scarred gray male in the Umbral pack, letting out a sharp authoritative bark.
The gray alpha lowered its head, its ears flattening submissively, and offered a low rumbling nod.
"They’ve agreed, my Lord!" Reina translated happily. "They recognize Luna as their pack leader, and by extension, they yield to your authority!"
"Mount up, girls!" Silas ordered. "Two to a wolf! Let’s get out of this storm!"
The recruits didn’t need to be told twice.
With eager, shivering sighs of relief, they hurried toward the beasts.
The Umbral Wolves knelt in the snow, allowing the armored women to vault onto their broad, muscular backs.
The thick coarse fur provided immediate, desperately needed insulation against the biting wind.
’I’m sure the other girls can manage or they’ve already arrived...’𝒻𝓇𝑒𝘦𝘸𝑒𝒷𝓃ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝒸ℴ𝘮
Aurelia stepped gracefully toward a massive one-eyed gray wolf near the rear of the pack.
