Did you manage to track down any new Umbral Wolves for the cavalry corps?"
Both women nodded vigorously.
Reina turned in the saddle, letting out a sharp, commanding whistle that cut through the gale.
From the snow-choked treeline, the shadows themselves seemed to detach and move.
One by one, feral shapes padded out into the open.
There were forty-six of them.
They were Umbral Wolves... both scarred males and lethal females.
"Good work."
They were roughly the size of heavy warhorses, their fur a jagged uneven mix of midnight black and ash gray.
Their yellow eyes glowed faintly in the blizzard, and their muzzles were pulled back in low submissive pants.
They looked wild and untamed, lacking the majestic divine coats of Luna and Valkyrie.
Silas let out a genuine sigh of relief with tension bleeding out of his shoulders.
"Forty-six of them," Reina reported proudly, patting Luna’s neck.
"We had to clear out a rather nasty parasitic hive-mind, but the next pack which we found is now subdued and ready for integration."
Silas looked over the feral pack.
’Well I can establish contracts with them once we get to Blessed Land.’
"Incredible work, both of you," Silas praised, his eyes shifting back to his shivering infantry squad.
"Reina, ask the pack alpha if my girls behind me can ride them...
They’re freezing, and we need to accelerate our march."
Silas could use the rune but he had initially planned to build their stamina this way.
Reina nodded, leaning forward and speaking a series of low clicks and chuffs to Luna.
Luna turned her massive head toward the largest heavily scarred gray male in the Umbral pack, letting out a sharp authoritative bark.
The gray alpha lowered its head, its ears flattening submissively, and offered a low rumbling nod.
"They’ve agreed, my Lord!" Reina translated happily.
"They recognize Luna as their pack leader, and by extension, they yield to your authority!"
"Mount up, girls!" Silas ordered.
"Two to a wolf!
Let’s get out of this storm!"
The recruits didn’t need to be told twice.
With eager, shivering sighs of relief, they hurried toward the beasts.
The Umbral Wolves knelt in the snow, allowing the armored women to vault onto their broad, muscular backs.
The thick coarse fur provided immediate, desperately needed insulation against the biting wind.
’I’m sure the other girls can manage or they’ve already arrived...’𝒻𝓇𝑒𝘦𝘸𝑒𝒷𝓃ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝒸ℴ𝘮
Aurelia stepped gracefully toward a massive one-eyed gray wolf near the rear of the pack.

chapters.title: Chapter 458: The Goddess And The Bird [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: As she reached out her delicate hand, the beast’s instincts flared.
"Gra!"
It didn’t recognize the divine scent of the Saintess... The wolf bared its yellow fangs, letting out a deep vibrating snarl that shook the snow from its mane; however Aurelia didn’t flinch.
’I’ve dealt with worse...’
She didn’t draw back her hand, nor did she reach for her weapon.
"Haah..."
Aurelia simply stopped, lowered her chin slightly, and opened her golden eyes wide.
For a single fleeting second, the terrifying weight of the Argent Flame flared within her pupils... a fraction of divine authority that carried the silent promise of incineration.
’There won’t be anything left of you.’
The wolf instantly clamped its jaws shut.
A high-pitched, pathetic whimper escaped its throat as it immediately dropped onto its belly in the snow, rolling slightly onto its side to expose its throat in an act of unhesitating submission.
"Good boy," Aurelia murmured with a serene angelic smile, gracefully sweeping her leg aside as she mounted the beast side-saddle, sitting with the perfect posture of royalty.
"Alright, the cavalry is formed!" Silas shouted, drawing his golden sword and pointing it directly toward the southern horizon. "Full gallop! Next stop, the Steel Weave walls of Blessed Land!"
"HOO-AH!"
With a thunderous earth-shaking roar of over fifty massive paws hitting the permafrost simultaneously, the newly formed cavalry corps exploded into a dead sprint.
They tore through the blizzard like a unified unstoppable spearhead, leaving a massive trench of churning snow in their wake as they charged back toward the safety and warmth of their home.
High above the treeline, clinging desperately to the frozen, swaying branch of a deadwood pine, a very peculiar bird watched the cavalry depart.
It was not a normal avian creature of the basin.
Its feathers were completely devoid of color, resembling jagged shards of dark obsidian, and it possessed a strange elongated beak that curved like a wicked scythe.
Its beady intelligent black eyes tracked Silas and his army until they completely disappeared into the whiteout.
The bird tilted its crested head, letting out a low clicking sound that resembled grinding gears.
Then, with a sudden, silent snap of its wings, the bird launched itself into the freezing updrafts.
It did not fly south toward the plains.
It banked sharply against the gale, flying like a silent obsidian rocket directly north, heading toward the deepest and most treacherous depths of the Umbral Basin.
As the bird soared over the jagged mountain peaks, the atmospheric pressure began to drastically change.
The chaotic blizzard below gave way to an area of suffocating stillness.
This was the forbidden sector of the Basin.
In these lightless valleys and plunging canyons, several monsters of Tier-3, Tier-4, and perhaps even rumors of ancient Tier-5 calamities slumbered.
The aura radiating from the deep trenches below was enough to crush a mortal man’s heart.
The bird had never actually encountered these titans, and it had no desire to.
It kept its altitude high, navigating through a narrow plunging crevice tucked between two massive cliff faces.
It dove into the underground fissure.
The descent felt endless.
The light faded entirely, replaced by a strange ethereal blue luminescence emanating from the walls.
The temperature plummeted past the point of freezing, dropping to an absolute zero that defied normal thermodynamics.
The bird finally flared its wings, coming in for a landing on a wide platform of solid permafrost.
SKRRR-SLIP!
The bird’s talons found absolutely no purchase.
It skidded comically across the frictionless ice, tumbling beak-over-tail feathers before crashing into a jagged ice stalagmite with a pathetic thud.
Shaking its head dizzily, the bird scrambled upright, ruffling its obsidian feathers, and looked upward.
Towering before the tiny avian was a massive ancient glacier that filled the entire chamber.
And suspended dead-center within the impenetrable block of absolute ice... was a woman.
She was completely entombed, frozen from her toes to her collarbone.
Only her head and the very tops of her pale shoulders were exposed from the flat surface of the ice wall.

Long, matted, midnight-black hair cascaded over her face, obscuring her features, caked in centuries of unmelting frost. She appeared entirely lifeless like a tragic statue forgotten by time and gods alike.
The bird hopped forward, clicking its beak nervously.
"Squawk! Squawk! Krrr-caw!"
For a long, terrifying moment, nothing happened then, the midnight-black hair shifted.
The woman’s eyelids fluttered, cracking the layer of frost binding her lashes.
She slowly opened her eyes.
Beneath the matted hair, her irises flared with an overwhelming divine green hue.
KRA-RUMBLE!
The instant her eyes opened, the entire chamber violently trembled. The shockwave of her awakening aura cracked the surrounding stalagmites and caused the bedrock to groan in agonizing submission.
Yet... the glacier entombing her body did not crack.
It did not melt and it did not yield even a single millimeter either. The ice binding her was a prison of conceptual cold, forged to hold a being of apocalyptic power.
The woman drew a slow ragged breath, the freezing air whistling through her dry cracked lips.
"Gah!"
She coughed violently, a wet rattling sound that echoed through the chamber, before slowly tilting her chin down to glare at the shivering bird.

"Did you say..." the woman rasped, her voice dry yet carrying a resonance that made the bird’s hollow bones vibrate in terror. "...there is a being... currently marching through this Basin... that possesses enough power to shatter this conceptual ice... and free me from this prison?"
The bird flapped its wings frantically, nodding its crested head in rapid succession.
"Squawk! Squawk! Caw!"
The woman stared at the bird, her divine green eyes narrowing into sharp terrifying slits of rage.
She inhaled deeply, drawing a massive pocket of compressed air into her lungs.
PTOO!
The woman forcefully spat a concentrated hyper-pressurized glob of saliva straight at the bird.
FWHOOOOOOOSH!
The spit shot through the air with the aerodynamic velocity and concussive force of an artillery shell.
The bird let out a terrified shriek, throwing itself flat against the permafrost barely a microsecond before the spit-rocket screamed over its head.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!

The saliva slammed into the cavern wall behind the bird, detonating with enough force to blast a ten-foot-wide crater into the solid bedrock, showering the shivering avian in crushed stone and ice shards.
"WHY THE FUCK ARE YOU STILL SITTING HERE, THEN?!" the woman roared, her voice exploding with furious divine volume that threatened to collapse the ceiling! "GO BRING THE BEING TO ME! YOU BIRD BRAIN!"
"Squawk! Squawk! Krrr-caw!"
The bird flapped its dark wings frantically, hopping backward on the frictionless ice and clicking its scythe-like beak as it desperately tried to communicate the peril of the situation.
It mimed a slashing motion with its wings, puffing out its chest and pointing upward toward the surface.
The woman’s blinding green eyes blinked slowly, the thick frost clinging to her eyelashes cracking with the subtle movement.
Her anger simmered down into sharp curiosity.
"The being would kill you if you came close?" the woman rasped, her voice dry and echoing with the weight of centuries, translating the bird’s frantic gestures with ease.

She tilted her chin a fraction of a millimeter within her icy collar. "He travels with an army, commands authority, and slaughters anomalies without hesitation... So, it is a Lord. A Sovereign who commands a territory if you will."
"Squawk!" The bird nodded its crested head vigorously, letting out a rapid succession of clicking sounds that vibrated through the freezing air.
"And what is the name of this territory he commands?" the woman asked, her green eyes narrowing slightly.
The bird puffed its chest out, letting out a melodic and surprisingly soft series of trills and whistles that contrasted sharply with its usual deep caws.
"Blessed Land?" the woman repeated, the words tasting strange and foreign on her cracked parched lips.
A faint and almost imperceptible smirk touched the corner of her mouth, momentarily softening her terrifying aura.
"Blessed Land... In a dark, miserable place like the Umbral Basin, a name like that sounds rather nice."
She closed her eyes for a moment, the divine green glow fading slightly as she let out a long foggy breath that immediately crystallized in the air.
"You said he is a Lord, right?" she asked, opening her eyes once more.
The bird nodded immediately.

"Then the solution is simple," the woman stated matter-of-factly, her voice echoing off the frozen stalactites. "A Lord is inherently greedy... They constantly seek power, resources, and formidable combatants to expand their borders. He would be immensely more interested in me if I simply agreed to submit to his authority and become a part of his territory."
She let out a dry, rattling chuckle that shook the foundations of the bedrock.

"I truly do not mind. I have been sealed in this frozen prison for centuries. My pride eroded away a long time ago. As long as this Lord can provide me with a warm hearth, a soft bed, and some genuinely good food... specifically roasted meat... I am perfectly fine with bending the knee. Tell him I will become his Hero."
She looked down at the obsidian bird, her eyes flashing with renewed impatience.
"Well? What are you waiting for? Fly to the surface and relay my terms to him immediately!"
The bird did not move.
Instead, it stood firmly on the permafrost, shivering slightly as it looked up at her, its beady black eyes blinking in complete silence.

"Did you not hear me, you useless pile of feathers?!" the woman complained, her voice rising in pitch as her divine aura flared once more, causing the ice chamber to tremble. "Go! Fly! Bring him here before he marches out of the Basin entirely, or I swear upon the heavens I will pluck every single feather from your body and roast you over a spit the moment I break free!"
"Krrr-caw! Squawk!"

The bird frantically hopped in a circle, squawking loudly and tapping its beak against its own chest, then pointing a wing at the woman, and finally dragging a talon across its throat in a dramatic, universally understood gesture of execution.
The woman’s green eyes widened slightly as the realization struck her.
"Ah..." she muttered, her anger evaporating into genuine, sudden dread.
What the bird was saying was true.
She could understand the avian creature because of her unique divine affinity with beasts.
But that did not mean this human Lord would be able to understand a single squawk.

To a Lord commanding an army in a hostile environment, a strange obsidian bird flying directly at him and squawking aggressively would not look like a messenger... it would look like a Tier-2 anomaly initiating an ambush.

"He... he wouldn’t understand a word you’re saying," the woman realized, a cold sweat breaking out across her frozen forehead. "He would see you as a threat. He would draw his blade and slice you out of the sky before you could even land... and then he would march away, leaving me down here for another five hundred years."
A deep sense of panic settled into her chest.
"Squawk?" The bird tilted its head, miming a writing motion with its talon against the ice.
"A note?" the woman asked, her eyes lighting up with desperate hope. "Yes! A written note! He is a human Lord... he can read! That is a brilliant suggestion! Bring me some paper and ink, quickly!"
The bird merely shrugged its wings, looking at her with a blank uncomprehending stare.
...It had absolutely no idea what paper or ink was.
However, it quickly turned around, waddling over to a pile of loose rubble near the edge of the cavern.
It pecked around for a moment before returning with a large and perfectly smooth slate of dark gray stone clasped in its beak.
It dropped the flat stone tablet onto the ice at the base of the glacier with a heavy clack.
"Good enough," the woman praised the bird, her voice trembling with excitement. "You are a remarkably clever creature.. Now, take a sharp rock and carve exactly what I dictate into that tablet!"
She cleared her dry throat, her divine green eyes glowing with sincerity as she began to dictate her plea for salvation.

"Write this," she commanded. "Dear Lord of Blessed Land, I am in urgent need of your help. I have been sealed for centuries in this exact position deep within the Umbral Basin, and you are the only one that possesses the power to free me. After you shatter this ice and free me, you can have me. I will gladly submit and allow you to add me to your collection of Heroes, as I am quite special. You could call me a Goddess of Beasts..."
She paused, licking her dry cracked lips as a loud embarrassing rumble echoed from her frozen stomach.
"...Please be quick. And please, bring meat."
She let out a long satisfied sigh, incredibly proud of her diplomatic composition.
"There," she smiled, looking down at the base of the glacier. "That should perfectly convey my value and my urgency. Have you finished carving the text?"

chapters.title: Chapter 459: Promotion [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She looked down at the obsidian bird.
The bird was simply standing on top of the smooth stone tablet, staring up at her. It slowly blinked its beady black eyes, looking at its own feathery wings, and then looking back at her.
"Squawk."
The woman’s smile slowly slipped from her face.
She stared at the bird’s wings... Wings that completely lacked hands, fingers, or opposable thumbs.
"Do you..." the woman whispered, her voice cracking with soul-crushing despair. "...Do you even know how to write?"
The bird shook its crested head.
The divine Goddess of Beasts closed her eyes, letting her head fall backward against the freezing ice with a heavy hollow thud.
A long agonizing groan escaped her lips, echoing through the vast empty tomb.
"It’s going to take a while..." she whimpered miserably to the empty cavern. "Maybe a few more years... maybe a few more centuries..."
The howling blizzard tore across the jagged shale of the Umbral Basin, transforming the perpetual twilight into a chaotic expanse of swirling white.
WHOOOOOOSH!
Tearing through the heart of the storm was a thundering cavalry formation.
At the vanguard, Valkyrie and Luna shattered the snowdrifts with their broad muscular chests, kicking up massive rooster tails of frost as they sprinted at a breakneck gallop.
Behind them, forty-six massive Umbral Wolves followed in perfect synchronized pursuit, carrying the armored recruit maidens of Blessed Land’s expeditionary force.
Silas leaned low over Valkyrie’s neck, his dark tunic flapping violently in the gale as he wrapped his thick cloak tightly around the shivering Princess huddled in front of him.
Through the blinding whiteout, an imposing silhouette began to materialize.
Rising into the stormy sky, completely unbothered by the freezing winds, were the towering Steel Weave walls of Blessed Land.
The metallic fortifications gleamed with a warm mana that seemed to push back the very storm itself.
As they closed the final hundred yards, Silas could see the bustling activity along the high battlements.
Standing near the central heavy ballista, wrapped in a thick, fur-lined cloak over her crisp leather archery gear, was Elara.
The sharp-eyed archer squinted through the falling snow, her hand resting cautiously on her longbow, before her eyes widened in recognition.
A beaming smile broke across Elara’s face. She threw both of her arms into the air, waving enthusiastically down at the approaching cavalry.
Silas chuckled, the freezing wind stinging his cheeks as he raised a hand and waved back.
As they breached the outer perimeter of the territory, Silas’s senses instantly reconnected with the massive sprawling network of his domain.
"Haah..."

He felt the radiant energy of the Spirit Trees and, most distinctly, he sensed the powerful, familiar mana signatures of Tasmin, Eluned, as well as Brida already safely within the walls, along with the resting auras of their respective squads.
’We were the last ones, huh?’ Silas thought, a warm sense of satisfaction blooming in his chest.
He didn’t mind as the expedition had been an overwhelming success across all fronts.
"OPEN THE GATES!" Elara’s voice boomed down from the battlements, amplified by a wind spell.
KRRRRRR-CLANK! BOOM!
The colossal Steel Weave gates groaned, the heavy locking mechanisms retracting with a deafening metallic screech as the massive doors swung inward.
Valkyrie didn’t slow down.

She leaped over the threshold, her paws hitting the pristine manicured cobblestones of the territory. Luna and the forty-six Umbral Wolves flooded in right behind her, their claws clattering against the stone as the entire squad officially crossed back into Blessed Land.
The instant the final wolf crossed the threshold—
BOOM! CLANG!
The massive gates slammed shut, sealing perfectly into the reinforced wall.
The change in atmosphere was instantaneous and jarring.
Outside the walls, the Umbral Basin was a frozen chaotic hellscape but the moment they entered Blessed Land, the biting, violent wind completely died.

The territory was still experiencing the snowfall... thick, beautiful white flakes gently drifting down from the sky but the climate control generated by the towering Spirit Trees completely neutralized the freezing temperatures.
The air was clean and invigorated with rich soothing life-mana. It was a picturesque peaceful winter wonderland, devoid of the lethal frostbite of the wilderness.

’Much better to have a snowstorm inside the territory instead of outside,’ Silas sighed contentedly, watching the tension completely melt away from the recruits’ shoulders as they sat up straighter in their saddles.
They navigated at a slow, comfortable trot through the winding, snow-dusted paths lined with towering Spirit Trees.
The glowing leaves of the trees cast a warm light that reflected off the fresh snow, illuminating the path toward the central Keep.
As they arrived at the sprawling, open courtyard in front of the Keep, Silas gently pulled back on the reins.
Valkyrie came to a smooth halt.
Silas vaulted off the saddle, landing lightly on the cobblestones.
He reached up, grasping the Princess by the waist and setting her down gently.
The moment his boots hit the ground, Valkyrie immediately turned her head, affectionately swiping her large wet tongue directly across Silas’s cheek.
SLURP!
"Alright, alright, good girl," Silas laughed, wiping the wolf saliva from his jaw as he patted her thick neck. "Go get some rest. You earned it today..."
Valkyrie let out a happy chuff, turning and padding away toward the Beast Pavilion, her tail wagging proudly.
Across the courtyard, the fifteen recruit maidens, Aurelia, Vala, and Reina all dismounted from their respective wolves.
The arrival of the massive cavalry unit had not gone unnoticed.

Dozens of women from the other squads who had already bathed, changed into warm, comfortable casual clothes, and were enjoying the afternoon rest spilled out into the snowy courtyard to greet the final returning unit.
Reina stepped forward, holding the reins of the Blessed Wolf as she offered Silas a crisp respectful salute.

"Lord Silas, I will personally escort this pack to the Beast Pavilion and ensure they are properly settled into the enclosures," Reina reported, her tone professional. "If there isn’t enough space for all forty-six, I will talk with you. Once they are fed and rested, and it is time for you to form the Contracts to evolve them, I will call for you."
"Excellent work today, Reina," Silas nodded approvingly. "Get them settled and get some rest yourself."
Reina bowed her head and turned, whistling sharply to command the massive pack of feral Umbral Wolves to follow her toward the eastern sector of the territory.
As she walked past the gathering crowd of Blessed Land women, a wave of shocked murmurs rippled through the onlookers.

"By the gods... forty-six of them?" one of the vanguard knights gasped, leaning over the wooden railing of a nearby barracks porch. "That’s more than three times the size of the last pack she brought in!"
"Our cavalry corps is going to be massive!" another woman cheered.
A few of the more seasoned battle-hardened women leaning against the armory walls exchanged wicked teasing grins as Reina walked past them.

"Look at our little Beast Tamer working overtime," a tall spear-woman teased loudly, her voice dripping with playful mockery. "Bringing in forty-six wolves in a single afternoon? You sure are putting in a lot of effort, Reina. What’s the goal here? Trying to rack up enough merit points to get dicked down by the Lord tonight?"
"Oooooh!" the surrounding women jeered, bursting into a chorus of raucous unladylike laughter.
Reina froze mid-step.
A volcanic crimson blush instantly exploded across her face, turning her cheeks, ears, and neck a brilliant shade of scarlet.
She whipped her head around, glaring at the teasing women with wide mortified eyes.

"S-SHUT UP!" Reina shrieked, her voice cracking in embarrassment as she hastily grabbed Luna’s reins and practically sprinted toward the Beast Pavilion, desperate to escape the relentless mockery of her sisters-in-arms. "THAT IS NOT WHY I DID IT!"
Silas watched her flee, shaking his head with an amused grin before his gaze drifted across the snowy courtyard.
Standing near the edge of the gathering was Vala.
The raven-haired woman had her dark cloak wrapped tightly around her slender frame.
As the chaotic chatter of the women filled the air, Vala’s dark piercing eyes locked directly onto Silas’s.
There were no words exchanged as there didn’t need to be.
Silas offered her a slow, deeply approving nod, acknowledging the terrifying exponential growth she had achieved on the battlefield today.
’She can come see me later too...’
Vala’s lips curled into a barely perceptible smirk of pride. She returned the nod, turning on her heel and moving toward the warmth of the inner sanctum.
With the wolves dispersed, only all of the recruits remained standing in the center of the snowy courtyard.
They stood in a perfect disciplined line, their ash-wood spears held proudly at their sides, their void-iron swords cleaned and sheathed.

Despite the freezing snow gathering on their shoulders and the heavy exhaustion weighing down their limbs, every single one of them stood with their heads held high, their eyes locked onto Silas with burning devotion.
Silas stepped forward, the snow crunching softly beneath his boots.
He swept his sovereign gaze across the women, his blue eyes looking very proud.

"You girls marched into the dark today," Silas began, his deep voice carrying clearly over the gentle rustle of the falling snow. "You faced so many different kinds of monsters, however you fought with discipline... you fought with courage and most importantly... you fought for each other, and you all came back alive."
He paused, letting the weight of his words settle over them.

"When you arrived in Blessed Land, you wore the title of ’recruit.’ A title given to you by a broken wall that threw you into the meat grinder without a second thought." Silas’s voice hardened slightly, imbued with authority. "But today, you proved that you are no longer recruits. You can be the backbone of my empire."
A collective breathless silence hung over the maidens.
"As of this moment," Silas declared, a brilliant proud smile breaking across his face. "You are officially recognized as full-fledged Soldiers of Blessed Land!"
"YEAAAAAH!"
The courtyard erupted.
The women broke formation, throwing their arms into the air in a deafening unified cheer of pure joy.
Brenda burst into tears, covering her face as Sarah tackled her into a massive, spinning hug.
Helen threw her head back and laughed, thrusting her ash-wood spear triumphantly toward the snowy sky.
This was good... They were not disposable fodder for the Unmovable Wall... they were cherished respected warriors of a Lord who had beaten their former Lord.

"Get to the Barracks!" Silas called out over their cheering, waving his hand toward the massive, warmly lit wooden halls in the distance. "Strip off that armor, hit the hot baths, and get yourselves clean! The kitchens are already preparing a massive feast in your honor tonight! Eat until you pass out!"

"THANK YOU, LORD SILAS!" the girls roared in unison, bowing deeply before breaking into a disorganized joyous sprint toward the Barracks, shoving and laughing with each other like children rushing toward a warm hearth.
Silas watched them go, a deep sense of fulfillment warming his chest against the winter chill.
He turned back toward the Keep. The Princess and Aurelia were waiting patiently for him near the massive oak doors.

"Well," Silas sighed softly, rolling his broad shoulders as the adrenaline of the expedition finally began to fade, replaced by the creeping ache of physical exhaustion. "I’m really tired but I can’t rest just yet. I need to go down to the forge and meet with Thora to discuss the excavation logistics for that Mana Diamond cavern we found."
"You must take care not to overexert yourself, Lord Silas," Aurelia murmured gently, her golden eyes filled with concern. "Even a Lord’s vitality requires proper restoration."
"I shall assist you, Lord Silas!" the Princess chimed in brightly, practically bouncing on the balls of her feet as she walked beside him up the stone steps.

The royal maiden was still riding the euphoric high of her first real taste of combat. "If Lady Thora requires a detailed layout of the tunnels, I can draw a perfect map from memory! After all, I am a seasoned warrior now! I executed two entire creatures today with flawless precision!"
"You did great, Princess," Silas chuckled, reaching out to affectionately ruffle her blue hair, making her puff out her cheeks in a cute proud pout. "You’re a natural-born killer."
’It’s still strange that she’s older than me.’
They reached the top of the stone steps, stopping directly in front of the massive iron-banded oak doors of the central Keep.
Silas reached for the heavy iron ring handle.
Before his fingers could even graze the metal, the heavy doors violently swung outward with a loud whoosh, nearly smacking him in the face.
Silas took a quick half-step backward, his brow furrowing in surprise.
Standing perfectly framed in the doorway, blocking the entrance to his own Keep, were two women.
The first was a strikingly beautiful woman with raven-black hair falling sharply to her shoulders.
She wore a sleek high-collared dark tunic, and her piercing stormy gray eyes were currently narrowed into a fierce agitated glare.
Clenched tightly between her teeth was a lit, expensive-looking cigar with a thin trail of blue smoke curling aggressively into the snowy air.
’She got a new one?’
Clinging tightly to her left arm, burying her face affectionately into the black-haired woman’s shoulder, was a stunningly beautiful Hero with flowing liquid-silver hair and a slender delicate frame.
It was Evelyn and her loyal Hero, Elm.

chapters.title: Chapter 460: Aeli Is High [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Both women stared directly at Silas, their expressions carrying an unmistakable frown.
Silas blinked, dropping his hand from the door handle. "Uh... what’s up?"
Evelyn took the cigar from her lips, blowing a puff of smoke into the cold air.
Her eyes were sharp, carrying the commanding weight of a fellow Lord.
"We need to have a very serious talk, Silas," Evelyn said, her voice low and dangerous. "Something came up and I need to know exactly what you—"
Evelyn’s voice completely died in her throat.
Her stormy gray eyes drifted past Silas’s broad shoulders and locked onto the blue haired woman standing just a few feet behind him.
Evelyn froze.
Her entire body went rigid a the lit cigar slipped from her fingers, tumbling silently through the air and landing in the fresh snow with a soft extinguishing hiss.
The Princess blinked, tilting her head slightly as she looked back at the imposing black-haired woman blocking the doorway.
At first, the Princess didn’t think much of her.
She assumed she was simply another one of Silas’s formidable commanders, perhaps someone in charge of the Keep’s internal logistics.
But then, the Princess’s bright azure eyes drifted slightly to the left.
She looked at the silver-haired Hero clinging so desperately to the black-haired woman’s arm.
The Princess was a royal, yes, but she was also a sheltered woman with an incredible amount of free time.
And during that free time, she had been an incredibly avid dedicated follower of the LordTube streaming network.
She knew the faces, the personalities, and the intricate dynamics of the top-ranking Lords.
The Princess stared at the silver hair and she recognized that face. It was Elm.
And Elm, as the entire digital world knew, was notoriously reclusive.
She had not appeared on a single public broadcast in months.
The only time the world had even seen her magic recently was when her signature four leaf clover spell had been violently unleashed across the battlefield during the Lord War against Blessed Land.
Elm was obsessively loyal to only one person in the entire cosmos... A notoriously smart Lord who was known for smoking sometimes.
The Princess looked at Elm, who was clinging to the arm of a black-haired woman with a cigar in her mouth.
The gears in the Princess’s brilliant brain clicked together with frictionless perfection.
The Princess gasped, her hands flying up to cover her mouth as her azure eyes widened to the size of dinner plates.
She pointed a trembling, delicate finger directly at Evelyn’s face.
"You..." the Princess exclaimed, her voice ringing out crystal clear across the snowy courtyard. "You’re Lord Sky!"
SILENCE.
The cold winter wind suddenly felt completely devoid of sound.
Evelyn’s face drained of all color, turning as pale as the snow beneath her boots. Her stormy gray eyes dilated in pure panic.
’Fuck.’ Evelyn thought, the single word echoing through the hollow terrified cavern of her mind.
Her meticulously crafted secret identity, the disguise she had maintained for so long had just been effortlessly shattered by a blue-haired Princess of all people in the span of three seconds.
Evelyn slowly turned her head, her panicked gray eyes locking onto Silas.
Silas stood perfectly still on the stone steps.
Slowly, a dark smug wicked smirk spread across Silas’s handsome face.
His blue eyes glinted with the dangerous amusement of a Lord who had just been handed the ultimate trump card.

’My secret identity as Vespera was revealed to this woman...’ Silas thought, his smirk widening into a full devilish grin as he stared directly into Evelyn’s terrified eyes. ’Did you really think I wouldn’t eventually find a way to reveal yours?’
Evelyn’s expression trembled violently.
The overwhelming wave of rage and profound embarrassment crashing through her system was astronomical as her fists clenched so tightly her knuckles turned white.
Looking at the incredibly punchable smirk plastered across Silas Graves’s face, Evelyn had only one coherent thought left in her mind.
She really... really wanted to kick him square in the balls...
’I hate you.’
Even though a volcanic eruption of rage was currently boiling just beneath the surface of her skin, Evelyn managed to catch herself.
Her stormy gray eyes flared with a pressurized intensity, but she forced her clenched jaw to relax.
The crushed unlit cigar in her hand was quietly tucked away into her pocket.

She took a slow, deep breath, smoothing out the front of her sleek dark tunic, and completely locked down the panicked aura of Evelyn, replacing it with the haughty untouchable confidence of Lord Sky.
She took a step forward, her boots clicking sharply against the stone as she marched directly past Silas, her shoulder brushing heavily against his.
"If you and I are going to have a talk about this," Evelyn muttered, her voice dropping into a low dangerous tone meant only for his ears. "come to my room later. We’ll make a proper date out of it."
Without waiting for his response, Evelyn stormed off down the corridor, the silver-haired Elm scurrying faithfully right behind her.
Silas stood on the Keep’s front steps, watching her retreating back until she completely disappeared around the corner.
An amused smirk tugged at the corner of his mouth.
He turned his head, looking down at the blue-haired royal woman standing beside him.
The Princess still had both hands clamped firmly over her mouth, her azure eyes wide with the lingering shock of her massive discovery.
"Princess," Silas said. "You are not to expose Evelyn’s identity to anyone. Understood?"
The Princess didn’t try to bargain and she didn’t ask for a favor in return.
She instantly dropped her hands and nodded her head with frantic obedience.
"My lips are entirely sealed, Lord Silas!" the Princess swore, crossing her heart with a delicate finger. "I swear upon my royal blood, Lord Sky’s identity is safe with me!"
"Good," Silas nodded, pushing open the heavy oak doors. "Come on inside. Let’s get out of this cold."
Silas, the Princess, and Aurelia stepped out of the freezing snowy courtyard and crossed the threshold into the main Living Room of the Keep.
The heavy doors clicked shut behind them, instantly cutting off the howling wind and replacing it with the warm crackling ambiance of the massive stone hearth blazing at the far end of the room.
But the comforting atmosphere was instantly shattered by the absurdity of the scene playing out in front of them.
Silas froze dead in his tracks.
"What the fuck is going on?" Silas whispered.
Lying completely sprawled out across the massive velvet-cushioned couch to their left was Morwenna.

The fierce Pirate Queen was unapologetically naked. Her tanned, athletic limbs were splayed in every direction, one leg hanging off the edge of the cushions, her chest rising and falling in a deep unconscious rhythm.
And directly across from her, occupying the opposite velvet couch, was Thor.
The literal Goddess of Thunder was in the exact same state.
She was completely nude, her breathtakingly muscular physique fully exposed to the warm air of the Keep.
Her divine weapon, Mjolnir, had been carelessly dropped onto the floor with its heavy Uru-metal head denting the polished oak floorboards.
Both women were dead to the world, snoring softly.
Before Silas could even process the nightmare of how Morwenna or even Thor... had ended up stripped and unconscious in the middle of the living room, a rustling sound caught his attention.
Crouching low behind a potted Spirit Fern near the edge of the couches was Eluned.
The Goddess was giggling silently to herself, her golden-green eyes sparkling with pure mischief.
Clutched firmly in her hands was a sleek camera, it was the same one as before.
Moving with the stealth of a highly trained assassin, Eluned slinked out from behind the fern.
She crept up right next to the unconscious naked Pirate Queen, holding the camera up and framing the perfect compromising shot.
CLICK-FLASH!
A blinding burst of white light illuminated the living room.
Morwenna let out a low irritated groan in her sleep, shifting her weight slightly, but she didn’t wake up.
The camera whirred mechanically, spitting out a freshly printed picture from its bottom slot.

Eluned snatched the photo from the air, letting out a high-pitched, victorious giggle, and instantly bolted for the central staircase with her bare feet slapping rapidly against the wood as she fled the crime scene before the Pirate Queen could wake up and murder her.
"Kekekekeke~"
The Princess and Aurelia stood completely frozen near the doorway, blinking in confusion.
"Lady Thor?!" the Princess suddenly gasped, completely ignoring the absurdity of the nudity as she rushed forward.
She dropped to her knees beside the Goddess of Thunder, reaching out with her small hands to shake Thor’s muscular bare shoulder. "Thor, you must wake up! You are exposed in the main hall!"
Thor didn’t even twitch. A small line of drool escaped the corner of the Thunder Goddess’s mouth as she continued to snore.
"It won’t work!" a sweet and incredibly cheerful voice chimed from above them.
SWOOSH!
Dropping directly from the second-floor balcony with the grace of a falling leaf, Aeli landed perfectly in the center of the living room.
The woman’s vibrant blond hair bounced around her shoulders, and her bright eyes were crinkled into a sweet smile.
"Aeli?" Silas asked, rubbing his temples. "Care to explain why I have two naked women passed out in my living room?"

"Oh, it’s simple, Lord Silas!" Aeli said, clasping her hands neatly behind her back. "They finished battling the first round where nobody won and then decided to walk around the Territory naked and then challenge themselves outside while naked!"
Aeli leaned forward, whispering conspiratorially as if sharing a fun secret.

"So... I spiked their post-battle protein shakes with a highly concentrated dose of Eluned’s special sleeping herbs! They crashed instantly! They are going to be knocked out cold for at least another six or seven hours... and I might have taken some weird ones too."
Silas visibly trembled.
The casual cheerful way Aeli admitted to effortlessly drugging a Pirate Queen and a literal Goddess of Thunder sent a sharp terrifying chill straight down his spine.
’This girl’s skills are far too advanced...’
She was becoming a second Eluned!
"Don’t worry, Lord Silas!" Aeli beamed, noticing his slight shudder.
She walked over, patting his arm affectionately. "I would never, ever drug you! Or any of our new friends, for that matter!"
Aeli turned her attention to the doorway, her bright eyes locking onto the serene form of Aurelia.
VUUUM!
In a fraction of a millisecond, Aeli vanished from Silas’s side and appeared directly behind Aurelia.
’And not to mention, she’s high too...’
She wrapped her arms around the Saintess’s waist in a tight affectionate hug, resting her chin on Aurelia’s shoulder.

"You must be the new girl!" Aeli chirped, ignoring the slight widening of Aurelia’s golden eyes at the speed of the movement. "Welcome properly to Blessed Land! We are going to be the best of friends!"
Aeli then spun around, pointing a finger directly at the blue-haired royal woman still kneeling next to Thor.

"And you too, Princess!" Aeli grinned. "Lord Silas reported you’re probably just a temporary guest until your kingdom is sorted out, but that doesn’t matter to me! As long as you are under this roof, we are all sisters! And as your new big sister, it is my duty to give you both the grand tour of the Keep!"
Aeli looked over her shoulder, batting her eyelashes innocently at Silas. "May I borrow them, my Lord?"
Silas let out a long, exhausted sigh, waving his hand in permission. "Go ahead, Aeli. Show them around."
"Yay!" Aeli cheered.
She grabbed Aurelia by the wrist, grabbed the Princess by the collar of her armor, and effortlessly dragged both of the bewildered women toward the central staircase.
Before she disappeared up the steps, Aeli paused, turning back to shoot Silas a slow wink.
’I’ve got them covered, Master... Enjoy yourself.’
Silas stared at the empty staircase as the giggling faded into the upper halls.
’That girl definitely needs a reward for her services later...’ Silas thought, shaking his head slowly. ’But as of right now, I just want to calm down and process today’s haul.’
The Keep was finally quiet, save for the crackling of the hearth and the deep synchronized snores of the two naked warriors.
Silas walked further into the living room, stopping between the two couches.
He looked down at Morwenna, her tanned skin glowing warmly in the firelight then, he slowly turned his head to look at Thor.
Silas was a Lord of immense willpower, but he was still a mortal man at his core.
And the sight of the Norse Goddess in all her unclad glory was staggering.
Her chest was massive, her waist carved with thick functional muscle, and her hips flared into incredibly soft sweeping curves that contrasted wildly with her terrifying strength.
’Her chest sure is big...’ Silas thought, his eyes tracing the divine architecture of her physique. ’And her body is undeniably curvy...’
He stared for exactly three seconds before forcing his gaze up to the ceiling.

sentences.text: Both women stared directly at Silas, their expressions carrying an unmistakable frown.
Silas blinked, dropping his hand from the door handle.
"Uh... what’s up?"
Evelyn took the cigar from her lips, blowing a puff of smoke into the cold air.
Her eyes were sharp, carrying the commanding weight of a fellow Lord.
"We need to have a very serious talk, Silas," Evelyn said, her voice low and dangerous.
"Something came up and I need to know exactly what you—"
Evelyn’s voice completely died in her throat.
Her stormy gray eyes drifted past Silas’s broad shoulders and locked onto the blue haired woman standing just a few feet behind him.
Evelyn froze.
Her entire body went rigid a the lit cigar slipped from her fingers, tumbling silently through the air and landing in the fresh snow with a soft extinguishing hiss.
The Princess blinked, tilting her head slightly as she looked back at the imposing black-haired woman blocking the doorway.
At first, the Princess didn’t think much of her.
She assumed she was simply another one of Silas’s formidable commanders, perhaps someone in charge of the Keep’s internal logistics.
But then, the Princess’s bright azure eyes drifted slightly to the left.
She looked at the silver-haired Hero clinging so desperately to the black-haired woman’s arm.
The Princess was a royal, yes, but she was also a sheltered woman with an incredible amount of free time.
And during that free time, she had been an incredibly avid dedicated follower of the LordTube streaming network.
She knew the faces, the personalities, and the intricate dynamics of the top-ranking Lords.
The Princess stared at the silver hair and she recognized that face.
It was Elm.
And Elm, as the entire digital world knew, was notoriously reclusive.
She had not appeared on a single public broadcast in months.
The only time the world had even seen her magic recently was when her signature four leaf clover spell had been violently unleashed across the battlefield during the Lord War against Blessed Land.
Elm was obsessively loyal to only one person in the entire cosmos...
A notoriously smart Lord who was known for smoking sometimes.
The Princess looked at Elm, who was clinging to the arm of a black-haired woman with a cigar in her mouth.
The gears in the Princess’s brilliant brain clicked together with frictionless perfection.
The Princess gasped, her hands flying up to cover her mouth as her azure eyes widened to the size of dinner plates.
She pointed a trembling, delicate finger directly at Evelyn’s face.
"You..." the Princess exclaimed, her voice ringing out crystal clear across the snowy courtyard.
"You’re Lord Sky!"
SILENCE.
The cold winter wind suddenly felt completely devoid of sound.
Evelyn’s face drained of all color, turning as pale as the snow beneath her boots.
Her stormy gray eyes dilated in pure panic.
’Fuck.’ Evelyn thought, the single word echoing through the hollow terrified cavern of her mind.
Her meticulously crafted secret identity, the disguise she had maintained for so long had just been effortlessly shattered by a blue-haired Princess of all people in the span of three seconds.
Evelyn slowly turned her head, her panicked gray eyes locking onto Silas.
Silas stood perfectly still on the stone steps.
Slowly, a dark smug wicked smirk spread across Silas’s handsome face.
His blue eyes glinted with the dangerous amusement of a Lord who had just been handed the ultimate trump card.

’My secret identity as Vespera was revealed to this woman...’ Silas thought, his smirk widening into a full devilish grin as he stared directly into Evelyn’s terrified eyes. ’Did you really think I wouldn’t eventually find a way to reveal yours?’
Evelyn’s expression trembled violently.
The overwhelming wave of rage and profound embarrassment crashing through her system was astronomical as her fists clenched so tightly her knuckles turned white.
Looking at the incredibly punchable smirk plastered across Silas Graves’s face, Evelyn had only one coherent thought left in her mind.
She really... really wanted to kick him square in the balls...
’I hate you.’
Even though a volcanic eruption of rage was currently boiling just beneath the surface of her skin, Evelyn managed to catch herself.
Her stormy gray eyes flared with a pressurized intensity, but she forced her clenched jaw to relax.
The crushed unlit cigar in her hand was quietly tucked away into her pocket.

She took a slow, deep breath, smoothing out the front of her sleek dark tunic, and completely locked down the panicked aura of Evelyn, replacing it with the haughty untouchable confidence of Lord Sky.
She took a step forward, her boots clicking sharply against the stone as she marched directly past Silas, her shoulder brushing heavily against his.
"If you and I are going to have a talk about this," Evelyn muttered, her voice dropping into a low dangerous tone meant only for his ears.
"come to my room later.
We’ll make a proper date out of it."
Without waiting for his response, Evelyn stormed off down the corridor, the silver-haired Elm scurrying faithfully right behind her.
Silas stood on the Keep’s front steps, watching her retreating back until she completely disappeared around the corner.
An amused smirk tugged at the corner of his mouth.
He turned his head, looking down at the blue-haired royal woman standing beside him.
The Princess still had both hands clamped firmly over her mouth, her azure eyes wide with the lingering shock of her massive discovery.
"Princess," Silas said.
"You are not to expose Evelyn’s identity to anyone.
Understood?"
The Princess didn’t try to bargain and she didn’t ask for a favor in return.
She instantly dropped her hands and nodded her head with frantic obedience.
"My lips are entirely sealed, Lord Silas!" the Princess swore, crossing her heart with a delicate finger.
"I swear upon my royal blood, Lord Sky’s identity is safe with me!"
"Good," Silas nodded, pushing open the heavy oak doors.
"Come on inside.
Let’s get out of this cold."
Silas, the Princess, and Aurelia stepped out of the freezing snowy courtyard and crossed the threshold into the main Living Room of the Keep.
The heavy doors clicked shut behind them, instantly cutting off the howling wind and replacing it with the warm crackling ambiance of the massive stone hearth blazing at the far end of the room.
But the comforting atmosphere was instantly shattered by the absurdity of the scene playing out in front of them.
Silas froze dead in his tracks.
"What the fuck is going on?" Silas whispered.
Lying completely sprawled out across the massive velvet-cushioned couch to their left was Morwenna.
The fierce Pirate Queen was unapologetically naked.
Her tanned, athletic limbs were splayed in every direction, one leg hanging off the edge of the cushions, her chest rising and falling in a deep unconscious rhythm.
And directly across from her, occupying the opposite velvet couch, was Thor.
The literal Goddess of Thunder was in the exact same state.
She was completely nude, her breathtakingly muscular physique fully exposed to the warm air of the Keep.
Her divine weapon, Mjolnir, had been carelessly dropped onto the floor with its heavy Uru-metal head denting the polished oak floorboards.
Both women were dead to the world, snoring softly.
Before Silas could even process the nightmare of how Morwenna or even Thor... had ended up stripped and unconscious in the middle of the living room, a rustling sound caught his attention.
Crouching low behind a potted Spirit Fern near the edge of the couches was Eluned.
The Goddess was giggling silently to herself, her golden-green eyes sparkling with pure mischief.
Clutched firmly in her hands was a sleek camera, it was the same one as before.
Moving with the stealth of a highly trained assassin, Eluned slinked out from behind the fern.
She crept up right next to the unconscious naked Pirate Queen, holding the camera up and framing the perfect compromising shot.
CLICK-FLASH!
A blinding burst of white light illuminated the living room.
Morwenna let out a low irritated groan in her sleep, shifting her weight slightly, but she didn’t wake up.
The camera whirred mechanically, spitting out a freshly printed picture from its bottom slot.

You are exposed in the main hall!"

chapters.title: Chapter 461: Golem Creation [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: ’However, lingering too long while she’s unconscious would be a massive disrespect,’ Silas reminded himself firmly. ’Especially considering the fact that when she eventually wakes up, Thor could effortlessly punch my head completely off my shoulders if she catches me staring.’
He decided to leave the Thunder Goddess exactly where she was as the heat of the Keep would keep her warm.
Instead, he turned back to the Pirate Queen.
Morwenna was hanging dangerously close to the edge of the velvet cushions with her arm dangling toward the floorboards.
Silas stepped up to the couch, sliding his left arm carefully beneath
Morwenna’s shoulders and his right hand firmly under her bare thighs.
As he hoisted her upward, his hand accidentally slipped higher, his palm pressing directly against the soft firm curve of her bare ass.
"Mmmgh..." Morwenna groaned aggressively in her sleep, her brow furrowing as she instinctively shifted her weight closer to his chest, seeking the warmth of his body.
"Easy, Morwenna," Silas muttered softly, adjusting his grip as he carried the naked Pirate Queen away from the living room and began the trek up the central wooden staircase.
He navigated the winding halls of the second floor, pushing open the heavy oak door to his master bedroom.
He had fully expected to find Eluned hiding under the sheets, waiting to ambush him with her camera.
But as he stepped inside, the room was completely empty.
The bed was perfectly made, and the windows were shut tight against the winter storm outside.
’She actually ran off somewhere else?’ Silas thought, a bit confused by the Goddess’s restraint. ’Probably went to go show off the picture to someone as perverted as her...’
Silas walked over to the edge of the mattress, gently lowering Morwenna down onto the soft fur-lined sheets.
He quickly pulled the thick, heavy duvet up over her shoulders, tucking the edges securely around her sides to keep the winter chill at bay.
Morwenna grumbled something completely unintelligible in her sleep, her face twisting into a grumpy agitated scowl as she tried to kick the blankets away.
Silas leaned down, pressing a soft lingering kiss directly against the center of the grumpy Pirate Queen’s forehead.
Like magic, the deep crease between her eyebrows instantly vanished.
Morwenna let out a long quiet sigh, her body going completely limp as she relaxed fully into the mattress with a peaceful smile touching her lips.
"Just get some rest, Morwenna," Silas whispered, stepping back from the bed.
The physical and mental exhaustion of the Umbral Basin expedition was finally catching up to him.
’And it’s going to be much more tomorrow...’
He reached up, unfastening the leather clasps of his dark tunic as he pulled the heavy shirt over his head, tossing it carelessly onto the empty side of the bed.
He unbuckled his heavy combat trousers next, stepping out of them and leaving himself in just a comfortable pair of dark linen shorts.
’But I’ll make it through, I’m their Lord after all... though it’s weird, I could have sworn someone was watching us while we were out in the forest or something.’
But when he had turned around... there was nothing.
Silas rolled his broad shoulders, his joints popping in satisfying succession as he walked across the bedroom and pushed open the door to his en-suite bathroom.
The air inside the marble-lined room was cold.
Silas walked over to the sunken soaking tub, twisting the polished brass knobs.
A heavy rush of steaming boiling-hot water immediately poured from the faucet, filling the room with thick soothing clouds of steam.

’Before I go down to the forge to see Thora and Rowenna about the new equipment,’ Silas thought, testing the scalding water with his fingertips and letting out a satisfied breath. ’Let’s take a bath. I need to wash the stench of blood off my skin.’
Two hours later, the climate outside the Keep had completely deteriorated.
Silas stood outside the massive, reinforced iron doors of the Blessed Land Foundry.
The climate control of the Spirit Trees was struggling to keep up with the chaotic intensity of the Umbral Basin blizzard raging just beyond the territory walls.
Heavy, wet flakes of snow were falling in thick sheets, accumulating rapidly on the cobblestone paths and coating the roof of the forge in a blanket of white.
"Damn this snow," Silas cursed, shivering slightly as a rogue gust of freezing wind slipped past the Spirit Tree canopy and bit at his exposed neck.
He didn’t waste another second as he grabbed the heavy iron ring handle and hauled the Foundry door open.
FWOOOOOOSH!
The instant the seal broke, a suffocating wall of pure, blistering heat slammed directly into his face.
It was like stepping into the mouth of an active volcano.
"Haah... Much better..."
Silas quickly slipped inside and slammed the heavy iron door shut behind him, cutting off the freezing wind and trapping the magnificent heat.
The interior of the Foundry was a sprawling network of elevated catwalks, bubbling crucibles of liquid steel, and heavy hydraulic hammers pounding rhythmically against glowing metal.
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!

The dozen of dwarven women were scurrying across the floor, their muscular arms slick with sweat as they carried heavy crates of raw ore, shouted measurements over the din of the machinery, and channeled pure elemental mana into the roaring furnaces.
"Lord Silas! Welcome back!"
Silas turned to see a stout muscled female dwarf approaching him with a wide, soot-stained grin.
She wiped her grease-covered hands on a thick leather apron, her eyes raking up and down his current attire with genuine appreciation.
After his bath, Silas hadn’t bothered to put any combat armor on.
Instead, he was wearing a set of loose-fitting, elegant dark robes that wrapped comfortably around his torso and draped past his knees.
The dark silk fabric was embroidered with runic patterns.

"Those are some incredibly sharp robes, my Lord!" the female dwarf complimented enthusiastically. "You look exactly like one of those high-tier cultivators from the Eastern Realms in books! Though, you’re missing the ridiculously long flowing hair to complete the look!"
Silas smiled, looking down at his dark attire.
"Thank you. It’s significantly more comfortable than wearing some tight clothes to a meeting."
"The Boss is already expecting you!" the dwarf shouted, gesturing for him to follow her as she turned and began marching down the central aisle of the forge. "Right this way!"
Silas followed her through the chaotic, beautifully organized heart of the Foundry.
As he walked past the blazing anvils, dozens of dwarven workers paused their hammering, offering him sharp respectful salutes and cheerful greetings, which he returned with easy nods.
They bypassed the main smelting floor entirely, heading toward a reinforced isolated corridor at the far back of the facility.
The female dwarf stopped in front of a massive armored vault door constructed entirely from several kinds of alloys.
Warning runes were etched into the metal frame, pulsing with a cautionary crimson light.
"They’re waiting inside, my Lord," the dwarf said, reaching out and pulling the heavy lever to disengage the magical locks.
The thick vault door swung open with a heavy pressurized hiss, revealing the interior of the secure chamber.
Silas stepped over the threshold, and the dwarf immediately pulled the door shut behind him, the locks engaging with a heavy final clank.
"Welcome, Lord Silas!" Thora’s booming voice echoed across the room. "Welcome to the primary testing chamber!"
Silas looked around.
The testing room was big, easily the size of a small gymnasium.
The walls, ceiling, and floor were completely plated in thick reinforced metal designed to absorb catastrophic kinetic impacts and magical detonations.
And currently, the entire center of the room was filled with rocks.
There were massive jagged boulders weighing thousands of pounds, smooth river stones, dense blocks of granite, and piles of coarse gravel-like shale.
The volume of raw unrefined earth was a bit too much.
Standing on the elevated observation platform alongside Thora was Rowenna.
The brilliant Rune Master of Blessed Land had dressed for the oppressive heat of the forge, completely discarding her usual formal attire.
"Haah..."

Rowenna was sporting a tight form-fitting black singlet and a pair of extremely short denim cut-offs, an outfit so casual it made it look as if she were preparing for a lazy afternoon nap rather than conducting a high-tier magical experiment.
Her long, gorgeous black hair, tinted with striking streaks of deep violet, was tied up into a messy bun, secured casually with a steel caliper.
Her bright piercing blue eyes locked onto Silas the moment he entered, a warm excited smile breaking across her stunningly beautiful face.
Rowenna raised a hand, waving enthusiastically at him from the platform.
Silas grinned, raising a hand in return as he climbed the metal stairs to join them on the observation deck.
"So," Silas said, leaning his forearms against the railing and looking down at the massive pile of rocks in the center of the room. "I take it we are ready for the first trial?"
"Exactly right, my Lord!" Thora grinned, her thick dwarven beard practically bristling with raw, unadulterated excitement.

She slammed a heavy fist against her leather apron. "Today is a monumental day for the Blessed Land industrial sector! This is going to be our very first, fully functional attempt at synthesizing and forming a Stone Golem!"
Silas nodded, his blue eyes turning serious.

"This is a desperately needed asset, Thora. We located a massive geode in Sector KB-22 today. It’s completely encrusted with raw, uncut Mana Diamonds but the entrance is narrow, and the structural integrity of the cavern is fragile. If we send regular infantry in there with pickaxes, we risk a cave-in or shattering the diamonds. We need automated tireless heavy machinery that can extract the ore with precision and also for carrying..."
"And that is exactly what we have built," Rowenna chimed in, her voice buzzing with pride as she stepped up beside Silas, pointing down at the boulders.

"Every single one of those rocks has been meticulously carved with microscopic interconnected runic arrays," Rowenna explained, her blue eyes shining. "Kinetic suspension runes, gravity wells, and a rudimentary artificial consciousness rune anchored to a central core stone. If the mana circuit connects flawlessly, the rocks will magnetically assemble themselves into a bipedal autonomous extraction unit."
"It’s time to see if the theory holds up to the heat of reality!" Thora bellowed.
The dwarven forge master reached beneath the control console, pulling out three heavy padded metal helmets equipped with thick, tinted glass visors.
She jammed one over her own head, securing the chin strap.
She shoved the second helmet into Silas’s chest, and tossed the third to Rowenna.

"Put these on!" Thora ordered, her voice muffled slightly by the metal casing. "If the runes fail and the gravitational core collapses, those rocks are going to detonate like a thousand pounds of shrapnel! Protect your eyes!"
Silas didn’t argue. He quickly slipped the heavy metal helmet over his head, adjusting the tinted visor as Rowenna did the same beside him.

Thora slammed her hand against a massive red lever on the console, engaging the thick transparent sky-glass blast shield that rose from the railing, completely separating the observation deck from the testing floor.
Thora looked over at Rowenna, raising her thick, calloused hand and giving the Rune Master an enthusiastic, aggressive thumbs-up.
"Clear for ignition, Rowenna!" Thora shouted. "Give it the spark!"
Rowenna took a deep breath, her violet-black hair shifting slightly as a terrifyingly dense concentrated aura of pure runic mana began to gather around her slender frame.
She raised her right hand, her thumb and middle finger pressed firmly together.
For a single breathless second, the entire testing chamber went dead silent.
Rowenna snapped her fingers.
SNAP!
VUUUUUUUUUM!
The instantaneous reaction was apocalyptic.
The instant the sharp sound echoed through the chamber, every single rune carved into the thousands of rocks below violently ignited.

A blinding incandescent surge of neon-blue magical energy erupted across the testing floor, linking the massive boulders and the tiny pebbles together in a glowing, geometric web of pure light.𝓯𝓻𝓮𝙚𝙬𝓮𝙗𝒏𝙤𝒗𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝒐𝓶
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The sudden violent shift in gravity generated a concussive shockwave of displaced air.

The blast pressure slammed into the transparent shield with the force of a harsh gust, violently rattling the metal framework and blasting Silas, Thora, and Rowenna with a terrifying backdraft of pressurized wind that whipped their clothes and hair.
KRRRRRRRR-CRUNCH! GRIND!
Down on the floor, gravity ceased to exist.
The massive thousand-pound boulders began to levitate, tearing themselves from the pile and smashing together mid-air with deafening ear-splitting crunches of grinding stone.

The smaller rocks swirled around them like an asteroid belt, fusing into the gaps and sealing the joints as a massive, glowing blue core stone anchored itself perfectly into the center of the chaotic maelstrom.
Silas gripped the metal railing, his golden ringed blue eyes completely wide behind his tinted visor as the blinding runic light reached its zenith.
It was time to see if it would work...
