He reached up, unfastening the leather clasps of his dark tunic as he pulled the heavy shirt over his head, tossing it carelessly onto the empty side of the bed.
He unbuckled his heavy combat trousers next, stepping out of them and leaving himself in just a comfortable pair of dark linen shorts.
’But I’ll make it through, I’m their Lord after all... though it’s weird, I could have sworn someone was watching us while we were out in the forest or something.’
But when he had turned around... there was nothing.
Silas rolled his broad shoulders, his joints popping in satisfying succession as he walked across the bedroom and pushed open the door to his en-suite bathroom.
The air inside the marble-lined room was cold.
Silas walked over to the sunken soaking tub, twisting the polished brass knobs.
A heavy rush of steaming boiling-hot water immediately poured from the faucet, filling the room with thick soothing clouds of steam.
’Before I go down to the forge to see Thora and Rowenna about the new equipment,’ Silas thought, testing the scalding water with his fingertips and letting out a satisfied breath. ’Let’s take a bath.
I need to wash the stench of blood off my skin.’
Two hours later, the climate outside the Keep had completely deteriorated.
Silas stood outside the massive, reinforced iron doors of the Blessed Land Foundry.
The climate control of the Spirit Trees was struggling to keep up with the chaotic intensity of the Umbral Basin blizzard raging just beyond the territory walls.
Heavy, wet flakes of snow were falling in thick sheets, accumulating rapidly on the cobblestone paths and coating the roof of the forge in a blanket of white.
"Damn this snow," Silas cursed, shivering slightly as a rogue gust of freezing wind slipped past the Spirit Tree canopy and bit at his exposed neck.
He didn’t waste another second as he grabbed the heavy iron ring handle and hauled the Foundry door open.
FWOOOOOOSH!
The instant the seal broke, a suffocating wall of pure, blistering heat slammed directly into his face.
It was like stepping into the mouth of an active volcano.
"Haah...
Much better..."
Silas quickly slipped inside and slammed the heavy iron door shut behind him, cutting off the freezing wind and trapping the magnificent heat.
The interior of the Foundry was a sprawling network of elevated catwalks, bubbling crucibles of liquid steel, and heavy hydraulic hammers pounding rhythmically against glowing metal.
CLANG!
CLANG!
CLANG!

The dozen of dwarven women were scurrying across the floor, their muscular arms slick with sweat as they carried heavy crates of raw ore, shouted measurements over the din of the machinery, and channeled pure elemental mana into the roaring furnaces.
"Lord Silas!
Welcome back!"
Silas turned to see a stout muscled female dwarf approaching him with a wide, soot-stained grin.
She wiped her grease-covered hands on a thick leather apron, her eyes raking up and down his current attire with genuine appreciation.
After his bath, Silas hadn’t bothered to put any combat armor on.
Instead, he was wearing a set of loose-fitting, elegant dark robes that wrapped comfortably around his torso and draped past his knees.
The dark silk fabric was embroidered with runic patterns.
"Those are some incredibly sharp robes, my Lord!" the female dwarf complimented enthusiastically.
"You look exactly like one of those high-tier cultivators from the Eastern Realms in books!
Though, you’re missing the ridiculously long flowing hair to complete the look!"
Silas smiled, looking down at his dark attire.
"Thank you.
It’s significantly more comfortable than wearing some tight clothes to a meeting."
"The Boss is already expecting you!" the dwarf shouted, gesturing for him to follow her as she turned and began marching down the central aisle of the forge.
"Right this way!"
Silas followed her through the chaotic, beautifully organized heart of the Foundry.
As he walked past the blazing anvils, dozens of dwarven workers paused their hammering, offering him sharp respectful salutes and cheerful greetings, which he returned with easy nods.
They bypassed the main smelting floor entirely, heading toward a reinforced isolated corridor at the far back of the facility.
The female dwarf stopped in front of a massive armored vault door constructed entirely from several kinds of alloys.
Warning runes were etched into the metal frame, pulsing with a cautionary crimson light.
"They’re waiting inside, my Lord," the dwarf said, reaching out and pulling the heavy lever to disengage the magical locks.
The thick vault door swung open with a heavy pressurized hiss, revealing the interior of the secure chamber.
Silas stepped over the threshold, and the dwarf immediately pulled the door shut behind him, the locks engaging with a heavy final clank.
"Welcome, Lord Silas!" Thora’s booming voice echoed across the room.
"Welcome to the primary testing chamber!"
Silas looked around.
The testing room was big, easily the size of a small gymnasium.
The walls, ceiling, and floor were completely plated in thick reinforced metal designed to absorb catastrophic kinetic impacts and magical detonations.
And currently, the entire center of the room was filled with rocks.
There were massive jagged boulders weighing thousands of pounds, smooth river stones, dense blocks of granite, and piles of coarse gravel-like shale.
The volume of raw unrefined earth was a bit too much.
Standing on the elevated observation platform alongside Thora was Rowenna.
The brilliant Rune Master of Blessed Land had dressed for the oppressive heat of the forge, completely discarding her usual formal attire.
"Haah..."

Rowenna was sporting a tight form-fitting black singlet and a pair of extremely short denim cut-offs, an outfit so casual it made it look as if she were preparing for a lazy afternoon nap rather than conducting a high-tier magical experiment.
Her long, gorgeous black hair, tinted with striking streaks of deep violet, was tied up into a messy bun, secured casually with a steel caliper.
Her bright piercing blue eyes locked onto Silas the moment he entered, a warm excited smile breaking across her stunningly beautiful face.
Rowenna raised a hand, waving enthusiastically at him from the platform.
Silas grinned, raising a hand in return as he climbed the metal stairs to join them on the observation deck.
"So," Silas said, leaning his forearms against the railing and looking down at the massive pile of rocks in the center of the room.
"I take it we are ready for the first trial?"
"Exactly right, my Lord!" Thora grinned, her thick dwarven beard practically bristling with raw, unadulterated excitement.
She slammed a heavy fist against her leather apron.
"Today is a monumental day for the Blessed Land industrial sector!
This is going to be our very first, fully functional attempt at synthesizing and forming a Stone Golem!"
Silas nodded, his blue eyes turning serious.
"This is a desperately needed asset, Thora.
We located a massive geode in Sector KB-22 today.
It’s completely encrusted with raw, uncut Mana Diamonds but the entrance is narrow, and the structural integrity of the cavern is fragile.
If we send regular infantry in there with pickaxes, we risk a cave-in or shattering the diamonds.
We need automated tireless heavy machinery that can extract the ore with precision and also for carrying..."
"And that is exactly what we have built," Rowenna chimed in, her voice buzzing with pride as she stepped up beside Silas, pointing down at the boulders.
"Every single one of those rocks has been meticulously carved with microscopic interconnected runic arrays," Rowenna explained, her blue eyes shining.
"Kinetic suspension runes, gravity wells, and a rudimentary artificial consciousness rune anchored to a central core stone.
If the mana circuit connects flawlessly, the rocks will magnetically assemble themselves into a bipedal autonomous extraction unit."
"It’s time to see if the theory holds up to the heat of reality!" Thora bellowed.
The dwarven forge master reached beneath the control console, pulling out three heavy padded metal helmets equipped with thick, tinted glass visors.
She jammed one over her own head, securing the chin strap.
She shoved the second helmet into Silas’s chest, and tossed the third to Rowenna.
"Put these on!" Thora ordered, her voice muffled slightly by the metal casing.
"If the runes fail and the gravitational core collapses, those rocks are going to detonate like a thousand pounds of shrapnel!
Protect your eyes!"
Silas didn’t argue.
He quickly slipped the heavy metal helmet over his head, adjusting the tinted visor as Rowenna did the same beside him.

Thora slammed her hand against a massive red lever on the console, engaging the thick transparent sky-glass blast shield that rose from the railing, completely separating the observation deck from the testing floor.
Thora looked over at Rowenna, raising her thick, calloused hand and giving the Rune Master an enthusiastic, aggressive thumbs-up.
"Clear for ignition, Rowenna!" Thora shouted.
"Give it the spark!"
Rowenna took a deep breath, her violet-black hair shifting slightly as a terrifyingly dense concentrated aura of pure runic mana began to gather around her slender frame.
She raised her right hand, her thumb and middle finger pressed firmly together.
For a single breathless second, the entire testing chamber went dead silent.
Rowenna snapped her fingers.
SNAP!
VUUUUUUUUUM!
The instantaneous reaction was apocalyptic.
The instant the sharp sound echoed through the chamber, every single rune carved into the thousands of rocks below violently ignited.

A blinding incandescent surge of neon-blue magical energy erupted across the testing floor, linking the massive boulders and the tiny pebbles together in a glowing, geometric web of pure light.𝓯𝓻𝓮𝙚𝙬𝓮𝙗𝒏𝙤𝒗𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝒐𝓶
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The sudden violent shift in gravity generated a concussive shockwave of displaced air.

The blast pressure slammed into the transparent shield with the force of a harsh gust, violently rattling the metal framework and blasting Silas, Thora, and Rowenna with a terrifying backdraft of pressurized wind that whipped their clothes and hair.
KRRRRRRRR-CRUNCH!
GRIND!
Down on the floor, gravity ceased to exist.
The massive thousand-pound boulders began to levitate, tearing themselves from the pile and smashing together mid-air with deafening ear-splitting crunches of grinding stone.

The smaller rocks swirled around them like an asteroid belt, fusing into the gaps and sealing the joints as a massive, glowing blue core stone anchored itself perfectly into the center of the chaotic maelstrom.
Silas gripped the metal railing, his golden ringed blue eyes completely wide behind his tinted visor as the blinding runic light reached its zenith.
It was time to see if it would work...

chapters.title: Chapter 462: Golem Creation [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The blinding surge of neon-blue magical energy swallowed the testing floor, accompanied by a concussive shockwave of displaced air that hammered against the transparent shield once more.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The gravity within the heavily reinforced testing chamber completely collapsed.
The massive thousand-pound boulders and jagged granite blocks tore themselves from the massive pile, swirling through the air in a chaotic, frictionless orbit around the glowing blue core stone.
Through the tinted visor of his metal helmet, Silas watched as the runic arrays etched into the individual rocks violently locked onto one another.
The kinetic suspension runes flared with intensity.
KRRRRRR-CLANG! GRIND!
The levitating rocks slammed together with deafening ear-splitting crunches.
The smaller shale and river stones filled the jagged gaps, acting as a flexible, grinding mortar as the chaotic maelstrom of earth suddenly took on a definitive bipedal shape.
The massive glowing core stone anchored itself perfectly into the center of a broad chest.
With a final grinding of tectonic force, the swirling vortex of stones locked into place.
FWOOOOOOSH!
The displaced air rushed back into the center of the room as the gravity aggressively reasserted itself.
Two colossal feet, formed from massive slabs of dense granite, slammed down onto the floorboards, sending a vibrating tremor straight up through the observation deck.
BANG!
The dust slowly settled.
Standing in the absolute center of the testing chamber was a towering fully assembled Stone Golem.

It was utterly massive, standing well over eighteen feet tall. Its broad shoulders were formed from jagged, interlocking boulders, and its thick tree-trunk legs were heavily reinforced with dense river stones.
Faint neon-blue runic circuits pulsed beneath the cracks in its rocky armor, pulsing in time with the central core stone embedded in its chest.
For a long tense second, the massive construct stood completely motionless with its heavy arms hanging loosely at its sides.
"By the gods..." Silas breathed, slowly reaching up to unbuckle his heavy metal helmet.
He pulled it off, his golden ringed blue eyes reflecting the pulsing light of the golem.
Thora ripped her helmet off, tossing it carelessly onto the console. A grin split across her soot-stained face.
"HAH! WE HAVE IGNITION!" Thora roared, her booming voice echoing off the walls. "STRUCTURAL INTEGRITY IS STABLE! CORE MANA CIRCULATION IS AT ONE HUNDRED PERCENT!"
Rowenna pulled her helmet off, her striking blue eyes shining with triumph.
The Rune Master leaned against the railing, letting out a long ecstatic sigh as she brushed a stray strand of violet-black hair from her sweaty forehead.

"The kinetic suspension runes are holding flawlessly," Rowenna observed, her voice trembling slightly with adrenaline. "The gravity wells are keeping the mass from crushing its own joints... It’s a complete success."
"Success?!" Thora cheered, slamming her heavy fist against her leather apron. "It’s a bloody masterpiece!"
Without another word, Thora vaulted over the sky-iron railing of the observation deck!
"Thora, wait!" Rowenna gasped, reaching out, but the forge master had already dropped the fifteen feet down to the testing floor.
Thora landed with a heavy thud, instantly sprinting toward the towering eighteen-foot golem.

She didn’t hesitate as she grabbed onto a protruding ledge of granite on the golem’s thick thigh and began scaling the massive construct like a mountain climber, her muscular arms hauling her up the jagged rocks until she triumphantly scrambled atop the golem’s broad, boulder-like shoulder.𝗳𝚛𝚎𝚎𝘄𝕖𝕓𝕟𝕠𝚟𝚎𝕝.𝗰𝕠𝐦
"WOOOOO-HOOOOOO!" Thora bellowed from her eighteen-foot perch, throwing both of her hands into the sweltering air of the forge. "LOOK AT THIS BEAUTY, MY LORD! SHE’S SOLID AS A MOUNTAIN!"
Silas couldn’t help but laugh, leaning over the railing as he looked up at the ecstatic dwarf.
"It is incredible work, Thora! Truly! With a brute like this, cracking the bedrock to reach the deeper deposits will be child’s play!"

"Ah, but here is the rub, Lord Silas!" Thora shouted down at him, patting the massive granite boulder she was sitting on. "This Extra-Large Class Golem is perfect for heavy excavation in wide-open environments! But for a place like Sector KB-22...? Or any narrow, subterranean cavern with regular-sized openings? A beast this big would only serve to completely obstruct the tunnels!"
Thora nimbly slid down the front of the golem, using the jagged rocks as stepping stones before dropping the last few feet to the floor.

"If this thing tries to swing a pickaxe in a thirty-foot cavern, it’ll bring the entire ceiling down on top of our vanguard!" Thora explained, walking back toward the observation deck. "So, while this initial integration is a massive success, we need versatility on the field."
Thora reached into the deep leather pouch strapped to her waist and pulled out a sleek, polished rectangular slab of dark ore.
The surface of the tablet was completely smooth, save for a series of intricat dormant runes etched into the metal.
She tossed the heavy tablet up to the observation deck.
Silas caught it effortlessly with one hand, examining the smooth surface.
It looked almost exactly like a magical tablet device.
"Rowenna, if you would do the honors of explaining the secondary sequence?" Thora grinned, crossing her thick arms over her chest.
Rowenna stepped up beside Silas with her slender fingers gently tracing the edge of the runic tablet.
"This is the master control terminal, Lord Silas," Rowenna explained as though she was a Professor and then the woman tapped the center of the tablet.
The metal immediately hummed to life, the etched runes glowing with a soft neon-blue light that perfectly matched the core of the golem standing below them.

"Through this terminal, we have established a direct magical tether to the golem’s central consciousness rune," Rowenna continued, her blue eyes reflecting the light of the screen. "With a single command, we can initiate Phase Two of the deployment sequence. We call it ’Fissure Division.’"
Silas raised an eyebrow, his instincts immediately recognizing the value. "Division? You can split the mass?"

"Exactly," Rowenna smiled proudly. "We designed the runic architecture so that the central core stone is not actually a single entity, but an amalgamation of three smaller cores functioning in unison. When we trigger the Fissure command, the Extra-Large golem will intentionally short-circuit its primary gravitational well, splitting its total mass into three distinct maneuverable Phase 2 Golems."

"They will be significantly smaller," Thora called out from the floor. "Which means they can easily fit into the narrow limestone corridors of the goblin caves without scraping the walls! But don’t let the size fool you... they are still powerhouses! They are designed with massive flat reinforced stone backs specifically meant to carry the heavy mining carts I’ve been fabricating!"

"Not only that," Rowenna added, her finger hovering over a specific glowing rune on the tablet. "But we integrated external weapon racks into their spinal columns. In the event of an ambush or a sudden monster attack in the deep tunnels, the warriors of Blessed Land won’t have to rely solely on their equipped weapons. The golems will act as mobile armories, holding heavy backup spears, shields, and explosive charges that the girls can grab instantly."
Silas stared at the tablet, his mind rapidly calculating the logistical superiority this gave his territory.
Automated heavy lifting, terrain adaptability, and mobile supply lines all rolled into a single magically constructed unit?
"It’s perfect," Silas stated, a genuine smile of admiration crossing his face. "Absolutely perfect... Let’s see it in action, Rowenna."
"With pleasure, my Lord."
Rowenna firmly pressed her thumb against the glowing Fissure rune.
BZZZZT-CRACK!
The massive eighteen-foot golem standing in the center of the room violently seized.
The glowing blue circuits running through its rocky exterior flared with intensity, sparking wildly like a short-circuiting power grid.
KRRRRRR-BOOM!
With a grinding explosion of kinetic force, the massive construct completely blew itself apart.
The rocks flew outward, hovering in the air for a fraction of a second before the primary core stone fractured into three distinct brilliantly glowing orbs.
The gravity wells instantly recalibrated as the massive pile of rocks divided perfectly into three equal thirds, swirling around the new cores and rapidly snapping into place.
CLACK-CLACK-CLACK-CLANG!
The entire process took less than three seconds.
Where the towering giant had just stood, there were now three identical, heavily armored Phase 2 Golems.
They were significantly smaller than their predecessor, but they were still immensely bulky and intimidating, easily standing nine feet tall... looming over Silas’s broad frame.
Their torsos were wide and flat, their backs forming a perfect reinforced stone plateau designed to haul immense weights.
Jutting from their stone shoulders were jagged hooks explicitly designed to cradle heavy weaponry.
"Phase Two deployment successful!" Rowenna cheered, clapping her hands together as the three golems stood perfectly still, their blue cores pulsing in synchronized harmony.
Thora let out another booming laugh, walking around the three constructs and slapping their thick stone legs approvingly.
"Look at them! Beautiful! Absolutely beautiful! They’re ready to haul tons of raw ores right out of the mountain!"

"The remote terminal is incredibly intuitive," Rowenna noted, showing Silas the glowing interface. "You simply tap the corresponding directional runes to guide them, or use the macro commands for specific tasks like loading, unloading, and defensive clustering."

"And if the terminal breaks?" Silas asked, playing devil’s advocate as he handed the tablet back to Rowenna. "The Umbral Basin is chaotic. If we get ambushed by a Tier-3 beast and this tablet gets crushed in the crossfire, do we lose control of the extraction units entirely?"
"I’m glad you asked, Lord Silas!" Thora grinned, walking back to the base of the observation deck and looking up at him. "Because I designed a completely foolproof failsafe for that exact scenario!"

Thora crossed her arms. "I specifically had Rowenna help me program another rune into their core stones. In case some incredibly dumb, reckless, ham-fisted idiot like Brida, for example accidentally steps on the remote or crunches it during a fight, the golems can be operated entirely through Voice Command!"
Silas frowned slightly, leaning over the railing.
"Hey now, don’t call Brida dumb. She’s one of the most effective and loyal commanders we have. Her combat instincts are razor-sharp too."

Thora snorted, rolling her eyes affectionately. "Oh, I know she can swing an axe, my Lord but if you put a delicate, intricate piece of magical technology in that woman’s hands, she’ll try to use it to hammer a nail. She’s as sharp as a sack of wet leather when it comes to runic engineering."
Silas blinked, completely pausing as his brain tried to process the dwarven idiom. "...As sharp as a sack of wet leather? What does that even mean?"
"It means she lacks the necessary structural density for high-tier magical comprehension," Thora stated with deadpan confidence.

Silas opened his mouth to question the logic of that insult, but eventually just shook his head, deciding it wasn’t worth the headache of unraveling dwarven linguistics. "Just show me the voice commands, Thora."
"Right!" Thora turned on her heel, facing the three massive, nine-foot golems.
She drew a deep breath, her voice booming with a commanding volume.
"UNITS! ENTER REST MODE!"
The three golems instantly reacted.
The glowing blue light emanating from their core stones dimmed to a faint pulse.
With heavy, synchronized movements, the three constructs dropped to one knee, lowering their massive flat backs to a perfectly horizontal, accessible level.
They froze in place, becoming completely rigid and inert like normal statues.

"Perfect!" Thora cheered, thumping her fists against her hips. "In this mode, they consume less than one percent of their total mana reserves, and their backs are perfectly aligned to be loaded with the heavy extraction carts!"
Thora pointed at the golem on the far right.
"UNIT THREE! AWAKEN! FORWARD MARCH!"
The core stone of the rightmost golem flared back to life.
It stood up smoothly, its massive stone feet hitting the floorboards with rhythmic thuds.
STOMP! STOMP! STOMP!
It walked forward on two legs, its gait perfectly balanced and incredibly stable despite its massive bulk.
"And for incredibly steep inclines or unstable cavern terrain where bipedal balance is compromised!" Thora shouted, raising a hand. "ALL FOURS!"
The golem immediately pitched forward.
It planted its massive stone hands onto the floor, its posture shifting seamlessly into a brutal quadrupedal stance like a massive silverback gorilla.
It continued to move forward, its weight perfectly distributed across four points of contact, making it virtually impossible to knock over.
Silas watched the massive stone beast navigate the floor with genuine awe.

"It’s amazing," Silas commended, his voice filled with deep respect for their craft. "You two have outdone yourselves... The engineering, the magical integration... it’s flawless. This completely changes our logistical capabilities."
Thora beamed with absolute pride. "ALL UNITS! DEACTIVATE!"
The walking golem immediately stopped, standing upright as all three constructs powered down, their core stones dimming entirely as they returned to the state of ordinary lifeless boulders.

"We gathered a massive surplus of heavy rocks from the western perimeter for this initial test," Thora said, wiping the sweat from her brow as sighed. "But there are a lot of places the girls need to be deployed tomorrow, and if you want a full fleet of these extraction golems ready by sunrise, Rowenna and I are going to need to source a lot more dense granite to form better optimized units."

The rocks flew outward, hovering in the air for a fraction of a second before the primary core stone fractured into three distinct brilliantly glowing orbs.
The gravity wells instantly recalibrated as the massive pile of rocks divided perfectly into three equal thirds, swirling around the new cores and rapidly snapping into place.
CLACK-CLACK-CLACK-CLANG!
The entire process took less than three seconds.
Where the towering giant had just stood, there were now three identical, heavily armored Phase 2 Golems.
They were significantly smaller than their predecessor, but they were still immensely bulky and intimidating, easily standing nine feet tall... looming over Silas’s broad frame.
Their torsos were wide and flat, their backs forming a perfect reinforced stone plateau designed to haul immense weights.
Jutting from their stone shoulders were jagged hooks explicitly designed to cradle heavy weaponry.
"Phase Two deployment successful!" Rowenna cheered, clapping her hands together as the three golems stood perfectly still, their blue cores pulsing in synchronized harmony.
Thora let out another booming laugh, walking around the three constructs and slapping their thick stone legs approvingly.
"Look at them!
Beautiful!
Absolutely beautiful!
They’re ready to haul tons of raw ores right out of the mountain!"
"The remote terminal is incredibly intuitive," Rowenna noted, showing Silas the glowing interface.
"You simply tap the corresponding directional runes to guide them, or use the macro commands for specific tasks like loading, unloading, and defensive clustering."
"And if the terminal breaks?" Silas asked, playing devil’s advocate as he handed the tablet back to Rowenna.
"The Umbral Basin is chaotic.
If we get ambushed by a Tier-3 beast and this tablet gets crushed in the crossfire, do we lose control of the extraction units entirely?"
"I’m glad you asked, Lord Silas!" Thora grinned, walking back to the base of the observation deck and looking up at him.
"Because I designed a completely foolproof failsafe for that exact scenario!"
Thora crossed her arms.
"I specifically had Rowenna help me program another rune into their core stones.

In case some incredibly dumb, reckless, ham-fisted idiot like Brida, for example accidentally steps on the remote or crunches it during a fight, the golems can be operated entirely through Voice Command!"
Silas frowned slightly, leaning over the railing.
"Hey now, don’t call Brida dumb.
She’s one of the most effective and loyal commanders we have.
Her combat instincts are razor-sharp too."
Thora snorted, rolling her eyes affectionately.
"Oh, I know she can swing an axe, my Lord but if you put a delicate, intricate piece of magical technology in that woman’s hands, she’ll try to use it to hammer a nail.
She’s as sharp as a sack of wet leather when it comes to runic engineering."
Silas blinked, completely pausing as his brain tried to process the dwarven idiom.
"...As sharp as a sack of wet leather?
What does that even mean?"
"It means she lacks the necessary structural density for high-tier magical comprehension," Thora stated with deadpan confidence.
Silas opened his mouth to question the logic of that insult, but eventually just shook his head, deciding it wasn’t worth the headache of unraveling dwarven linguistics.
"Just show me the voice commands, Thora."
"Right!" Thora turned on her heel, facing the three massive, nine-foot golems.
She drew a deep breath, her voice booming with a commanding volume.
"UNITS!
ENTER REST MODE!"
The three golems instantly reacted.
The glowing blue light emanating from their core stones dimmed to a faint pulse.
With heavy, synchronized movements, the three constructs dropped to one knee, lowering their massive flat backs to a perfectly horizontal, accessible level.
They froze in place, becoming completely rigid and inert like normal statues.
"Perfect!" Thora cheered, thumping her fists against her hips.
"In this mode, they consume less than one percent of their total mana reserves, and their backs are perfectly aligned to be loaded with the heavy extraction carts!"
Thora pointed at the golem on the far right.
"UNIT THREE!
AWAKEN!
FORWARD MARCH!"
The core stone of the rightmost golem flared back to life.
It stood up smoothly, its massive stone feet hitting the floorboards with rhythmic thuds.
STOMP!
STOMP!
STOMP!
It walked forward on two legs, its gait perfectly balanced and incredibly stable despite its massive bulk.
"And for incredibly steep inclines or unstable cavern terrain where bipedal balance is compromised!" Thora shouted, raising a hand.
"ALL FOURS!"
The golem immediately pitched forward.
It planted its massive stone hands onto the floor, its posture shifting seamlessly into a brutal quadrupedal stance like a massive silverback gorilla.
It continued to move forward, its weight perfectly distributed across four points of contact, making it virtually impossible to knock over.
Silas watched the massive stone beast navigate the floor with genuine awe.
"It’s amazing," Silas commended, his voice filled with deep respect for their craft.
"You two have outdone yourselves...
The engineering, the magical integration... it’s flawless.
This completely changes our logistical capabilities."
Thora beamed with absolute pride.
"ALL UNITS!
DEACTIVATE!"
The walking golem immediately stopped, standing upright as all three constructs powered down, their core stones dimming entirely as they returned to the state of ordinary lifeless boulders.
"We gathered a massive surplus of heavy rocks from the western perimeter for this initial test," Thora said, wiping the sweat from her brow as sighed.

"But there are a lot of places the girls need to be deployed tomorrow, and if you want a full fleet of these extraction golems ready by sunrise, Rowenna and I are going to need to source a lot more dense granite to form better optimized units."

chapters.title: Chapter 463: Incubation Room [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas reached into his inventory and with a blue flash of mana, a map materialized in his hand.
He unrolled it against the control console, smoothing out the edges.

"Well you can get those around here..." Silas said, tapping a thick circled coordinate on the western edge of the Umbral Basin map. "This is Mine KB-22, the one we mentioned already. The entire entrance corridor is littered with massive limestone blocks and heavy shale that the goblins used for fortifications... It’s perfect raw material."
He moved his finger slightly north, tapping a second red circle.

"And this is the place where we encountered the spider monsters this morning. If you can harvest the stone from that place, your next batch of golems will be nearly indestructible, after all, they survived Aurelia’s Argent Flames."
Thora leaned over the map, her dwarven eyes scanning the topographical lines with intense focus.

"Dense bedrock, eh? That’s prime material. I’ll add both of these coordinates to the main industrial survey maps immediately... We can send a heavy transport unit out to harvest the stone before nightfall."

"Thank you, Thora," Silas said warmly, rolling the map back up and handing it to the forge master. "And thank you, Rowenna. The work you two are doing in this forge is the backbone of Blessed Land’s expansion."
Rowenna smiled, her cheeks flushing slightly from the sweltering heat of the forge and the heavy praise of her Lord.
"We serve at your pleasure, Lord Silas. It is our honor to build your empire."
Silas smiled. He stepped forward, placing his broad hands gently on the shoulders of both women.
He leaned down, pressing a soft affectionate kiss directly onto the center of Rowenna’s sweaty forehead.
"Hm?"
Rowenna gasped softly, her bright blue eyes widening as a brilliant crimson blush instantly exploded across her cheeks.
She lowered her gaze, her fingers nervously twisting the fabric of her casual singlet as a small blissful smile touched her lips.
Silas turned his head, planting an equally affectionate kiss onto Thora’s soot-stained forehead.
Thora didn’t blush. Instead, the dwarven forge master let out a raucous perverted cackle, looking up at him with a teasing glint in her eye.

"Oh, a forehead kiss?" Thora teased loudly, elbowing him lightly in the ribs. "Come on now, Lord Silas! We just built you three autonomous heavy-lifting magical golems! Surely a reward of that magnitude warrants going a little further beyond the forehead, eh? The forge is hot, but I can certainly turn up the heat!"
Silas rolled his eyes. Without a moment’s hesitation, he raised his right hand and delivered a sharp perfectly executed flick directly to the center of Thora’s forehead.
THWACK!
"OW!" Thora yelped, stumbling backward and rubbing her forehead with a dramatic scowl. "Gods above, you hit like a ballista!"

"That’s for being too bold in the workplace," Silas chuckled, waving a hand dismissively as he turned toward the heavy vault door. "I wish you both luck with the next batch of golems. I’ll see you at the feast tonight."
"We’ll be there!" Thora grumbled, still rubbing her forehead. "And I’m drinking your finest ale as compensation for this assault!"
Silas thanked the dwarven workers on the main floor as he walked past the blazing anvils with the heat of the Foundry baking into his dark robes.
He reached the massive front doors, grabbing the heavy iron ring and hauling it open.
FWOOOOOOSH!
The instantaneous transition from the volcanic, sweltering heat of the forge to the freezing howling blizzard outside was staggering.
The snow was beating down significantly harder now, the thick white flakes completely obscuring the sky and burying the cobblestone paths beneath heavy knee-deep drifts.
The wind shrieked through the Spirit Trees, ripping at Silas’s dark robes the moment he stepped outside.

"Gods, this storm is relentless... Is it really coming from Asgard?" Silas sighed, pulling the collar of his robes tight against his neck as the heavy iron door of the Foundry slammed shut behind him.
He didn’t bother summoning a mount for the short distance.
Lowering his head against the biting wind, Silas jogged across the snow-choked central plaza, his boots crunching heavily through the fresh powder.

He navigated past the towering glowing Spirit Trees that Eluned planted in this area, letting their ambient life-mana push back the worst of the freezing chill, until he finally reached a specific sector of the territory.
Rising from the snow was the Mythic Pack-Lord’s Sanctuary.
Though Silas personally preferred to call it the Beast Pavilion, the structure was nothing short of an architectural masterpiece.
The massive sprawling stables were constructed from dense, dark obsidian masonry that perfectly matched the commanding aesthetic of the main Keep.
Sloped ironwood roofs extended outward into deep, heavy overhangs, completely shielding the massive open-air paddock from the howling blizzard above.
Silas jogged under the safety of the ironwood overhang, stamping the heavy snow from his boots.
The moment he crossed the threshold of the Sanctuary, the chaotic freezing tension of the storm completely vanished.
The floor tiles beneath his boots radiated a deep soothing heat that kept the entire paddock comfortably warm year-round.
Etched along the top parapets and the center support pillars were glowing green nature runes and silver starlight symbols.
It was the [Nature’s Calm] rune.
The air inside the Sanctuary didn’t smell like wet fur, mud, or beasts. It smelled incredibly clean, filled with the crisp invigorating scent of a deep pine forest after a fresh rain.
The mana hummed with a soothing frequency designed specifically to completely eliminate beast aggression and panic.
"Lord Silas!"
Silas looked toward the center of the massive open-air yard.
Sitting in the middle of the paddock was a beautiful automated freshwater fountain drawing clean, crystal-clear spring water directly from the territory’s underground aquifer.
And standing near the edge of the fountain was Reina.
The Beast Tamer had changed out of her heavy winter cloak and was currently wearing a simple waterproof leather apron over her tunic, her sleeves rolled up to her elbows.
Silas smiled, walking deeper into the Sanctuary as he greeted her.
"Reina. The pavilion looks incredibly lively today."
It was an understatement... The Sanctuary was bustling with chaotic joyous activity.

Not only were the newly acquired Umbral Wolves resting comfortably on the geothermally heated floors, completely pacified by the [Nature’s Calm] runes, but the original Blessed Wolves were also present.
Dozens of women from the Blessed Land Vanguard were scattered throughout the massive paddock, armed with heavy wooden buckets, thick scrub brushes, and massive bars of lavender-scented soap.
"Hehe~ You all are too cute!"
"I’ll never get tired of this!"
They were currently in the process of thoroughly bathing the massive, feral beasts, scrubbing the blood, mud, and grime of the Umbral Basin from their thick coats.
Near the back of the stable, Silas spotted Vala.
The terrifying raven-haired woman was currently holding a massive wooden scrub brush, violently scrubbing the back of the massive, one-eyed gray alpha wolf that Aurelia had subdued earlier that day.

The arrogant beast was currently sitting perfectly still, its tongue lolling out of its mouth as it let out soft submissive pants, completely subdued by the soothing atmosphere of the pavilion and Vala’s surprisingly firm hands.

"It’s a full house, my Lord," Reina smiled proudly, wiping the suds from her hands with a clean towel as she walked over to him. "I’ve completed the head count and the logistics too. Even with the original Blessed Wolves residing here, the Sanctuary’s scalable infrastructure has more than enough space to comfortably house the forty-six new additions."
Reina looked back at the massive gray wolves resting peacefully on the warm stone tiles.
"The anti-aggression runes are working flawlessly. There hasn’t been a single territorial dispute or snarl since we brought them inside... They are very docile."
She turned her bright eyes back to Silas, her Beast Tamer mana humming with eager anticipation.

"They are fed, watered, and currently being cleaned. All that remains is for you to establish the Contract, bind them to your authority, and trigger their golden-furred evolutions to make them official members of Blessed Land’s cavalry!"
Silas looked at the forty-six wolves.
He could feel the latent potential radiating from their massive frames.
With a single tab, he could elevate them from feral anomalies into beasts of war.
But as Reina stepped back, expecting him to walk forward and begin the bonding ritual, Silas simply smiled.
"Before we get to that, Reina..." Silas murmured, his voice dropping slightly as he raised his right hand.
FWOOOOOOSH!
With a brilliant, blinding flash of condensed blue spatial mana, an object materialized directly into Silas’s palm.
He gripped it firmly, lowering his arm to present the object to the Beast Tamer.
It was the Royal Spider Egg.
The egg was massive, roughly the size of a small boulder, completely encased in a hardened translucent sapphire-blue shell that pulsed with a faint internal light.
The aura of the egg radiated from the unhatched creature within, completely contrasting with the soothing natural mana of the wolf pavilion.
Reina gasped, her eyes widening in shock as she stared at the glowing blue egg, instinctively taking a half-step backward.
Silas looked up from the heavy egg, his blue eyes locking onto the stunned Beast Tamer with a calm look.
"Do we have anywhere in this territory," Silas asked smoothly, the pulsing blue light reflecting against his dark robes. "to properly incubate an apex predator’s egg?"
Reina blinked.
...Once.
...Twice.
She stared at the pulsing, translucent sapphire shell resting in Silas’s palm, her Beast Tamer instincts warring between professional awe and a deep-seated apprehension.
The aura radiating from the colossal egg was quite murderous.
"An egg..." Reina murmured, finally finding her voice over the chaotic splashing of the Blessed Wolves behind her.
She gave her head a quick shake, her professional demeanor snapping back into place. "Yes, Lord Silas! The Sanctuary is fully equipped for this. Please, follow me."
She turned on her heel, leading him away from the open-air paddock and down a quiet, obsidian-lined corridor at the rear of the pavilion.
At the very end of the hall, Reina pushed open a reinforced ironwood door.
Instantly, a wave of almost tropical humidity washed over them.
The incubator room was entirely different from the crisp pine-scented air of the main stables.
The walls were lined with smooth dark basalt, and the floor was constructed from a porous heat-retaining ceramic.
Arranged in a perfect semi-circle across the center of the room were several wide, bowl-shaped nesting slots.
Beneath each slot rested a complex, dormant magic circle carved directly into the stone, waiting to be fueled.

"This room..." Reina whispered, a nostalgic bittersweet smile touching her lips as she trailed her fingers over the edge of a nesting slot. "It is incredibly similar to the nursery my father managed back in my home world, long before I was ever summoned... He bred scaled drakes for the royal guard. This is a dedicated incubation chamber so you just need to place the egg onto one of the pedestal slots to link it to the grid."
She stepped back, gesturing toward the center pedestal. "What exactly kind of beast is inside that shell, my Lord?"
Silas stepped forward, carefully lowering the egg into the primary slot.
"It’s a Royal Spider, give or take."
Reina completely froze.
The blood drained from her face, her shoulders instantly stiffening.
"A... a spider?" she squeaked, her voice pitching up a bit. "An eight-legged... venomous... giant spider?"

"Terrifying, isn’t it?" Silas chuckled, his golden ringed blue eyes glinting with a wicked, teasing amusement as he watched the Beast Tamer visibly shudder. "Don’t worry, Reina. As the Beast Tamer, you’ll only have to feed it, groom it, and handle it every single day once it hatches."
Reina let out a small miserable whimper, her hands instinctively wrapping around her own arms as a phantom itch crawled up her spine.
She swallowed hard, forcing her professional pride to override her crippling arachnophobia.
"I... I can handle it," Reina stammered, puffing out her chest in a desperate attempt to look brave. "It is my duty to Blessed Land! I will raise this spider into a fine, disciplined mount!"
"That’s the spirit," Silas grinned, tapping his dimensional ring. "Because there isn’t just one... There are six."
FWOOSH! FWOOSH! FWOOSH!
With rapid flashes of blue spatial mana, Silas manifested the remaining five sapphire eggs, hovering them gently in the humid air.
Reina violently flinched, letting out a strangled gasp as her knees nearly buckled.
She looked at the six spider eggs, doing the terrifying mental math of exactly how many hairy legs that equated to.
But she dug her fingernails into her palms, steadied her breathing, and pointed a trembling finger toward the remaining empty slots.
"R-right this way, Lord Silas," Reina choked out with her face turning pale. "Place them right there."
’I’ll do them for you because I like you...’
Silas easily guided the remaining five eggs into the dormant circular pedestals.
The heavy sapphire shells clicked softly against the stone, settling perfectly into the grooves.

"Now," Reina explained, taking a deep breath and stepping up to the master control pedestal at the front of the array. "We just need to manually jump-start the primary magic circle to link the heat to the eggs. It just requires a pulse of raw mana..."
"Understood," Silas nodded.
They both reached forward to press their palms against the central runic plate.
Because they moved at the exact same time, Silas’s broad calloused hand clamped firmly over the top of Reina’s delicate fingers just as she touched the stone.
Reina gasped softly.
VUUUUUUUM!

But she dug her fingernails into her palms, steadied her breathing, and pointed a trembling finger toward the remaining empty slots.
"R-right this way, Lord Silas," Reina choked out with her face turning pale.
"Place them right there."
’I’ll do them for you because I like you...’
Silas easily guided the remaining five eggs into the dormant circular pedestals.
The heavy sapphire shells clicked softly against the stone, settling perfectly into the grooves.
"Now," Reina explained, taking a deep breath and stepping up to the master control pedestal at the front of the array.
"We just need to manually jump-start the primary magic circle to link the heat to the eggs.
It just requires a pulse of raw mana..."
"Understood," Silas nodded.
They both reached forward to press their palms against the central runic plate.
Because they moved at the exact same time, Silas’s broad calloused hand clamped firmly over the top of Reina’s delicate fingers just as she touched the stone.
Reina gasped softly.
VUUUUUUUM!

chapters.title: Chapter 464: A Speech Before Rebirth [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: A brilliant warm golden-blue light erupted from the control pedestal!

Their combined mana instantly flooded the circuit as the dormant magic circles beneath all six eggs flared to life, humming with a deep vibration as soothing heat began to properly incubate the sapphire shells.
But Reina wasn’t looking at the eggs.
She was staring blankly at Silas’s large hand resting warmly over hers, their mana perfectly intertwined and flowing together to bring the new life into the world.
A sudden rush of heat flooded Reina’s face.
A brilliant crimson blush exploded across her cheeks, spreading all the way down to her collarbone and her heart began to hammer erratically against her ribs.

’Wait...’ Reina thought, her brain completely short-circuiting in a haze of panic. ’We just infused our mana together... to incubate the babies... Does that mean I’m the mama... and Lord Silas is the papa?!’
The golden-blue light of the incubation pedestal slowly faded, sinking deep into the porous ceramic stone and leaving the six sapphire spider eggs pulsing with a warm rhythm.
Silas pulled his broad hand back, letting his mana circulation settle.
As he turned his head to look at Reina, his brow furrowed in mild amusement.
The Beast Tamer was standing perfectly still, her hands clasped tightly against her waterproof leather apron.
Her face, from the tip of her chin all the way to the delicate points of her ears, was burning with a brilliant shade of crimson.
Her eyes were wide, completely out of focus as she stared blankly at the stone pedestal, her mind clearly lost in some chaotic panicked spiral of thoughts.
"Reina?" Silas asked, his deep voice cutting through the humid silence.
He tilted his head slightly, studying the intense flush on her cheeks. "Why is your face so red? Is the heat in here set too high?"
Reina violently flinched, snapping out of her romantic panic like a startled deer.
"N-no! Not at all, Lord Silas!" Reina stammered frantically, averting her eyes and desperately waving her hands in front of her chest to dismiss the question.

She stepped backward, nearly tripping over her own boots. "It’s just... the mana! Yes! The sudden surge of raw mana reacting with my meridians caused a minor circulatory flush! It’s a completely normal physiological reaction to high-tier incubation magic! Nothing to worry about!"
Silas stared at her for a long quiet second, easily seeing right through the completely fabricated excuse.
But rather than press the issue and embarrass her further, a warm smile spread across his face.
He closed the distance between them with a single step and raised his hand, placing it gently but firmly onto Reina’s shoulder.
Reina froze, her breath catching in her throat at the sudden comforting weight of his hand.
"Regardless of the heat," Silas murmured, his voice softening into a tone of deep gratitude, "I need to thank you, Reina."
Reina blinked, finally forcing herself to meet his piercing blue eyes.
"T-thank me? For what, my Lord? I merely showed you the room."

"For this," Silas said, gesturing his free hand around the massive, state-of-the-art incubation chamber, and by extension, the entire sprawling Mythic Sanctuary waiting outside. "None of this infrastructure would have been possible if you hadn’t taken the initiative to drop that idea into the Suggestion Box. You saw a critical flaw in our territory’s logistics, and you stepped up to fix it. This pavilion, the Blessed Wolves, the new Umbral cavalry... it all exists because of you."
Reina stood completely paralyzed.
The embarrassed beating of her heart slowed, replaced by a deep overwhelming swell of emotional warmth that spread through her chest.
She had submitted that suggestion on a whim, hoping, but never truly expecting, that the Lord would actually listen to a mere recruit but Silas had listened.
He had read her words, invested into her vision, and elevated her to a position of authority over the territory’s most vital assets.
A soft radiant smile touched Reina’s lips.
The lingering blush on her cheeks shifted from embarrassment to pride.

"That’s right..." Reina whispered softly, her eyes shining as she looked at him. "If that Suggestion Box hadn’t been placed in the Barracks... if you hadn’t taken the time to read it... I wouldn’t be standing here right now." She bowed her head respectfully, her voice steady and filled with devotion. "Thank you for reading my entry, Lord Silas. And thank you for trusting me with this."

"You earned it, Reina," Silas replied, giving her shoulder a final, approving squeeze before dropping his hand. "Now, come on... We have forty-six feral wolves waiting for their contracts, and I’m sure the girls are anxious to get it over with."
They turned away from the pulsing sapphire eggs, walking back down the dark basalt corridor and pushing open the heavy ironwood door to re-enter the main paddock of the Beast Pavilion.
The transition from the quiet humid nursery to the sprawling outdoor Sanctuary was jarring as the massive open-air stable was an absolute madhouse of joyous activity.
The heavy, snow-laden blizzard was still howling fiercely against the slanted ironwood roofs above, but inside the heated paddock, the atmosphere was a bustling soapy wonderland.

Dozens of women from the Blessed Land that Silas had seen earlier, having stripped off their heavy armor in favor of light linen tunics, rolled-up trousers, and waterproof aprons, were scattered across the stone tiles.
They were still armed with heavy wooden buckets sloshing with warm water, massive bristle brushes, and thick, fluffy towels, actively wrangling the massive Umbral Wolves.

The [Nature’s Calm] runes etched into the pillars were doing their job flawlessly... despite being surrounded by humans and soapy water, the forty-six feral wolves were entirely docile, letting out content rumbling pants as they were scrubbed clean.

"Oh my gods, look at his little paws!" one of the women cooed loudly, vigorously towel-drying the sharp claws of a gray wolf that was easily the size of a warhorse. "He’s so cute! Who’s a good predator? You are!"
"Hold still, you giant baby," Sarah laughed from the next stall over, wrestling with a wet, struggling black wolf that was playfully trying to bite the wooden handle of her scrub brush.
Silas and Reina walked out onto the main concourse, observing the wholesome chaos.
Near the center aquifer fountain, one specific woman... a fiery redhead whose name Silas recalled was Clara was currently locked in a battle of wills with a filthy mud-caked Umbral Wolf.
The beast was stubbornly sitting on its haunches, refusing to lift its chin so she could wash its neck.
Clara had clearly lost her patience.
She was holding a heavy, pressurized rubber hose connected directly to the magical aquifer pump, blasting the massive wolf right in the chest at absolute, full throttle.

"Lift your damn head, you stubborn mutt!" Clara yelled over the roaring spray of the water, completely unimpressed by the feral beast’s terrifying size. "You smell like a rotting goblin swamp! You think any of the pretty Wolves are going to look twice at you with that matted fur? You’re never going to get laid looking like a mud-rat!"
The massive wolf let out a pathetic whining yelp, squinting its yellow eyes against the pressurized water and finally tipping its head back in defeat.
Silas let out a deep laugh that echoed over the splashing water. "You tell him, Clara! Keep strict discipline in the ranks!"
Clara froze instantly.
The pressurized hose slipped from her grip, thrashing wildly on the stone floor and spraying water in every direction as she whipped around to face the Lord.
Her eyes blew wide in panic as she hadn’t realized Silas was standing mere feet behind her.
"B-boss!" Clara stammered, frantically wiping her wet, soapy hands on her apron and snapping into a rigid and slightly crooked military salute.
"At ease," Silas smiled warmly as he looked her over.
Her fiery red hair, usually kept in a strict military braid, had come undone in the chaos of the washing, currently tied up in a loose, chaotic, wet bun with stray strands framing her flushed face.
It gave her a wild and incredibly charming look.
"Your hair looks good like that, Clara," Silas noted casually, offering a genuine compliment. "It suits you."
Clara stopped breathing.
Her entire face instantly detonated into a shade of red that rivaled her own hair.
Her pupils dilated, and her brain completely, utterly short-circuited under the sudden unexpected praise from her Lord.
She stared blankly at his handsome face, her lips parting as a low unhinged mutter slipped past her teeth.
"Master’s gonna fuck me tonight..." Clara whispered, staring into the middle distance.
Silas froze.
The warm smile completely evaporated from his face, replaced by a look of paralyzed bewilderment.
He stood there, completely lost for words, desperately trying to process what the hell he had just heard.
Before Silas could even formulate a response to the staggeringly bold, perverted mutter, a hand clamped down on his wrist with the force of a vice grip.
Reina stepped forward, her eyes narrowed into a judgmental glare aimed directly at Clara.
"We are leaving," Reina announced sharply, forcibly dragging Silas away from the fountain by his wrist.
Silas stumbled after the Beast Tamer, looking back over his shoulder at Clara, who was currently covering her face with her hands and sinking slowly to the wet floor in absolute, mortified agony.
’It seems...’ Silas thought, shaking his head as he followed Reina toward the center of the paddock, ’a staggering majority of my girls have suppressed perverted tendencies.’
"Alright, everyone, listen up!" Reina shouted, clapping her hands together.

Her voice carried with the unquestioned authority of the territory’s Beast Tamer, instantly cutting through the chatter and the splashing water. "Baths are done! Towel them off and herd them to the center of the paddock! I want all forty-six wolves in a straight, organized formation! Now!"
The women immediately scrambled into action.

They tossed their scrub brushes aside, quickly running heavy linen towels over the damp wolves before coaxing, pushing, and pulling the massive beasts toward the center of the geothermally heated tiles.
Within minutes, the chaotic mob of beasts had been arranged into five neat, organized rows facing the main entrance of the Sanctuary.
Most of the wolves sat obediently, their tails thumping against the stone as they basked in the warmth of the room.
But right at the front of the formation, the one-eyed gray alpha wolf... the incredibly arrogant beast that Vala had been aggressively scrubbing earlier remained standing.
’Why is it stubborn now...?’
It puffed out its chest, refusing to sit, looking around the paddock with an air of stubborn defiance.
Reina narrowed her eyes. She marched right up to the massive alpha, pointing a stern finger directly at its nose.
"Sit your ass down, Howard," Reina commanded flatly.
The terrifying alpha wolf instantly dropped its rear onto the stone tiles, letting out a soft compliant whine.
Standing a few feet away, Silas completely lost his composure. He slapped a hand over his mouth, his shoulders shaking with silent uncontrollable laughter.
’Howard?’ Silas thought, struggling to breathe as he looked at the menacing wolf. ’She named the arrogant beast in the pack... Howard?!’
Reina ignored his laughter, turning on her heel to face him. "The formation is ready, Lord Silas."
Silas took a deep breath, forcing his amusement down and allowing the commanding aura of his Gold Core to rise to the surface.
’Even if they are wolves... I need to give another motivational speech.’
...Truly being a Lord was hard work.
Silas stepped to the front of the pack, sweeping his piercing blue gaze across the forty-six damp Umbral Wolves.
"You were born in the dark," Silas began, his voice projecting with a deep authority that made the very air in the pavilion vibrate.
The wolves’ ears perked up instantly, their yellow eyes locking onto him, captivated by the overwhelming pressure of his presence.
"You were hunted by monsters, corrupted by the magic of the Umbral Basin, and forced to fight for every scrap of survival in a wasteland..."
He slowly paced in front of the formation, his dark robes sweeping over the wet stone.

"But that life ends today," Silas declared, his voice rising in power. "You have been brought to Blessed Land... Here, you will not freeze... You will not starve... You will be treated with the utmost respect, and you will be feared by our enemies... You are no longer feral beasts scavenging in the snow. From this moment forward, you are the Cavalry of my empire!"
Silas stopped in the center, projecting his aura outward. "Will you serve?"
"HO-WOOOOOOOOOOOOO!"
A deafening earth-shaking chorus of forty-six synchronized howls erupted into the air.

The sound was so powerful it rattled the ironwood beams of the roof, shaking the dust from the rafters as the beasts threw their heads back and pledged their absolute loyalty to the predator standing before them.
Silas smiled, nodding his head. He looked to his right, gesturing for Reina to take the floor.
Reina stepped forward, her Beast Tamer mana flaring with a bright vibrant hue as she raised both of her hands, her voice ringing out clear and true.
"To serve Blessed Land, you must leave your corrupted past behind!" Reina shouted to the pack. "Bow your heads! Prepare to be reborn!"
Without a single moment of hesitation, all forty-six Umbral Wolves, including the arrogant Howard, bowed their snouts completely flat against the warm stone tiles in a posture of total submission.

chapters.title: Chapter 465: Bribing Evelyn [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Reina closed her eyes, taking a deep centering breath.
Her hands began to glow with a brilliant golden light that rapidly overtook her natural green mana.
"Beast..." Reina muttered, her voice echoing with magical resonance. "...Arrest."
Instantly, a wave of pure concentrated golden energy erupted from Reina’s body.
It didn’t shoot forward like a spell... instead, it wafted outward, blooming into the air like the opening petals of a massive ethereal golden flower.
The glowing pollen of the spell drifted gently across the paddock, descending like falling snow to touch the bowed heads of the forty-six beasts.
She had used this exact skill, [Beast Arrest], in the Umbral Basin to initially subdue them and make them join her.
But now, within the confines of the territory, she was using the Skill’s secondary function... establishing the foundational tethers required for a formal Contract.
The moment the golden floral energy latched onto the wolves, a sharp crystalline chime rang out in Silas’s mind.
A glowing blue holographic window materialized directly in his field of vision.
[Territorial Event Triggered!]
[46 Umbral Wolves want to join Blessed Land as Mounts.]
[Would you like to allow? Y / N]
Silas let out a slow, heavy sigh, watching the prompt hover in the air.
’It’s happening...’ Silas thought, bracing himself for the massive expenditure of internal mana.
He raised his hand and tapped the Y.
VUUUUUUUUUUUM!
The instantaneous reaction was catastrophic.
Silas’s Gold Core, sitting perfectly in the center of his dantian, violently throbbed.
"Haah..."

A staggering wave of pure mana erupted from his chest as the beam shot forward, instantly shattering into forty-six separate pillars of pure energy that violently crashed down onto the kneeling Umbral Wolves.
"AWOOOOOOOO!" the wolves howled, not in pain, but in overwhelming evolutionary shock.
The transformation followed...
The corrupted, jagged midnight-black and ash-gray fur that covered their bodies began to rapidly dissolve, burning away like ash in a furnace.
In its place, thick luxurious coats of pure radiant silver and brilliant gold began to rapidly grow.
Their jagged infected scars faded into smooth, pristine muscle. Their feral sickly yellow eyes shifted into glowing intelligent hues of sapphire and amber.
The evolutionary process took time.
The volume of mana required to purify forty-six Tier-2 anomalies simultaneously was staggering.
The air in the pavilion crackled with heavy static as the golden light completely blinded everyone in the room.
’It’s not that much to my reserves to be honest..’
But Reina didn’t look away.
She stood perfectly still, her hands clasped to her chest, basking in the terrifying, magnificent glory of it.
She watched the golden light pour endlessly from Silas’s chest, her heart hammering with reverence.
’My Lord... is truly a different beast completely,’ she thought in pure awe. ’No normal Lord could output this level of mana without collapsing.’
Slowly, the blinding golden light began to die down, retracting back into Silas’s chest.
The dust settled over the stone tiles.
Kneeling perfectly in the center of the paddock were forty-six magnificent Blessed Wolves.
Their platinum-silver and gold coats shimmered beautifully under the pavilion’s lighting, their frames radiating a clean aura that entirely matched Valkyrie and Luna.
For a second, there was complete silence then, the women lost their minds.

"THEY ARE SO FLUFFY!" Clara shrieked, completely forgetting her earlier embarrassment as she and a dozen other girls rushed forward, throwing their arms around the massive, kneeling wolves, burying their faces in the incredibly soft fur.
The wolves let out happy rumbling chuffs, leaning into the affectionate scratches.
As the girls celebrated, a rapid sequence of chimes echoed in Silas’s mind.
[Territorial Integration Successful!]
[Species Evolution Triggered: Corrupted Umbral Wolves have been purified.]
[New Species: Blessed Wolves.]
[Hidden Mission: Gain 50 New Species In Your Territory has been completed!]
[Reward: Mystery Box]
[Pact Established: Master-Slave Territorial Contract.]
[Note: As the Sovereign Lord of the Blessed Land, you hold absolute authority over these entities. You may revoke their contract and banish them from the territory at any time.]
Silas casually swiped his hand through the air, dismissing the contract tab.
He had seen the Master-Slave warning before before when binding the last set to the territory, so it didn’t concern him in the slightest.
But his blue eyes locked heavily onto the fourth notification.

’A Hidden Mission? Gain 50 new species...’ Silas thought, a spark of intense intrigue lighting up his mind. ’Between the various crops Eluned planted, the different livestock, the elemental slimes, the dire wolves, and now the cavern spiders incubating in the back... I must have finally hit the threshold?’
He looked at the digital icon of the Mystery Box hovering in his inventory space.
The urge to tap it immediately and see what cosmic reward the world had generated... was it strong?

’No,’ Silas decided, forcibly closing his inventory interface. ’A mystery gift from a Hidden Mission could be anything from a legendary weapon to a massive architectural blueprint that might spawn right on top of my head. I should roll it when I’m in private... My office, later tonight.’
Besides, he still had somewhere crucial to be.
There was a very specific reason Evelyn had braved the freezing blizzard to storm up to his Keep earlier that afternoon, and he knew exactly what it was.

’I need to apologize, too,’ Silas thought, running a hand through his dark hair as a spike of genuine guilt hit his chest. ’I definitely should have sent a priority message to her warning her that the Princess of the world was residing in my Keep. I was too focused on other stuff...’
Silas turned, preparing to leave the bustling pavilion as he waved a hand in the air.
"I leave the rest to you, Reina!" Silas called out over the joyful chatter of the girls. "Make sure they are fully fed and integrated with the original pack!"
Reina snapped a sharp salute. "Leave it to me, Lord Silas!"
As Silas turned to walk toward the exit, his eyes locked onto Vala.
The raven-haired woman was standing near the edge of the fountain, casually wiping down one of the newly evolved wolves, but her sharp eyes were fixed directly on him.
Silas didn’t speak.
He caught her gaze, holding it for a fraction of a second, and deliberately mouthed the words.
’Meet me in the office in the evening...’
Vala’s hands paused on the wet towel.

A sudden deep flush of red crept up the back of her pale neck, coloring her cheeks but she didn’t say a word, nor did she make a grand gesture, but she offered him a single imperceptible nod of confirmation before quickly looking back down at the wolf.
Silas smirked, turning on his heel and marching out into the driving snow.
’Now how can I settle with Evelyn?’
Knock! Knock!
The heavy sound echoed through the luxurious velvet-lined guest quarters in the apartment.
Sitting in a plush leather armchair near the frost-covered window, Evelyn let out a long exhale.
She was currently on her fourth cigarette of the hour.
She pinched the filter between her lips, pulling a fresh one from the silver case resting on the side table.
"Haah..."
Without reaching for a match, she simply snapped her fingers.
A tiny spark of violent mana ignited at the tip of her thumb, lighting the end of the cigarette with a sharp hiss.
She took a deep dragging pull, the cherry glowing bright orange before she exhaled a thick cloud of blue smoke toward the ceiling.
"Fuck... Fuckk..."
She was stressed, beyond stressed even.
’My identity... What do I do now?’
The diplomatic nightmare of having her true identity as Lord Sky compromised was giving her a massive throbbing headache right between her eyes.
"Come in," Evelyn called out, her voice slightly raspy from the smoke.
The heavy wooden door clicked open, and Silas stepped into the room.
Evelyn immediately huffed, crossing her arms over her chest.
She opened her mouth, fully prepared to unleash a devastating, expletive-laden tirade about his lack of communication and his generally punchable face.
’Why is the Princess even here in the first place? Isn’t she unawakened?’
But before she could even utter a single syllable, Silas moved.
He extended his right arm forward, presenting a large chilled crystal cup directly into her line of sight.
The cup was filled to the brim with incredibly thick, rich, perfectly churned vanilla cream, drizzled with dark chocolate syrup and topped with crushed nuts.
"Kaelia’s first successful attempt at making actual ice cream," Silas announced smoothly, his voice sounding incredibly casual.
Before Evelyn could even react to the cup, Silas shifted his left arm, producing a beautifully arranged silver platter.
Stacked high on the polished metal were freshly baked, steaming cinnamon buns dripping with white icing, thick glazed doughnuts, and several slices of incredibly dense, moist chocolate cake.
"She was baking this afternoon," Silas added, offering the platter forward like a peace offering to an angry deity.
Evelyn completely froze.

Her stormy gray eyes darted from the chilled cup of artisanal ice cream to the massive platter of steaming, sugar-glazed pastries, and finally up to the handsome slightly apologetic face of the younger Lord standing in her doorway.
The corners of Evelyn’s lips involuntarily crinkled.
’Is he...’ Evelyn thought, the absurdity of the situation temporarily overriding her boiling rage. ’Is this bastard seriously trying to apologize to me with a tray of baked goods?’
It was infuriating... but it was also very patronizing.
And, if she was being entirely honest with herself... it was incredibly cute.
Evelyn had a notoriously massive weakness for high-quality sweets, a fact that was incredibly difficult to satisfy when she was in the Sovereign Realm.
’Sure, I have chefs but not to this level...’𝐟𝕣𝗲𝕖𝕨𝗲𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝗲𝚕.𝗰𝚘𝐦
The smell of the warm cinnamon and the chilled vanilla cream was assaulting her senses, completely shattering her aggressive posture.
’Maybe...’ Evelyn thought, her stormy eyes softening just a fraction as she looked at the glazed doughnuts. ’Maybe I don’t want to kick him in the balls that much.’
Evelyn let out a long defeated sigh.
She reached up, plucking the lit cigarette from her lips and tossing it into a nearby crystal ashtray.
"Alright..."
She reached forward, completely abandoning her anger as she accepted the heavy silver platter with one hand and the chilled cup of ice cream with the other.
Silas smiled.
He stepped fully into the room, casually kicking the heavy wooden door shut with his heel.
Evelyn didn’t waste a single second.
She sat the platter down on her lap, immediately biting into a thick glazed doughnut.
Her eyes fluttered shut as the warm, sugary dough practically melted on her tongue.

"My gods," Evelyn moaned softly around a mouthful of pastry, her professional Lord persona completely evaporating. "The culinary infrastructure in your territory is disgusting... This is one of the best things I have tasted in three months."
"I’ll pass your compliments along to the chef," Silas chuckled, walking over and leaning casually against the edge of her wooden writing desk.

He watched in mild fascination as Evelyn took a spoon, scooped up a massive dollop of the vanilla ice cream, and slapped it directly onto the top of her half-eaten doughnut before taking another massive bite.
Silas kept his smile perfectly polite, but inwardly, his mind was reeling.

’Who the hell chainsmokes several cigarettes in a row, and then immediately starts eating ice cream stacked on top of a hot doughnut?’ Silas thought, genuinely impressed by the chaos of her digestive system. ’Her internal organs must be forged from vibranium or something.’
Evelyn chewed happily, swallowing the absurd combination of hot dough and cold cream before wiping her mouth with a napkin.
Her stormy gray eyes locked back onto Silas as the fierce intelligence returned to her gaze.
"So," Evelyn said, gesturing with her spoon. "Before we get into the absolute disaster of your lack of communication regarding the Princess... I should probably congratulate you."
Silas raised an eyebrow. "Congratulate me? For what?"
Evelyn took another bite of cake.

"For the fact that your ’Lord Vespera’ network account just officially crossed forty million active followers this afternoon. The global network is completely losing its mind over your mysterious female alter-ego. We might actually have to coordinate and post a video of her soon just to keep the engagement metrics high."
Silas blinked, his jaw dropping slightly as he almost choked on his own spit.
"Forty million?" Silas asked in disbelief. "She is that popular?"
Evelyn snorted, rolling her eyes as she scooped more ice cream.

"Are you joking? Silas, you created a breathtakingly beautiful and mysterious woman who single-handedly crushed the Unmovable Wall... Your female disguise is currently the most popular sought-after woman in the entire world."
Silas rubbed his temples, a headache beginning to form at the logistical nightmare of managing a globally famous alter-ego that didn’t actually exist.
"But that is not why I came to your Keep today," Evelyn continued, her tone suddenly dropping the casual banter.
She set the spoon down with her expression turning incredibly serious... She was serious.
Evelyn looked directly into his eyes.

"The World Council has officially gotten in contact with my secure terminal," Evelyn stated, her voice quiet but echoing loudly in the silent room. "They are demanding a formal face-to-face summit regarding the aftermath of the Lord War and the rising influence of Blessed Land."
She paused, leaning forward in her leather chair.
"We need to decide on a date."
