chapters.title: Chapter 466: Preparations For The World Council Meeting [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas’s casual demeanor vanished instantly as his blue eyes sharpened into terrifying slits.
The World Council, huh?
Silas gave a slow nod.
"Right," Silas murmured. "It’s time for the meeting with the World Council."
Silas had been turning the prospect of this summit over in his mind for quite a long time now.
As he leaned back against the edge of the heavy wooden writing desk, watching Evelyn demolish a slice of rich chocolate cake, he felt a strange thrumming anticipation settling into his chest.
The time had finally come to set a concrete date...
He was more than prepared for it. His internal calculations were already running through the myriad of political, economic, and territorial angles he could exploit.
The major objective here was incredibly simple: gain as much as humanly, or perhaps divinely, possible from them.

Given that he had successfully awakened a Mythic Gold Core... an anomaly of raw power that completely shattered the conventional scaling metrics of the Awakened Society... Silas knew he was walking into this summit holding a royal flush.
He was going to have a field day with the global elites.

’It’s quite funny, really,’ Silas thought with a confident smirk playing at the corners of his lips. ’I’m actually feeling genuinely excited about walking into a room full of the highest powers in the Awakened Society and flipping their entire worldview completely upside down...’
Evelyn swallowed a massive bite of cake, chasing it with a spoonful of Kaelia’s vanilla ice cream.

"If we are going to do this," Evelyn stated, pointing her silver spoon directly at his chest, "a proper finalized date has to be set for the meeting. The World Council doesn’t just clear their schedule for random upstarts, even if you did just gain a lot of support from the World. I’ll coordinate the encrypted communications on my end, and I will accompany you to the summit in my disguise... Though, I suppose I should mention it is going to be my very first time formally meeting the World Council in person, too."
She didn’t wait for his response, immediately going back to stuffing her face with a glazed doughnut.
Silas let out a slow sigh, crossing his arms over his chest. Personally he would like to go as soon as possible but right now, he factored in the current logistical constraints of the Keep.

"The Princess is going to remain here in Blessed Land for exactly one week. So, we have six more days of playing host to global royalty... I think we should definitively schedule the summit for the day after she departs. That way, our hands are clean, and we don’t risk any cross-contamination between her presence here and the Council’s intelligence network."
’How the hell did she even get here anyway?’ Evelyn thought but she didn’t ask, she really knew it was on some bullshit.
He tapped his chin thoughtfully.

"Perhaps we can arrange it to fall exactly on the day of a major pre-existing global meeting. If they are already gathered, we can crash the party and meet all the key members simultaneously without having to track them down individually."
Evelyn paused mid-chew.
She set her spoon down on the silver platter, reaching into the deep pocket of her sleek dark tunic as she pulled out a high-end encrypted smartphone.
"I see..."
Her thumb swiftly swiping across the glass screen as she opened the Y app... the global network’s primary digital hub for news, Lord interactions, and Awakened rumors.
Her stormy gray eyes scanned the rapidly scrolling text.

"Well, look at this," Evelyn mumbled around a mouthful of dough, her eyes lighting up with calculating intrigue. "It seems the World Council is actually hosting a massive summit in exactly a week and a few days. They are gathering all the sitting Presidents of the major terrestrial countries and more importantly... the King and the Prince of the world are both confirmed to be in attendance."
Silas raised an eyebrow.

Even though the human realm was an incredibly modern, technologically advanced world complete with smartphones, digital streaming networks, and global internet access, the traditional archaic titles of "King" and "Prince of the World" were not merely ceremonial.
...They were titles forged in the fires of an apocalyptic crucible, at least that was what one would say.

Decades ago, when the dimensional barriers first began to fracture and the Sovereign Realm threatened to completely consume the Human world in a tidal wave of anomalous beasts and rogue mana, it was the Royal Family that had stepped forward to save humanity from utter extinction.
They had exhausted their vast generational wealth and leveraged unparalleled magical engineering to create colossal Suppression Engines.
These giant monolithic machines were planted deep within the bedrock of every major country on Earth.
The machines forcibly stabilized the dimensional tear, effectively preventing Sovereign Realm gates from opening randomly in populated cities.

They were the sole reason humanity had survived the initial integration as the entire modern world owed them an unpayable debt of blood and gratitude, which was exactly why the royal family retained unquestioned global authority.
’Plus they’re rich too...’

"There’s more," Evelyn noted, her thumb scrolling further down the Y feed. "The tabloids and the Awakened forums are completely buzzing. There are some unconfirmed rumors circulating that an illegitimate royal daughter is going to be formally introduced at this summit."
"An illegitimate girl?" Silas asked. "That’s going to cause a massive media circus."

"Which makes it the perfect time for us to show up," Evelyn smiled, locking her phone screen and slipping it back into her pocket. "It’s taking place a week and a few days from now. Just after your little royal houseguest vacates the premises..."
Silas nodded, a sharp glint flashing in his blue eyes. "Let’s meet the World Council then."
Evelyn smiled with a genuine happy expression that completely matched his own ambition.

"You’re smart, Silas. I’ll give you that. Crashing their most publicized high-security summit of the decade? This should be perfect. It establishes total dominance from the second we walk through the doors."
She tilted her head, wiping a smudge of icing from her cheek. "As long as you’re not suddenly feeling chickened out?"
Silas scoffed, rolling his shoulders with effortless imposing confidence.
"How could I possibly feel chickened out? They should be the ones feeling terrified..."
He pushed off the edge of the writing desk, standing to his full, towering height.
"Thank you for handling the communications, Evelyn and for everything else you’re doing behind the scenes."
Evelyn simply waved a hand dismissively, immediately grabbing another thick slice of chocolate cake and stuffing her mouth full.𝐟𝕣𝕖𝐞𝐰𝕖𝚋𝐧𝗼𝚟𝐞𝕝.𝗰𝐨𝐦
Silas watched her struggle to swallow the dry cake as he let out a quiet chuckle.
His right hand flared with a brilliant condensed flash of blue spatial mana and reaching into the dimensional pocket, he pulled out a cold bottle of sparkling spirit-water and extended it toward her.
Evelyn took the bottle gratefully, twisting the cap off and chugging it down to clear her throat.
She wiped her mouth with the back of her hand, letting out a satisfied breath.

"I will get in contact with the World Council’s secure terminal tonight and lay the groundwork," Evelyn promised, a smug satisfied smile touching her lips. "And you are very welcome for the administrative carry, Silas."
"I’ll leave you to your sugar coma, then," Silas smirked, turning on his heel and walking toward the heavy wooden door.
"Hold on. Stop," Evelyn commanded and Silas paused, his hand hovering mere inches from the brass doorknob.
He turned around with his brow furrowing slightly in question. "What is it n—"
WHOOOOOOSH!
Evelyn didn’t speak, she moved instead.
Channeling the terrifying physical parameters of a top-tier Lord, Evelyn completely blurred out of existence.
She crossed the fifteen feet of plush carpeting separating them in seconds as she planted her pivot foot with bone-shattering force, her hips snapping violently.
’It’s time for my revenge...’
She executed a flawless and devastatingly fast front kick aimed squarely at Silas’s groin.
KRA-BOOOOOOM!
The impact was catastrophic.

The force of Evelyn’s reinforced boot connecting with its target generated a concussive shockwave as a violent ring of displaced air exploded outward from the point of impact, violently rustling the heavy velvet curtains and rattling the crystal ashtray on the table.
Evelyn stood with her leg fully extended with a smug on her face.

’That’s for terrifying me and compromising my secret identity, you arrogant bastard,’ she thought, fully expecting Silas to immediately drop to his knees, completely paralyzed by the agonizing pain of a powerful strike to the nuts.
But a second passed.
...Then another.
Evelyn’s smug grin slowly began to falter.
She looked up and saw Silas was standing perfectly still.
He hadn’t bent forward and he hadn’t flinched, hell he hadn’t even blinked.

His posture was completely relaxed, his hands resting casually at his sides as he looked down at Evelyn’s boot pressed against his groin, and then slowly raised his eyes to meet her horrified trembling stormy gray gaze.
Evelyn rapidly pulled her leg back, stumbling a half-step backward in disbelief.

’No reaction...?’ Evelyn’s mind screamed, her brain completely short-circuiting as she stared at him. ’I just channeled enough raw force to completely shatter a door! How the hell is his physical constitution that high?! What kind of monstrous unbreakable body does this man possess?!’
Silas simply stood there, brushing an invisible speck of dust from the front of his dark trousers.
He looked at Evelyn, his blue eyes filled with disappointment.

"I am the younger one in this alliance of ours, Evelyn," Silas said, his voice carrying the weight of a tired parent scolding a toddler. "And yet, somehow, I consistently behave far more mature than you."
Silas let out a sharp dismissive sound.
"Tch."
Without another word, Silas reached out, grabbed the doorknob, and stepped out into the hallway, pulling the heavy wooden door shut with a soft final click.
Left entirely alone in the quiet velvet-lined room, Evelyn stood completely frozen in place.
Her leg was trembling slightly from the sheer of hitting his unbreakable frame as her stormy gray eyes were wide, staring blankly at the closed door.
’Not even a single reaction?’ Evelyn thought, a deep sense of existential dread and inadequacy crashing over her like a tidal wave.
She looked down at her own hands, flexing her fingers as a cold sweat broke out across her neck.
’...Why do I feel so unbelievably weak?’
Out in the quiet torch-lit corridor of the Keep, Silas let out a slow steady exhale, adjusting the front of his dark robes.
’At least I’ve settled her now,’ Silas thought, rolling his shoulders to shake off the lingering pressure of the kick. ’She’s strong but not strong enough...’
His Gold Core constitution was a terrifying cheat code.
His physical power and durability were so astronomically high that Evelyn’s strike had felt like nothing more than a gentle breeze against a solid mountain
Silas pushed open the heavy oak doors of the Keep, stepping onto the plush rugs.
The massive stone hearth had burned down to a pile of glowing, crackling orange embers, casting deep dancing shadows across the velvet furniture.
Morwenna was gone, safely tucked into his bed upstairs, but lying completely sprawled out across the opposite couch was the Norse Goddess of Thunder.
Thor was still unapologetically naked.

Her statuesque, heavily muscled physique was bathed in the warm dim light of the embers as her chest rose and fell in a deep slumber with a soft vibrating hum of lightning mana crackling across her skin.
Silas sighed, pinching the bridge of his nose.
’Aeli really didn’t have to drug them up that bad,’ he thought, shaking his head at his Archon’s efficiency. ’This is just a logistical hazard.’
He kept his eyes firmly locked straight ahead, determined to walk past the couch without disrespecting the unconscious demigoddess.
Silas took three quiet steps past the edge of the velvet cushions.
WHOOOOOOSH!
Without a single warning, Thor’s calloused right hand shot upward from the couch.
Silas froze instantly, his combat instincts flaring, but the movement wasn’t an attack.
Thor’s hand hovered perfectly in the air, completely suspended by a humming field of anti-gravity lightning mana.
Her eyes were still firmly shut, her chest still rising and falling in deep drugged sleep.
’She is sleeping...’ Silas realized, staring at the hovering hand with wide, bewildered eyes. ’But she is levitating her arm subconsciously? Or... is she faking being asleep?’
Before Silas could step out of reach, the levitating hand drifted downward, landing squarely on top of his head.
Pat! Pat! Pat!
Thor’s incredibly powerful hand delivered three gentle headpats to the Sovereign Lord of Blessed Land, ruffling his dark hair with surprising tenderness.
"Mmmm..." Thor mumbled in her deep sleep-heavy voice as a small dopey smile crossing her lips. "Good boy..."

sentences.text: Silas’s casual demeanor vanished instantly as his blue eyes sharpened into terrifying slits.
The World Council, huh?
Silas gave a slow nod.
"Right," Silas murmured.
"It’s time for the meeting with the World Council."
Silas had been turning the prospect of this summit over in his mind for quite a long time now.
As he leaned back against the edge of the heavy wooden writing desk, watching Evelyn demolish a slice of rich chocolate cake, he felt a strange thrumming anticipation settling into his chest.
The time had finally come to set a concrete date...
He was more than prepared for it.
His internal calculations were already running through the myriad of political, economic, and territorial angles he could exploit.
The major objective here was incredibly simple: gain as much as humanly, or perhaps divinely, possible from them.
Given that he had successfully awakened a Mythic Gold Core... an anomaly of raw power that completely shattered the conventional scaling metrics of the Awakened Society...
Silas knew he was walking into this summit holding a royal flush.
He was going to have a field day with the global elites.

’It’s quite funny, really,’ Silas thought with a confident smirk playing at the corners of his lips. ’I’m actually feeling genuinely excited about walking into a room full of the highest powers in the Awakened Society and flipping their entire worldview completely upside down...’
Evelyn swallowed a massive bite of cake, chasing it with a spoonful of Kaelia’s vanilla ice cream.
"If we are going to do this," Evelyn stated, pointing her silver spoon directly at his chest, "a proper finalized date has to be set for the meeting.
The World Council doesn’t just clear their schedule for random upstarts, even if you did just gain a lot of support from the World.
I’ll coordinate the encrypted communications on my end, and I will accompany you to the summit in my disguise...
Though, I suppose I should mention it is going to be my very first time formally meeting the World Council in person, too."
She didn’t wait for his response, immediately going back to stuffing her face with a glazed doughnut.
Silas let out a slow sigh, crossing his arms over his chest.
Personally he would like to go as soon as possible but right now, he factored in the current logistical constraints of the Keep.
"The Princess is going to remain here in Blessed Land for exactly one week.
So, we have six more days of playing host to global royalty...
I think we should definitively schedule the summit for the day after she departs.
That way, our hands are clean, and we don’t risk any cross-contamination between her presence here and the Council’s intelligence network."
’How the hell did she even get here anyway?’ Evelyn thought but she didn’t ask, she really knew it was on some bullshit.
He tapped his chin thoughtfully.
"Perhaps we can arrange it to fall exactly on the day of a major pre-existing global meeting.
If they are already gathered, we can crash the party and meet all the key members simultaneously without having to track them down individually."
Evelyn paused mid-chew.
She set her spoon down on the silver platter, reaching into the deep pocket of her sleek dark tunic as she pulled out a high-end encrypted smartphone.
"I see..."
Her thumb swiftly swiping across the glass screen as she opened the Y app... the global network’s primary digital hub for news, Lord interactions, and Awakened rumors.
Her stormy gray eyes scanned the rapidly scrolling text.
"Well, look at this," Evelyn mumbled around a mouthful of dough, her eyes lighting up with calculating intrigue.
"It seems the World Council is actually hosting a massive summit in exactly a week and a few days.
They are gathering all the sitting Presidents of the major terrestrial countries and more importantly... the King and the Prince of the world are both confirmed to be in attendance."
Silas raised an eyebrow.

Even though the human realm was an incredibly modern, technologically advanced world complete with smartphones, digital streaming networks, and global internet access, the traditional archaic titles of "King" and "Prince of the World" were not merely ceremonial.
...They were titles forged in the fires of an apocalyptic crucible, at least that was what one would say.

Decades ago, when the dimensional barriers first began to fracture and the Sovereign Realm threatened to completely consume the Human world in a tidal wave of anomalous beasts and rogue mana, it was the Royal Family that had stepped forward to save humanity from utter extinction.
They had exhausted their vast generational wealth and leveraged unparalleled magical engineering to create colossal Suppression Engines.
These giant monolithic machines were planted deep within the bedrock of every major country on Earth.
The machines forcibly stabilized the dimensional tear, effectively preventing Sovereign Realm gates from opening randomly in populated cities.

They were the sole reason humanity had survived the initial integration as the entire modern world owed them an unpayable debt of blood and gratitude, which was exactly why the royal family retained unquestioned global authority.
’Plus they’re rich too...’
"There’s more," Evelyn noted, her thumb scrolling further down the Y feed.
"The tabloids and the Awakened forums are completely buzzing.
There are some unconfirmed rumors circulating that an illegitimate royal daughter is going to be formally introduced at this summit."
"An illegitimate girl?" Silas asked.
"That’s going to cause a massive media circus."
"Which makes it the perfect time for us to show up," Evelyn smiled, locking her phone screen and slipping it back into her pocket.
"It’s taking place a week and a few days from now.
Just after your little royal houseguest vacates the premises..."
Silas nodded, a sharp glint flashing in his blue eyes.
"Let’s meet the World Council then."
Evelyn smiled with a genuine happy expression that completely matched his own ambition.
"You’re smart, Silas.
I’ll give you that.
Crashing their most publicized high-security summit of the decade?
This should be perfect.
It establishes total dominance from the second we walk through the doors."
She tilted her head, wiping a smudge of icing from her cheek.
"As long as you’re not suddenly feeling chickened out?"
Silas scoffed, rolling his shoulders with effortless imposing confidence.
"How could I possibly feel chickened out?
They should be the ones feeling terrified..."
He pushed off the edge of the writing desk, standing to his full, towering height.
"Thank you for handling the communications, Evelyn and for everything else you’re doing behind the scenes."
Evelyn simply waved a hand dismissively, immediately grabbing another thick slice of chocolate cake and stuffing her mouth full.𝐟𝕣𝕖𝐞𝐰𝕖𝚋𝐧𝗼𝚟𝐞𝕝.𝗰𝐨𝐦
Silas watched her struggle to swallow the dry cake as he let out a quiet chuckle.
His right hand flared with a brilliant condensed flash of blue spatial mana and reaching into the dimensional pocket, he pulled out a cold bottle of sparkling spirit-water and extended it toward her.
Evelyn took the bottle gratefully, twisting the cap off and chugging it down to clear her throat.
She wiped her mouth with the back of her hand, letting out a satisfied breath.
"I will get in contact with the World Council’s secure terminal tonight and lay the groundwork," Evelyn promised, a smug satisfied smile touching her lips.
"And you are very welcome for the administrative carry, Silas."
"I’ll leave you to your sugar coma, then," Silas smirked, turning on his heel and walking toward the heavy wooden door.
"Hold on.
Stop," Evelyn commanded and Silas paused, his hand hovering mere inches from the brass doorknob.
He turned around with his brow furrowing slightly in question.
"What is it n—"
WHOOOOOOSH!
Evelyn didn’t speak, she moved instead.
Channeling the terrifying physical parameters of a top-tier Lord, Evelyn completely blurred out of existence.
She crossed the fifteen feet of plush carpeting separating them in seconds as she planted her pivot foot with bone-shattering force, her hips snapping violently.
’It’s time for my revenge...’
She executed a flawless and devastatingly fast front kick aimed squarely at Silas’s groin.
KRA-BOOOOOOM!
The impact was catastrophic.

The force of Evelyn’s reinforced boot connecting with its target generated a concussive shockwave as a violent ring of displaced air exploded outward from the point of impact, violently rustling the heavy velvet curtains and rattling the crystal ashtray on the table.
Evelyn stood with her leg fully extended with a smug on her face.

’That’s for terrifying me and compromising my secret identity, you arrogant bastard,’ she thought, fully expecting Silas to immediately drop to his knees, completely paralyzed by the agonizing pain of a powerful strike to the nuts.
But a second passed.

Evelyn’s smug grin slowly began to falter.

He hadn’t bent forward and he hadn’t flinched, hell he hadn’t even blinked.

Evelyn rapidly pulled her leg back, stumbling a half-step backward in disbelief.

What kind of monstrous unbreakable body does this man possess?!’
Silas simply stood there, brushing an invisible speck of dust from the front of his dark trousers.

chapters.title: Chapter 467: Vala’s Talent
paragraphs: Silas stood completely paralyzed, his brain flatlining as the Goddess of Thunder treated him like a golden retriever.
After delivering the final headpat, the anti-gravity mana completely dissipated.
Thor’s heavy arm dropped like a stone, smacking back down onto the velvet cushions as she rolled over, burying her face into the upholstery and resuming her deep rattling snores.
Silas stood in the dim light, staring at her naked back with his eye twitching slightly.
’I feel...’ Silas thought, an overwhelming mixture of terror and bewilderment washing over him. ’Like I have just been violated.’
Not wanting to risk another subconscious display of divine affection, Silas immediately broke into a brisk silent sprint.
He cleared the living room in seconds, rushing up the private spiraling wooden staircase before Thor felt the sudden sleepy urge to pat him some more.
Silas reached the highest floor of the Keep, pushing open the reinforced door to his private Office.
The room was quiet, completely insulated from the howling winter blizzard raging outside the thick glass windows.
"Haah..."
He walked across the room, letting out a long sigh of exhaustion as he collapsed into the high-backed leather chair behind his massive desk.

Resting perfectly in the center of the polished wood was a thick stack of logistical reports and a freshly updated bound ledger containing a comprehensive list of all the women currently residing in the territory.
"Right," Silas muttered, rubbing his tired eyes. "I have to sort them out into squads."
Tomorrow was going to be an incredibly labor-intensive day.
They had to deploy back to the Umbral Basin to excavate the raw Mana Diamonds and harvest the ores.
He needed to perfectly balance the infantry for perimeter defense, the heavy lifters for extraction, and the elemental casters for utility.
Silas picked up a quill, scanning the long list of names.

’Haah...’ Silas thought, feeling the creeping ache of the day’s constant combat and plans settling into his bones. ’I’ll join the expedition personally, of course but I am adding Kadi to my direct oversight group.’
Kadi was his second secretary, a brilliant and incredibly reliable Earth mage.
If she was in his group, she could effortlessly manipulate the cavern terrain, meaning he wouldn’t have to lift a single finger or swing his sword.
He could just sit back on a conjured stone chair and supervise.

’I want to laze around a bit tomorrow,’ Silas justified to himself, quickly scribbling Kadi’s name next to his own on the deployment manifest. ’Is it a crime for a Lord to want his second secretary in his group so he can slack off? Absolutely not...’
With the deployment logistics temporarily sorted, Silas set the quill down.
He leaned back in his leather chair with a sudden spark of anticipation reigniting his focus.
It was time to claim his reward.
Silas focused his mind, channeling a brief pulse of mana to interface with the System.

A sleek glowing blue holographic window materialized instantly over his desk as he navigated to his inventory, bringing up the specific tab that held the Mystery Box he had earned from completing the Hidden Mission.
The digital icon of the box hovered in the air, pulsing with an alluring enigmatic golden glow.
’I’m not sure I’ve ever seen anything about a reward like this on the global Lord forums...’ Silas thought, his eyes narrowing as he analyzed the icon.
The forums were usually incredibly thorough about datamining System mechanics, but Hidden Missions were notoriously unpredictable.
Regardless of the lack of information, he would gladly take free resources.
Silas reached out, pressing his index finger directly against the glowing holographic box.
Chime!
The box flared with a brilliant golden light... Silas squinted, leaning forward in anticipation, waiting for the grand reveal of his cosmic loot.
But a second later, the golden glow sputtered, fizzled out entirely, and died down as the box simply sat there, completely unopened and unchanged.
Silas blinked. He pulled his hand back, staring at the screen in pure confusion.
’What just happened?’ Silas thought. He reached out and pressed the box again.
Chime!
It glowed, and then immediately died down the moment he lifted his finger.
Silas’s eye twitched.
’Do I need to... spam the pressing?’ he wondered, a deep sense of irritation bubbling in his chest. ’What the hell is this, some kind of cheap mobile kid’s game?’
Grumbling under his breath about the System’s terrible user interface design, Silas raised his hand and began rapidly tapping his finger against the holographic box.
Chime! Chime! Chime! Chime!
With every rapid tap, the golden glow grew brighter and more unstable.
The digital box began to violently tremble on the screen, the lid shaking as if barely containing the immense pressure inside.
Chime! KRA-CRACK!
Suddenly, the box burst wide open in a shower of brilliant digital confetti and swirling golden light.
The glowing particle effects cleared, revealing two sleek floating reward cards hovering in the center of the interface.
[Congratulations, You Have Received:]
[- 25 Troop Summoning Tickets]
[- Tier 1 Warehouse Blueprint]
Silas leaned forward, his blue eyes carefully reading over the glowing text.
’25 Troop Summoning Tickets?’ Silas thought, a genuine smile of satisfaction crossing his face.
That was an incredibly solid reward.
That would allow him to tap into the summoning portal and pull twenty-five brand new fully materialized girls directly into the territory.
He desperately needed more hands to manage the rapidly expanding infrastructure, especially with the new agricultural zones and the massive cavalry corps requiring constant maintenance.
He shifted his gaze to the second reward.
’A Tier 1 Warehouse Blueprint...’ Silas mused, tapping his chin.

He would have to check into the specific material requirements and dimensions of the blueprint later, but building a dedicated magically reinforced warehouse where raw materials, ores, and monster parts were kept organized wasn’t a bad outcome at all.

’We can’t keep putting all of the raw ore and monster carcasses that could be used for weapons directly into the forge,’ Silas rationalized. ’It’s cluttering Thora’s workspace and creating a massive fire hazard. A dedicated storage facility will streamline our entire industrial supply chain...’
All in all, the rewards had come at the perfect time, considering they were preparing to launch a massive full-scale mining operation into the Umbral Basin tomorrow morning.
The twenty-five new summons could be immediately put to work processing the incoming stone and diamonds.
Silas let out a heavy sigh, running both hands through his dark hair as the weight of his responsibilities pressed down on him.
’That’s just more work to do at the end of the day...’ Silas thought, looking at the stacks of paperwork on his desk.𝗳𝚛𝗲𝕖𝚠𝚎𝚋𝗻𝗼𝕧𝗲𝐥.𝚌𝚘𝐦
Expanding the territory meant expanding the bureaucracy.
Managing the logistics, the housing, the food supplies, and the interpersonal dynamics of hundreds of people was a never-ending, exhausting grind.
But as he looked out the reinforced glass window, watching the swirling snow of the blizzard falling over the glowing, peaceful canopy of his Spirit Trees, a deep sense of pride anchored him.
Regardless of the exhaustion, he was completely ready for it.
That was exactly what it meant to be a Lord.
To carry the weight of the world, to build an unassailable sanctuary in the dark, and to protect the people who relied on him...
’Besides I love all of them, it’s the little I can do.’
RATTLE! RATTLE!

The quiet contemplative silence of the office was suddenly broken as the reinforced glass window on the far side of the room, completely battered by the freezing winds of the blizzard outside, suddenly began to tremble violently.
Before Silas could even reach for the hilt of his sword, the brass locking mechanism on the inside of the window frame clicked open with a sharp metallic clack, completely bypassed from the outside.
The window swung open inward as a howling freezing gust of snow and wind blasted into the warm office, scattering several loose logistical reports across the mahogany desk.
Silas didn’t flinch as he simply watched the windowsill.
Moving with the terrifying silence and frictionless grace of a phantom, a slender figure vaulted perfectly through the open window frame.
She executed a flawless mid-air acrobatic flip with her dark cloak snapping violently in the wind before she landed on the plush carpet without making a single sound.

Without missing a beat, the figure immediately spun around, pushing the heavy glass window shut and securing the brass lock, instantly cutting off the shrieking blizzard and plunging the office back into quiet warmth.
The intruder turned back around, her raven-black hair falling sharply around her beautiful face.
It was Vala.

The magic swordsman didn’t hesitate for a microsecond as she immediately dropped down onto one knee, bowing her head in perfect reverence, her dark eyes locked firmly onto the floorboards directly in front of his desk.
"I have arrived as requested, my Lord," Vala murmured. "Awaiting your command."
Silas leaned back in his heavy leather chair, the exhaustion of the day completely melting away as he looked down at his fiercely loyal Hiden Blade.
A warm affectionate smile spread across his handsome face.
"Welcome, Vala."
Silas leaned back in his high-backed leather chair, his piercing golden ringed blue eyes locked onto the slender, cloaked figure kneeling perfectly still on the plush mahogany carpet.
’She really has grown incredibly strong,’ Silas thought, his senses washing over Vala’s kneeling form.
He could feel the mana in the room reacting to her presence.
’I’m glad.’
Silas’s mind drifted back to the very first time they had met like this.
Just before the Lord War, back when he was utilizing the Upgrade System to elevate the base ranks of his summoned troops.
’If I remember correctly... She awakened a Magic Swordsman class.’
On the surface, it was a respected versatile combat role but Vala’s specific parameters were different.
’She has the potential to wield and seamlessly integrate up to ten distinct elemental affinities,’ Silas recalled with a smile of disbelief touching his lips.
That fact alone was a complete contradiction of conventional magical theory.

Mortal meridians were fragile... If a standard Awakened warrior attempted to circulate violently opposing elements like raw fire and ice through their body simultaneously, their mana channels would instantly detonate, cooking them alive from the inside out.
The only reason Silas could effortlessly wield multiple elements was because he possessed a Gold Core.
Vala on the other hand did not have a Gold Core.
She was a mortal woman yet, her spiritual architecture, her very genetic makeup, was a flawless conduit capable of cycling the elemental spectrum without tearing herself apart.
She was special...
’Naturally I wanted to make her S-Rank immediately... but thankfully I made a System Query first.’
He could upgrade her to S-Rank but after that, she could lose the opportunity to awaken her other elements... He didn’t want that for her which was why she was still a Magic Swordsman now.
’She’s very special...’
And that was exactly why he had pulled her from the standard vanguard formations.

It was why he had partnered her with Luna and Reina, sending her out into the freezing wastes to hunt monsters, partly because he was worried for Reina and more so for her to try as much as possible to awaken the rest.
It was why she was, and always would be, his Hidden Blade.
"You can raise your head, Vala," Silas commanded softly, the deep tone of his voice breaking the quiet of the office.
Vala immediately complied.
She lifted her chin, her raven-black hair falling back to reveal her strikingly beautiful features.
Her dark eyes met his, burning with a fierce devotion that never failed to send a faint thrill down Silas’s spine.
"I have already asked Reina about the mission," Silas continued, leaning forward and resting his elbows on the polished mahogany desk.
He interlaced his fingers, holding her gaze. "I am fully aware that the mission was a flawless success but I am not asking her right now... I am asking you."
Silas tilted his head slightly. "How did it feel out there, Vala?"
Vala didn’t hesitate.
"The combat was seamless, my Lord," she reported. "My internal mana circulation is expanding rapidly. I am growing stronger with every monster I execute."
She paused with an unshakeable determination hardening her dark eyes.
"I will master every element this world possesses," Vala vowed, her tone dipping into a quiet intensity. "And I will most certainly prove that you were right to choose me as your Hidden Blade."

paragraphs: ’Framed?’ Silas thought, his mind rapidly latching onto the word. ’Eluned was framed?...’
He wanted to pry.
The Lord within him demanded to know the names of the gods who held that grudge, to catalog the potential threats that might one day look toward Blessed Land seeking to finish what they started.
"Thor, what exactl—"
"Bah! No matter! Ancient rot is best left buried under the snow!"
Before Silas could finish his sentence, Thor violently snapped out of her melancholy.
The suffocating aura vanished, replaced instantly by her usual reckless vigor.
She shook out the dark spirit-wood robes, whipped them through the air with a loud crack, and shoved her massive arms straight through the sleeves.
She pulled the garment shut, tying the thick sash around her waist with a triumphant grunt.
"There!" Thor declared proudly, striking a heroic pose with her hands planted firmly on her hips, puffing out her chest. "Fits like a dwarven breastplate! Perfection!"
Silas blinked then, he looked down and then, he looked back up.
A slow incredulous smile crept across his face, followed by an unavoidable breathless chuckle.
"Thor," Silas said, stepping forward. "You put it on backward."
"What?" Thor barked, looking down at herself.

The high embroidered mandarin collar that was supposed to rest against the nape of her neck was currently choking her throat, while the deep overlapping front panels were flapping uselessly against her spine, exposing the entirety of her massive muscular back and the twin ridges of her shoulder blades to the cold air.
"Nonsense!" Thor scoffed, pulling at the suffocating collar. "The cloth covers the meat, doesn’t it? It functions!"
"You’re going to strangle yourself the moment you bend over," Silas laughed, walking up behind her. "Stand still... Let me fix it before you rip the seams that Eluned spent time weaving."
Thor grunted, but she obediently dropped her arms, allowing Silas to step into her personal space.
Silas untied the rough haphazard knot she had made with the sash, sliding his hands along the thick textured fabric of the robes.
To adjust the shoulders, he had to reach around her sides, stepping exceptionally close to the towering demigoddess.
The heat radiating off her skin was staggering like standing before an open blast furnace in Thora’s foundry.
As he pulled the fabric forward, rotating the robes so the collar fell naturally, his arms brushed lightly against the sides of her heavy unconstrained chest.
Even beneath the thick weave of the spirit-wood fibers, the staggering mass of her bust was impossible to ignore.
"You know," Silas muttered under his breath, his hands working the delicate clasps at her front, "for a warrior who spends her life swinging a divine warhammer, your chest really is large."
Thor threw her head back, letting out a short amused snort that rustled the stray hairs on his forehead.

"Gwahaha! And what of it?" she replied, looking down her nose at him with an unapologetic smirk. "A weak, flat chest carries no breath for battle! These lungs have swallowed the winds of cosmic tempests, mortal! They need room to expand! I like them just fine as they are."
She tilted her head, her storm-blue eyes narrowing into a sharp playful slits as she watched his hands work the front of her robes.
"Tell me, Lord of Blessed Land," Thor purred, her voice dropping into a deep vibrating rumble that Silas felt in the soles of his boots. "Do you like them as well?"
Silas paused.
His fingers rested lightly against the dark sash. He looked up, his dark eyes meeting the ancient electric blue gaze of Odin’s daughter.
He didn’t flinch, nor did he offer a simpering cowardly denial.
"They are magnificent," Silas answered honestly, pulling the sash tight and securing it with a clean efficient knot. "A man would have to be blind or dead not to appreciate them."
"GWAHAHAHAHA!"
Thor erupted in a roar of triumphant, boisterous laughter that shook the dust from the ceiling rafters... She was thoroughly delighted by his blunt honesty.

"Good lad! A man who speaks his mind without choking on his own tongue!" Thor shouted, grinning wildly as she raised a massive iron-gauntleted hand to give him an affectionate encouraging pat on the shoulder. "I knew you had—"
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The iron gauntlet, Járngreipr, carried the full unmitigated weight of a divine warrior who had forgotten that she was wearing a belt that doubled her strength.
The moment her hand made contact with Silas’s right shoulder, the physics of the room completely detonated.
A shockwave the color of violent violet lightning exploded outward as the air violently compressed, shrieking like a dying jet engine, and Silas ceased to exist on the living room floor.
SHATTER-CRASH!
Silas became a human artillery shell.
He shot backward in a horizontal blur of speed, bypassing the hallway and smashing violently through the reinforced iron-banded oak front doors of the Keep!
The four-inch-thick timber splintered into a million jagged shards, the heavy iron hinges ripping clean out of the stone masonry with an ear-splitting screech.
Silas sailed through the blizzard air for forty yards, hurtling across the frozen courtyard before crashing into the deep knee-high snowbank near the central plaza with a muffled explosive thud.
Snow flew thirty feet into the howling winter air, raining down in a massive glittering plume.
Silence descended over the courtyard, save for the howling wind and slowly, the snow shifted.
A broad dark-robed hand emerged from the white drift, planting itself firmly against the frozen cobblestones beneath.
Silas pushed himself upright, violently shaking his head to dislodge the half-ton of freezing powder that had buried him.

His dark robes were caked in white, his hair was plastered to his forehead, and his right shoulder was throbbing with a dull ache that only a Mythic Gold Core could have absorbed without his entire skeleton turning to fine porcelain dust.
"Gods above..." Silas wheezed, coughing out a mouthful of fresh snow.

He rolled his right shoulder, the joint popping with a terrifying sound as his internal gold core pulsed, flooding his flesh with divine vitality and instantly knitting the bruised muscle fibers back together.
’If I weren’t Gold core, my entire upper torso would be a red paste on the courtyard stones.’
Heavy crunching footsteps echoed through the storm.
Thor stepped out through the gaping jagged hole where the Keep’s front doors used to be.
She was wading through the knee-deep snow completely unfazed by the sub-zero wind biting at her bare ankles as her wild blonde hair whipped furiously behind her.
Her face was twisted into a look of genuine, almost childlike panic.

"Silas!" Thor bellowed, jogging toward him with her iron gauntlets raised in surrender. "Lad! By the blood of Ymir, I am sorry! I forgot to suppress the gauntlets! Megingjörð was still feeding feedback into my strike! Are your bones whole?!"
Silas hauled himself entirely out of the snowbank, brushing the thick white flakes from his robes with exaggerated stoic patience.
Behind Thor, a soft, ethereal light began to bleed from the shattered doorframe of the Keep.
The splintered fragments of wood, infused with territory’s living mana, began to tremble.
Like living vines, the jagged pieces pulled themselves back together, the iron hinges snapping smoothly back into the stone mortar with a series of clean organic clicks.
Within three seconds, the front doors had completely regenerated, sealing the Keep’s interior once more from the freezing elements.
Silas exhaled a long cloud of white steam, looking at the towering demigoddess who stood a full head taller than him.

"I am fine, Thor," Silas muttered, his voice flat, though his eye twitched slightly. "My core is dense enough to take a beating but next time you feel the urge to show affection, a simple verbal compliment will suffice."
He glanced past her, looking toward the sealed front doors.
"Where is Mjölnir?" Silas asked, noticing the empty loop on her belt. "Did you leave a divine artifact resting on the living room floorboards?"
Thor waved a dismissive iron-clad hand through the howling wind, completely unconcerned.

"Bah! It sits upon the velvet rug where I dropped it," Thor snorted. "Mjölnir is not a stray dog... it doesn’t wander off into the snow. Besides, who in this realm could possibly lift it to steal it? Even if that giant ox-demon from the northern peaks wandered into your hall, he’d sooner snap his spine than budge the handle an inch. It will come to my hand when I call it so I do not need to clutch it like a nervous child clutching a wooden doll."
She paused, crossing her massive arms over her chest, the dark spirit-robes stretching tight across her brawn.
Her storm-blue eyes scanned the darkened, snowy paths of the settlement.
"Where is everyone?" Thor demanded, her stomach letting out a low rumbling growl that sounded eerily like distant thunder. "The Keep is a tomb... Did that elven girl put the entire army to sleep?"
Silas shook the remaining snow from his sleeves, pointing a finger toward the sprawling illuminated complex situated on the eastern side of the inner wall.

"Everyone completed their work hours ago," Silas explained. "Right now, most of them are packed into the Mess Hall inside the Barracks. They’ve tapped three barrels of dwarven stout, roasted a lot of boars and we’re doing a feast to celebrate the promotion of the scouts."
The moment the words stout and feast left his mouth, Thor went unnervingly still.
Silas watched her closely.

The boisterous, loud-mouthed warrior’s expression visibly locked up as a subtle involuntary twitch pulled at the left corner of her eye, her nostrils flaring as if she could already smell the roasted pork through three miles of driving blizzard.
Her pupils dilated into pure lightning.
"Alcohol..." Thor whispered, the word carrying more reverence than any prayer she had ever uttered. "Roasted boar..."
Silas barely had time to point toward the Barracks entrance.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The snow beneath Thor’s bare feet vaporized.

A concussive pressure wave tore across the central plaza, blasting a clean sixty-foot trench straight through the three-foot snowdrifts as the God of Thunder launched herself forward like an intercontinental ballistic missile.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHAHA!"
Her booming thunderous laughter echoed across the entire territory, drowning out the howling blizzard as her massive dark-robed frame blurred through the storm.
"STAND ASIDE, MORTALS! TIME TO GO DRINK!"
BANG!

The reinforced timber doors of the Barracks were violently thrown wide, slamming against the stone walls with enough force to rattle the windowpanes, and Thor vanished into the warm torch-lit interior, swallowed instantly by the roaring cheers, clinking tankards, and chaotic singing of the Blessed Land women.
Silas stood alone in the frozen trench, the snow gently falling onto his dark hair.
He let out a slow exhausted breath, the white vapor trailing into the sky.

’These gods...’ Silas thought, shaking his head with a tired wry smirk. ’Are complicated creatures... Capable of shattering a continent in the morning, and reduced to feral beasts by the promise of free alcohol by nightfall.’
Before the trench could fill with fresh snow, the heavy doors of the Barracks clicked open a fraction.
Slipping out into the freezing wind, clutching a thick fur-lined cloak tightly around her stout muscled frame, was Thora.
The dwarven forge master had clearly just extracted herself from the center of the revelry.
Her braided head was flecked with white foam from dwarven stout, and her cheeks were flushed a deep healthy crimson from the roaring hearths inside.
She spotted Silas standing in the cleared path and began marching toward him, her heavy iron-toed boots crunching rhythmically through the snow.
Silas watched her approach, feeling a pang of genuine guilt.
’Ah yes... She did say it was important.’
He knew how sacred post-battle drinking was to the dwarven clans, as Thora explained, considering she was a Princess too.
To pull Thora away from an active keg of ale was an offense that usually resulted in a broken nose.
’But the warehouse is important too.’
Thora stopped three feet in front of him, planting her thick calloused hands onto her hips and folding her arms across her leather apron.
Her breath puffed out in heavy irritated clouds of steam.

"Lord Silas," Thora grunted. "I understand that logistics wait for no man. I understand that the expansion of Blessed Land requires steady infrastructure, and that a proper storage depot is the backbone of any serious mining campaign but I want it on the formal record... pulling a dwarf away from freshly tapped stout while the meat is still dripping on the spit is a crime against the ancestors!"
Silas didn’t argue.
Instead, Silas took a single step forward, reached out with his right hand, gently caught the rough soot-stained chin of the dwarven forge master, and leaned down.
He pressed his lips firmly against hers and Thora’s eyes blew wide open.
’Thora is a really easy woman though...’
Her thick eyelids fluttered, her entire body freezing mid-rant.
The fiery stubborn dwarf went completely rigid, her brain stalling out in a haze of sudden unexpected sensory overload.
Silas lingered for two slow heartbeats, tasting the bitter tang of dwarven stout and the trace of forge-ash on her lips, before smoothly pulling back with a calm handsome smirk.
He didn’t say a word.
Silas simply turned on his heel, his dark robes swirling in the wind, and began walking toward the western perimeter of the inner territory.
"Follow me, Thora," Silas called over his shoulder. "We have work to do."

The heat radiating off her skin was staggering like standing before an open blast furnace in Thora’s foundry.
As he pulled the fabric forward, rotating the robes so the collar fell naturally, his arms brushed lightly against the sides of her heavy unconstrained chest.
Even beneath the thick weave of the spirit-wood fibers, the staggering mass of her bust was impossible to ignore.

She tilted her head, her storm-blue eyes narrowing into a sharp playful slits as she watched his hands work the front of her robes.
"Tell me, Lord of Blessed Land," Thor purred, her voice dropping into a deep vibrating rumble that Silas felt in the soles of his boots.
"Do you like them as well?"
Silas paused.
His fingers rested lightly against the dark sash.
He looked up, his dark eyes meeting the ancient electric blue gaze of Odin’s daughter.
He didn’t flinch, nor did he offer a simpering cowardly denial.
"They are magnificent," Silas answered honestly, pulling the sash tight and securing it with a clean efficient knot.
"A man would have to be blind or dead not to appreciate them."
"GWAHAHAHAHA!"
Thor erupted in a roar of triumphant, boisterous laughter that shook the dust from the ceiling rafters...
She was thoroughly delighted by his blunt honesty.
"Good lad!
A man who speaks his mind without choking on his own tongue!" Thor shouted, grinning wildly as she raised a massive iron-gauntleted hand to give him an affectionate encouraging pat on the shoulder.
"I knew you had—"
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The iron gauntlet, Járngreipr, carried the full unmitigated weight of a divine warrior who had forgotten that she was wearing a belt that doubled her strength.
The moment her hand made contact with Silas’s right shoulder, the physics of the room completely detonated.
A shockwave the color of violent violet lightning exploded outward as the air violently compressed, shrieking like a dying jet engine, and Silas ceased to exist on the living room floor.
SHATTER-CRASH!
Silas became a human artillery shell.
He shot backward in a horizontal blur of speed, bypassing the hallway and smashing violently through the reinforced iron-banded oak front doors of the Keep!
The four-inch-thick timber splintered into a million jagged shards, the heavy iron hinges ripping clean out of the stone masonry with an ear-splitting screech.
Silas sailed through the blizzard air for forty yards, hurtling across the frozen courtyard before crashing into the deep knee-high snowbank near the central plaza with a muffled explosive thud.
Snow flew thirty feet into the howling winter air, raining down in a massive glittering plume.
