chapters.title: Chapter 472: Warehouse Building [II]
paragraphs: Left standing in the snow, Thora blinked rapidly.
Her calloused fingers slowly rose to touch her lips, her ears twitching as a brilliant fiery blush spread from the tips of her ears down to her collarbone, out-shining the alcohol flush.
An amused grin cracked across her soot-stained face.
’By the stone...’ Thora thought, her heart hammering against her ribs like a hydraulic forge hammer. ’What a smooth-talking criminal... He knows exactly how to handle a stubborn woman.’
This was one of the many reasons she wanted to be bred by her Lord.
"Oi! Wait for me, you cheeky bastard!" Thora yelled, breaking into a brisk rolling jog.
She caught up to his long strides in seconds.
Without asking for permission, Thora leaped upward with surprising dwarven agility, grabbing the thick fabric of his robes and scrambling up his back like a squirrel scaling a sturdy pine tree.
She hauled herself up, planting her boots securely on his broad shoulders and sitting comfortably atop his collar, casually resting her elbows on top of his dark head.
Silas didn’t even break stride as his physical constitution carried her dense dwarven weight as if she were made of dry leaves... as usal.
"Carry your master builder, Lord Silas!" Thora cackled into his hair. "If I’m missing out on my ale, my boots aren’t touching the slush!"
"Fair enough," Silas chuckled, his boots crunching steadily through the snow.
Together, they moved deeper into the western quadrant of Blessed Land.
They passed the glowing doors of the Library, where the silhouette of some girls could be seen reading.
They navigated past the sprawling Multi-Room Apartments that Silas had constructed during the previous expansion phase to house the girls.
Finally, they arrived at a wide vacant expanse of flat ground situated barely fifty yards from the towering black obsidian walls that formed the primary boundary of the territory.
The ground here was shielded from the worst of the wind by the height of the outer fortifications, and the earth mana from the nearby Spirit Tree roots kept the soil relatively stable.
Silas came to a halt, letting out a small breath.

"This should be a good place to put a warehouse, shouldn’t it?" Silas asked, looking out over the open, empty field. "It has direct wide-road access to the primary gates, so when the Phase 2 Golems return from Sector KB-22 and the other mines loaded with raw ore, they won’t have to navigate through the residential side or crowd the forge entrance."

From her perch on his shoulders, Thora leaned forward, her sharp dwarven eyes scanning the topography, measuring the drainage angles and the distance to the outer walls with innate instinctual precision.

"Aye," Thora nodded, knocking her knuckles approvingly against his skull. "Good ground with solid bedrock sitting barely four feet below the topsoil. It won’t sink under the weight of three thousand tons of unrefined ores and Mana Diamonds so drop the foundation here, my Lord."
Silas took a deep centering breath.
He closed his eyes, extending his consciousness into the reality of the territory.
In his chest, his Gold Core hummed with a deep melodic vibration, connecting his soul directly to the authority of the Lord Interface.
’Open Interface... Build Tab.’
VUUUUUUUUUM.
A wash of brilliant condensed azure energy rippled outward from Silas’s frame, lightly rustling the hem of his dark robes and casting a vibrant digital reflection across the snow.
Before his eyes, the clean holographic displays of the System appeared.
He navigated through his personal inventory, his thoughts zeroing in on the newly acquired reward from the Hidden Mission.
’Select: Basic Logistics Warehouse Blueprint...’
PZZZZT-FLASH!
Instantly, the system window expanded, accompanied by a massive, semi-translucent 3D wireframe diagram that projected directly onto the snowy field before them.
The glowing blue wireframe stood forty feet tall and over eighty feet wide.

It was an intricate rotating holographic skeleton of the proposed structure, showcasing the structural load-bearing beams, the thick perimeter foundation, the high-clearance timber trusses, and the wide double-bay entry doors designed specifically for heavy transport.
Silas raised his right hand, his fingers smoothly manipulating the holographic projection in mid-air.
With subtle gestures, he rotated the wireframe thirty degrees to the east, aligning the primary loading bay perfectly with the main cobblestone transit road.

"Oho!" Thora gasped from his shoulders, leaning down so far her cheek brushed against his cheek as she stared at the glowing blue lines. "Look at that modular grid! The timber truss distribution is bloody brilliant! Who needs paper and ink when you can paint the bones of a building right onto the dirt? That is remarkably clean engineering, my Lord!"
As Silas locked the orientation into place, the text of the System prompt crystallized before him.
[Unlocked Blueprint:] Basic Logistics Warehouse - Tier 1
[Type:] Logistics / Storage Facility
[Materials Required:] 300 Refined Stone, 400 Lumber, 50 Tempered Iron.

[Description:] A standard dry-storage facility designed to store raw ores, building materials, and non-perishable resources safely out of the elements. Features reinforced stone perimeter walls to deter pests, heavy timber pallet racking for modular stacking, and an iron-bolted double door wide enough for small transport carts. Reduces resource degradation caused by extreme weather and frees up space in primary production hubs.
Silas studied the parameters, his analytical mind thoroughly satisfied.

’It’s a remarkably solid baseline,’ Silas evaluated. ’For a Tier 1 structure, it addresses every immediate logistical bottleneck we need... There are no advanced magical arrays or expansion fields yet, but that doesn’t matter in the slightest. The moment the physical frame settles, I’m dumping raw UP straight into the Upgrade System to elevate it directly to Tier 3.’
He glanced toward the horizon, where the lights of the guest house flickered in the blizzard.

’There’s still some time before I can comfortably upgrade the new recruits with UP,’ Silas mused carefully. ’Evelyn and the rest of the girls from the Unmovable Wall are still residing in the Keep and the Princess is observing everything with those sharp royal eyes... I need to wait until their visit concludes and they depart Blessed Land before I start triggering mass evolutions. The fewer prying eyes watching my core mechanics, the better...’
Silas lowered his gaze back to the glowing blue interface, checking the live inventory ledger.
[Refined Stone:] [Available] / 300 (Ready)
[Lumber:] [Available] / 400 (Ready)
[Tempered Iron:] [Available] / 50 (Ready)
[Would you like to build?]𝘧𝓇𝑒𝑒𝑤ℯ𝑏𝓃𝘰𝑣ℯ𝘭.𝘤ℴ𝘮
[Y / N]
Silas looked at the green, glowing "Ready" markers and let out a soft dry chuckle.
’Thanks Ev...’
Earlier that evening, before Thor had awakened and before he had descended to the living room, he had gone back to Evelyn.

Between her bouts of inhaling chocolate cake and threatening to kick him in the groin, he had successfully leveraged their territorial trade agreement to borrow the necessary deficit of Refined Stone and Tempered Iron directly from her storage rings.

’A Lord borrowing raw iron from his ally just to erect a wooden shed,’ Silas thought with a small sigh slipping past his lips. ’We really need to start producing and refining these foundational materials on our own.’
He raised his eyes to the towering blue wireframe hovering over the snow as his mind locked onto the glowing prompt.
’Build!’
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!

The atmospheric pressure violently ruptured as the glowing 3D wireframe, hovering ten feet above the earth, suddenly dropped like a lead weight, slamming into the frozen ground with a deafening concussive sound.
The moment the blueprint touched the soil, the digital blue lines violently flared with blinding golden light.
The snow covering the eighty-foot expanse was instantly displaced, blasted outward in a perfect, circular shockwave of pressurized air that whipped Silas’s dark robes violently around his legs.
KRRRRRR-CRUNCH!
Raw matter began pouring in from the ether, manifesting out of thin air in a terrifying beautiful display of territorial creation magic.
Massive rectangular blocks of dense grey Refined Stone materialized out of golden spatial fissures, slamming into the earth with earth-shaking impacts.
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!
The foundation laid itself in seconds, interlocking with microscopic precision to form a seamless moisture-proof slab.
Immediately following the stone, colossal beams of cured heavy Lumber dropped from the sky, pivoting on invisible axes and slotting into the mortise-and-tenon joints with deafening, hydraulic snaps.
THWACK-THWACK-THWACK!
Iron brackets, glowing cherry-red with residual friction, manifested along the stress points, bolting the massive timber trusses together.
The high-clearance roof assembled itself at breakneck speed, heavy slate shingles sliding across the rafters and locking down against the howling blizzard.
Finally, two colossal iron-banded double doors slammed shut at the primary loading bay with the heavy master latch dropping into place with a definitive sound.
CLACK!
The blinding golden light rapidly retracted, sinking into the newly forged walls.

The wind howled, swirling a fresh dusting of white snow against the dark, imposing stone base of the completed facility as standing eighty feet wide, forty feet tall, and solid as a mountain fortress, the Tier 1 Basic Logistics Warehouse stood proudly against the winter storm.
Silence returned to the western wall.
Sitting atop Silas’s broad shoulders, her jaw slack and her soot-stained hands still resting dumbly against his dark hair, Thora stared at the fully materialized building.
Her breath puffed out in a single stunned cloud of vapor.
"...Woah."
The winter wind shrieked against the towering obsidian perimeter of Blessed Land, whipping plumes of dry powdery snow across the dark cobblestone pathways.
Silas stood with his boots planted firmly in the slush, the dark fabric of his cultivator-style robes snapping rhythmically against his calves.
On his shoulders, Thora remained perched like an oversized gargoyle, her soot-stained hands resting comfortably on his dark hair while her eyes were wide with awe.

"By the stone..." Thora breathed again, her voice full of of genuine disbelief as she stared at the newly materialized Tier 1 structure. "Everytime Lord Silas... Every single time I see this, it never fails to send a chill down my spine. Watching timber and granite knit together out of thin air like living bone... it’s bloody unnatural. Beautiful, but unnatural as hell."
Silas let out a quiet amused breath that misted into the freezing air as a smirk tugged at the corner of his mouth.
He had summoned strong women and brought structures into reality with a mere flick of his wrist, yet the effortless magic of territorial creation was something he would never truly get used to.
’Haah...’
It was staggering how easily the world bent to a Lord’s command when the resources were paid in full but Silas was not a man to let early success cloud his vision.
A simple dry-storage shed made of pine trusses and standard iron bolts was fine for a frontier outpost, but Blessed Land was rapidly evolving into an empire...

’A simple wooden warehouse isn’t going to cut it,’ Silas thought, his blue eyes narrowing with quiet ambition. ’Not when we’re about to crack open all the mines we can and pull a lot of ores from the earth so we still have to upgrade it.’

"It’s decent enough for a baseline," Silas said aloud, reaching up to tap Thora’s steel-toed boot where it rested near his collarbone. "Keeps the snow off the timber and gives the carts a roof but it’s raw and unfinished."
Thora snorted, leaning forward so heavily that her leather apron pressed against the back of his head.
"Decent? Lad, that timber is cured cedar and the mortar is set tighter than a dwarven vault! What do you mean, ’unfinished’?"
"I mean," Silas chuckled, "it can be far better than this... Much better."
Thora paused, and then a wide, knowing grin spread across her soot-streaked cheeks.
Her amber eyes gleamed with raw greed for high-tier craftsmanship.
She had witnessed the miracle of the Beast Pavilion’s transformation from a distance... she knew the terrifying ungodly power her Lord possessed when it came to reshaping reality.
"Right then," Thora murmured, crossing her muscular arms over her chest and settling back into her perch. "Show me what your strange gods have in store, Lord Silas. Let’s see this ’better.’"
Silas took a slow centering breath.
He closed his eyes for a fraction of a second, his consciousness diving inward, brushing past the raging furnace of his Mythic Gold Core.
’System~ Let’s get to upgrading~’
VUUUUUUUUUM!
A wash of pale azure light rippled outward from his chest, illuminating the falling snow like a cloud of glowing blue fireflies.
Silas opened his eyes as the familiar semi-translucent holographic glass materialized before him, hovering silently against the backdrop of the wooden warehouse.

’It shouldn’t be too costly...’ Silas mused inwardly, his fingers twitching slightly as he prepared to navigate the prompts. ’Skipping a tier always stings, but with the UP reserves we’ve banked from clearing the goblins and subduing the basin monsters, we have plenty of room to breathe.’
The interface shifted, the text sharpening into crystal-clear focus.
[Logistics Warehouse]
[Tier: 1 Construct (Common)]
[Durability: 500 / 500]
[Status: Operational.]
[Upgrade System: Would you like to upgrade Tier 1 Basic Logistics Warehouse directly to Tier 3 Sovereign Distribution Nexus?]
[Cost: 320 UP]
[Y / N]
Silas stared at the glowing blue letters floating in the freezing air, his eyebrows climbing toward his hairline.
For a second, the composure of the Lord cracked, and a strangled breathless chuckle slipped past his teeth.

sentences.text: Left standing in the snow, Thora blinked rapidly.
Her calloused fingers slowly rose to touch her lips, her ears twitching as a brilliant fiery blush spread from the tips of her ears down to her collarbone, out-shining the alcohol flush.
An amused grin cracked across her soot-stained face.
’By the stone...’ Thora thought, her heart hammering against her ribs like a hydraulic forge hammer. ’What a smooth-talking criminal...
He knows exactly how to handle a stubborn woman.’
This was one of the many reasons she wanted to be bred by her Lord.
"Oi!
Wait for me, you cheeky bastard!" Thora yelled, breaking into a brisk rolling jog.
She caught up to his long strides in seconds.
Without asking for permission, Thora leaped upward with surprising dwarven agility, grabbing the thick fabric of his robes and scrambling up his back like a squirrel scaling a sturdy pine tree.
She hauled herself up, planting her boots securely on his broad shoulders and sitting comfortably atop his collar, casually resting her elbows on top of his dark head.
Silas didn’t even break stride as his physical constitution carried her dense dwarven weight as if she were made of dry leaves... as usal.
"Carry your master builder, Lord Silas!" Thora cackled into his hair.
"If I’m missing out on my ale, my boots aren’t touching the slush!"
"Fair enough," Silas chuckled, his boots crunching steadily through the snow.
Together, they moved deeper into the western quadrant of Blessed Land.
They passed the glowing doors of the Library, where the silhouette of some girls could be seen reading.
They navigated past the sprawling Multi-Room Apartments that Silas had constructed during the previous expansion phase to house the girls.
Finally, they arrived at a wide vacant expanse of flat ground situated barely fifty yards from the towering black obsidian walls that formed the primary boundary of the territory.
The ground here was shielded from the worst of the wind by the height of the outer fortifications, and the earth mana from the nearby Spirit Tree roots kept the soil relatively stable.
Silas came to a halt, letting out a small breath.
"This should be a good place to put a warehouse, shouldn’t it?" Silas asked, looking out over the open, empty field.

"It has direct wide-road access to the primary gates, so when the Phase 2 Golems return from Sector KB-22 and the other mines loaded with raw ore, they won’t have to navigate through the residential side or crowd the forge entrance."

From her perch on his shoulders, Thora leaned forward, her sharp dwarven eyes scanning the topography, measuring the drainage angles and the distance to the outer walls with innate instinctual precision.
"Aye," Thora nodded, knocking her knuckles approvingly against his skull.
"Good ground with solid bedrock sitting barely four feet below the topsoil.
It won’t sink under the weight of three thousand tons of unrefined ores and Mana Diamonds so drop the foundation here, my Lord."
Silas took a deep centering breath.
He closed his eyes, extending his consciousness into the reality of the territory.
In his chest, his Gold Core hummed with a deep melodic vibration, connecting his soul directly to the authority of the Lord Interface.
’Open Interface...
Build Tab.’
VUUUUUUUUUM.
A wash of brilliant condensed azure energy rippled outward from Silas’s frame, lightly rustling the hem of his dark robes and casting a vibrant digital reflection across the snow.
Before his eyes, the clean holographic displays of the System appeared.
He navigated through his personal inventory, his thoughts zeroing in on the newly acquired reward from the Hidden Mission.
’Select: Basic Logistics Warehouse Blueprint...’
PZZZZT-FLASH!
Instantly, the system window expanded, accompanied by a massive, semi-translucent 3D wireframe diagram that projected directly onto the snowy field before them.
The glowing blue wireframe stood forty feet tall and over eighty feet wide.

It was an intricate rotating holographic skeleton of the proposed structure, showcasing the structural load-bearing beams, the thick perimeter foundation, the high-clearance timber trusses, and the wide double-bay entry doors designed specifically for heavy transport.
Silas raised his right hand, his fingers smoothly manipulating the holographic projection in mid-air.
With subtle gestures, he rotated the wireframe thirty degrees to the east, aligning the primary loading bay perfectly with the main cobblestone transit road.
"Oho!" Thora gasped from his shoulders, leaning down so far her cheek brushed against his cheek as she stared at the glowing blue lines.
"Look at that modular grid!
The timber truss distribution is bloody brilliant!
Who needs paper and ink when you can paint the bones of a building right onto the dirt?
That is remarkably clean engineering, my Lord!"
As Silas locked the orientation into place, the text of the System prompt crystallized before him.
[Unlocked Blueprint:] Basic Logistics Warehouse - Tier 1
[Type:] Logistics / Storage Facility
[Materials Required:] 300 Refined Stone, 400 Lumber, 50 Tempered Iron.
[Description:] A standard dry-storage facility designed to store raw ores, building materials, and non-perishable resources safely out of the elements.
Features reinforced stone perimeter walls to deter pests, heavy timber pallet racking for modular stacking, and an iron-bolted double door wide enough for small transport carts.
Reduces resource degradation caused by extreme weather and frees up space in primary production hubs.
Silas studied the parameters, his analytical mind thoroughly satisfied.
’It’s a remarkably solid baseline,’ Silas evaluated. ’For a Tier 1 structure, it addresses every immediate logistical bottleneck we need...
There are no advanced magical arrays or expansion fields yet, but that doesn’t matter in the slightest.
The moment the physical frame settles, I’m dumping raw UP straight into the Upgrade System to elevate it directly to Tier 3.’
He glanced toward the horizon, where the lights of the guest house flickered in the blizzard.

’There’s still some time before I can comfortably upgrade the new recruits with UP,’ Silas mused carefully. ’Evelyn and the rest of the girls from the Unmovable Wall are still residing in the Keep and the Princess is observing everything with those sharp royal eyes...
I need to wait until their visit concludes and they depart Blessed Land before I start triggering mass evolutions.
The fewer prying eyes watching my core mechanics, the better...’
Silas lowered his gaze back to the glowing blue interface, checking the live inventory ledger.
[Refined Stone:] [Available] / 300 (Ready)
[Lumber:] [Available] / 400 (Ready)
[Tempered Iron:] [Available] / 50 (Ready)
[Would you like to build?]𝘧𝓇𝑒𝑒𝑤ℯ𝑏𝓃𝘰𝑣ℯ𝘭.𝘤ℴ𝘮
[Y / N]
Silas looked at the green, glowing "Ready" markers and let out a soft dry chuckle.
’Thanks Ev...’
Earlier that evening, before Thor had awakened and before he had descended to the living room, he had gone back to Evelyn.

Between her bouts of inhaling chocolate cake and threatening to kick him in the groin, he had successfully leveraged their territorial trade agreement to borrow the necessary deficit of Refined Stone and Tempered Iron directly from her storage rings.

’A Lord borrowing raw iron from his ally just to erect a wooden shed,’ Silas thought with a small sigh slipping past his lips. ’We really need to start producing and refining these foundational materials on our own.’
He raised his eyes to the towering blue wireframe hovering over the snow as his mind locked onto the glowing prompt.
’Build!’
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!

The atmospheric pressure violently ruptured as the glowing 3D wireframe, hovering ten feet above the earth, suddenly dropped like a lead weight, slamming into the frozen ground with a deafening concussive sound.
The moment the blueprint touched the soil, the digital blue lines violently flared with blinding golden light.
The snow covering the eighty-foot expanse was instantly displaced, blasted outward in a perfect, circular shockwave of pressurized air that whipped Silas’s dark robes violently around his legs.
KRRRRRR-CRUNCH!
Raw matter began pouring in from the ether, manifesting out of thin air in a terrifying beautiful display of territorial creation magic.
Massive rectangular blocks of dense grey Refined Stone materialized out of golden spatial fissures, slamming into the earth with earth-shaking impacts.
CLANG!
CLANG!
CLANG!
The foundation laid itself in seconds, interlocking with microscopic precision to form a seamless moisture-proof slab.
Immediately following the stone, colossal beams of cured heavy Lumber dropped from the sky, pivoting on invisible axes and slotting into the mortise-and-tenon joints with deafening, hydraulic snaps.
THWACK-THWACK-THWACK!
Iron brackets, glowing cherry-red with residual friction, manifested along the stress points, bolting the massive timber trusses together.
The high-clearance roof assembled itself at breakneck speed, heavy slate shingles sliding across the rafters and locking down against the howling blizzard.
Finally, two colossal iron-banded double doors slammed shut at the primary loading bay with the heavy master latch dropping into place with a definitive sound.
CLACK!
The blinding golden light rapidly retracted, sinking into the newly forged walls.

The wind howled, swirling a fresh dusting of white snow against the dark, imposing stone base of the completed facility as standing eighty feet wide, forty feet tall, and solid as a mountain fortress, the Tier 1 Basic Logistics Warehouse stood proudly against the winter storm.
Silence returned to the western wall.
Sitting atop Silas’s broad shoulders, her jaw slack and her soot-stained hands still resting dumbly against his dark hair, Thora stared at the fully materialized building.
Her breath puffed out in a single stunned cloud of vapor.
"...Woah."
The winter wind shrieked against the towering obsidian perimeter of Blessed Land, whipping plumes of dry powdery snow across the dark cobblestone pathways.
Silas stood with his boots planted firmly in the slush, the dark fabric of his cultivator-style robes snapping rhythmically against his calves.
On his shoulders, Thora remained perched like an oversized gargoyle, her soot-stained hands resting comfortably on his dark hair while her eyes were wide with awe.
"By the stone..." Thora breathed again, her voice full of of genuine disbelief as she stared at the newly materialized Tier 1 structure.
"Everytime Lord Silas...
Every single time I see this, it never fails to send a chill down my spine.
Watching timber and granite knit together out of thin air like living bone... it’s bloody unnatural.
Beautiful, but unnatural as hell."
Silas let out a quiet amused breath that misted into the freezing air as a smirk tugged at the corner of his mouth.
He had summoned strong women and brought structures into reality with a mere flick of his wrist, yet the effortless magic of territorial creation was something he would never truly get used to.
’Haah...’
It was staggering how easily the world bent to a Lord’s command when the resources were paid in full but Silas was not a man to let early success cloud his vision.
A simple dry-storage shed made of pine trusses and standard iron bolts was fine for a frontier outpost, but Blessed Land was rapidly evolving into an empire...

’A simple wooden warehouse isn’t going to cut it,’ Silas thought, his blue eyes narrowing with quiet ambition. ’Not when we’re about to crack open all the mines we can and pull a lot of ores from the earth so we still have to upgrade it.’
"It’s decent enough for a baseline," Silas said aloud, reaching up to tap Thora’s steel-toed boot where it rested near his collarbone.
"Keeps the snow off the timber and gives the carts a roof but it’s raw and unfinished."
Thora snorted, leaning forward so heavily that her leather apron pressed against the back of his head.
"Decent?
Lad, that timber is cured cedar and the mortar is set tighter than a dwarven vault!
What do you mean, ’unfinished’?"
"I mean," Silas chuckled, "it can be far better than this...
Much better."
Thora paused, and then a wide, knowing grin spread across her soot-streaked cheeks.
Her amber eyes gleamed with raw greed for high-tier craftsmanship.
She had witnessed the miracle of the Beast Pavilion’s transformation from a distance... she knew the terrifying ungodly power her Lord possessed when it came to reshaping reality.
"Right then," Thora murmured, crossing her muscular arms over her chest and settling back into her perch.
"Show me what your strange gods have in store, Lord Silas.
Let’s see this ’better.’"
Silas took a slow centering breath.
He closed his eyes for a fraction of a second, his consciousness diving inward, brushing past the raging furnace of his Mythic Gold Core.
’System~ Let’s get to upgrading~’
VUUUUUUUUUM!
A wash of pale azure light rippled outward from his chest, illuminating the falling snow like a cloud of glowing blue fireflies.
Silas opened his eyes as the familiar semi-translucent holographic glass materialized before him, hovering silently against the backdrop of the wooden warehouse.

’It shouldn’t be too costly...’ Silas mused inwardly, his fingers twitching slightly as he prepared to navigate the prompts. ’Skipping a tier always stings, but with the UP reserves we’ve banked from clearing the goblins and subduing the basin monsters, we have plenty of room to breathe.’
The interface shifted, the text sharpening into crystal-clear focus.
[Logistics Warehouse]
[Tier: 1 Construct (Common)]
[Durability: 500 / 500]
[Status: Operational.]
[Upgrade System: Would you like to upgrade Tier 1 Basic Logistics Warehouse directly to Tier 3 Sovereign Distribution Nexus?]
[Cost: 320 UP]
[Y / N]
Silas stared at the glowing blue letters floating in the freezing air, his eyebrows climbing toward his hairline.
For a second, the composure of the Lord cracked, and a strangled breathless chuckle slipped past his teeth.

chapters.title: Chapter 473: Sovereign Distribution Nexus
paragraphs: ’Sovereign Distribution Nexus?’ Silas thought, fighting the overwhelming urge to laugh out loud. ’What in the hell is a Sovereign Distribution Nexus? How does a pile of timber and slate suddenly become a cosmic nexus?!’
The System truly had a flair for dramatic names yet, despite the theatrical naming conventions, Silas knew better than to question the results.
The Absolute Upgrade System had never once failed him.
Every single time he sank UP into a structure, the evolution fundamentally shattered the conventional laws of physics and magic alike.
It reconstructed reality... easily at that.
He tilted his head back, catching Thora’s eager wide-eyed gaze.
"Ready?" Silas asked.
"Do it, my Lord!" Thora urged, her voice practically vibrating with excitement. "Push the bloody button and let’s see the magic!"
Silas smiled and raised his hand, his index finger firmly pressing the glowing golden [Y].
BZZZZT-KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
The instantaneous reaction tore through the atmospheric pressure with the concussive force of an artillery barrage.
A blinding dual-layered aura of incandescent azure and radiant gold violently erupted from the foundation of the Tier 1 warehouse.
The wooden walls, the slate roof, and the iron brackets didn’t merely change... they dissolved into pure, glowing particulate matter, expanding outward in a swirling vortex of raw magical energy.
’Thinking back on it... Won’t this look weird from Evelyn’s point of view?’
He thought about the black haired woman and sighed, if she asked any stupid questions, he would stuff her mouth full of cake.
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
A violent gale-force shockwave blasted through the western courtyard, instantly scouring the three-foot snowdrifts into fine sparkling mist.
Silas’s cultivator robes whipped furiously against his legs, the hem snapping like gunshots, but his dense physical constitution kept him rooted to the earth as if he were forged of solid tungsten.
Above him, Thora clamped her thick thighs tightly around his neck, burying her fingers into his dark hair to keep from being thrown off by the howling pressurized wind.
KRRRRRR-CRUNCH! GRIND!
Within the swirling pillar of blue-gold fire, colossal structural changes were violently taking place.
The footprint of the building changed, elongating into a low-slung, sweeping rectangular form.
The modest cedar lumber and grey stone were overwritten at the atomic level.
In their place, colossal blocks of dense pitch-black obsidian-mythril composite slammed down from the ether, locking together with seamless precision.
Deep hums of spatial distortion echoed through the night air like low vibrating bass notes that resonated directly in Silas’s ribcage.
Pale-blue runic arrays carved themselves across the dark masonry, glowing like cold neon against the midnight black of the stone.
And then, with a final tectonic tremor that pulsed through the bedrock, the blinding light snapped inward, collapsing into the core of the structure.
CLANG!
The wind died instantly as the scattered snow drifted lazily through the sudden eerie quiet.
Standing before them, where a humble warehouse had existed mere moments before, was a structure that belonged elsewhere.
The dark obsidian-mythril walls swallowed the torchlight, broken only by a continuous unbroken slit of pale blue light bleeding out from beneath the roofline.

The front entrance was no longer a pair of hinged doors, but a single colossal sliding mythril vault gate, deeply etched with the crest of Blessed Land... a cracked obsidian shield, an upright golden sword, and a crossed pickaxe.
’I... I... I like it.’
Silas and Thora stared at the finished building in stunned silence.
A single simultaneous word slipped past both of their lips, their voices echoing softly into the cold night:
"...Woah."

"Sweet mother of the forge..." Thora breathed, her jaw practically hanging open as she tugged urgently at Silas’s robes, trying to shake him out of his trance. "My Lord! Look at the stone! That’s not refined granite... that’s void-tempered obsidian laced with mythril veins! You couldn’t crack that wall with a battery of siege ballistas! Come on, move your boots! We have to go inside! We have to see what the hell it looks like in there!"

"Hold on, Thora. Wait a second," Silas laughed, gently grabbing her wrist to keep her from violently yanking his collar. "Let me read the parameters first so we know what we’re actually walking into."
He swiped his hand through the lingering azure mist, bringing the updated System window into clear view.
[Sovereign Distribution Nexus]
[Tier: 3 Construct (Epic)]
[Durability: 3,200 / 3,200]
[Passive Effects:]
[Void-Compression Shelving]: Interior storage space is spatially compressed, allowing the warehouse to hold roughly ten times its physical footprint in actual resource volume.
[Zero-Decay Field]: Completely halts organic/material degradation on all stored goods... no more spoilage, rust, or weather damage regardless of what’s stockpiled inside.

[Auto-Sorting Runeline]: A self-operating conveyor and sorting rune network automatically categorizes and shelves incoming resources by type without requiring manual labor, freeing up worker hours for other tasks.

[Instant Requisition]: Any Lord-authorized officer can mentally query the warehouse’s exact live inventory from anywhere within the territory, without physically walking to the building to check stock.
Silas read through each entry with slow meticulous focus with a deep sense of satisfaction warming his chest.

’Ten times the physical footprint...’ Silas calculated, his analytical mind rapidly projecting the territory’s industrial trajectory. ’And a Zero-Decay Field... That means we can stockpile monster carcasses, rare alchemical herbs, and delicate mana ores indefinitely without losing a single percentage of potency.’
The automation was the real masterpiece.
With the Auto-Sorting Runelines handling the physical categorization of goods, the girls wouldn’t have to spend hours after brutal expeditions hauling crates and sorting iron ingots by hand.
They could dump their carts at the door, and the facility would swallow and catalog the resources automatically.
And then there was [Instant Requisition].
Silas glanced up at the dwarven woman perched on his shoulders.
Thora was the beating heart of the territory’s production lines.
She was the one who forged the armor, refined the ingots, and built the Phase 2 Golems.
Giving her direct mental access to the territory’s stockpile would eliminate the need for a lot of things.
"Thora," Silas said, stepping forward toward the mythril gate. "I’m binding this place’s master requisition rights directly to you."
Thora blinked down at him, her bushy eyebrows furrowing.
"To me? My Lord, that’s authority over the kingdom’s breadbasket... You sure you trust a thirsty dwarf with the keys to the kingdom?"

"I trust you to build my empire," Silas replied smoothly, his voice leaving no room for doubt. "And you can’t build an empire if you have to walk across the territory in a blizzard every time you need ten bars of tempered iron."
As Silas reached the threshold, he raised his hand to find the door’s locking mechanism, but he never had to touch it.
SHRRRRRRRRRRR!
With a deep frictionless mechanical hum, the mythril vault gate parted smoothly down the center.
There were no hinges and no grinding stone, the two halves of the massive gate simply slid into recessed pockets within the obsidian walls, revealing the expanse beyond.
The moment they crossed the threshold, the air changed completely.
The warm living cedar scent of the previous structure was completely gone.
Instead, the air inside was cold and the place was dead quiet, save for a low-frequency hum that vibrated so deeply it bypassed the eardrums, thrumming straight through the marrow of their bones.
And the visual scale was breathtakingly impossible.
From the outside, the building appeared to be a modest low-slung hall roughly eighty feet wide.
But stepping through the gate, the space violently expanded.
The interior was colossal like a vast cathedral of industry that stretched out for hundreds of yards in every direction, fading into a soft glowing blue haze in the far distance.
"By the ancestors’ golden beards..." Thora whispered, her voice completely stripped of its usual boisterous volume.𝒻𝘳𝘦𝘦𝘸ℯ𝒷𝘯𝘰𝑣ℯ𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝘮
Towering rows of obsidian-mythril shelving racks rose forty feet toward the vaulted ceiling, stretching into seemingly endless aisles.
The racks were currently empty, their polished dark surfaces gleaming under the ambient light.
Along the edge of every single shelf, a thin recessed strip of glowing cyan runic script flickered and scrolled silently... the dormant Auto-Sorting Runelines, waiting for inventory to categorize.
Beneath Silas’s boots, the floor was a masterpiece of polished dark volcanic stone.
Inlaid into the surface was a sprawling intricate network of branching pale-blue veins that pulsed with soft light, resembling a circuit board etched into living rock.
These were the physical routing paths designed to magnetically guide automated pallets across the facility without a single worker lifting a finger.
And hovering in the center of the colossal expanse, suspended five feet above the floor with nothing physically supporting it, was the core.
It was a perfect, slowly rotating sphere of pure compressed void-space, roughly the size of a bowling ball.
Its surface was an impossible light-swallowing black, flecked with tiny, swirling motes of silver starlight that drifted within its miniature event horizon.
’In a Tier 3 building?!’
It was the beating heart of the spatial compression here, the anchor that bent the laws of physics to allow a mountain of resources to fit inside a single room.
’Well at least it has a barrier... a very strong one at that...’
Silas wasn’t confident enough in reaching it.
"Look at this place..." Thora muttered, sliding down from Silas’s shoulders and dropping onto the polished stone floor with a dull clatter of her iron boots.
She walked slowly down the central aisle, her thick calloused hands trailing along the smooth edge of an obsidian rack with her fingers tracing the dormant cyan runes.
"It’s not just a warehouse. It’s a bloody machine my Lord... you could store an entire mountain range in these aisles!"
Silas walked up beside her, admiring the clean ruthless geometry of the hall.
Unlike the Beast Pavilion, which was warm and comforting, the Nexus was sterile as it was built for one purpose... Total industrial domination.
"Do you see the pedestal near the entrance?" Silas asked, pointing back toward the gate.
Just inside the mythril doors stood a sleek waist-height pillar carved from solid obsidian.
Embedded into the angled top of the pillar was a smooth, glowing glass-like terminal pulsing with pale blue energy.
’Wait let me confirm first with a query...’
A few moments later, Silas looked at Thora.

"That’s the Requisition Anchor," Silas explained, walking over to it with Thora trailing eagerly behind. "To grant an officer permanent remote access to the territory’s stockpile, both the Lord and the designated officer have to physically synchronize their mana with the terminal."
Thora didn’t hesitate for a second.
"Say no more, my Lord. Let’s link it."
Silas placed his broad palm flat against the left side of the smooth runic terminal.
Thora stepped up beside him, planting her rough, soot-stained hand firmly on the right.
VUUUUUUUUUM!
A sharp warm current of azure mana surged from Silas’s Gold Core, shooting down his arm and flooding into the stone pedestal.
Simultaneously, Thora’s dwarven mana flared with a deep amber hue as the two magical signatures collided within the runic array, swirling together before locking into place with a crystalline chime.
[Authority Granted: Forge Master Thora has been registered as a Master Logistics Officer.]
[Instant Requisition Function: Active.]
Thora gasped softly, her amber eyes widening as her mental field suddenly brushed against the vast empty digital ledger of the warehouse.

She could feel the precise capacity of every shelf, the status of every automated routing vein, and the dormant void-core humming in the center of the room, all accessible with a single stray thought.
"Incredible..." Thora whispered, pulling her hand back and staring at her palm in pure wonder.
A toothy grin split across her face.

"Tomorrow morning, my Lord, the moment we return from mining, I’m clearing out the entire Foundry floor! Every scrap of raw iron, every crate of coal, and every single unrefined gem is moving straight into these racks!"
"Good," Silas nodded, his blue eyes gleaming. "Clear the forge so you have room to assemble the heavy cannons we were planning to mount on the walls."
"Aye, that we do!" Thora barked happily, turning toward the open mythril gate.
She looked up at Silas with an expectant cheeky glint in her eye.

"Now, my Lord... seeing as I’ve graciously helped you commission the greatest warehouse this world has ever seen, you owe me a ride back to the Barracks. The ale is calling my name, and my legs are far too short to wade through three feet of fresh slush!"
Silas chuckled, shaking his head. "Fair enough. Let’s go check on the recruits."
He was planning on heading to the Barracks anyway.
Aurelia and the Princess were both currently attending the post-expedition feast, and while the Saintess was relatively composed, the Princess of the world was out of her element.
She was twenty-five years old, but her sheltered sanitized upbringing in the royal palaces meant she had zero resistance to the ungodly potency of Sovereign Realm alcohol.

Dwarven stout alone was dense enough to strip paint off armor... if the Princess started chugging high-tier spirits, she might literally melt her liver, and the absolute last thing Silas needed on his hands was a dead global royal lying in his mess hall.
They stepped out into the freezing night, the mythril gate sliding shut behind them with that smooth hum.
Thora scrambled effortlessly back up onto Silas’s broad shoulders, her boots hooking comfortably under his collar as Silas set a brisk steady jog through the snowy streets.
The wind was howling fiercely, but the dense heat-radiating walls of the newly constructed Nexus shielded the road, giving them a clear path toward the glowing noisy area ahead.
Within minutes, the towering silhouette of the Barracks loomed before them.

Standing before them, where a humble warehouse had existed mere moments before, was a structure that belonged elsewhere.
The dark obsidian-mythril walls swallowed the torchlight, broken only by a continuous unbroken slit of pale blue light bleeding out from beneath the roofline.

The front entrance was no longer a pair of hinged doors, but a single colossal sliding mythril vault gate, deeply etched with the crest of Blessed Land... a cracked obsidian shield, an upright golden sword, and a crossed pickaxe.
I like it.’
Silas and Thora stared at the finished building in stunned silence.
A single simultaneous word slipped past both of their lips, their voices echoing softly into the cold night:
"...Woah."
"Sweet mother of the forge..." Thora breathed, her jaw practically hanging open as she tugged urgently at Silas’s robes, trying to shake him out of his trance.
"My Lord!
Look at the stone!
That’s not refined granite... that’s void-tempered obsidian laced with mythril veins!
You couldn’t crack that wall with a battery of siege ballistas!
Come on, move your boots!
We have to go inside!
We have to see what the hell it looks like in there!"
"Hold on, Thora.
Wait a second," Silas laughed, gently grabbing her wrist to keep her from violently yanking his collar.
"Let me read the parameters first so we know what we’re actually walking into."
He swiped his hand through the lingering azure mist, bringing the updated System window into clear view.
[Sovereign Distribution Nexus]
[Tier: 3 Construct (Epic)]
[Durability: 3,200 / 3,200]
[Passive Effects:]
[Void-Compression Shelving]: Interior storage space is spatially compressed, allowing the warehouse to hold roughly ten times its physical footprint in actual resource volume.
[Zero-Decay Field]: Completely halts organic/material degradation on all stored goods... no more spoilage, rust, or weather damage regardless of what’s stockpiled inside.

[Auto-Sorting Runeline]: A self-operating conveyor and sorting rune network automatically categorizes and shelves incoming resources by type without requiring manual labor, freeing up worker hours for other tasks.

[Instant Requisition]: Any Lord-authorized officer can mentally query the warehouse’s exact live inventory from anywhere within the territory, without physically walking to the building to check stock.
Silas read through each entry with slow meticulous focus with a deep sense of satisfaction warming his chest.
’Ten times the physical footprint...’ Silas calculated, his analytical mind rapidly projecting the territory’s industrial trajectory. ’And a Zero-Decay Field...
That means we can stockpile monster carcasses, rare alchemical herbs, and delicate mana ores indefinitely without losing a single percentage of potency.’
The automation was the real masterpiece.
With the Auto-Sorting Runelines handling the physical categorization of goods, the girls wouldn’t have to spend hours after brutal expeditions hauling crates and sorting iron ingots by hand.
They could dump their carts at the door, and the facility would swallow and catalog the resources automatically.
And then there was [Instant Requisition].
Silas glanced up at the dwarven woman perched on his shoulders.
Thora was the beating heart of the territory’s production lines.
She was the one who forged the armor, refined the ingots, and built the Phase 2 Golems.
Giving her direct mental access to the territory’s stockpile would eliminate the need for a lot of things.
"Thora," Silas said, stepping forward toward the mythril gate.
"I’m binding this place’s master requisition rights directly to you."
Thora blinked down at him, her bushy eyebrows furrowing.
"To me?
My Lord, that’s authority over the kingdom’s breadbasket...
You sure you trust a thirsty dwarf with the keys to the kingdom?"
"I trust you to build my empire," Silas replied smoothly, his voice leaving no room for doubt.
"And you can’t build an empire if you have to walk across the territory in a blizzard every time you need ten bars of tempered iron."
As Silas reached the threshold, he raised his hand to find the door’s locking mechanism, but he never had to touch it.
SHRRRRRRRRRRR!
With a deep frictionless mechanical hum, the mythril vault gate parted smoothly down the center.
There were no hinges and no grinding stone, the two halves of the massive gate simply slid into recessed pockets within the obsidian walls, revealing the expanse beyond.
The moment they crossed the threshold, the air changed completely.
The warm living cedar scent of the previous structure was completely gone.
Instead, the air inside was cold and the place was dead quiet, save for a low-frequency hum that vibrated so deeply it bypassed the eardrums, thrumming straight through the marrow of their bones.
And the visual scale was breathtakingly impossible.
From the outside, the building appeared to be a modest low-slung hall roughly eighty feet wide.
But stepping through the gate, the space violently expanded.
The interior was colossal like a vast cathedral of industry that stretched out for hundreds of yards in every direction, fading into a soft glowing blue haze in the far distance.
"By the ancestors’ golden beards..." Thora whispered, her voice completely stripped of its usual boisterous volume.𝒻𝘳𝘦𝘦𝘸ℯ𝒷𝘯𝘰𝑣ℯ𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝘮
Towering rows of obsidian-mythril shelving racks rose forty feet toward the vaulted ceiling, stretching into seemingly endless aisles.
The racks were currently empty, their polished dark surfaces gleaming under the ambient light.
Along the edge of every single shelf, a thin recessed strip of glowing cyan runic script flickered and scrolled silently... the dormant Auto-Sorting Runelines, waiting for inventory to categorize.
Beneath Silas’s boots, the floor was a masterpiece of polished dark volcanic stone.
Inlaid into the surface was a sprawling intricate network of branching pale-blue veins that pulsed with soft light, resembling a circuit board etched into living rock.
These were the physical routing paths designed to magnetically guide automated pallets across the facility without a single worker lifting a finger.
And hovering in the center of the colossal expanse, suspended five feet above the floor with nothing physically supporting it, was the core.
It was a perfect, slowly rotating sphere of pure compressed void-space, roughly the size of a bowling ball.
Its surface was an impossible light-swallowing black, flecked with tiny, swirling motes of silver starlight that drifted within its miniature event horizon.
’In a Tier 3 building?!’
It was the beating heart of the spatial compression here, the anchor that bent the laws of physics to allow a mountain of resources to fit inside a single room.
’Well at least it has a barrier... a very strong one at that...’
Silas wasn’t confident enough in reaching it.
"Look at this place..." Thora muttered, sliding down from Silas’s shoulders and dropping onto the polished stone floor with a dull clatter of her iron boots.
She walked slowly down the central aisle, her thick calloused hands trailing along the smooth edge of an obsidian rack with her fingers tracing the dormant cyan runes.
"It’s not just a warehouse.
It’s a bloody machine my Lord... you could store an entire mountain range in these aisles!"
Silas walked up beside her, admiring the clean ruthless geometry of the hall.
Unlike the Beast Pavilion, which was warm and comforting, the Nexus was sterile as it was built for one purpose...
Total industrial domination.
"Do you see the pedestal near the entrance?" Silas asked, pointing back toward the gate.
Just inside the mythril doors stood a sleek waist-height pillar carved from solid obsidian.
Embedded into the angled top of the pillar was a smooth, glowing glass-like terminal pulsing with pale blue energy.
’Wait let me confirm first with a query...’
A few moments later, Silas looked at Thora.
"That’s the Requisition Anchor," Silas explained, walking over to it with Thora trailing eagerly behind.
"To grant an officer permanent remote access to the territory’s stockpile, both the Lord and the designated officer have to physically synchronize their mana with the terminal."
Thora didn’t hesitate for a second.
"Say no more, my Lord.
Let’s link it."
Silas placed his broad palm flat against the left side of the smooth runic terminal.
Thora stepped up beside him, planting her rough, soot-stained hand firmly on the right.
VUUUUUUUUUM!
A sharp warm current of azure mana surged from Silas’s Gold Core, shooting down his arm and flooding into the stone pedestal.
Simultaneously, Thora’s dwarven mana flared with a deep amber hue as the two magical signatures collided within the runic array, swirling together before locking into place with a crystalline chime.
[Authority Granted: Forge Master Thora has been registered as a Master Logistics Officer.]
[Instant Requisition Function: Active.]
Thora gasped softly, her amber eyes widening as her mental field suddenly brushed against the vast empty digital ledger of the warehouse.

She could feel the precise capacity of every shelf, the status of every automated routing vein, and the dormant void-core humming in the center of the room, all accessible with a single stray thought.
"Incredible..." Thora whispered, pulling her hand back and staring at her palm in pure wonder.
A toothy grin split across her face.
"Tomorrow morning, my Lord, the moment we return from mining, I’m clearing out the entire Foundry floor!
Every scrap of raw iron, every crate of coal, and every single unrefined gem is moving straight into these racks!"
"Good," Silas nodded, his blue eyes gleaming.
"Clear the forge so you have room to assemble the heavy cannons we were planning to mount on the walls."
"Aye, that we do!" Thora barked happily, turning toward the open mythril gate.
She looked up at Silas with an expectant cheeky glint in her eye.
"Now, my Lord... seeing as I’ve graciously helped you commission the greatest warehouse this world has ever seen, you owe me a ride back to the Barracks.
The ale is calling my name, and my legs are far too short to wade through three feet of fresh slush!"
Silas chuckled, shaking his head.
"Fair enough.
Let’s go check on the recruits."
He was planning on heading to the Barracks anyway.
Aurelia and the Princess were both currently attending the post-expedition feast, and while the Saintess was relatively composed, the Princess of the world was out of her element.
She was twenty-five years old, but her sheltered sanitized upbringing in the royal palaces meant she had zero resistance to the ungodly potency of Sovereign Realm alcohol.

Dwarven stout alone was dense enough to strip paint off armor... if the Princess started chugging high-tier spirits, she might literally melt her liver, and the absolute last thing Silas needed on his hands was a dead global royal lying in his mess hall.
They stepped out into the freezing night, the mythril gate sliding shut behind them with that smooth hum.
Thora scrambled effortlessly back up onto Silas’s broad shoulders, her boots hooking comfortably under his collar as Silas set a brisk steady jog through the snowy streets.
The wind was howling fiercely, but the dense heat-radiating walls of the newly constructed Nexus shielded the road, giving them a clear path toward the glowing noisy area ahead.
Within minutes, the towering silhouette of the Barracks loomed before them.

chapters.title: Chapter 474: Thor Loses?!
paragraphs: Even through the thickness of the whole place, the sound of the celebration was deafening.
"RAHHHHHHHHH!"

Roaring laughter, the clattering of wooden tankards, rhythmic foot-stomping, and the chaotic drunken singing of more than a hundred armed women bled through the cracks of the building, filling the snowy courtyard with a vibrant warmth.
’Haah... I really want to get drunk.’
Silas pushed open the heavy double doors, stepping out of the freezing blizzard and into the sweltering heat of the Mess Hall.
FWOOOOOOOSH!
The instantaneous transition was overwhelming.
The air inside was thick with the rich savory smell of roasted boar, melted butter, spilled dwarven ale, and the smell of Eluned’s fermented spirit-wine.
Massive iron chandeliers hung from the rafters, blazing with hundreds of beeswax candles that cast a warm, golden glow over the chaotic scene below.
It was pandemonium.
The seasoned veterans of the Blessed Land and the wide-eyed new recruits were completely intermingled, their armor discarded in messy piles along the perimeter walls.
Girls in simple linen shirts and trousers were arm-wrestling on overturned tables, dancing on the benches, and loudly boasting about their kills today.
At the massive head table near the roaring hearth sat Thor.
The God of Thunder had completely abandoned all pretenses of divine dignity.
She was draped in the dark spirit-wood robes Silas had fixed for her earlier, the sleeves rolled past her massive corded forearms.

In her left hand, she was casually holding an entire roasted boar leg, tearing off half-pound chunks of succulent meat with her bare teeth, while her right hand held a colossal wooden keg of dwarven stout like a regular coffee mug, tipping it back and chugging gallons of foaming dark ale without pausing for breath.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHA!" Thor’s booming earth-shaking laughter cut through the din of the hall like a lightning strike.
She slammed the empty keg onto the oak table with enough force to crack the two-inch-thick timber, wiping foam from her lips with the back of her wrist.
"BRING MORE! By Odin’s missing eye, this flesh is tender! The hogs in Asgard taste of dry ash compared to this! More meat! More ale! Is there no stout left in this frozen valley?!"
The maidens erupted into wild drunken cheers, completely captivated by the demigoddess’s bottomless appetite.
The moment Thora spotted the drinking contest from atop Silas’s shoulders, her dwarven pride completely overrode her exhaustion.
"Out of the way, my Lord! My people are being challenged!" Thora yelled, nimbly hopping down from Silas’s collar and hitting the floor with an agile roll.
She sprinted across the mess hall toward the private brewing station behind the bar, shoving empty barrels out of her path.
Silas watched with mild horror as Thora re-emerged seconds later, aggressively wheeling a heavy iron-reinforced wooden cart directly toward Thor’s table.
Resting in the center of the cart was a single dusty glass demijohn wrapped in silver-leaf runes.
It was the Blessed Drink.

A hyper-concentrated distillation that Thora had brewed in secret as a single shot of this demonic concoction had famously knocked both Morwenna and Eluned completely flat on their backs for hours on end.
Thora slammed the cart to a halt right in front of the towering blonde god. She folded her muscular arms, puffing out her chest with reckless dwarven bravado.

"You think you’ve tasted real drink, blonde giant?!" Thora challenged, her gravelly voice cutting through the noise. "Standard stout is mother’s milk! If you truly claim to hold the sky in your fists, drink the Blessed Fire! I dare you!"
Thor’s storm-blue eyes lit up with wild delight.
"Oho?! A challenge from the mountain-folk?! Pour it, little smith! Pour it to the brim!"
Under normal circumstances, Thora would have accompanied a drink like this with a barrage of filthy perverted dwarven jokes about breasts.
But as she looked at Thor’s massive corded neck and the terrifying, casual presence of Mjölnir’s master, survival instinct kicked in.
Thora kept her mouth firmly shut; she liked breathing, and she knew this towering woman could snap her spine like a dry twig without breaking a sweat.
Thora uncorked the demijohn, pouring a thick glowing amber liquid into a massive horn cup.
The liquid literally hissed against the horn, releasing tiny wisps of blue vapor.
Thor snatched the cup, raising it high. "To Blessed Land!"
She tipped her head back and emptied the horn in a single massive swallow.
Silas, who was slowly walking past the table, paused mid-stride, bracing for an explosion.
GULP!
Thor lowered the empty horn.
For exactly two seconds, nothing happened as the demigoddess stood completely frozen with her eyes wide.
Then, the liquid hit her divine nervous system like an atmospheric storm.
BZZZZT!
Thor’s eyes visibly rolled back into her head, the pupils fluttering wildly as tiny arcs of cerulean lightning crackled uncontrollably across her skin.
Her massive frame swayed, leaning heavily to the left before she forcefully caught herself on the edge of the oak table, splintering the edge under her grip.
"Haaaaah..." Thor wheezed, a massive steam-laden breath escaping her lips as her cheeks flushed a brilliant red.
She blinked heavily, shaking her head to clear the static. "...That... that is pretty damn strong! Gwahaha! It kicks like a frost giant’s mule!"
Thora’s jaw dropped in disbelief that the woman was still standing but a dwarf never retreated from a drinking duel.
"Pretty strong?!" Thora shouted, immediately grabbing the demijohn again. "You haven’t seen anything yet! Have another, giantess!"
"POUR IT!" Thor roared, slamming the horn back down.
Thora filled the horn to the brim as Thor grabbed it, threw her head back, and chugged the second dose without hesitation.
THUD!
The horn fell from her fingers, clattering across the floorboards.
Thor’s eyelids instantly slammed shut.

Her towering muscled frame tilted forward like a felled redwood tree, crashing flat against the oak table with a deafening boom that sent roasted meats, wooden plates, and beer mugs flying into the air.
The God of Thunder was out cold, snoring softly into a plate of mashed potatoes.
"YEAAAAAAAH!" Thora screamed in hysterical victory, leaping onto the bench and throwing both fists into the air! "DOWN GOES THE SKY! THE DWARVES REIGN SUPREME!"
The girls roared with laughter, pounding the tables and raising their mugs to the victorious smith.
Silas rubbed his temples, letting out a long exhausted sigh as he navigated past the chaotic drinking circle.
’Gods above, my territory is run by lunatics.’
He scanned the crowded smoky room, his sharp eyes searching through the sea of drunken warriors.
’Where is the Princess?’ Silas thought, picking up his pace.
He found her barely ten yards away, nestled deep within a circle of rowdy recruits near the corner hearth.
The scene was a diplomatic nightmare that would probably have him executed by the King.
The Princess of the world... the dignified and educated twenty-five-year-old Princess to global human authority had completely shed her royal elegance.

Her hair ribbons were gone, her azure locks spilling wildly around her shoulders, her silk blouse was rumpled, her sleeves rolled up, and her porcelain cheeks were burning with a deep intoxicated crimson.
She was standing precariously on top of a low wooden stool, holding a massive, foaming mug of dwarven cider in both hands.
"Chug! Chug! Chug! Chug!" five vanguard recruits chanted loudly, banging their daggers against the stone floor in rhythm.
The Princess tipped the massive mug back, chugging the entire contents in five massive unladylike gulps.
Foam dripped down her chin, soaking into her collar as she slammed the empty tankard against the wall with a hollow bang.
She wiped her mouth with her forearm, threw her hands into the air, and let out a wild screech that silenced half the mess hall:
"I AM DANGEROUS!"
"YEAAAAAAAH! PRINCESS IS BUILT DIFFERENT!" the recruits roared back, howling with laughter and clinking their mugs together in celebration!
Silas didn’t waste a single second.
He blurred forward, his boots crossing the gap in a fraction of a heartbeat.

Before the Princess could order another round or declare war on an imaginary enemy, Silas stepped into the circle, reached out with one broad arm, hooked his hand around her waist, and hoisted her bodily off the wooden stool.
"Whoa—hey!" the Princess yelped, flailing her arms as the room suddenly tilted sideways.
Silas tossed her effortlessly over his broad right shoulder, hauling the twenty-five-year-old global royal like a sack of Yukon potatoes.

"Party’s over for the royal delegation," Silas announced firmly, fixing the chanting recruits with a sharp stern glare. "If any of you give her another drop of alcohol tonight, you’re on latrine duty for the next month."
The recruits instantly sobered up, snapping into nervous crooked salutes. "Yes, Lord Silas! Understood, Boss!"

"Put me down, Silas!" the Princess complained loudly, her voice slurred as she weakly pounded her tiny fists against his muscular back. "I was winning! I have diplomatic immunity! Put me down right now!"
"You’re slurring your words, your Highness," Silas muttered dryly, completely ignoring her useless squirming as he adjusted his grip on her thighs. "Your liver is currently waving a white flag..."
As he turned to head toward the mess hall exit, Silas paused, his eyes sweeping across the opposite side of the room.
’Where the hell is Aurelia?’ Silas wondered, his brow furrowing. ’The Saintess usually keeps a much tighter leash on herself...’
He wanted to ask her about her past, he was interested.
Silas found her shortly after and the sight made Silas stop dead in his tracks.
Over by the secondary bar, a long dining table had been cleared of plates and tankards.
Standing directly atop the polished oak table were Aurelia and Tasmin.
The serene Saintess of the Argent Flame had completely abandoned every pretense of calm as her golden hair was a chaotic tangled mess around her flushed sweaty face.
She and Tasmin were actively standing face-to-face, holding half-empty bottles of elven spirit-wine, aggressively shaking their hips and dancing to the chaotic beat of a dwarven war drum.

"YOU THINK YOUR SPELLS ARE POWERFUL?!" Tasmin screamed over the music, laughing hysterically as she bumped her hip hard against Aurelia’s, nearly knocking the holy woman off the table. "TRY SWINGING A DAGGER IN THE MUD FOR EIGHT HOURS!"

"I CAN PURIFY YOUR ENTIRE BLOODLINE, YOU DAGGER-SWINGING BRUTE!" Aurelia shouted back, pointing the neck of her wine bottle directly at Tasmin’s nose before bursting into an uncontrollable fit of giggles and taking another swig.
Both women were unapologetically smashed.
Silas stood there for a long second, watching the Saintess shake her ass on a mess hall table while trading insults with a commander.
He looked down at the floor, and then looked back up at Aurelia, who was currently attempting to balance her wine bottle on her forehead while Tasmin cheered her on.
’...You know what?’ Silas thought with a wry smile touching his lips. ’Let her enjoy herself... At least she isn’t climbing the rafters...’

Deciding against interrupting the Saintess’s rare moment of chaotic freedom, Silas turned on his heel and scurried out of the Barracks, hauling the still-grumbling Princess out into the freezing winter night.
FWOOOOOOSH!
The sub-zero wind immediately hit them, causing the Princess to violently shiver against his back.
"C-cold..." she whimpered, her earlier bravado instantly evaporating as she buried her flushed face into the thick fabric of his dark cultivator robes. "Silas... it’s freezing..."
"Hold on, then," Silas murmured softly.
He channeled a brief gentle pulse of warm mana from his Gold Core, allowing his body heat to expand outward like an invisible blanket, completely sheltering the trembling woman from the blizzard.
He jogged steadily across the snow-covered central plaza, heading straight for the massive silhouette of the Keep.
The front doors swung open smoothly to receive him.
Silas stepped into the quiet warm interior of the main hall, completely leaving the storm behind.
He climbed the central wooden staircase, ascending to the second-floor guest wing where Kadi had meticulously prepared a private, luxurious suite specifically for the royal visitor.
Silas pushed open the bedroom door with his elbow.
The suite was beautifully furnished, with a crackling private fireplace, thick velvet curtains, and an oversized bed lined with warm fur blankets.
He walked over to the mattress, carefully lowering the Princess onto the soft sheets.

"Nnnngh..." the Princess grumbled, rolling onto her side and pulling her knees toward her chest. She blinked heavily, her azure eyes struggling to focus on Silas’s handsome face as he leaned over the bed.
A soft vulnerable smile touched her lips as she reached out a delicate uncoordinated hand, weakly tugging at the sleeve of his robes.

"Thank you, Lord Silas..." she whispered, her voice thick with sleep and alcohol. "For... for giving me joy and letting me drink alcohol. I’ve never drank it before... It’s good and makes me fuzzy and happy. You’re... you’re a good person..."
Before Silas could offer a polite response, the Princess leaned her head forward.
With clumsy drunken affection, she pressed a soft kiss directly onto the center of his left cheek.
Her head instantly dropped back onto the plush pillows, her breathing deepening into a steady slumber the very second her cheek hit the fabric.
Silas stood by the bedside, raising his hand to touch the warm spot on his cheek.
A quiet chuckle escaped his lips.
He reached down, pulling the heavy fur duvet up over her shoulders, tucking the edges securely around her neck to keep her warm throughout the night.
"Get some sleep, Princess," Silas murmured quietly, turning toward the bedroom door. "Tomorrow’s a long day."
He stepped out into the quiet corridor, gently clicking the door shut behind him.
’But seriously... she’s never drank alcohol before?’
