Her hair ribbons were gone, her azure locks spilling wildly around her shoulders, her silk blouse was rumpled, her sleeves rolled up, and her porcelain cheeks were burning with a deep intoxicated crimson.
She was standing precariously on top of a low wooden stool, holding a massive, foaming mug of dwarven cider in both hands.
"Chug!
Chug!
Chug!
Chug!" five vanguard recruits chanted loudly, banging their daggers against the stone floor in rhythm.
The Princess tipped the massive mug back, chugging the entire contents in five massive unladylike gulps.
Foam dripped down her chin, soaking into her collar as she slammed the empty tankard against the wall with a hollow bang.
She wiped her mouth with her forearm, threw her hands into the air, and let out a wild screech that silenced half the mess hall:
"I AM DANGEROUS!"
"YEAAAAAAAH!
PRINCESS IS BUILT DIFFERENT!" the recruits roared back, howling with laughter and clinking their mugs together in celebration!
Silas didn’t waste a single second.
He blurred forward, his boots crossing the gap in a fraction of a heartbeat.

Before the Princess could order another round or declare war on an imaginary enemy, Silas stepped into the circle, reached out with one broad arm, hooked his hand around her waist, and hoisted her bodily off the wooden stool.
"Whoa—hey!" the Princess yelped, flailing her arms as the room suddenly tilted sideways.
Silas tossed her effortlessly over his broad right shoulder, hauling the twenty-five-year-old global royal like a sack of Yukon potatoes.
"Party’s over for the royal delegation," Silas announced firmly, fixing the chanting recruits with a sharp stern glare.
"If any of you give her another drop of alcohol tonight, you’re on latrine duty for the next month."
The recruits instantly sobered up, snapping into nervous crooked salutes.
"Yes, Lord Silas!
Understood, Boss!"
"Put me down, Silas!" the Princess complained loudly, her voice slurred as she weakly pounded her tiny fists against his muscular back.
"I was winning!
I have diplomatic immunity!
Put me down right now!"
"You’re slurring your words, your Highness," Silas muttered dryly, completely ignoring her useless squirming as he adjusted his grip on her thighs.
"Your liver is currently waving a white flag..."
As he turned to head toward the mess hall exit, Silas paused, his eyes sweeping across the opposite side of the room.
’Where the hell is Aurelia?’ Silas wondered, his brow furrowing. ’The Saintess usually keeps a much tighter leash on herself...’
He wanted to ask her about her past, he was interested.
Silas found her shortly after and the sight made Silas stop dead in his tracks.
Over by the secondary bar, a long dining table had been cleared of plates and tankards.
Standing directly atop the polished oak table were Aurelia and Tasmin.
The serene Saintess of the Argent Flame had completely abandoned every pretense of calm as her golden hair was a chaotic tangled mess around her flushed sweaty face.
She and Tasmin were actively standing face-to-face, holding half-empty bottles of elven spirit-wine, aggressively shaking their hips and dancing to the chaotic beat of a dwarven war drum.
"YOU THINK YOUR SPELLS ARE POWERFUL?!" Tasmin screamed over the music, laughing hysterically as she bumped her hip hard against Aurelia’s, nearly knocking the holy woman off the table.
"TRY SWINGING A DAGGER IN THE MUD FOR EIGHT HOURS!"

"I CAN PURIFY YOUR ENTIRE BLOODLINE, YOU DAGGER-SWINGING BRUTE!" Aurelia shouted back, pointing the neck of her wine bottle directly at Tasmin’s nose before bursting into an uncontrollable fit of giggles and taking another swig.
Both women were unapologetically smashed.
Silas stood there for a long second, watching the Saintess shake her ass on a mess hall table while trading insults with a commander.
He looked down at the floor, and then looked back up at Aurelia, who was currently attempting to balance her wine bottle on her forehead while Tasmin cheered her on.
’...You know what?’ Silas thought with a wry smile touching his lips. ’Let her enjoy herself...
At least she isn’t climbing the rafters...’

Deciding against interrupting the Saintess’s rare moment of chaotic freedom, Silas turned on his heel and scurried out of the Barracks, hauling the still-grumbling Princess out into the freezing winter night.
FWOOOOOOSH!
The sub-zero wind immediately hit them, causing the Princess to violently shiver against his back.
"C-cold..." she whimpered, her earlier bravado instantly evaporating as she buried her flushed face into the thick fabric of his dark cultivator robes.
"Silas... it’s freezing..."
"Hold on, then," Silas murmured softly.
He channeled a brief gentle pulse of warm mana from his Gold Core, allowing his body heat to expand outward like an invisible blanket, completely sheltering the trembling woman from the blizzard.
He jogged steadily across the snow-covered central plaza, heading straight for the massive silhouette of the Keep.
The front doors swung open smoothly to receive him.
Silas stepped into the quiet warm interior of the main hall, completely leaving the storm behind.
He climbed the central wooden staircase, ascending to the second-floor guest wing where Kadi had meticulously prepared a private, luxurious suite specifically for the royal visitor.
Silas pushed open the bedroom door with his elbow.
The suite was beautifully furnished, with a crackling private fireplace, thick velvet curtains, and an oversized bed lined with warm fur blankets.
He walked over to the mattress, carefully lowering the Princess onto the soft sheets.
"Nnnngh..." the Princess grumbled, rolling onto her side and pulling her knees toward her chest.
She blinked heavily, her azure eyes struggling to focus on Silas’s handsome face as he leaned over the bed.
A soft vulnerable smile touched her lips as she reached out a delicate uncoordinated hand, weakly tugging at the sleeve of his robes.
"Thank you, Lord Silas..." she whispered, her voice thick with sleep and alcohol.
"For... for giving me joy and letting me drink alcohol.
I’ve never drank it before...
It’s good and makes me fuzzy and happy.
You’re... you’re a good person..."
Before Silas could offer a polite response, the Princess leaned her head forward.
With clumsy drunken affection, she pressed a soft kiss directly onto the center of his left cheek.
Her head instantly dropped back onto the plush pillows, her breathing deepening into a steady slumber the very second her cheek hit the fabric.
Silas stood by the bedside, raising his hand to touch the warm spot on his cheek.
A quiet chuckle escaped his lips.
He reached down, pulling the heavy fur duvet up over her shoulders, tucking the edges securely around her neck to keep her warm throughout the night.
"Get some sleep, Princess," Silas murmured quietly, turning toward the bedroom door.
"Tomorrow’s a long day."
He stepped out into the quiet corridor, gently clicking the door shut behind him.
’But seriously... she’s never drank alcohol before?’

chapters.title: Chapter 475: Mine BVR [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The Keep was dead silent now.
As Silas walked down the dimly lit hallway, his boots made muffled thuds against the plush carpet.
’I’m tired...’
He felt the immense crushing weight of the day’s events finally catching up to him.
The scouting expedition, the tension with Evelyn, the negotiation with Thor, the construction of the Nexus... every single muscle in his body was screaming for rest.

’Now... tomorrow’s mining operation,’ Silas thought, running a tired hand through his dark hair. ’We break ground in KB-22 as well as the rest of the mines at first light... The golems need to be loaded, the Vanguard needs to be sobered up, and we have to extract every single Mana Diamond before the monsters catch our scent.’
He passed by the open door of Eluned’s private quarters as Silas paused, glancing inside.
The World-Tree Goddess was curled up peacefully on her massive, vine-woven bed, completely lost to the world.
Her green-tinted hair spilled across the pillows like living moss, and her breathing was soft.
’She slept quite early, is there something she wants to do tomorrow?’
Eluned was still sound asleep however Silas smiled, quietly continuing down the hall toward his own master bedroom.
He reached his door, turned the brass knob, and pushed it open.
The room was dark, illuminated only by the silvery moonlight bleeding through the frost-rimed windows.
Silas kicked his boots off by the door and stepped inside, his eyes naturally falling onto the massive bed in the center of the room.
There, lying completely sprawled beneath the heavy sheets, was Morwenna.
The Pirate Queen was exactly where he had left her hours ago with her tanned, athletic frame completely naked beneath the covers and her long messy hair fanning across the dark velvet sheets.
Silas blinked, crossing his arms as he looked down at her sleeping form.

’Thor woke up, drank half the mess hall under the table, and passed out again... and Morwenna hasn’t even moved an inch?’ Silas thought with a small smirk tugging at his lips. ’Aeli’s sleeping draught must have hit her with the force of an anchor.’
Silas didn’t bother overthinking it.
He reached down, untying the sash of his dark cultivator robes.
’Let’s get this off...’
He pulled the heavy fabric over his shoulders, tossing it onto the wooden armchair by the window, and stepped out of his trousers, leaving himself in just a comfortable pair of dark linen shorts.
"Getting on..."
Silas walked around to the empty side of the bed, gently lifting the heavy fur duvet and sliding his tired frame beneath the covers.
The mattress dipped under his weight as Silas rolled onto his side, naturally sliding his right arm across the bed until his broad hand rested against Morwenna’s smooth warm waist.
He pulled her gently toward him, cuddling the naked Pirate Queen against his chest.
Her skin was hot, radiating the natural vitality of a powerful warrior.
’I haven’t shown her what I did with the Second Style yet... Well maybe tomorrow.’
Silas buried his face into the crook of her neck, inhaling the intoxicating scent of her that clung to her collarbone.
He pressed a soft warm kiss directly against the soft skin of her neck.
"Goodnight, Morwenna," Silas whispered into her hair and he closed his eyes.
Within seconds, the soothing warmth of his Gold Core slowed, matching the quiet breathing of the woman in his arms, and the Lord of Blessed Land finally drifted off into a deep dreamless sleep.
The room returned to stillness.
Outside, the blizzard howled softly against the glass like a distant harmless whisper.
Slowly... agonizingly slowly... the quiet was broken by the faintest hitch in breathing.
Underneath the heavy duvet, Morwenna’s long dark eyelashes fluttered.
Her eyes cracked open in the darkness, glowing with a vibrant amber hue.
She wasn’t asleep, Morwenna hadn’t been asleep for the last five minutes.

The Pirate Queen lay completely frozen in his embrace, feeling the comforting weight of Silas’s muscular arm wrapped securely around her bare waist, and the steady warmth of his chest pressing firmly against her naked back.
The phantom heat of his kiss was still burning against her neck, sending tiny electric shivers straight down her spine.
A brilliant crimson blush exploded across Morwenna’s tanned cheeks, burning all the way down to her collarbone.
Her heart began to hammer wildly against her ribs, so loud she was terrified it would wake him.
She bit her lower lip, pulling the sheets slightly higher with trembling fingers, her tough ruthless facade completely melting into mush in the quiet dark.
’C-captain...’ Morwenna thought, a soft flustered whimper catching in her throat as she closed her eyes again, leaning back into his warmth.
The dawn that broke over Blessed Land did not bring warmth like Silas wanted.
It brought an iron-gray sky and a biting needle-sharp frost that clung to every surface like ground glass.

Down in the courtyard before the Keep, Silas had been standing by the mounting posts, rubbing his gloved hands together and grumbling under his breath at the howling draft funneling off the northern peaks.
Even with the internal furnace of his core humming steadily beneath his ribs, the damp bite of the basin’s sub-zero squalls grated on him.
Everyone could see he hated the snow... not the snow rather but the constant snowing.
For Tasmin, however, the morning was nothing short of perfection.
The cold made the blood circulate faster.
It kept the senses razor-sharp, tightened the sinews, and made the shadows pooling beneath the rocky ridges crisp as well.
"Haah..."
She stood at the head of a ten-woman vanguard column, resting one gloved hand casually on the pommel of her sidearm as she adjusted the heavy fur mantle over her shoulders.
Beneath her, a Blessed Wolf shifted its weight, its paws sinking barely an inch into the crust of frozen snow.
Its fur bristled against the wind, while a tranquil golden hum resonated through the silver-inlaid harness wrapped around its broad chest.
The Tier 3 Pack-Lord’s Sanctuary had done wonders for these beasts as their breath rose in steady calm plumes of vapor, lacking the feral agitation common to wild basin wolves.
Behind Tasmin sat nine other women, their mounts formed up in a clean disciplined double file.

It was an intentional split... Four battle-hardened veterans who had bled alongside Blessed Land before the Lord War had even ignited, and four fresh recruits whose leather was still stiff and whose eyes darted nervously across the jagged horizon.
Then a dwarf.
Tasmin glanced back over her shoulder, letting her gaze sweep the line.
The terrain stretching out toward the eastern crags was notoriously brutal... a broken expanse of shattered shale, black frost, and jagged volcanic outcrops hidden beneath treacherous drifts.
On foot, an expedition out here was an ankle-shattering slog that could bleed a squad’s stamina dry before a single pickaxe struck stone.
Mounted on the Blessed Wolves, however, the jagged terrain was practically a highway.
The beasts moved with a fluid grace, their broad pads distributing weight across the snowdrifts effortlessly.

"Pick up the slack, girls," Tasmin called out, her voice cutting cleanly through the whistling wind. "Look ahead. That jagged spine of black slate right past the second ridge? That’s the boundary marker so we’re almost at the breach."
A chorus of sharp gasps and enthusiastic cheers erupted from the ranks behind her.
Several of the younger recruits pumped their gloved fists into the air, their faces flushed bright red from the frost and sheer adrenaline.
"Finally!" a young archer with cropped chestnut hair grinned, leaning over her wolf’s neck. "My knees were starting to freeze solid in these stirrups!"

"You won’t be complaining about frozen knees once we start swinging," an older shield-bearer beside her retorted with a rough, good-natured bark of laughter. "You’ll be sweating through your undergarments within ten minutes of clearing the entrance."
Tasmin watched them, a slow knowing smirk curving her lips.
The high spirits weren’t purely born of military pride... There was a far more competitive edge humming through the ranks today, and every single woman in the squad knew it.

Before the deployment manifests had been signed at first light, Silas had stood before the gathered squads in the central square, his dark eyes sweeping over the ranks as he laid down the terms of the day.
’Whoever mines the most,’ he had declared, his voice carrying the calm weight of a decree, ’will receive a special reward directly from their Lord.’
That single sentence had set the entire garrison ablaze.
A special reward... From him...
Tasmin’s fingers tightened slightly against the leather of her reins as heat flared unbidden in her chest.
She wanted that reward.
She wanted it more than she cared to admit aloud.
It was impossible not to feel the tension buzzing through the territory... ever since the construction of the multi-room apartments, secrecy was an illusion.

When Vala had slipped through the compound yesterday evening, rushing down the central hallway toward her private quarters with her dark cloak clutched tight and her breath coming in shallow ragged hitches, the entire floor had smelled it.𝘧𝑟𝑒𝑒𝘸𝘦𝘣𝑛𝑜𝘷𝑒𝓁.𝘤𝘰𝓂
She carried the unmistakable intoxicating musk of their Lord and it had lingered in the draft of the corridor like heavy incense.

’Vala got to taste him,’ Tasmin thought, her amber eyes darkening with quiet ravenous envy as she stared out at the jagged rocks ahead. ’She got to kneel before him and take that grace into her mouth... I’ve bled for this territory since the first foundations were laid in the dirt so I deserve to have my mouth full of his essence too.’
She exhaled a hot trembling breath that vanished into the freezing air, forcibly shoving the perverted distraction into the dark recesses of her mind.
Discipline first... Desire second... If she wanted to be on her knees in his private quarters, she had to earn it with results.
A heavy thudding vibrated through the earth, cutting through the sound of the wind.
Tasmin pulled her mount slightly to the right and cast a glance backward.
Following roughly twenty paces behind the mounted column, moving on all fours with terrifying weight, was a Phase 2 Golem.
The construct was a titan of dwarven engineering.
Its chassis was forged from heavy slabs of volcanic bedrock bound together by thick bands of Deep-Earth Alloy and tempered iron.
It moved with a steady motion, its four massive stone limbs driving into the snow with enough force to crack the shale beneath.

Bolted across its broad, hunched back was an intricate system of heavy-duty transport bins and reinforced tool-racks, their surfaces etched with pale runic stabilization lines designed to absorb shock and prevent loaded minerals from grinding to dust during transit.
Even after watching Thora hammer the rune-plates into the chassis yesterday, seeing a four-legged siege automaton casually pacing a cavalry column was deeply unsettling.
Yet, beneath the unease, Tasmin felt a swell of satisfaction.
’We’re advancing,’ she thought, watching the golem’s central core pulse with a dull steady blue glow.
Riding alongside Tasmin’s left flank was a stout broad-shouldered dwarf, completely clean-faced, her skin weathered by the fierce subterranean winds of her homeland.
She wore a tailored suit of reinforced leather mining gear over steel-mesh underlays, her thick fingers deftly manipulating a roll of vellum that she had braced against her knee.
"Are we on the marker, Durna?" Tasmin asked, nodding toward the jagged rock wall looming ahead.
The dwarf spat a glob of chewing tobacco into the snow and tapped a blunt finger against a charcoal-drawn grid on the map.

"Aye, right on the nose, Captain," Durna grunted, her rough mountain-bred dialect clipping the words short. "Just past that sheer shelf of basalt where the ice hangs like daggers... The opening sits in the blind spot of the ridge."
Sure enough, as the wolves loped around the bend of the rock face, a wide gaping fissure in the mountain flank carved itself out of the gloom.
The opening was irregular, roughly fourteen feet tall and nearly twenty feet wide at the base, its jagged edges rimmed with thick sheets of black frost.
Stretched across the entrance, shimmering with a translucent violet lattice, was an intricate magical ward.
’Rowenna’s work...’ Tasmin noted, pulling her wolf to a halt.
Because Silas couldn’t personally tour every single cavern entrance in the vast Umbral Basin to maintain seals, Rowenna had mass-produced boundary runes.
These wards were anchored directly into the stone lintels, keeping the feral creatures of the frozen wastes from nesting in the surveyed veins before the mining squads were mobilized.
Tasmin raised her right hand, extending two fingers toward the glowing barrier.
She drew upon the subtle trace of mana letting a whisper of mana bleed into her voice.
"Dispel."
PING!

The violet barrier resonated like a struck crystal bell as the intricate geometric runes flashed once, folding inward like burning paper, before dissolving into harmless motes of purple light that drifted harmlessly down onto the snow.
The dark yawning mouth of the cavern stood wide open.
Durna pulled her mount up beside Tasmin, looking into the darkness with a grim assessing eye.
"Welcome to Mine BVR Star, girls. Mind your step; the frost inside is slicker than grease..."
Tasmin gave the dwarf a strange sideways look.
"BVR Star? Seriously? How the hell does Thora come up with these designations? Did she just pull random consonants out of an empty ale barrel?"

"Clan codes, Captain," Durna snorted, rolling up her paper with a sharp snap. "BVR stands for Black Vein Runic... The ’Star’ part is because the primary yield here isn’t mundane iron... it’s Star-Iron that exists in pure unrefined clusters. Master Thora doesn’t name things for poetry, she names them for the ledger."

The opening was irregular, roughly fourteen feet tall and nearly twenty feet wide at the base, its jagged edges rimmed with thick sheets of black frost.
Stretched across the entrance, shimmering with a translucent violet lattice, was an intricate magical ward.
’Rowenna’s work...’ Tasmin noted, pulling her wolf to a halt.
Because Silas couldn’t personally tour every single cavern entrance in the vast Umbral Basin to maintain seals, Rowenna had mass-produced boundary runes.
These wards were anchored directly into the stone lintels, keeping the feral creatures of the frozen wastes from nesting in the surveyed veins before the mining squads were mobilized.
Tasmin raised her right hand, extending two fingers toward the glowing barrier.
She drew upon the subtle trace of mana letting a whisper of mana bleed into her voice.
"Dispel."
PING!

The violet barrier resonated like a struck crystal bell as the intricate geometric runes flashed once, folding inward like burning paper, before dissolving into harmless motes of purple light that drifted harmlessly down onto the snow.
The dark yawning mouth of the cavern stood wide open.
Durna pulled her mount up beside Tasmin, looking into the darkness with a grim assessing eye.
"Welcome to Mine BVR Star, girls.
Mind your step; the frost inside is slicker than grease..."
Tasmin gave the dwarf a strange sideways look.
"BVR Star?
Seriously?
How the hell does Thora come up with these designations?
Did she just pull random consonants out of an empty ale barrel?"
"Clan codes, Captain," Durna snorted, rolling up her paper with a sharp snap.
"BVR stands for Black Vein Runic...
The ’Star’ part is because the primary yield here isn’t mundane iron... it’s Star-Iron that exists in pure unrefined clusters.
Master Thora doesn’t name things for poetry, she names them for the ledger."

paragraphs: Tasmin shook her head, raising her hand to signal the column. "Hold your mounts at the threshold."
She swung her gaze back toward the massive construct that had come to a halt ten paces out.
"Golem, halt," she ordered.
KRRR-CLANG!
The Phase 2 Golem locked its limbs, the pneumatic hiss of its internal mana vents venting a cloud of white steam into the freezing morning air.
It stood motionless with its wide armored chassis looming over the wolves.
Tasmin looked at the mouth of the cave, then back at the construct.
She remembered the briefing Thora had given them by the foundry fires early that morning.
The dwarven forge master had been ruthlessly practical about the logistical hurdles of the day.

’Listen close, because I won’t repeat myself while the ale is wearing off...’ Thora had barked, leaning over an iron workbench. ’The Umbral Basin is riddled with fracture-tunnels... Some cavern mouths are broad enough to march an entire battalion through abreast but others like BVR Star have choke-points. Narrow throats where the bedrock squeezed tight centuries ago as a Phase 2 chassis in its four-legged form is broad as an imperial carriage... If the mouth pinches, it gets jammed.’𝒻𝘳ℯℯ𝑤ℯ𝒷𝘯ℴ𝓋ℯ𝘭.𝑐ℴ𝑚
Thora had tapped the schematics with a soot-stained knuckle.

’So I built in an override... It’s called the Phase 3 Protocol. It splits the core mana loop, uncouples the secondary spine, and separates the Phase 2 unit into two smaller independent Phase 3 quad-units. They can squeeze through the narrow fissures, crawl through the throat, and then lock their cores back together once they reach the primary chamber. You have a second option, of course... you can order the golem to simply smash the opening wider with its siege fists but frankly, Rowenna and I haven’t coded enough structural intelligence into their core yet. If you tell a golem to widen a tunnel, it’s just as likely to bring down fifty tons of ceiling on your skulls so don’t be stupid and use the split protocol.’
Tasmin let out a slow sigh, looking up at the construct.
"Protocol Phase 3," Tasmin commanded. "Decouple."
WHIRRRR-CLANK!
The central amber optic on the golem’s brow flickered wildly.
Deep within its stone torso, heavy mechanical latches snapped open with the sound of snapping iron bars.
The central alloy spine hissed, venting a violent burst of pressurized mana from its midline.
Before the eyes of the wide-eyed recruits, the massive twelve-foot-wide construct began to structurally divide.

The thick interlocking basalt plates along the sternum parted cleanly as the auxiliary limbs shifted their weight, swinging outward on heavy ball-and-socket joints, while the secondary mana conduits re-routed their flows.
Within five seconds, the singular siege engine had separated into two sleek low-slung six-foot-tall Phase 3 constructs, each carrying half of the modular alloy storage bins on their backs.
They looked like heavy four-legged stone hounds, their smaller amber cores blinking in synchronized unison.
"Holy shit..." one of the recruits whispered, her knuckles whitening on her wolf’s reins. "It just... broke in half and grew legs."
"Shut your mouth and keep moving," Tasmin chuckled, nudging her wolf forward. "You’re in Blessed Land now so get used to the impossible."
Mine BVR Star was a relatively modest excavation site compared to the sprawling industrial zones of the basin.
Because of its constrained footprint, Silas had allocated only a single Phase 2 unit to Tasmin’s team.
Brida, who had been deployed to the crags miles to the south, had also received a single unit.

The Phase 1 golems... the true behemoths capable of hauling a lot of loads had been reserved for the high-priority targets. One had gone to Mine KB-22, where Lord Silas himself was leading the primary excavation into the massive Mana Diamond clusters.

The other had been assigned to Mine XVIT, a completely unmapped high-risk one far to the northwest where Goddess Eluned and Morwenna were overseeing the harvesting of living spirit-ores and unrefined void-veins.
Tasmin led the column beneath the jagged stone arch of the cavern mouth.
The two smaller Phase 1 golems followed in single file, their stone pads clicking softly against the frozen rock, their reduced profiles clearing the narrow granite overhangs with inches to spare.
Once the entire squad, the wolves, and the constructs had navigated the thirty-yard entrance throat, the cavern suddenly opened up into a massive vault.
It was a vast natural stone amphitheater.

The ceiling vaulted thirty feet overhead, supported by thick, natural pillars of black basalt that were slick with moisture and the air was strikingly still, noticeably warmer than the howling blizzard outside, though it carried a strange smell.
Tasmin reined in her mount and turned back toward the two smaller golems.
"Phase 2 Protocol," she commanded. "Reconverge."
CLANK-HISS-CRUNCH.
The two stone constructs stepped side by side, their internal magnetic arrays drawing them together with terrifying hydraulic force.

The central spine locked shut, the heavy alloy plates slotted together with a series of thunderous, metallic snaps, and within seconds, the single monolithic Phase 2 Golem was whole once more, standing tall and immobile in the center of the chamber.
Durna swung her leg over her wolf, dropping heavily to the stone floor with a sharp clatter of her steel-toed boots.
She walked forward, waving a hand toward the surrounding walls.
"Take a look, girls," Durna grinned, her voice echoing off the cavern ceiling. "This is what you’re sweating for."
The women dismounted, their eyes wide as they took in the chamber.
BVR Star was not simply an empty hole in the ground...
Embedded deep within the dark basalt walls, and even protruding in massive ridges directly from the stone floor, were vast sprawling formations of Star-Iron.
In the dim light of their torches, the mineral was breathtakingly beautiful.

It didn’t look like common rust-colored iron, instead it was a deep midnight-blue metal, so dark it seemed to absorb the light around it, but its entire crystalline surface was flecked with microscopic glowing silver motes that pulsed softly in the gloom, resembling a living constellation of stars trapped within the stone.
In several alcoves, the ore had grown outward into massive tree-like crystal clusters that branched toward the ceiling like dark glittering coral.
"It’s... it looks like the night sky," a recruit breathed, reaching out a hesitant hand toward a nearby protrusion.

"Don’t touch it with bare skin, lass!" Durna barked sharply, causing the girl to yank her hand back as if burned. "Star-Iron is dense as lead and temperamental as an angry badger... You handle it wrong or strike it with brute force, and the mana lattice inside can destabilize. It requires a master forge to work, and it requires dwarven hands to mine."
The dwarf turned toward the massive construct idling behind them.

"Captain Tasmin," Durna called out. "Tell the big bastard to lay flat. If we’re hauling out three tons of this stuff today, I don’t want the girls breaking their spines trying to hoist fifty-pound chunks over an eight-foot bin wall and make sure it drops down before you pull the kit down... no sense denting the master’s tools on the bedrock."
Tasmin nodded, turning to the construct. "Golem, ground posture. Lay flat."
PSSSSSSSSSH.
The Phase 2 Golem responded instantly.
Its massive, four-legged joints folded outward with a deep hydraulic sigh, lowering its heavy undercarriage directly onto the cavern floor.
In this grounded state, the top edges of its reinforced transport bins sat barely waist-high... a perfectly level accessible loading platform.
Tasmin walked over to the side of the construct, her boots finding purchase on the alloy mounting rungs.
She scrambled up onto the back of the resting golem with feline agility.
Mounted securely behind the central mana manifold were two heavy-duty alloy chests.
One was packed tight with custom-forged dwarven pickaxes, pry-bars, and runic chisels, all crafted from tempered steel designed not to spark against reactive ores.
The other chest contained their work gear.
Tasmin flipped the heavy iron latches open with a pair of sharp clicks.
"Catch," Tasmin called down, hoisting the bundles of gear and dropping them smoothly to the waiting girls below.
The squad quickly set about stripping off their heavy travel furs.
The cavern was insulated from the freezing wind, and the friction of heavy mining meant excess fabric was a liability.
The custom mining attire that Thora had commissioned from the territory’s tailor overnight was a masterclass in functional and incredibly flattering design.

The girls peeled off their thick wool coats and heavy plate pauldrons, leaving themselves in form-fitting flexible undergarments made of a dark breathable stretch-fabric reinforced with fine steel-mesh underlays along the vital zones.

Over this, they strapped thick supple leather harnesses that crossed tightly over their chests, supporting their torsos and cinching snugly around their waists and muscular thighs to distribute the strain of heavy lifting.
"Gods, these straps are tight," a blonde veteran muttered, twisting her torso as she pulled a leather buckle through an iron loop.
The harness pulled the dark fabric taut across her prominent, sweat-sheened chest, pushing her cleavage upward while accentuating the sharp defined curve of her waist.
"Thora definitely didn’t leave much room for modesty."

"Modesty doesn’t haul iron, Lyra," another girl laughed, sliding into a pair of tight steel-reinforced trousers that clung snugly to the heavy curve of her hips and thighs as she bent over to lace her boots. "Besides, if the Lord drops by for an inspection later, I certainly won’t complain if his eyes wander."
A chorus of breathless giggles rippled through the squad as the women adjusted their gear, checking the tension of their thigh holsters and securing their hair into tight braids.

There was a raw unashamed vitality to them... strong and beautifully toned bodies honed by brutal combat, now bound in dark leather and steel mesh that showed off every flex of corded muscle and feminine curve.
Once the squad was fully suited, Durna stepped to the center of the chamber, holding a polished dwarven pickaxe in one hand.

"Gather round, you lot!" Durna shouted, her voice snapping the girls out of their playful banter. "Listen up, because this isn’t standard trench-digging. You don’t take a pickaxe to an Umbral Basin vein the way you’d hack at firewood... Master Thora’s words are law in this territory and as she said, You don’t fight the mountain... You simply read it."
Durna walked up to a smooth, vertical slab of black basalt where a massive cluster of Star-Iron protruded like dark crystals.
"Step one," Durna said, pressing her bare palm flat against the cold, unrefined rock face.

She closed her eyes, her weathered features settling into an expression of deep meditative concentration. "You press your flesh to the stone with no gloves. You close your eyes, and you feel the vibrations. The rock has a grain, just like ironwood and the mana flowing through the subterranean aquifers creates micro-tremors so you have to find where the stone wants to part."
The recruits watched silently, leaning forward with keen interest.

"Step two," Durna continued, opening her eyes and tracing a blunt, calloused finger along the surface of the basalt, about eight inches to the left of the midnight-blue ore. "Look right here. Do you see this faint discolored gray track? That’s what we call the bleed-line..."
"What makes it gray?" a recruit asked, squinting at the rock.

"Heat and time, lass," Durna explained. "High-density mana crystals like Star-Iron generate internal spiritual heat over centuries... That heat slowly cooks the surrounding rock, pushing all the mineral impurities outward into a distinct brittle fault line. Now... this is the most important rule in dwarven mining... Never strike the bleed-line directly."
"Why not?" Tasmin chimed in, crossing her arms over her chest to emphasize the lesson. "Tell them what happens, Durna."

"If you hit the bleed-line directly," Durna said, her voice dropping into a stern growl, "the shockwave doesn’t break the stone... it travels straight down the fault path like lightning and violently detonates the crystal lattice of the Star-Iron behind it. You’ll shatter fifty pounds of high-tier enchanting metal into worthless inert gray dust before you ever see it. You’ll ruin the yield, and Thora will personally skin you alive."
Durna raised her pickaxe, stepping back.

"Instead, you measure roughly six inches outside the bleed-line which is... right here." She tapped the dark basalt with the tip of her boot. "And when you swing, you don’t use your back and you don’t channel mana either. You need pure technique... Let the weight of the forged head do the work, and snap your wrists right at the point of impact."
Durna planted her feet.
Her posture was relaxed as she brought the pickaxe back in a smooth effortless arc, letting the tool drop toward the stone.
Right at the apex of the swing, her wrists snapped forward with clean whip-like precision.
TINK!
It wasn’t a deafening bone-jarring crash... instead it was a single high-pitched metallic chime that resonated cleanly through the vaulted cavern.
For half a second, nothing seemed to happen.
Then, right from the point of impact, a series of microscopic hairline fractures spider-webbed outward in a flawless geometric circle.
CRRR-SLIDE!
With a clean scraping sigh, an entire two-hundred-pound slab of outer basalt separated from the bedrock, sliding smoothly down the wall and landing harmlessly in the dust.
Behind it, completely exposed and undamaged, lay a massive, twelve-inch branch of glowing midnight-blue Star-Iron, pulsing with tiny silver constellations in the dark.
The recruits gasped, their eyes shining with pure awe.
"That..." the young chestnut-haired girl whispered, "was incredible."

"That’s craftsmanship, lass," Durna smirked, tossing a spare pickaxe to the nearest recruit. "Now grab your tools, find a section of wall, and start reading the stone... Every five hundred pounds of clean ore loaded into the golem gets logged in your name. Get to work!"

chapters.title: Chapter 477: Hive Of Shapeshifters [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Within minutes, the vast chamber of Mine BVR Star was filled with the hypnotic music of industry.
Tink! Tink! Tink!
The sounds were crisp and precise.
The veterans, having practiced the technique from the last couple of women who mined, worked with fluid mesmerizing grace.
Slabs of dark basalt cleaved cleanly away from the veins, tumbling down to be broken into manageable chunks and hauled over to the grounded golem.
The recruits struggled at first, their swings occasionally hitting too heavy or missing the fault lines, but under Durna’s sharp barking instruction, they quickly found the rhythm.
Sweat began to sheen across their exposed collarbones and bare shoulders, glistening in the soft ambient glow of the Star-Iron.
As the work progressed, the competitive tension melted into a lively infectious rhythm.

"Hey, Lyra!" one of the younger girls called out, heaving a thirty-pound chunk of glittering midnight-blue rock into the golem’s side bin with a dull thud. "That’s three loads for me! If you keep babying that chisel, the Lord is going to be rewarding me long before you even wash the dust off your face!"

"In your dreams, rookie!" Lyra shot back, swinging her pickaxe with a clean tink that dropped a massive slab of basalt. "The Lord likes women who know how to handle heavy tools with endurance! You’ll be crying for a water break before midday!"

"Oh, please!" another recruit chimed in, wiping her sweaty forehead with the back of a leather-gloved forearm, her chest heaving against her harness. "Neither of you has a chance! Did you see the way he looked at all of us during the morning briefing? He wants someone who can keep up with him in the field and in the sheets! I’m mining ten carts today if it kills me!"
From her position at the mobile workstation mounted near the golem’s primary manifold, Durna let out a hacking laugh, furiously scribbling weights and names into her vellum ledger.
"Keep flapping those gums, girls!" Durna yelled over the chime of the picks. "The more you argue, the faster you swing! At this rate, we’ll fill the chassis before the noon bells ring in the Keep!"
Down at the far end of the chamber, an older veteran with a clear melodic voice suddenly began to hum a rhythmic low-tempo marching tune.
Within seconds, she put words to the beat... a rough spirited work-song about bleeding in the snow, serving the black banner of Blessed Land, and coming home to the warm hearth of their Lord.
One by one, the other women picked up the melody.
Their voices rose together, blending into a rich, echoing chorus that filled the cavern vault, turning the grueling labor into an exhilarating unified celebration of strength.
Tink! Tink! Clang!
Every strike landed on the beat of the song.
The Phase 2 Golem remained resting on its belly, its massive alloy bins steadily filling with heaps of glittering constellation-flecked ore, unharmed by the careful deliberate loading.
Tasmin stood near the eastern wall, watching the squad with a satisfied smile.
She had already put in thirty minutes of heavy labor herself.

Utilizing her native shadow-affinity, she had condensed the darkness around her boots into dense whip-thin tendrils of solidified shadow, using them like auxiliary pry-bars to pop loosened slabs of bedrock away from the deep veins with effortless efficiency.
Her personal bin on the golem was already piled high with high-grade Star-Iron.
’It’s good work,’ Tasmin thought, looking at the glowing blue ore reflecting in the sweat on her arms. ’Clean yield and fast extraction... My Lord will certainly be pleased with the ledger.’
She lowered her pickaxe, leaning the heavy steel head against the cavern floor.
Her amber eyes narrowed as a dark frustration bubbled beneath the surface.
’...But it’s not enough.’
Mining a few hundred pounds of Star-Iron was standard duty.
Every girl in this room was doing it... Even if she broke the squad record and hauled five carts back to the Sovereign Distribution Nexus, it wouldn’t set her apart.
It wouldn’t make Silas look at her with that sudden electrifying intensity.
It wouldn’t earn her the right to kneel in his private office, to look up into those piercing blue eyes, and to have his hands tangled in her hair while she took him into her mouth.
To get that kind of recognition from her Lord, a woman had to bring him something extraordinary.
...A breakthrough or an eliminated threat.
Tasmin stepped away from the active rock face as she casually tossed her pickaxe aside, letting the tool clatter against a pile of discarded basalt rubble.
"Take a breather, Captain?" Durna called out from the golem, looking up from her vellum ledger.

"I’m going to run a perimeter sweep along the deeper fissures," Tasmin replied, her voice cool and authoritative as she adjusted the leather harness across her chest. "Keep the rhythm going, but keep your ears open... Watch the cavern mouth for any monsters that might catch our scent. You’ve got five veteran blades on the floor, so I’m not worried, but don’t get sloppy."
"Understood," Durna nodded, returning to her notes. "Don’t wander too deep... These basalt formations can run for miles."
Tasmin gave a dismissive wave and turned toward the far shadowed eastern wall of the cavern, well away from the torchlight and the singing recruits.𝒻𝑟𝘦𝘦𝘸ℯ𝒷𝑛𝘰𝓋ℯ𝘭.𝘤𝘰𝘮
She approached a massive irregular fissure where the bedrock had buckled inward centuries ago.
The ceiling dropped low here, casting deep ink-black shadows across the rubble. Tasmin closed her eyes, exhaling a slow breath as she extended her shadow perception.

Her internal mana surged but she didn’t push her senses outward like an elemental mage... she sank them downward, letting her consciousness bleed into the literal shadows pooling across the stone floor.
To Tasmin, darkness was not an absence of light but rather an interconnected liquid web that touched every crack, every seam, and every hidden void in the world.
Almost immediately, her perception hit an anomaly.
’...What is that?’
Directly ahead, resting against the lowest section of the wall where the floor met the bedrock, was a colossal rounded boulder roughly nine feet wide.
To the naked eye, it appeared to be a solid, impassable wall of fallen granite.
But through the liquid lens of her shadow-sense, Tasmin felt the gap.
There was a continuous hollow draft seeping around the jagged perimeter of the boulder as the stone wasn’t an integral part of the mountain but rather a plug.
It had been wedged into an existing passage.
More importantly, brushing against the fringes of her mana from the other side of that stone plug was a distinct sickening spiritual signature.
It was a foreign greasy mana carrying the unmistakable rotten stench of a monster she hated.
’Monsters,’ Tasmin thought, her eyes snapping open as her amber pupils narrowed into vertical slits. ’Right on the other side of our perimeter wall.’
She didn’t call for the squad as instead, Tasmin stepped directly into the darkness pooling beneath the overhang.
Her physical body dissolved, melting into pure liquid blackness with a soundless shhhk.
She became a shadow.
Frictionless, weightless, and entirely two-dimensional, Tasmin glided across the stone, sliding effortlessly into the narrow half-inch gap between the massive boulder and the bedrock wall.
Behind her, a couple of the recruits paused their singing for a second, glancing over at the empty space where their captain had just been standing.
"Captain just went into the shadows," the young chestnut-haired girl noted, blinking at the dark wall.
"Good," Lyra smirked, swinging her pickaxe with a clean tink. "That means she’s not hauling ore. More quota for the rest of us! Keep swinging, girls, the Lord’s reward is practically mine!"
On the other side of the boulder, Tasmin emerged from the narrow seam, reconstituting her shadow against the floor of a new subterranean world.
’What the actual fuck...’ Tasmin thought, her mind reeling as she took in the layout.
This wasn’t a simple cave pocket.
Behind the stone plug lay a colossal descending subterranean fracture system that stretched far deeper into the mountain roots than Mine BVR Star ever did.
The stone here was jagged, black, and slick with a foul-smelling translucent slime.

The boulder that sealed the entrance had been deliberately placed... if someone stood on the outside and moved the rock even an inch, they would find only narrow fist-sized crevices resembling crude eyeholes, carved specifically to allow something inside to peer out into the mining chamber without being seen.
It was an observation blind.
Tasmin didn’t linger as she remained in her liquid shadow state, flowing across the wet stone floor like spilled ink, completely silent as she descended the winding passage.
She hadn’t traveled thirty yards down the dark tunnel before her senses screamed...
A figure was slinking up the incline, moving directly toward the boulder plug.
Tasmin paused her drift, flattening herself into the seam between the floor and the wall.
The creature was walking on two legs.
It possessed the silhouette of an ordinary human... in fact, it wore the rough linen trousers and laced boots of a Blessed Land frontier scout.
But as it stepped beneath a patch of bioluminescent moss clinging to the ceiling, the truth was laid bare.
The skin was too tight and the joints moved with a jerky, unnatural elasticity, like meat being puppeted by invisible wires.
And most damning of all: as the creature passed directly beneath the glowing moss, the floor beneath its boots remained completely illuminated.
It cast no shadow.
’A shapeshifting wolf...’ Tasmin thought, a cold violent revulsion rippling through her core.

Tasmin and the others had went into deliberation, again it was still very crazy that these monsters could see your face once and copy it and not only that but it seemed like they could access surface memories too.
They didn’t seem all that strong but still... Tasmin wanted nothing more than to slaughter all of them.
The creature was sniffing the air, its nostrils flaring as it caught the faint scent of sweat and female laughter bleeding through the eyeholes of the boulder ahead.
It bared its teeth, revealing a double row of serrated, needle-thin wolf fangs behind a human mouth as it was heading straight for her squad.
’Tch.’
From within the deep blackness of the floor, Tasmin struck.
She didn’t manifest nor did she give the abomination a single second to comprehend its death.
FZZZZT-SHKLK!
Four massive pitch-black Shadow Spikes violently erupted directly from the floorboards beneath the creature’s feet.
The solid spear-like constructs tore through the beast’s knees, impaling its thighs and driving straight upward through its torso, lifting the creature bodily off the ground.
Before it could emit even a muffled hiss, a fifth spike shot from the wall, punching cleanly through the base of its skull and pinning its head to the jagged basalt with a wet splintering crunch.
Black foul-smelling ichor hissed against the stone.
The creature’s human flesh melted away in death, dissolving into the mangled, mangy gray fur of a six-foot wolf but Tasmin didn’t even pause to watch it die.
She disengaged her mana, leaving the carcass pinned like a butterfly to the rock, and surged downward through the descending tunnel.
It was a long steep dive.
The fissure plunged hundreds of feet into the subterranean bedrock, twisting and turning through ancient vents.
As she neared the lower terminus, a diffuse illumination began to wash over the dark stone.
’Light?’ Tasmin wondered with her shadow-form accelerating. ’This deep underground?’
The narrow tunnel abruptly ended.
Tasmin’s shadow shot out into the open air for a fraction of a second before her instincts kicked in.

She snapped her mana upward, shooting like a streak of black lightning across thirty feet of empty space and anchoring herself seamlessly into the dense pitch-black shadows blanketing the cavern ceiling.
She clung there, perfectly flat, looking down at the horror below and the cavern was colossal.
It was a hollow that dwarfed even the central plaza of Blessed Land.

The ceiling vaulted nearly eighty feet overhead, but the most striking feature was a colossal fissure in the high stone roof... a natural skylight that opened directly to the surface of the Umbral Basin.
Through that massive hole, the iron-gray daylight of the morning bled downward, accompanied by a swirling drift of pale white snow that fluttered silently through the freezing draft.
Beneath that falling snow lay an entire civilization of nightmares.
It was a massive, thriving hive of the shapeshifting beasts.
Hundreds of them were moving across the cavern floor.
Some prowled in their native wolf forms but dozens of others were walking on two legs, wearing the stolen faces of human beings.
Tasmin’s breath caught in her throat, a cold suffocating fury seizing her chest.
’I fucking hate them...’
They had even constructed crude makeshift dwellings out of shattered bedrock, frozen timber, and the gnawed ribcages of massive basin megafauna.
And in the center of the cavern, bathed directly in the beam of daylight and falling snow, sat the alpha.
It was an enormous four-armed abomination, twice the size of a standard wolf, its flesh shifting constantly between scarred human muscle and dense armored wolf hide.
A suffocating oppressive aura of high-tier corrupted mana bled from its body, sending ripples through the cold air.
’It’s Tier 3, huh...? Maybe even beyond that...’

chapters.title: Chapter 478: Hive Of Shapeshifters [II]
paragraphs: Tasmin hung from the ceiling shadows with her heart hammering against her ribs as her mind calculating at terminal velocity.

’This is a staging ground,’ Tasmin realized, her eyes burning with pure ambition. ’They’ve been tunneling beneath the eastern crags, watching our perimeter, waiting for the right moment to breach the mines and slaughter our workers...’
...This was it.
...This was the extraordinary breakthrough she had been starving for!

’If I exterminate this hive...’ Tasmin thought, a wild delirious smirk stretching across her face in the dark. ’If I wipe out this entire anomalous nest and lay the head of this alpha at his feet... I will prove myself to Lord Silas. He won’t just reward me. He will take me into his bed. He will—’
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The thought was violently shattered.
The entire western bedrock wall of the colossal cavern... a solid expanse of granite ten feet thick suddenly vibrated with a deafening bone-crushing shockwave.
KRA-CRUNCH!
Dust, shattered stone, and ice rained down from the ceiling rafters.
The hundreds of shapeshifting wolves froze in terror, their crimson eyes snapping toward the western wall.
The four-armed alpha leaped to its feet, letting out a deafening roar that rattled the stalactites.
"GRAHHHH!"
Tasmin clung to the ceiling shadows, her eyes widening in horror.
’What the—’
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A second impact struck the stone as a colossal circular web of glowing crimson fractures violently spider-webbed across the ten-foot-thick wall.
The stone groaned, the internal crystalline construct screaming under an incomprehensible pressure.
’Fuck—’ Tasmin’s mind screamed.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The third strike detonated the wall!
The entire section of bedrock violently exploded inward in a cataclysmic shower of pulverized gravel, flaming rock shards, and howling pressurized wind.
Shooting straight through the pulverized breach, completely enveloped in an incandescent roaring aura of crimson battle-energy came a solitary figure.
It was Brida.
The Titan was hurtling through the air thirty feet above the cavern floor, her massive rune-forged tower shield held locked across her chest.
Her hair was wild, her crimson eyes blazing with battle-crazed joy, and a massive grin split across her face as she looked down at the sea of terrified monsters below.
Mid-flight, Brida channeled the entirety of her explosive mana into the face of her tower shield, the heavy alloy plate igniting with a blinding apocalyptic red fire.
She threw her head back, her voice echoing off the cavern walls like a rolling thunderclap.
"AEGIS CHARGE!"
KRA-BAAAAAAAANG!
Brida collided with the cavern floor like a falling meteor.

The explosion was catastrophic as a thirty-foot-wide crater blasted into the bedrock, sending a concussive shockwave tearing across the cavern that pulverized dozens of makeshift dens and launched fifty shrieking wolves bodily into the air.
Rock, dust, and flaming red mana rained down through the falling snow.
Up in the ceiling shadows, Tasmin stared down at the crater in brain-melting disbelief.
’Fucking hell...’ Tasmin’s eye twitched violently in the dark. ’Why the absolute fuck is Brida here?!’

The violent shockwave of Brida’s cratering impact was still tearing through the hollow, ripping jagged stalactites from the eighty-foot vaulted ceiling and sending them crashing like stone spears into the frozen dirt.
Dust, pulverized granite, and scorching crimson embers swirled violently through the draft bleeding down from the skylight, mingling with the slow perpetual drift of surface snow.
Up in the pitch-black seam where the cavern wall met the vaulted ceiling, Tasmin gulped.
Her throat felt completely parched and her nails dug into the spatial fabric of the shadows as her amber eyes went wider staring straight down into the smoking thirty-foot crater.

’She... she really just dropped through ten feet of solid mountain rock,’ Tasmin thought with a cold bead of sweat rolling down the nape of her neck. ’She didn’t perform any reconnaissance... Surprisingly, that’s just like Brida.’
Down below, the dense cloud of gray chalk and pulverized stone parted with an aggressive whipping rush of wind.
FWOOSH!
Brida stood dead center in the shattered crater, her boots planted knee-deep in the pulverized rubble.
Her hair whipped around her shoulders like untamed fire, and her heavy armor rattled as her broad chest expanded with a massive chest-rattling breath.
She threw her head back, her jaw covered in chalky white dust, and let out a booming unhinged bark of laughter.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHA!"
The sound was thunderous, echoing off the jagged basalt walls with enough concussive volume to rattle the teeth of the snarling beasts crawling out of the debris.
"I finally found you!" Brida roared, grinning with all thirty-two teeth exposed.
With a brutal flick of her wrists, she hoisted her massive thick-bladed Titan’s Cleaver from the crater floor.
She gave the colossal slab of tempered alloy a casual, one-handed spin, the oversized counterweighted pommel whistling through the air with a terrifying sequence of heavy air-splitting whooshes.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH!
The draft generated by the spinning cleaver literally blasted the hanging smoke away from her face.
Like every other woman who had pulled on custom leather harnesses and sharpened her tools in the courtyard at dawn, Brida had spent the entire morning wracked by an itch she couldn’t scratch.
The Lord’s morning decree had burned into her mind like a brand.
Silas had looked across the formation with those calm eyes and offered a reward to whoever brought home the greatest haul.

And Brida, whose devotion to the Lord burned with a feverish competitive intensity that was far more than the heat of Thora’s forge had no intention of settling for a handful of common mining credits.
’Everyone’s mining but I’m glad I ended up here...’
She hadn’t planned on ending up in an underground hive.
Her squad had arrived at their assigned sector three miles to the south, unlimbered their Phase 2 Golem, and begun chipping away at a shallow surface seam of basalt.
But then Brida’s keen instincts had flared as she had caught a scent... a greasy foul smell of rotten wolf marrow bleeding through a hairline fracture near the rear wall of their cave.
She had crept closer, only to spot a narrow spyhole bored through the rock.
Looking back at her through the dark had been a single milky-white eye set into the stolen face of a Blessed Land guard atop the gates.
The monster had been peeking. It had been crouched there, silently taking notes on their numbers, measuring their movements, watching the girls adjust their harnesses.
The audacity of it had set Brida’s blood on fire.
’Good times...’

She had simply planted her back foot, channeled every ounce of her mana into her right fist, and driven her iron-plated gauntlet straight through the stone wall, catching the peering aberration by its throat and crushing its windpipe into paste before it could blink.

’I didn’t have time to dig around for a connecting tunnel,’ Brida thought with her grin widening as she rested the blunt spine of the Titan’s Cleaver against her shoulder pauldron. ’I just barrelled myself through the walls in the direction where it came from!’
She had literally turned herself into a human battering ram.

Three miles of subterranean fault lines, collapsed fissures, and solid granite barriers, and Brida had simply lowered her shoulder, engaged her unyielding forward momentum, and smashed straight through the mountain roots like a runaway locomotive until she smelled a whole cluster of them rotting on the other side...
And now, she was standing in the middle of their nest.
SHKLK!
Without waiting for the dazed pack to organize, Brida exploded into motion.
She didn’t bother using a skill as she merely stepped forward with terrifying hydraulic power, driving the flat of her heavy cleaver into the chest of the nearest bipedal wolf.
CRUNCH!

The blow caved the beast’s ribcage inward like an empty tin can, launching the eight-foot monstrosity forty feet across the cavern where it smashed into a jagged stalagmite, snapping in half with a wet squelching thud.
From the cavern ceiling, Tasmin let out a venomous hissed breath.
’Like hell you’re taking this entire nest for yourself!’
SHSHSHK.
A patch of darkness detached from the eighty-foot ceiling, dropping like an executioner’s cloak.
Midway to the floor, the shadows snapped into physical reality with a sharp pop of displaced air.
Tasmin landed cleanly on the balls of her boots, dropping into a low crouch atop the crushed remains of a stone hovel, her twin void-black daggers sliding into her palms with a metallic hiss.

"Brida!" Tasmin snapped, her amber eyes burning with murderous competitive fire as she rose to her full height. "Keep your heavy, iron-plated paws off my targets! I spent twenty minutes tracking this nest through the stone seams! This is my operational sector!"
Brida paused mid-swing, the blade of her cleaver burying itself half an inch into the floorboards as she glanced over her shoulder.
She blinked, and then another loud mocking laugh tore from her chest.

"Your sector?!" Brida hollered back, stepping over a twitching corpse and casually crushing its skull beneath her steel-shod heel with a sickening splat. "Are you blind? Who broke the wall? Who dropped through the ceiling? Who made the entrance?! I found this place first!"
"You didn’t find it, you fell through a hole you made like a drunken ox!" Tasmin yelled with her figure instantly dissolving into a liquid blur of black mist.
SHING-SHING-SHING!
Tasmin reappeared behind a cluster of three snarling abominations.
Her void-black blades flickered through the gloom, carving three clean horizontal lines across their throats.
The armor-piercing enchantments on her daggers bypassed the creatures’ dense bone collars as if they were soft butter, severing windpipes and arteries in a single fluid heartbeat.

Black boiling ichor sprayed across the snow, but Tasmin was already sliding beneath the reaching sickle-claws of a fourth beast, her boots sweeping its legs out from under it. As the creature fell, she drove her reverse-gripped dagger straight down through its sternum, pinning it to the stone.
THWACK!𝒇𝒓𝙚𝒆𝔀𝓮𝓫𝒏𝓸𝙫𝓮𝓵.𝓬𝙤𝙢

"I was already in the ceiling before your thick skull even touched the rock!" Tasmin barked, wrenching the blade free and flicking the black blood onto the dirt. "I mapped the alpha! I took out their forward sentry at the upper boundary!"
"Oh, please!" Brida yelled back, her cleaver whistling through the air in a sweeping two-handed horizontal arc.
KRA-SHING!
Two bipedal wolves that had tried to leap at her exposed flank were cleaved completely in two at the waist, their upper torsos cartwheeling through the air before splashing wetly against the rubble.

"Mapping isn’t killing, Tasmin!" Brida shouted, ducking beneath a sweeping bone scythe and driving her heavy elbow into a monster’s jaw, shattering its teeth into powder. "You were probably sitting up there admiring your braids while waiting for someone with actual muscle to show up and do the heavy lifting!"
"I was preparing an execution web, you oversized battering ram!"
FZZT-CLANG!
Tasmin flipped backward through the air, her twin chains whipping out from beneath her leather harness.
The dark enchanted links wrapped tightly around the ankles of a lunging aberration, hauling it backward off its feet.
She yanked with both arms, dragging the shrieking monster directly into the path of Brida’s backswing.
THUD-CRUNCH!
The blunt spine of Brida’s cleaver smashed through the beast’s cranium, obliterating it instantly.
"Nice toss!" Brida grinned, not missing a beat. "See? You make a decent squire when you try!"
"I am going to strangle you with these chains while you sleep, Brida, I swear to the Lord..." Tasmin hissed, but she couldn’t stop the fierce exhilarating adrenaline from singing in her veins.
For the next five minutes, the cavern was transformed into a slaughterhouse.
They bickered with every breath, trading sharp, biting insults with the easy familiarity of sisters who had bled in the same mud for months, but their combat synergy was terrifying.

Where Brida was an immovable roaring wall of destruction... shattering bones, detonating kinetic shockwaves with her shield, and crushing formations under the weight of her cleaver, Tasmin was the cold silent scalpel.

She slipped through the blind spots Brida created, her shadow-steps placing her behind every beast that flinched, her blades severing tendons, puncturing lungs, and pinning regenerators to the stone before their wounds could knit.
CRACK! SQUELCH! SHING!
Severed limbs, shattered ribs, and pools of boiling, acidic blood carpeted the floor as the makeshift hovels of the hive were crushed into splintered kindling.
Gradually, the chaotic noise of combat began to thin.
The howling shrieking horde of hundreds had been violently whittled down to a brutal suffocating crawl.
The two commanders came to a halt back-to-back in the center of the devastated clearing, breathing heavily.

Brida’s heavy plate was caked in black ichor and gray stone dust as her Titan’s Cleaver dripping with foul fluids and Tasmin stood lightly on the balls of her feet, her dark leather harness clinging to her sweat-sheened skin and her chest heaving as she spun her daggers into reverse grips.
Around them, barely a dozen creatures remained alive.
They had backed away into the shadows beneath the far rock wall, their sickle-claws trembling against the stone.
And towering directly in front of them, standing bathed in the pale daylight and swirling snow falling from the skylight, was the massive four-armed alpha.
Brida spat a mouthful of dust onto the ground, resting her heavy blade across her shoulder as she glanced sideways at Tasmin.
"Well," Brida murmured, her voice dropping the loud mockery, settling into a low appreciative hum. "Look at what’s left... Not bad for a couple of mining guards..."
Tasmin wiped a stray lock of dark hair from her forehead, her amber eyes scanning the surviving cluster.
"Twelve standard abominations," Tasmin muttered, her breath coming in steady controlled clouds of vapor. "Plus the big bastard in the center."

sentences.text: Tasmin hung from the ceiling shadows with her heart hammering against her ribs as her mind calculating at terminal velocity.

’This is a staging ground,’ Tasmin realized, her eyes burning with pure ambition. ’They’ve been tunneling beneath the eastern crags, watching our perimeter, waiting for the right moment to breach the mines and slaughter our workers...’
...This was it.
...This was the extraordinary breakthrough she had been starving for!
’If I exterminate this hive...’ Tasmin thought, a wild delirious smirk stretching across her face in the dark. ’If I wipe out this entire anomalous nest and lay the head of this alpha at his feet...
I will prove myself to Lord Silas.
He won’t just reward me.
He will take me into his bed.
He will—’
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The thought was violently shattered.
The entire western bedrock wall of the colossal cavern... a solid expanse of granite ten feet thick suddenly vibrated with a deafening bone-crushing shockwave.
KRA-CRUNCH!
Dust, shattered stone, and ice rained down from the ceiling rafters.
The hundreds of shapeshifting wolves froze in terror, their crimson eyes snapping toward the western wall.
The four-armed alpha leaped to its feet, letting out a deafening roar that rattled the stalactites.
"GRAHHHH!"
Tasmin clung to the ceiling shadows, her eyes widening in horror.
’What the—’
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A second impact struck the stone as a colossal circular web of glowing crimson fractures violently spider-webbed across the ten-foot-thick wall.
The stone groaned, the internal crystalline construct screaming under an incomprehensible pressure.
’Fuck—’ Tasmin’s mind screamed.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The third strike detonated the wall!
The entire section of bedrock violently exploded inward in a cataclysmic shower of pulverized gravel, flaming rock shards, and howling pressurized wind.
Shooting straight through the pulverized breach, completely enveloped in an incandescent roaring aura of crimson battle-energy came a solitary figure.
It was Brida.
The Titan was hurtling through the air thirty feet above the cavern floor, her massive rune-forged tower shield held locked across her chest.
Her hair was wild, her crimson eyes blazing with battle-crazed joy, and a massive grin split across her face as she looked down at the sea of terrified monsters below.
Mid-flight, Brida channeled the entirety of her explosive mana into the face of her tower shield, the heavy alloy plate igniting with a blinding apocalyptic red fire.
She threw her head back, her voice echoing off the cavern walls like a rolling thunderclap.
"AEGIS CHARGE!"
KRA-BAAAAAAAANG!
Brida collided with the cavern floor like a falling meteor.

The explosion was catastrophic as a thirty-foot-wide crater blasted into the bedrock, sending a concussive shockwave tearing across the cavern that pulverized dozens of makeshift dens and launched fifty shrieking wolves bodily into the air.
Rock, dust, and flaming red mana rained down through the falling snow.
Up in the ceiling shadows, Tasmin stared down at the crater in brain-melting disbelief.
’Fucking hell...’ Tasmin’s eye twitched violently in the dark. ’Why the absolute fuck is Brida here?!’

The violent shockwave of Brida’s cratering impact was still tearing through the hollow, ripping jagged stalactites from the eighty-foot vaulted ceiling and sending them crashing like stone spears into the frozen dirt.
Dust, pulverized granite, and scorching crimson embers swirled violently through the draft bleeding down from the skylight, mingling with the slow perpetual drift of surface snow.
Up in the pitch-black seam where the cavern wall met the vaulted ceiling, Tasmin gulped.
Her throat felt completely parched and her nails dug into the spatial fabric of the shadows as her amber eyes went wider staring straight down into the smoking thirty-foot crater.
’She... she really just dropped through ten feet of solid mountain rock,’ Tasmin thought with a cold bead of sweat rolling down the nape of her neck. ’She didn’t perform any reconnaissance...
Surprisingly, that’s just like Brida.’
Down below, the dense cloud of gray chalk and pulverized stone parted with an aggressive whipping rush of wind.
FWOOSH!
Brida stood dead center in the shattered crater, her boots planted knee-deep in the pulverized rubble.
Her hair whipped around her shoulders like untamed fire, and her heavy armor rattled as her broad chest expanded with a massive chest-rattling breath.
She threw her head back, her jaw covered in chalky white dust, and let out a booming unhinged bark of laughter.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHA!"
The sound was thunderous, echoing off the jagged basalt walls with enough concussive volume to rattle the teeth of the snarling beasts crawling out of the debris.
"I finally found you!" Brida roared, grinning with all thirty-two teeth exposed.
With a brutal flick of her wrists, she hoisted her massive thick-bladed Titan’s Cleaver from the crater floor.
She gave the colossal slab of tempered alloy a casual, one-handed spin, the oversized counterweighted pommel whistling through the air with a terrifying sequence of heavy air-splitting whooshes.
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH!
The draft generated by the spinning cleaver literally blasted the hanging smoke away from her face.
Like every other woman who had pulled on custom leather harnesses and sharpened her tools in the courtyard at dawn, Brida had spent the entire morning wracked by an itch she couldn’t scratch.
The Lord’s morning decree had burned into her mind like a brand.
Silas had looked across the formation with those calm eyes and offered a reward to whoever brought home the greatest haul.

And Brida, whose devotion to the Lord burned with a feverish competitive intensity that was far more than the heat of Thora’s forge had no intention of settling for a handful of common mining credits.
’Everyone’s mining but I’m glad I ended up here...’
She hadn’t planned on ending up in an underground hive.
Her squad had arrived at their assigned sector three miles to the south, unlimbered their Phase 2 Golem, and begun chipping away at a shallow surface seam of basalt.
But then Brida’s keen instincts had flared as she had caught a scent... a greasy foul smell of rotten wolf marrow bleeding through a hairline fracture near the rear wall of their cave.
She had crept closer, only to spot a narrow spyhole bored through the rock.
Looking back at her through the dark had been a single milky-white eye set into the stolen face of a Blessed Land guard atop the gates.
The monster had been peeking.
It had been crouched there, silently taking notes on their numbers, measuring their movements, watching the girls adjust their harnesses.
The audacity of it had set Brida’s blood on fire.
’Good times...’

She had simply planted her back foot, channeled every ounce of her mana into her right fist, and driven her iron-plated gauntlet straight through the stone wall, catching the peering aberration by its throat and crushing its windpipe into paste before it could blink.

’I didn’t have time to dig around for a connecting tunnel,’ Brida thought with her grin widening as she rested the blunt spine of the Titan’s Cleaver against her shoulder pauldron. ’I just barrelled myself through the walls in the direction where it came from!’
