chapters.title: Chapter 479: Hive Of Shapeshifters [III]
paragraphs: "How about we share the glory?" Brida asked, nudging Tasmin’s shoulder with her armored elbow. "Half and half for the ledger? We tell the Lord we breached the nest together?"
Tasmin glanced at her, seeing the wide battle-hungry grin on the brawler’s face.
A soft genuine smirk touched her own lips.
"Fine," Tasmin conceded softly. "Half and half but I get the first strike on the—"
SZZZZZZZZZT... BUBBLE... SQUELCH!
The words died in Tasmin’s throat.
Across the cavern, the twelve surviving monsters didn’t charge as instead, they suddenly collapsed to their knees with their bodies convulsing in violent unnatural spasms.
CRACK-SNAP-POP!
The sound of snapping bone was sickeningly loud, echoing off the stone like dry branches breaking under an avalanche.
Their stolen skins began to violently boil, but this time, the transformation didn’t stop at their standard eight-foot wolf-aberration forms.
Dark oily mana erupted from their spines in thick, greasy plumes.
Their rib cages violently expanded outward, tearing through their chests to form external armor-plated bone carapaces.

Their limbs doubled in thickness, corded with dark, pulsating purple veins, and their four-foot sickle-claws fused together, thickening into jagged, three-pronged bone blades that crackled with unstable corrosive lightning.
’The fuck....?’
SKREEEEEEEEEECH!

The pressure in the cavern plummeted as four of the twelve had ballooned into hulking quad-pedal siege beasts, while the remaining eight rose as towering ten-foot armored dreadnoughts, their jaws dripping with glowing violet venom that ate clean through the bedrock where it fell.
"Oh, look at that," Brida whispered, her eyes widening with genuine glee. "They brought out the reserve rations... These ones actually have some meat on them..."

"They’re burning their life force from what I can see," Tasmin warned, her muscles tensing like coiled steel springs. "They’re much faster now so don’t let those bone blades graze you... the venom is pressurized."
BOOM!
The four quad-pedal siege beasts moved simultaneously.
They detonated off the rock face, moving with terrifying near-instantaneous speed that kicked up twin roostertails of pulverized stone.
The nearest dreadnought closed the forty-foot gap in seconds, its jagged three-pronged bone blade descending toward Brida’s skull in an executioner’s strike.
’I’m guessing that they’re at Tier 3... all of them.’ Tasmin thought, ’This’ll be my first time facing so many.’
CLANG-KRAAAACK!
Brida didn’t retreat.
She dropped her center of gravity, slamming the base of her tower shield into the dirt just as the bone blade connected.
The feedback was monstrous as the shockwave blasted the snow away from their boots, but Brida’s body remained rigid, anchored by the unyielding power of her physical constitution.
Her teeth gritted, her hair flaring as the shield’s crimson runes flared bright violet, drinking in the massive kinetic shock.
"Is that all?!" Brida roared into the beast’s face.
FWOOM!
She engaged her shield bash, detonating the absorbed energy right into the creature’s chest.
KRA-POW!
The concussive blast blew the dreadnought’s external bone carapace to splinters, sending it skidding backward across the floor.
Before it could recover its footing, a streak of pure black lightning cut through its blind spot.
Tasmin appeared directly above the reeling beast as she didn’t use her daggers this time... she channeled her mana into her weighted chains.
CLINK-CLINK-WHIP!
The two were holding back a lot... this was underground and Tasmin had already informed her that her own mine was not too far away and she didn’t want anything to happen to it.
The dark links wrapped securely around the dreadnought’s throat and right arm.
Tasmin landed on its broad shoulders, planting her boots against its spine and leaning her entire body weight backward into the pull.
CRACK!
The beast’s neck strained with its jaws snapping wildly at the air.
"Brida! Clear the flank!" Tasmin shouted.
"On it!"
Brida spun on her heel, swinging her Titan’s Cleaver in a devastating low-to-high uppercut that caught a lunging quad-pedal beast right beneath the jaw.
SHKLK-CRUNCH!
The massive blade cleaved straight through the monster’s skull, splitting it from snout to crown.
Without pausing, Brida used the momentum of the swing to pivot, driving the iron rim of her shield directly into the side of the dreadnought Tasmin had pinned.
BOOM!
The combined force of the shield slam and the chain-strangle completely snapped the beast’s spine, sending it crashing to the dirt in a lifeless twitching heap.
For the next two minutes, the vault became an arena of relentless high-speed violence.
The empowered aberrations fought with savage suicidal coordination.
One lunged low to sweep Brida’s ankles with a sweeping sickle-claw, while another leaped from the high basalt pillars, aiming to crush her neck from above.
"Up, Brida!" Tasmin called out, melting into the shadows beneath the floor.
Brida didn’t even look up as she trusted Tasmin’s call implicitly... Why wouldn’t she?
She raised her shield directly overhead, locking her arms into a rigid impenetrable roof.
BANG!
The descending beast crashed against the top rim of the shield, its bone claws shattering against the dwarven alloy.
Before it could bounce off, Tasmin erupted from the darkness directly behind it in mid-air.
SHING-SHING!
Her void-daggers drove cleanly through the creature’s eye sockets, penetrating deep into its brainstem.
Tasmin kicked the limp carcass away, using it as a stepping stone to launch herself across the cavern toward the remaining dreadnoughts.
She moved like water... slipping beneath thrusts, sliding along the spatial seams, her blades finding the soft gaps beneath the external bone plates with lethal precision.
Every time a beast managed to corner her, Brida was there, smashing into its flank like an armored siege engine, breaking its momentum and shattering its guard.
CRUNCH! THUD! SPLAT!
One by one, the empowered abominations were butchered.
The last dreadnought let out a wet gurgling wheeze as Tasmin’s dagger punctured its throat from behind, while Brida’s heavy boot caved its chest in from the front.
The body hit the stone, dissolving into black acidic slime.
Silence descended over the clearing once more.

Save for the ragged breathing of the two women, the only sound was the howling wind drifting through the skylight, carrying fresh flakes of white snow that settled gently atop the mountains of butchered corpses.
And then, a deep earth-trembling vibration rolled through the bedrock.
THUMP. THUMP. THUMP.
At the far end of the cavern, bathed in the column of daylight, the four-armed alpha stepped forward.
The creature stood twelve feet tall, its massive bipedal frame corded with dense dark muscle that looked like braided steel cables.
In its upper hands, it gripped two colossal petrified bone clubs carved from the ribs of ancient basin drakes.
In its lower hands, six-foot bone scythes clicked and scraped against each other, dripping with glowing corrosive venom.
Its crimson eyes swept across the field of dead children, its nostrils flaring as it took in the scent of their blood.
"RAAAAAAAAHHHHHHHH!"
The roar was so concussive it blew the falling snow backward, tearing loose shale from the walls.
"Right," Brida muttered, wiping blood from her forehead with her knuckles whitening on the grip of her cleaver. "The head of the snake."
"No games this time, Brida," Tasmin breathed, her amber eyes locking onto the alpha’s joints. "We hit it together and we take its limbs first."
"Don’t have to tell me twice!"
BOOM!
They jumped the alpha simultaneously.
Brida led the charge, a direct frontal assault meant to draw its primary focus.
She charged across the thirty-yard gap, her tower shield glowing with violent red battle-mana.
The alpha snarled, swinging both of its massive drake-bone clubs downward in a crushing overhead smash meant to flatten her into the stone.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
’It’s Tier 4 too... or at the peak of Tier 3 rather.’
The clubs collided with the top rim of Brida’s shield with the force of an avalanche.

The bedrock beneath her boots violently shattered, sinking four inches into the dirt and blood trickled from the corner of Brida’s mouth as the monstrous weight of the strike shuddered through her bones, but her knees never buckled.
’Ah... I’m bleeding? How weird.’
Her unyielding constitution held the line, anchoring her against the impossible impact.
"TOO WEAK!" Brida screamed, her face flushed red as she pushed upward with all of her strength, throwing the massive bone clubs off balance.
In that exact microsecond of exposed recovery, Tasmin struck.
She didn’t run along the ground as she manifested directly out of the deep shadow cast by the alpha’s own raised arms.
SHSHSHK!
Tasmin blurred across its upper torso, her twin void-black daggers spinning in a blinding horizontal vortex.
SHING-SHING!
The blades bit deep into the thick, fibrous tendons of the alpha’s upper shoulders.

Black blood erupted like geysers, and with two sickening thwacks, both of the alpha’s upper arms... still clutching the petrified clubs were sheared completely off at the shoulder joints, tumbling heavily to the floor.
SKREEEEEEEEEE!
The beast shrieked in agony, but its lower arms immediately reacted, the six-foot bone scythes whipping inward to bisect Tasmin in mid-air.
"GET AWAY FROM HER!"
Brida stepped in, swinging her Titan’s Cleaver with the full rotation of her hips!
KRA-SHING!
The heavy alloy blade met the incoming bone scythes head-on.
The concentrated kinetic force sheared through the lower limbs, severing both scythes at the elbow with a deafening metallic snap as all four arms hit the dirt, dissolving into frothing gray slime.
The alpha stumbled backward, bleeding profusely from four massive cauterized stumps, its chest heaving as it backed toward the center of the daylight beam.
"We got it!" Brida laughed, raising her cleaver for the finishing blow. "It’s done!"
"Brida, wait!" Tasmin shouted with her senses screaming. "Back up! Back up right now!"
SZZZZZZT... GURGLE... SHRRRRK!
’It’s going to Tier 4!’
The alpha didn’t die.

Instead, its severed shoulder stumps violently ruptured as thick, black, rubbery masses of flesh erupted outward, not in the shape of arms, but in thick muscular tentacles lined with rows of barbed jagged bone suckers!
The creature’s entire silhouette violently melted and expanded as its wolf-like skull split down the center, folding backward into a bulbous grotesque cephalopod mantle.
Its legs dissolved into four more colossal twenty-foot-long tentacles that slammed into the cavern floor with earth-shaking thuds.

Within seconds, the bipedal wolf had completely transformed into a colossal, eight-tentacled, octopus-like underground monstrosity, its rubbery hide glistening with an impenetrable sheen of corrosive oily mucus.
WHIP-CRACK!
A massive twenty-foot tentacle lashed out faster than the eye could track.
BANG!
The strike caught Brida right in the chest, bypassing her guard and launching her armored frame sixty feet across the cavern.
She skipped twice across the jagged stone floor before slamming hard into the base of a basalt pillar, coughing out a spray of crimson blood.
"Brida!" Tasmin yelled with her heart lurching.
SWOOSH!
Two more barbed tentacles swept toward Tasmin, tearing through the air with the screech of high-velocity artillery.
Tasmin dropped into the shadows, sinking beneath the floorboards just as the tentacles smashed into the stone, pulverizing a five-foot trench where she had stood a fraction of a second before.
She emerged thirty feet away, sliding to a halt beside Brida.
Brida pushed herself up from the rubble, spitting a mouthful of dark blood into the snow.
"Haah... Haah..."
She wiped her jaw with her gauntlet, her breath coming in ragged shallow gasps, but the wild fire in her eyes hadn’t dimmed in the slightest.
"Gods damn it..." Brida coughed, leaning heavily on her cleaver. "That thing... hits like a siege catapult."
’...But bleeding feels so good.’
Was that why she let that hit her? Brida wanted to feel what it meant to bleed some more, it wasn’t her first time bu—

"Snap out of whatever you’re thinking... Its hide changed," Tasmin said, her voice dead serious as she watched the massive octopus-aberration drag its colossal bulk toward them as its tentacles whipping the air into a frenzy. "The mucus is absorbing impact so slicing it with normal edges won’t work as it’ll just deflect the blade."
Brida looked at Tasmin and Tasmin looked at Brida.
’I need to focus...’ Brida thought, she felt something weird with blood but she couldn’t act on it right now, she would ask her Lord.
Without a single word spoken, a silent mutual understanding passed between the two veterans as they nodded in unison.
’Together.’
"I’ll lock it down," Tasmin whispered, her mana flaring to its absolute limit. "You take the head."
"Make it count, Tas," Brida grinned, her muscles locking into position.
BOOM!
They leaped forward into the final clash.

The octopus-beast roared, a wet horrifying sound that bubbled from its central maw as all eight massive tentacles whipped forward simultaneously, creating a churning, impenetrable wall of bone-barbed muscle meant to crush anything in its path but Tasmin didn’t dodge.
She channeled her mana into her gear.
FZZZZZZT-KRA-FLASH!
Her long, dark chains ignited with roaring blinding crimson flames.
"Voltaic Chain Execution!" Tasmin roared!
She cast both chains forward, the burning links whistling through the air like twin fiery dragons.
The super-heated chains wrapped tightly around four of the primary tentacles, searing through the thick mucus and biting deep into the rubbery flesh.
Tasmin planted her boots into the stone, anchoring her weight as the violent flames spread, cooking the beast’s nervous system and completely paralyzing its forward momentum.
The monster shrieked, thrashing violently as its remaining tentacles whipped wildly to tear Tasmin apart.
"NOW, BRIDA!" Tasmin screamed, her muscles tearing under the immense crushing strain of holding the titan down. "KILL IT!"
Shooting straight through the gap created by the burning chains came Brida.
The women was not running... She was... flying?
Enveloped in an roaring pillar of deep crimson battle-mana, Brida launched herself thirty feet into the air, soaring directly above the thrashing pinned monstrosity.
She gripped the hilt of her Titan’s Cleaver with both hands, raising the colossal slab of steel high above her head.
Her face was twisted into a look of dominance.
"EARTH-SHATTERING CLEAVE!"
Brida brought the cleaver down with the wrath of an angry god.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The blade struck the central mantle of the octopus-beast dead center and the explosion was apocalyptic.
A blinding crimson shockwave detonated outward, tearing the burning tentacles to shreds and splitting the cavern floor in a thirty-meter-long, jagged chasm.
The colossal monster was cleaved in half, its rubbery bulk detonating into a massive raining shower of black blood, pulverized flesh, and dissolved slime.
THUD!𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Brida landed on the far side of the chasm, dropping to one knee as the cleaver buried itself to the hilt in the cracked stone.
’Good... I still feel this itch.’
The itch for blood...
The raining ichor splattered against the cavern floor, slowly hissing into harmless steam beneath the soft, persistent drift of surface snow.
It was over.
...The entire hive was dead.

sentences.text: "How about we share the glory?" Brida asked, nudging Tasmin’s shoulder with her armored elbow.
"Half and half for the ledger?
We tell the Lord we breached the nest together?"
Tasmin glanced at her, seeing the wide battle-hungry grin on the brawler’s face.
A soft genuine smirk touched her own lips.
"Fine," Tasmin conceded softly.
"Half and half but I get the first strike on the—"
SZZZZZZZZZT...
BUBBLE...
SQUELCH!
The words died in Tasmin’s throat.
Across the cavern, the twelve surviving monsters didn’t charge as instead, they suddenly collapsed to their knees with their bodies convulsing in violent unnatural spasms.
CRACK-SNAP-POP!
The sound of snapping bone was sickeningly loud, echoing off the stone like dry branches breaking under an avalanche.
Their stolen skins began to violently boil, but this time, the transformation didn’t stop at their standard eight-foot wolf-aberration forms.
Dark oily mana erupted from their spines in thick, greasy plumes.
Their rib cages violently expanded outward, tearing through their chests to form external armor-plated bone carapaces.

Their limbs doubled in thickness, corded with dark, pulsating purple veins, and their four-foot sickle-claws fused together, thickening into jagged, three-pronged bone blades that crackled with unstable corrosive lightning.
’The fuck....?’
SKREEEEEEEEEECH!

The pressure in the cavern plummeted as four of the twelve had ballooned into hulking quad-pedal siege beasts, while the remaining eight rose as towering ten-foot armored dreadnoughts, their jaws dripping with glowing violet venom that ate clean through the bedrock where it fell.
"Oh, look at that," Brida whispered, her eyes widening with genuine glee.
"They brought out the reserve rations...
These ones actually have some meat on them..."
"They’re burning their life force from what I can see," Tasmin warned, her muscles tensing like coiled steel springs.
"They’re much faster now so don’t let those bone blades graze you... the venom is pressurized."
BOOM!
The four quad-pedal siege beasts moved simultaneously.
They detonated off the rock face, moving with terrifying near-instantaneous speed that kicked up twin roostertails of pulverized stone.
The nearest dreadnought closed the forty-foot gap in seconds, its jagged three-pronged bone blade descending toward Brida’s skull in an executioner’s strike.
’I’m guessing that they’re at Tier 3... all of them.’ Tasmin thought, ’This’ll be my first time facing so many.’
CLANG-KRAAAACK!
Brida didn’t retreat.
She dropped her center of gravity, slamming the base of her tower shield into the dirt just as the bone blade connected.
The feedback was monstrous as the shockwave blasted the snow away from their boots, but Brida’s body remained rigid, anchored by the unyielding power of her physical constitution.
Her teeth gritted, her hair flaring as the shield’s crimson runes flared bright violet, drinking in the massive kinetic shock.
"Is that all?!" Brida roared into the beast’s face.
FWOOM!
She engaged her shield bash, detonating the absorbed energy right into the creature’s chest.
KRA-POW!
The concussive blast blew the dreadnought’s external bone carapace to splinters, sending it skidding backward across the floor.
Before it could recover its footing, a streak of pure black lightning cut through its blind spot.
Tasmin appeared directly above the reeling beast as she didn’t use her daggers this time... she channeled her mana into her weighted chains.
CLINK-CLINK-WHIP!
The two were holding back a lot... this was underground and Tasmin had already informed her that her own mine was not too far away and she didn’t want anything to happen to it.
The dark links wrapped securely around the dreadnought’s throat and right arm.
Tasmin landed on its broad shoulders, planting her boots against its spine and leaning her entire body weight backward into the pull.
CRACK!
The beast’s neck strained with its jaws snapping wildly at the air.
"Brida!
Clear the flank!" Tasmin shouted.
"On it!"
Brida spun on her heel, swinging her Titan’s Cleaver in a devastating low-to-high uppercut that caught a lunging quad-pedal beast right beneath the jaw.
SHKLK-CRUNCH!
The massive blade cleaved straight through the monster’s skull, splitting it from snout to crown.
Without pausing, Brida used the momentum of the swing to pivot, driving the iron rim of her shield directly into the side of the dreadnought Tasmin had pinned.
BOOM!
The combined force of the shield slam and the chain-strangle completely snapped the beast’s spine, sending it crashing to the dirt in a lifeless twitching heap.
For the next two minutes, the vault became an arena of relentless high-speed violence.
The empowered aberrations fought with savage suicidal coordination.
One lunged low to sweep Brida’s ankles with a sweeping sickle-claw, while another leaped from the high basalt pillars, aiming to crush her neck from above.
"Up, Brida!" Tasmin called out, melting into the shadows beneath the floor.
Brida didn’t even look up as she trusted Tasmin’s call implicitly...
Why wouldn’t she?
She raised her shield directly overhead, locking her arms into a rigid impenetrable roof.
BANG!
The descending beast crashed against the top rim of the shield, its bone claws shattering against the dwarven alloy.
Before it could bounce off, Tasmin erupted from the darkness directly behind it in mid-air.
SHING-SHING!
Her void-daggers drove cleanly through the creature’s eye sockets, penetrating deep into its brainstem.
Tasmin kicked the limp carcass away, using it as a stepping stone to launch herself across the cavern toward the remaining dreadnoughts.
She moved like water... slipping beneath thrusts, sliding along the spatial seams, her blades finding the soft gaps beneath the external bone plates with lethal precision.
Every time a beast managed to corner her, Brida was there, smashing into its flank like an armored siege engine, breaking its momentum and shattering its guard.
CRUNCH!
THUD!
SPLAT!
One by one, the empowered abominations were butchered.
The last dreadnought let out a wet gurgling wheeze as Tasmin’s dagger punctured its throat from behind, while Brida’s heavy boot caved its chest in from the front.
The body hit the stone, dissolving into black acidic slime.
Silence descended over the clearing once more.

Save for the ragged breathing of the two women, the only sound was the howling wind drifting through the skylight, carrying fresh flakes of white snow that settled gently atop the mountains of butchered corpses.
And then, a deep earth-trembling vibration rolled through the bedrock.
THUMP.
THUMP.
THUMP.
At the far end of the cavern, bathed in the column of daylight, the four-armed alpha stepped forward.
The creature stood twelve feet tall, its massive bipedal frame corded with dense dark muscle that looked like braided steel cables.
In its upper hands, it gripped two colossal petrified bone clubs carved from the ribs of ancient basin drakes.
In its lower hands, six-foot bone scythes clicked and scraped against each other, dripping with glowing corrosive venom.
Its crimson eyes swept across the field of dead children, its nostrils flaring as it took in the scent of their blood.
"RAAAAAAAAHHHHHHHH!"
The roar was so concussive it blew the falling snow backward, tearing loose shale from the walls.
"Right," Brida muttered, wiping blood from her forehead with her knuckles whitening on the grip of her cleaver.
"The head of the snake."
"No games this time, Brida," Tasmin breathed, her amber eyes locking onto the alpha’s joints.
"We hit it together and we take its limbs first."
"Don’t have to tell me twice!"
BOOM!
They jumped the alpha simultaneously.
Brida led the charge, a direct frontal assault meant to draw its primary focus.
She charged across the thirty-yard gap, her tower shield glowing with violent red battle-mana.
The alpha snarled, swinging both of its massive drake-bone clubs downward in a crushing overhead smash meant to flatten her into the stone.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

The clubs collided with the top rim of Brida’s shield with the force of an avalanche.

The bedrock beneath her boots violently shattered, sinking four inches into the dirt and blood trickled from the corner of Brida’s mouth as the monstrous weight of the strike shuddered through her bones, but her knees never buckled.
I’m bleeding?
How weird.’
Her unyielding constitution held the line, anchoring her against the impossible impact.
"TOO WEAK!" Brida screamed, her face flushed red as she pushed upward with all of her strength, throwing the massive bone clubs off balance.
In that exact microsecond of exposed recovery, Tasmin struck.
She didn’t run along the ground as she manifested directly out of the deep shadow cast by the alpha’s own raised arms.
SHSHSHK!
Tasmin blurred across its upper torso, her twin void-black daggers spinning in a blinding horizontal vortex.
SHING-SHING!
The blades bit deep into the thick, fibrous tendons of the alpha’s upper shoulders.

Black blood erupted like geysers, and with two sickening thwacks, both of the alpha’s upper arms... still clutching the petrified clubs were sheared completely off at the shoulder joints, tumbling heavily to the floor.
SKREEEEEEEEEE!
The beast shrieked in agony, but its lower arms immediately reacted, the six-foot bone scythes whipping inward to bisect Tasmin in mid-air.

Brida stepped in, swinging her Titan’s Cleaver with the full rotation of her hips!

The heavy alloy blade met the incoming bone scythes head-on.

chapters.title: Chapter 480: Mine XVIT
paragraphs: Tasmin let out a long shuddering breath, her chains clattering loosely against her leather greaves as she collapsed back onto her heels.
She was completely exhausted, her muscles burning with lactic acid and her dark harness soaked in sweat and black blood.
Across the chasm, Brida slowly pulled herself up to her feet.
She let out a long wheezing sigh, raising a battered, armor-plated gauntlet to wipe a thick streak of black blood from her cheek.
She walked slowly over the smoking rubble, stopping beside Tasmin.
She looked down at the smaller panting woman, and for a moment, her wild battle-crazed face softened into a remarkably gentle expression.
"Hey," Brida murmured, offering a hand to haul Tasmin up.
Tasmin took it, letting Brida pull her to her feet.
"Good fight," Brida said quietly, looking out over the quiet devastated cavern.
She paused, and then let out another soft, tired breath. "Look... about the ledger and about Lord Silas."
Tasmin blinked, looking up at her.

"You found the nest, Tasmin," Brida said, her tone carrying a rare, solemn weight. "You tracked it through the seams. You held the bastard down so I could land the cleaver. I’m... I’m going to let you have the win. You report this to Lord Silas. Tell him you cleared the staging ground. That’s what sisters do, right? You deserve the reward."
Tasmin’s amber eyes widened in stunned shock.
Her heart tightened in her chest as a wave of overwhelming warmth washed over her, completely melting the competitive edge she had held all morning.
’She’s... she’s really letting me have it?’ Tasmin thought, a soft emotional flush rising to her cheeks. ’After all that bickering... after breaking through the wall... she’s stepping aside for me.’
Tasmin swallowed hard, her voice trembling slightly with raw gratitude.

"Brida..." Tasmin whispered, reaching out to touch the dented pauldron on Brida’s shoulder. "I... thank you. I’m sorry for snapping at you earlier. I shouldn’t have called you an ox, you really saved—"
Before the words could fully leave her mouth, Brida’s gentle solemn expression violently shattered.
A massive smirk split across the brawler’s face.
WHOOSH!
Brida kicked off the stone, leaping twenty feet straight up into the air and grabbing the jagged edge of the breach she had smashed through earlier!
She pulled herself up into the tunnel, poking her head back out to look down at Tasmin with a roaring hysterical cackle.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHA! ARE YOU DUMB, TASMIN?!" Brida screamed down into the cavern, clutching her stomach with laughter! "DID YOU ACTUALLY BELIEVE THAT SHIT?! YOU THINK I’M GIVING UP THE REWARD?!"
Tasmin stood completely frozen with her jaw slack.

"I’M TAKING THIS WIN STRAIGHT TO HIS BEDROOM, YOU SILLY BITCH!" Brida hollered, already sprinting down the tunnel toward the surface. "I’M GOING TO TELL HIM I CLEARED THE WHOLE NEST SOLO! I’M GETTING PREGNANT BY DINNERTIME! SEE YA, SISTER!"
Her heavy steel-toed boots echoed through the tunnel as she ran off at top speed, laughing like a maniac.
Silence returned to the cavern.
Tasmin stood alone in the center of the bloody pulverized hollow.
Her outstretched hand slowly lowered as her gentle touched expression hardened into a look of pure homicidal rage.
Her left eye began to twitch with such violent intensity that her eyelid felt like it was going to snap.
’...I really, truly, passionately hate you, Brida,’ Tasmin thought, her veins practically turning to liquid ice.
SHSHSHK!
With a soundless, furious hiss, Tasmin’s physical body dissolved entirely, melting into the pitch-black shadows pooling along the floor.
She surged up the vertical shaft at terminal velocity, determined to catch the brawler and slit her throat before she ever reached the Lord’s quarters.
Far to the northwest, nestled deep within the frozen jagged labyrinth of the outer crags, lay Mine XVIT.
Unlike the relatively modest and contained hollow of BVR Star, XVIT was a monster of a subterranean formation.
The cavern mouth was nearly sixty yards wide, opening into a colossal, sweeping chasm that descended miles into the subterranean crust.
Deep within the cavern, the darkness was entirely banished.
Standing at the front of the expeditionary column, holding her wooden staff lightly in one hand, was Goddess Eluned.
The former World Spirit didn’t carry a torch as she didn’t need one.
Her entire physical being was radiating a soft incandescent green luminescence.
The verdant light pulsed like a gentle, living heartbeat, bleeding into every shadow, illuminating the vast cavern with the warm vibrant clarity of a midsummer forest canopy.
Walking beside her, her scabbard slapping rhythmically against her leather-clad thigh, was Morwenna.
The Pirate Queen looked up at the ceiling, then turned her sharp amber eyes toward the glowing green woman beside her, letting out an annoyed exasperated click of her tongue.
She rolled her eyes so hard they practically caught on her eyelids.
"Do you really have to glow like that, you ridiculous light-weed?" Morwenna muttered, adjusting the fur mantle around her neck. "My eyes are burning... You look like a walking, overgrown dandelion."
Eluned didn’t flinch. She simply tilted her head, a serenely venomous smile curving her soft lips.
"Oh? Does my natural vitality offend your delicate eyes, Captain?" Eluned asked, her voice like honey and bells.
With a smooth practiced flick of her wrist, Eluned reached into the sleeve of her robes.
She pulled out a small crisp rectangular piece of enchanted parchment and held it up right before Morwenna’s face.
Morwenna’s eyes locked onto the image and her breath instantly hitched.
The parchment was an enchanted high-definition spiritual photograph that Eluned had quietly snapped early this morning before Silas had left the bed.
’She doesn’t know I have two... hehe~’
The image showed Morwenna lying completely, shamelessly naked across the velvet sheets of Silas’s master bedroom.

The duvet was pulled low, showing the smooth athletic expanse of her tanned back, the deep curve of her waist, and the flushed messy-haired look of complete vulnerable bliss plastered across her sleeping face as Silas’s hand rested comfortably against her bare hip.
An apocalyptic crimson blush exploded across Morwenna’s tanned cheeks, traveling all the way down to her collarbone.
"WHERE DID YOU GET THAT?!" Morwenna screeched, her tough ruthless pirate captain persona violently melting into flustered hysteria.
She lunged forward, her hand snatching at the paper like a striking viper.
SWOOSH!
Eluned’s hand blurred, retracting the photograph back into her voluminous sleeve with the casual fluid grace of a high goddess dodging a clumsy child.

"Ah-ah-ah," Eluned purred, swaying her hips playfully as she stepped just out of reach, her green eyes sparkling with mischief. "A lady should never destroy art, Morwenna... Especially art that proves our fierce sea-dog sleeps like a purring kitten when our Lord cuddles her..."

"I AM GOING TO CHOP YOU INTO FIREWOOD, YOU LEAF-BRAINED PARASITE!" Morwenna roared, her hand dropping to the hilt of her Tidebringer, her knuckles whitening as she prepared to tackle the goddess right into the dirt!
"Uh... Miss Eluned? Captain Morwenna?"
A small gravelly voice broke through the impending catfight.
Both women paused, their heads snapping toward the left wall of the cavern.
Standing beside a grounded colossal Phase 1 Titan Golem was a stout, clean-faced dwarven miner named Bodil.
The dwarf had her hand raised cautiously, holding a heavy-duty pickaxe in one hand while looking between the glowing goddess and the furious pirate with wide, nervous eyes.
"What is it, Bodil?" Eluned asked, instantly smoothing her expression back into a mask of divine, maternal composure as she smoothed the front of her robes.
"There’s... an issue with the survey, ma’am," Bodil said, pointing a soot-stained finger toward the cavern wall.
Morwenna frowned, walking over with heavy, aggressive stomps, her blush still faintly lingering on her cheeks.
"What issue? Did the vein pinch out?"
"No, Captain," Bodil replied, shaking her head.
She pulled a coarse wire brush from her belt and vigorously scrubbed at the dark stone wall, wiping away a thick layer of mineral dust and frost. "Look closely."
Eluned stepped forward, her ambient green light illuminating the cleared section.
Both women leaned in.
The wall didn’t look like ordinary basalt or granite.
Beneath the chalky dust, the material was terrifyingly uniform.
It was a dense seamless metallic mass that looked remarkably like a natural cave wall at first glance, but as the dust cleared, the truth was laid bare.
The entire cavern was not carved from stone.
...The cave itself was made of the alloy.
It was a vast continuous subterranean shell of an unknown high-density mineral that pulsed with a deep dormant mana field.
The metal was a dark iridescent slate-gray, laced with microscopic veins of pale silver that thrummed with ancient pressurized power.
"It’s a continuous deposit..." Eluned murmured, her slender fingers reaching out to touch the metallic surface.
She closed her eyes, feeling the staggering amount of the earth mana locked inside. "It isn’t a vein running through stone... The entire chamber is a hollowed node."
"Aye," Bodil nodded grimly. "And that’s the problem."
The dwarf stepped back, planted her boots firmly into the dirt, and brought her dwarven-forged tempered steel pickaxe back in a full two-handed swing.
TINK!
The sharp, metallic chime echoed off the walls.
Bodil lowered the tool, pointing to the point of impact.
There was no crack and there was no spider-webbing fracture line, hell there wasn’t even a dislodged fleck of dust.

The heavy master-forged steel pickaxe had left behind a microscopic hairline scratch barely an eighth of an inch deep, while the shockwave had sent painful bone-jarring vibrations straight up the dwarf’s forearms.

"It’s too hard," Bodil reported, wincing as she rolled her wrists. "Standard dwarven mining technique can’t crack the bleed-line because there is no bleed-line... The entire formation is uniform. If we try to mine this with standard tools, we’ll shatter fifty pickaxes before we fill a single golem bin."
Morwenna crossed her arms over her chest, tapping her boot against the floor as she scowled at the impenetrable metallic wall.

"Then we don’t pick at it like birds," Morwenna declared bluntly, her pirate instincts taking over. "If the box won’t open, you break the whole damn box. Let’s collapse the cavern... We bring the golem’s siege fists up, crack the ceiling, drop the entire chamber, and haul the shattered boulders back to Thora’s foundry to be melted down."

Bodil looked horrified. "Captain, you can’t! This alloy is tied into the tectonic foundation of the ridge! If you try to use blunt force to shatter a mass this dense, you’ll cause a seismic collapse! It’s too strong! You’ll bury us all alive before the metal yields!"
Eluned stood quietly, listening to the debate.
She turned her gaze upward, looking at the solid, eighty-foot-thick ceiling of metallic alloy and mountain rock that hung over their heads.
A faint serene smile curved her lips.
"Too strong?" Eluned whispered softly. "Nothing born of this earth is too strong for my Roots."
She planted the base of her wooden staff lightly against the cavern floor.
Eluned didn’t shout an incantation as she simply closed her eyes, exhaling a single gentle breath.
VUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUM!
Deep within the mantle beneath their boots, something colossal suddenly woke up.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A deafening earth-shattering detonation tore through the ceiling of the cavern.
The solid, eight-foot-thick plate of impenetrable metallic alloy and eighty feet of mountain granite above them violently ruptured outward in an explosion of pulverized dust and flying boulders.
Shooting straight up through the shattered ceiling and launching fifty yards into the howling, snowy air of the Umbral Basin was a colossal radiant emerald root.
The root was as thick as an ancient watchtower, covered in glowing green bark and pulsing with raw World-Tree mana.
It curved gracefully against the iron-gray winter sky, arching like the spine of a sleeping dragon, before plunging back downward through the mountain flank.
CRASH! KRRRR-GRIND!
More massive roots burst from the earth, wrapping themselves around the entire exterior and interior of the cavern like colossal, living wooden cages.

The roots squeezed, their divine fibers constricting with steady hydraulic pressure, perfectly stabilizing the fractured mountain while simultaneously carving clean massive slabs of the impenetrable alloy away from the bedrock without causing a single cave-in!
Out on the frozen surface of the basin, a pack of roaming corrupted beasts that had been stalking the ridge froze in mind-shattering terror.
They looked up at the colossal glowing emerald root towering against the blizzard, their crimson eyes wide with paralyzing dread.
What in the name of the gods was this apocalyptic power...?
And sitting silently atop a jagged, frost-covered basalt spire barely three hundred yards away, completely undisturbed by the howling wind, was a small solitary bird.
Its feathers were a mottled gray, blending seamlessly into the storm but it did not shiver.
Its sharp, unnervingly intelligent eyes slowly narrowed, locking onto the glowing roots of the World Spirit with cold precision.
The bird turned its head slightly, watching the emerald light pulse against the snow, and remained unnervingly still.
"Squawk..."

sentences.text: Tasmin let out a long shuddering breath, her chains clattering loosely against her leather greaves as she collapsed back onto her heels.
She was completely exhausted, her muscles burning with lactic acid and her dark harness soaked in sweat and black blood.
Across the chasm, Brida slowly pulled herself up to her feet.
She let out a long wheezing sigh, raising a battered, armor-plated gauntlet to wipe a thick streak of black blood from her cheek.
She walked slowly over the smoking rubble, stopping beside Tasmin.
She looked down at the smaller panting woman, and for a moment, her wild battle-crazed face softened into a remarkably gentle expression.
"Hey," Brida murmured, offering a hand to haul Tasmin up.
Tasmin took it, letting Brida pull her to her feet.
"Good fight," Brida said quietly, looking out over the quiet devastated cavern.
She paused, and then let out another soft, tired breath.
"Look... about the ledger and about Lord Silas."
Tasmin blinked, looking up at her.
"You found the nest, Tasmin," Brida said, her tone carrying a rare, solemn weight.
"You tracked it through the seams.
You held the bastard down so I could land the cleaver.
I’m going to let you have the win.
You report this to Lord Silas.
Tell him you cleared the staging ground.
That’s what sisters do, right?
You deserve the reward."
Tasmin’s amber eyes widened in stunned shock.
Her heart tightened in her chest as a wave of overwhelming warmth washed over her, completely melting the competitive edge she had held all morning.
’She’s... she’s really letting me have it?’ Tasmin thought, a soft emotional flush rising to her cheeks. ’After all that bickering... after breaking through the wall... she’s stepping aside for me.’
Tasmin swallowed hard, her voice trembling slightly with raw gratitude.
"Brida..." Tasmin whispered, reaching out to touch the dented pauldron on Brida’s shoulder.
"I... thank you.
I’m sorry for snapping at you earlier.
I shouldn’t have called you an ox, you really saved—"
Before the words could fully leave her mouth, Brida’s gentle solemn expression violently shattered.
A massive smirk split across the brawler’s face.
WHOOSH!
Brida kicked off the stone, leaping twenty feet straight up into the air and grabbing the jagged edge of the breach she had smashed through earlier!
She pulled herself up into the tunnel, poking her head back out to look down at Tasmin with a roaring hysterical cackle.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHA!
ARE YOU DUMB, TASMIN?!" Brida screamed down into the cavern, clutching her stomach with laughter!
"DID YOU ACTUALLY BELIEVE THAT SHIT?!
YOU THINK I’M GIVING UP THE REWARD?!"
Tasmin stood completely frozen with her jaw slack.
"I’M TAKING THIS WIN STRAIGHT TO HIS BEDROOM, YOU SILLY BITCH!" Brida hollered, already sprinting down the tunnel toward the surface.
"I’M GOING TO TELL HIM I CLEARED THE WHOLE NEST SOLO!
I’M GETTING PREGNANT BY DINNERTIME!
SEE YA, SISTER!"
Her heavy steel-toed boots echoed through the tunnel as she ran off at top speed, laughing like a maniac.
Silence returned to the cavern.
Tasmin stood alone in the center of the bloody pulverized hollow.
Her outstretched hand slowly lowered as her gentle touched expression hardened into a look of pure homicidal rage.
Her left eye began to twitch with such violent intensity that her eyelid felt like it was going to snap.
’...I really, truly, passionately hate you, Brida,’ Tasmin thought, her veins practically turning to liquid ice.
SHSHSHK!
With a soundless, furious hiss, Tasmin’s physical body dissolved entirely, melting into the pitch-black shadows pooling along the floor.
She surged up the vertical shaft at terminal velocity, determined to catch the brawler and slit her throat before she ever reached the Lord’s quarters.
Far to the northwest, nestled deep within the frozen jagged labyrinth of the outer crags, lay Mine XVIT.
Unlike the relatively modest and contained hollow of BVR Star, XVIT was a monster of a subterranean formation.
The cavern mouth was nearly sixty yards wide, opening into a colossal, sweeping chasm that descended miles into the subterranean crust.
Deep within the cavern, the darkness was entirely banished.
Standing at the front of the expeditionary column, holding her wooden staff lightly in one hand, was Goddess Eluned.
The former World Spirit didn’t carry a torch as she didn’t need one.
Her entire physical being was radiating a soft incandescent green luminescence.
The verdant light pulsed like a gentle, living heartbeat, bleeding into every shadow, illuminating the vast cavern with the warm vibrant clarity of a midsummer forest canopy.
Walking beside her, her scabbard slapping rhythmically against her leather-clad thigh, was Morwenna.
The Pirate Queen looked up at the ceiling, then turned her sharp amber eyes toward the glowing green woman beside her, letting out an annoyed exasperated click of her tongue.
She rolled her eyes so hard they practically caught on her eyelids.
"Do you really have to glow like that, you ridiculous light-weed?" Morwenna muttered, adjusting the fur mantle around her neck.
"My eyes are burning...
You look like a walking, overgrown dandelion."
Eluned didn’t flinch.
She simply tilted her head, a serenely venomous smile curving her soft lips.
"Oh?
Does my natural vitality offend your delicate eyes, Captain?" Eluned asked, her voice like honey and bells.
With a smooth practiced flick of her wrist, Eluned reached into the sleeve of her robes.
She pulled out a small crisp rectangular piece of enchanted parchment and held it up right before Morwenna’s face.
Morwenna’s eyes locked onto the image and her breath instantly hitched.
The parchment was an enchanted high-definition spiritual photograph that Eluned had quietly snapped early this morning before Silas had left the bed.
’She doesn’t know I have two... hehe~’
The image showed Morwenna lying completely, shamelessly naked across the velvet sheets of Silas’s master bedroom.

The duvet was pulled low, showing the smooth athletic expanse of her tanned back, the deep curve of her waist, and the flushed messy-haired look of complete vulnerable bliss plastered across her sleeping face as Silas’s hand rested comfortably against her bare hip.
An apocalyptic crimson blush exploded across Morwenna’s tanned cheeks, traveling all the way down to her collarbone.
"WHERE DID YOU GET THAT?!" Morwenna screeched, her tough ruthless pirate captain persona violently melting into flustered hysteria.
She lunged forward, her hand snatching at the paper like a striking viper.
SWOOSH!
Eluned’s hand blurred, retracting the photograph back into her voluminous sleeve with the casual fluid grace of a high goddess dodging a clumsy child.
"Ah-ah-ah," Eluned purred, swaying her hips playfully as she stepped just out of reach, her green eyes sparkling with mischief.
"A lady should never destroy art, Morwenna...
Especially art that proves our fierce sea-dog sleeps like a purring kitten when our Lord cuddles her..."

"I AM GOING TO CHOP YOU INTO FIREWOOD, YOU LEAF-BRAINED PARASITE!" Morwenna roared, her hand dropping to the hilt of her Tidebringer, her knuckles whitening as she prepared to tackle the goddess right into the dirt!

Captain Morwenna?"
A small gravelly voice broke through the impending catfight.

Standing beside a grounded colossal Phase 1 Titan Golem was a stout, clean-faced dwarven miner named Bodil.

chapters.title: Chapter 481: Mine XVIT [II]
paragraphs: The jagged ceiling of Mine XVIT did not simply crumble like the bird expected at all... it unwove under the crushing pressure of primordial wood.
High above the mountain rift, perched upon a frost-bitten pinnacle of basalt that jutted like a broken fang against the bruised gray clouds of the Umbral Basin, the watcher bird clung to the stone.
Its talons, hard and black as cold-forged iron, bit into the slick permafrost.
It did not shudder against the sub-zero squall that whipped down from the northern ridges as its obsidian feathers, razor-edged and dark as dried blood, lay flat against its narrow aerodynamic frame.
Its beady black eyes, unnervingly lucid and lacking any sort of animal stupidity, remained locked onto the gaping wound in the mountain’s crest.
The creature understood the geology of this frozen basin far better than the two-legged mortals who had set up their noisy palisades at the southern gates.

For centuries, Mine XVIT had been an anomaly among anomalies... a cursed pocket of petrified impenetrable dark alloy that swallowed pickaxes and turned the blades of mountain ogres into blunt iron spoons.
It was a seamless tomb of cold ore that laughed at force.
Nothing short of the ancient earth-dragons or the apocalyptic breath of a high-tier calamity was supposed to leave so much as a hairline groove upon its skin.
Yet now, the entire peak was groaning.
KRRRRRR-GRIND!
Deep within the fracture colossal roots as thick as the ancient watchtowers of imperial citadels twisted and bunched like the flexing pythons of an ancient forest god.

They were not mundane pine or rot-resistant cedar... they glowed with a breathtaking emerald fire that bled clean through the snow-mist, illuminating the jagged rock face in an unearthly midsummer twilight.
The bird’s scythe-curved beak clicked open slightly.
A strange ratcheting noise like the grinding of copper gears rattled deep in its throat.
Through a jagged split where the mountain’s crust had parted beneath the swelling timber, the avian caught sight of the figures standing inside the cavern vault.
There was the woman in emerald green.

She did not sweat, nor did she strain her back against the bedrock as she merely stood with one slender hand resting against a smooth wooden staff, her long moss-tinted hair billowing lazily in an ethereal draft that had no right existing fifty yards underground.
The mana pouring off her slender shoulders was not the aggressive aura of a martial artist, nor was it the volatile flame of a common basin mage... it was deep and vast as an ocean of living sap.
It possessed the slow terrifying inevitability of tectonic drift.
’She is...’ The bird’s crested head tilted sharply to the left, its black pupils contracting to pinpoint specks. ’She is stronger than the Lord.’
It had observed Silas Graves.
It had watched the black-haired Lord on multiple occasions but this woman... this green-clad pillar of vitality wasn’t merely wielding power.
She was the power, an ancient, primordial spirit wrapped in mortal skin.
Next to her stood another female... a tall warrior wrapped in dark furs and salt-worn leather with a weapon resting against her hip.

That one looked strange; her cheeks were violently flushed an indignant crimson, her boots stomping the ground as she barked at the green woman with her jaw tight and her fists clenched like an embarrassed child.
Yet beneath that ridiculous undignified display of flushed cheeks and fluttering fury, the bird could smell the iron in her blood.
’...Strong.’
They were both monsters as they possessed more than enough raw conceptual weight to shatter the impenetrable.
’The ice...’
The bird’s thoughts raced with frantic clarity.
Down in the lightless absolute-zero depths of the northern trench, where the ancient glacier refused to yield even a single millimeter, its master was still waiting.
She was frozen to her collarbone, coughing up bitter frost, and threatening to turn every feather on its wings into roasted skewers if it didn’t return with salvation.

The Lord with the golden blade had an army, and that army smelled of sharp steel, suspicion, and arrows that would pin a curious bird to a pine trunk before it could utter three squawks but this woman? This woman made of nature?
Surely a being of nature would understand the language of beasts!
Surely she wouldn’t immediately loose a volley of arrows at a messenger!
’I will tell her,’ the bird resolved, its wings trembling with renewed urgency. ’I will fly through the crack, land upon that wooden staff, and screech the coordinates until she follows...’
SNAP!
The bird kicked off from the basalt ledge, its dark, blade-like wings catching the howling updraft with a muted hiss.
It folded its plumage tight, diving like a black dart through the falling snow, aiming straight for the gaping fissure in the ceiling of Mine XVIT.
Thirty yards... Twenty yards...
The fragrant scent of crushed pine blasted upward from the cavern throat.
The bird opened its scythe-beak, drawing freezing air into its hollow chest to loose its desperate high-pitched plea.
’Squaaaa—’
It never got the chance.
Far down within the bowels of the alloy cavern, the emerald roots encountered a stubborn node.
Deep within the eastern foundation of the mountain, a colossal pillar of hyper-compressed star-ore resisted the spiritual intrusion.
The root didn’t yield... it constricted, surging with an apocalyptic burst of divine vitality that violently bypassed the material threshold.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The collision detonated an atmospheric shockwave of pure pressure!
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
A concussive column of pressurized air, pulverized granite dust, and screaming emerald mana erupted upward through the roof fracture like the exhaust of an imperial siege cannon.
"SKREEEEEEEEEEEK?!"
The obsidian bird was caught dead in the center of the vertical gale.
The concussive force slapped it out of the sky before its vocal cords could finish a single syllable.
Its feathers ruffled violently, its scythe-curved beak was forced shut by three hundred pounds of atmospheric thrust, and its beady eyes rolled backward in panic.
WHOOOOOOSH... ZOOOOOM!
Like a pebble skipped off a catapult arm, the bird was launched backward through the blizzard at supersonic velocity.
It tumbled end-over-end through the bruised clouds, shrieking silently as the jagged terrain of the outer basin blurred into a white streak beneath its tailfeathers.
It was hurled miles to the north, screaming through the sky on a trajectory that carried it straight back toward the suffocating, frozen canyons from whence it had flown.
Down in the illuminated belly of Mine XVIT, the emerald light finally began to settle.
The air was dense with the warm rich fragrance of crushed pine needles...
Where there had once been a dark, impenetrable dome of seamless slate-gray alloy, there was now open, yawning space.

"Step back toward the threshold, girls," Eluned’s voice chimed with effortless serenity, carrying over the muffled thud of falling pebbles. "Bring the construct out to the approach ramp and mind the shale."
The ten women who formed the extraction detachment scrambled toward the entrance, their boots slipping slightly on the pulverized dust.
Walking in their midst with heavy, earth-trembling steps was the colossal Phase 1 Titan Golem.

The four-legged stone behemoth, tall as an imperial watchtower, navigated the widening mouth of the cave, its massive amber optics pulsing with a dull compliant hum as it positioned its expansive alloy bins just outside the main chamber.
Once the last boot had cleared the interior perimeter, Eluned gently raised the tip of her wooden staff.
CRRR-CRUNCH!
The emerald roots tightened in a final majestic contraction.
Like a thousand living wooden fingers peeling an orange, the massive roots methodically crushed the remaining structural shell of the cavern but it was not mindless devastation.
The divine mana guided the fracture lines, breaking the impenetrable slate-gray alloy into clean, uniform rectangular blocks roughly the size of travel trunks.
Then, with an eerie weightless grace that defied every law of physics, the glowing roots shifted.
They scooped through the rubble, cradling hundreds of tons of high-density ore, and lifted them smoothly through the cracked ceiling.
THUD! CLANG! RATTLE!
One after another, the massive slabs of virgin alloy were neatly deposited directly into the reinforced transport bins bolted across the Phase 1 Titan Golem’s back.
The heavy-duty suspension of the construct hissed, venting plumes of pressurized steam as the bins rapidly filled with millions of credits’ worth of pristine unmarred ore.
Within three minutes, the roots unraveled.
They shrank back into the earth with a soft, rustling sigh, leaving behind a perfectly hollowed-out, clean-swept rock bed.
Not a single pebble of the mysterious alloy remained...
The entire deposit had been extracted, cataloged by spiritual force, and stacked into the golem’s bins without a single pickaxe striking the rock.
Eluned turned around, a serene radiant smile gracing her porcelain features as she smoothed the emerald folds of her dress.
"There," Eluned announced softly, her hands folding neatly over her staff. "A most efficient extraction... The mountain has yielded its bounty to Blessed Land."
She paused as the cavern threshold was dead silent.
Standing beside the laden golem, Bodil the dwarven miner was staring at the empty cavern floor with her jaw hanging so slack it nearly brushed the leather collar of her harness.
Her master-forged steel pickaxe dangled limply from her calloused hand, completely forgotten.
Behind her, the other women stood in frozen unblinking rows.
Their leather straps were still pristine and their hands were completely free of rock dust.
Their sweat hadn’t even begun to warm the steel-mesh fabric clinging to their skin and beside them stood Morwenna.
The Pirate Queen slowly lowered the hand that had been resting on her weapon, her amber eyes widening before narrowing into a look of delight.
A slow wicked grin spread across her face, revealing sharp gleaming teeth.
"Uh... Miss Eluned?" Bodil squeaked, her raspy dwarven voice cracking slightly in the cold air.
"Yes, Bodil?" Eluned tilted her head, maintaining her tranquil saintly composure.
"You... you did it all," Bodil stammered, gesturing with the blunt end of her pickaxe toward the immaculate, empty pit. "Every scrap... The whole bloody node..."
A tall blonde woman stepped forward, her eyebrows furrowing as a look of soul-deep panic began to dawn on her youthful face.

"Wait..." the recruit muttered, looking down at her spotless hands, and then looking up at the filled bins on the golem’s back. "If you just... ripped the whole mine out with your roots in two minutes... what about the ledger?"
"The ledger?" another girl gasped, her eyes widening in horror. "The Lord’s morning decree! He said the reward goes to whoever mines the most! Whoever sweats for the territory!"

"We didn’t swing a single pick!" a third woman shouted, her voice rising into an anxious wail. "We haven’t logged a single pound of ore under our names! How are we supposed to win the Lord’s reward if the Goddess just solod the entire damn mountain?!"
"I wanted to earn that reward!"
"I bought this new lavender oil from the apothecary just for tonight!"
"Miss Eluned, that’s completely unfair!"
A cacophony of bitter heartbroken complaints erupted from the vanguard ranks.
The girls stomped their boots, waving their unchipped chisels and glaring at the World Spirit with betrayed tearful pouts.
Eluned’s serene smile froze.
A tiny imperceptible bead of cold sweat formed at her temple, sliding slowly down her cheek.
She reached up, her slender fingers delicately clenching around the collar of her robes, her breath hitching in her throat.

’I’m... I’m an idiot,’ Eluned screamed inwardly, her divine mind screeching to a violent mortified halt. ’I completely forgot! Silas didn’t send them out here just to haul rocks... this was supposed to be a morale-building team exercise! He set up that ridiculous competition to motivate them! If I steal all the credit and leave their ledgers blank, these girls are going to despise me! They’ll look at me like an overbearing monster who ruined their chances with our Lord!’
Beside the trembling goddess, Morwenna’s grin was practically splitting her face in two.
The Pirate Queen crossed her arms over her chest, leaning her hip against the side of the Titan Golem, fairly vibrating with malicious satisfaction.

"Oh, look at that," Morwenna drawled, her voice dripping with venomous amusement. "The grand Goddess... so eager to show off her pretty green branches that she forgot basic crew management. Look at them, Eluned. You just broke their little hearts. What are you going to do now? Weave them some pretty little daisy chains to wipe their tears?"
Eluned’s emerald eyes flared.

’Think, Eluned,’ she told herself, her heart fluttering beneath her ribs. ’You are an ancient divine entity and you have governed ecosystems for a long time so surely you can talk your way out of a pack of sulking women!’
Suddenly, her gaze locked onto the leather satchel hanging from Bodil’s hip.
With the terrifying effortless speed of a high spirit, Eluned’s hand blurred.
SWOOSH.
"Oi!" Bodil yelped as the thick map of the Umbral Basin was neatly plucked from her belt before she could even blink.
Eluned unrolled the map with a dramatic authoritative snap of her wrists, holding it high so that every single woman in the squad could clearly see the markings.
Her expression instantly shifted, returning to the radiant and confident composure of a wise benevolent elder sister.

"Calm yourselves, my lovely warriors," Eluned announced, her voice ringing out like silver chimes and instantly cutting through the grumbling. "Do you truly think I would rob you of your glory? Do you take me for a callous thief of your rightful rewards?"
