chapters.title: Chapter 485: Popping Up From The Ground [II]
paragraphs: Silas stood completely motionless in the center of the glittering geode, his right hand still clutching the handle of the runic pickaxe.
His dark eyebrows knit together, his piercing blue eyes slowly blinking once, then twice, as his mind processed the absurdity of the words that had just exploded out of the woman’s mouth.
Around them, the cavern was so silent that the distant drip-drip-drip of condensation off a limestone stalactite sounded like a hammer striking an anvil.
Brenda’s jaw was dropped so low it looked unhinged.

Sarah was frozen in mid-step with her void-iron blade dangling loosely by her knee and Aurelia’s serene smile had locked into an expression of paralyzed bewilderment, while the Princess’s face was rapidly cycling through three distinct shades of apocalyptic scarlet.
Even the Phase 1 Titan Golem resting outside in the goblin settlement seemed to emit a low confused mechanical hiss through the narrow entrance fissure.
However Brida didn’t care in the slightest.

She stood there, covered head-to-toe in chalky gray bedrock dust, pulverized shale, and streaks of half-congealed, foul-smelling black monster marrow with her hands planted firmly against her armored hips.

"Well, my Lord?!" Brida urged, leaning forward so aggressively that the battered steel plates of her cuirass clinked against her collar. "Are you listening to me?! Hurry up and say yes! I practically turned three miles of solid mountain roots into gravel just to bring you the news before anyone else could open their mouths!"
Before Silas could even part his lips to speak, the light in the eastern corner of the chamber warped.
SHSHSHK!
The deep ink-black shadow pooled beneath an overhanging crystalline shelf suddenly boiled.
It rose from the two-dimensional rock floor like a surging wave of pitch, twisting violently before snapping into three-dimensional reality with a sharp concussive pop of displaced air.
Out stepped Tasmin.
The commander hit the limestone on one knee with her hands slapping against the gravel to steady herself.
"Haah... Haah... Haah..." Her breath came in burning gasps that whistled through her clenched teeth.
Her tailored leather mining harness was drenched in cold sweat and black ichor, the dark fabric plastered tight against her heaving ribs.
Strands of ink-black hair clung to her flushed forehead, and her fingers trembled with the agonizing aftershocks of sheer spatial exhaustion.

Traversing nearly three miles of subterranean bedrock through the liquid void of the shadow-realm... sliding through microscopic stone pores, navigating tectonic fault lines, and matching the raw sprint of a Titan had pushed her internal mana circuits to the brink.
’Fuck, I won’t ever do that again...’
Her reserves were smoking, her legs felt like lead, and the lingering spiritual static made her teeth ache.
Yet, as the cold air filled her lungs, Tasmin felt a dark exhilarating thrill hum beneath the fatigue.
’...Or maybe I will.’
It had been a brutal punishing transit, but surviving that kind of high-velocity spatial tunneling was the kind of trial that hardened her far faster than any safe drill in the courtyard.
She forced herself upright, her boots skidding on the crystalline dust as her amber eyes locked onto Brida’s back with pure, unadulterated venom.
"SHE IS LYING!"
Tasmin’s voice tore through the geode.

"My Lord, do not listen to a single syllable that falls out of this treacherous woman’s mouth!" Tasmin rasped, pointing a shaking, gloved finger straight at Brida’s head. "She didn’t solo a damn thing! I was the one who located the nest! I pinned the vanguard and I burned the alpha’s limbs with my chains as I was the one who held it down! She’s taking credit for my blood!"
Under normal circumstances, Tasmin prided herself on being the professional... the cold collected shadow commander who spoke in calm reports and let her lethal results speak for themselves.
She never whined and she never engaged in petty squabbling in front of the ranks... well not everytime.
But right now?

After Brida had pulled that gentle sisterly act down in the ruins of the hive... after she had looked Tasmin in the eye, offered her the win with that soft emotional voice, and then immediately jumped through the ceiling screaming that she was going to get bred by dinnertime... any semblance of composure had been incinerated into ash.
Tasmin had felt genuine warmth in her chest for a fleeting second, only to have it violently ripped away by an overgrown black-haired ape.
It was a betrayal of the highest and most personal order.
Brida whirled around, her amber eyes flashing with defiant unrepentant fire.
"Oh, look who finally crawled out of the dirt! What took you so long, shadow?! If you wanted the credit, your little boots should have moved faster! First to the Keep gets the prize... that’s law!"

"You threw me a fake apology, you deceitful muscle-bound hyena!" Tasmin hissed, taking a threatening step forward, her twin void-black daggers slipping from her belt with a wicked metallic hiss. "You pretended to be my sister!"
"I am your sister!" Brida roared back, not yielding an inch of ground. "And sisters don’t let sisters hog the Lord’s private chambers when there’s a reward on the table! All’s fair in love and war!"
"I will sever your vocal cords and hang them from the palisade—"
"Enough. Both of you..."
Silas raised both hands, waving them downward in a firm sweeping motion.
He didn’t shout, but the authority vibrating within his voice cut through the screaming match like a heated blade through tallow.
"Stand down... Take a breath and stop yelling before you bring down the ceiling stalactites on our heads."𝘧𝘳𝘦ℯ𝓌𝘦𝒷𝘯𝑜𝑣𝘦𝓁.𝒸𝘰𝓂
The two S-Rank women froze.

Brida’s mouth snapped shut, though a defiant puff of air blew past her lips, while Tasmin lowered her daggers an inch, her jaw remaining clenched tight as she forced her trembling shoulders to settle.
Silas let out a massive soul-deep sigh with the tension finally bleeding out of his broad shoulders.
He rested the blunt head of the runic pickaxe casually against his right shoulder, wiping a streak of sweat from his temple with the back of his bare forearm.
Brida’s eyes instantly tracked the motion.

Her fiery gaze drifted down from his face, sweeping across the broad, sculpted expanse of his chest, taking in the way the dark dwarven leather harness pulled the thin linen tight against his dense abdominals and the hard corded ridges of his lats.
A low appreciative whistle caught in her throat with her brows raising in mock outrage.

"Hold on a bloody minute..." Brida murmured, looking from Silas to the blushing women standing behind him. "What is this outfit? Why is the harness so tight? My Lord, you’re standing in a damp hole in the ground looking like a piece of high-grade imperial eye candy... It is completely unfair that these girls got to stand around staring at your chest all morning while Tasmin and I were swimming through rotting monster guts!"
Behind them, Thora let out a sharp indignant squeak, stepping around an alloy storage crate with her hands planted on her hips.

"Oi! Watch your mouth!" Thora barked, her clean-shaven face smudged with soot and chalk dust. "You’re interrupting sacred dwarven labor with your screeching! This is a high-yield industrial site, not a tavern brawl! We have thousands of pounds of Mana Diamonds to harvest before sunset, and your little domestic dispute is slowing down my quota!"
Brida blinked, glancing down at the four-foot-tall dwarf, and then a wide, disarming grin broke across her battered face.

"Ah, Thora!" Brida boomed, stepping forward and clapping a heavy hand against her breastplate. "Don’t be like that! I have to say, though... that tailored steel-mesh suit looks magnificent on you! It hugs your waist so well I almost didn’t recognize our fierce forge master! You look downright radiant without that forge apron covering your curves!"
Thora froze.
The dwarf’s pale cheeks instantly erupted into a brilliant, incandescent shade of volcanic crimson.
She sputtered, her blunt fingers frantically tugging at the leather straps around her ribs as her amber eyes darted wildly across the limestone floor.

"I... what... shut up!" Thora stammered, coughing violently into her fist as she turned her back on them, aggressively kicking a loose pebble into the darkness. "Shameless! Absolutely shameless flattery! Don’t think sweet words will get you a discount on your next weapon refinement, you lunatic!"
Silas pinched the bridge of his nose, shaking his head. "Alright, that’s enough clowning around. Brida... Tasmin... Look at me..."
Both commanders instantly snapped their attention back to their Lord, standing straight as iron rods.
Silas’s blue eyes narrowed, his tone dropping into a cool penetrating voice that brooked zero room for deception.

"I can smell the ichor on both of you from ten paces away," Silas said calmly, his gaze shifting between their battered armor and exhausted expressions. "I know you were in a clash with monsters but you know me, and you know how I run this territory. I do not tolerate lies, and I do not tolerate false reports so now... what actually happened out there? Give me the truth."
Brida’s boisterous posture softened slightly. She scratched the back of her neck, shifting her weight from one boot to the other with a sheepish crooked grin.
"Well..." Brida muttered, glancing sideways at Tasmin. "The truth is... Tasmin and I butchered the whole nest together. Every last one of them."

"She didn’t find it first, either," Tasmin chimed in, crossing her arms over her chest, though her tone was significantly calmer now. "I was conducting an internal perimeter sweep through the eastern fault lines of Mine BVR Star... I used my shadow perception, found an artificial stone plug, and slipped through. I found an observation blind, eliminated a sentry heading for our workers, and tracked the tunnel down to the staging grounds."

"And then I showed up!" Brida interjected proudly, puffing out her chest. "Because one of the ugly bastards was peeking through a crack near my squad’s sector three miles away! I punched through the wall, took its head off, and decided to take the straight line! I barreled through the bedrock until I broke through the hive’s flank!"
"You didn’t ’barrel through,’ you detonated a ten-foot granite wall and landed in the middle of their hollow like an unguided siege shell!" Tasmin snapped.
"And it worked!" Brida shouted back. "It broke their formation!"
"It alerted three hundred monsters to our exact coordinates!"
"And they’re all dead, aren’t they?!"
"Only because I locked down their limbs before they tore your throat out!"
"Alright, peace!" Silas commanded, his voice cutting off the rising bickering once more.

He looked at the two of them, taking in the frayed edges of their gear, the dried venom clinging to their greaves, and the undeniable fact that despite the shouting, neither woman possessed a single serious wound.
A slow smile spread across Silas’s face. He stepped forward, reaching out and clapping a firm, warm hand on each of their shoulders.
"First of all," Silas said and his voice made both women’s breath hitch, "thank you. Both of you..."
Brida blinked, the cocky smirk vanishing from her face. Tasmin looked up, her amber eyes softening as the lingering anger melted into quiet vulnerable shock.

"Those shapeshifting abominations are one of the most dangerous threats in the Umbral Basin," Silas continued, his grip tightening reassuringly against their pauldrons. "A monster that can steal a face and mimic a voice is a cancer to a closed territory... The fact that you two located an entire territory of them and eradicated the entire population before they could launch a coordinated strike on our mining lines... that is a massive strategic victory for Blessed Land and you saved lives today... You protected your sisters too so I am proud of you."
A deep rosy flush crept up the back of Brida’s neck, the fierce woman suddenly finding the limestone floor fascinating.
Tasmin’s lips parted slightly, her chest swelling with a warmth so sweet and intoxicating it made her knees feel weak.

"However," Silas added, his tone sharpening slightly, "tell me about their combat capabilities. The reports from yesterday indicated they were primarily infiltration units... sight-and-sound mimics that lacked physical shadows but did they show anything else down there?"
Brida nodded eagerly, glad for the chance to deliver vital intelligence.

"They’re worse than we thought, my Lord," Brida explained, her expression turning grave. "The regular runts just wear stolen skin but the stronger ones... they aren’t limited to human disguises. When we cornered them, their flesh began to boil and expand. They transformed into massive, ten-foot armored dreadnoughts and quad-pedal beasts as they gained external bone carapaces, pressurized venom, and completely different anatomical structures."
"And the Alpha, I guess there was one?" Silas asked, his brows furrowing.

"That one was a nightmare," Tasmin took over, her mind engaging smoothly. "Initially, it manifested as a twelve-foot bipedal horror with four arms, wielding petrified drake-bone clubs and bone scythes... Brida and I coordinated a joint assault and severed all four of its limbs at the joints but instead of dying, it ascended to Tier 4 instantaneously."

"It turned into a colossal octopus," Brida said, waving her hands in wide circles to emphasize the scale. "I’m not joking, my Lord! Massive, twenty-foot rubbery tentacles lined with bone-suckers! It had an impenetrable mucus coating that absorbed impacts! My cleaver was practically bouncing off its hide! If Tasmin hadn’t channeled her chains to burn through the slime and cook its nervous system, we would have been in a brutal war of attrition."
Silas listened intently, mentally archiving every single detail into his strategic ledger.

’Genetic fluidity,’ Silas analyzed grimly. ’They aren’t just mimics, they possess unstable mutagenic cores from what I can see... If an Alpha can shift from a bipedal bruiser to an impact-absorbing cephalopod mid-combat to counter bladed weapons, what else is lurking in the deeper northern trenches? Other Tier 4 variants could be capable of adapting to elemental fire or holy mana on the fly.’

"Excellent work," Silas said aloud, nodding slowly. "That information is invaluable... We’ll adjust the guard rotations at the palisades and have Thora prepare special armor-piercing incendiary rounds for the ballistas."

chapters.title: Chapter 486: A New Mission For Brida And Tasmin
paragraphs: Silas paused, letting his gaze linger on the two women a his eyes narrowed into a dry piercing squint.

"Now... answer me this," Silas murmured, his voice laced with amusement. "Did you two sprint three miles through subterranean fault lines straight to this cavern... without checking on your mining squads first?"
Dead silence fell once more.
Brida froze mid-breath as her eyes darted toward the high crystalline ceiling and her fingers twitched against the pommel of her cleaver.
Tasmin’s composure shattered instantly.
Her pale cheeks flared with deep agonizing guilt as her mouth opened, but only a dry squeak escaped her throat.
The reality of what they had done suddenly crashed down upon them like a mountain avalanche.
Brida had literally blown a hole in the earth and run straight toward the scent of Silas’s mana without ever looking back at the women sitting at her outpost.

And Tasmin... who had originally intended to climb back up the shaft to rejoin her squad at BVR Star had completely abandoned all military protocol once she replayed Brida shouting that she was going to claim the Lord’s reward alone, diving headfirst into the shadows to hunt her down.
They had left their squads completely unattended in the middle of a hostile basin...
"Uh..." Brida swallowed hard, sweating profusely beneath her leather harness. "Well... you see, my Lord... the threat was urgent! We had to deliver the report immediately!"
"I was pursuing a rogue Brida," Tasmin attempted weakly, her voice barely a whisper as she stared at her boots. "I... I was ensuring your security..."

"You two are unbelievable," Silas sighed, though he couldn’t entirely hide the wry exasperated smirk tugging at the corners of his lips. "What you accomplished down there was incredible but you could have checked your outposts, ensured your perimeter wards were holding, and delivered the report tonight over dinner."
He shook his head, crossing his arms over his chest.

"Regardless," Silas continued, his eyes gleaming with a challenging spark, "since you both abandoned your posts to come chasing after my morning decree... it seems you’re both still dead-set on competing for the special reward."
Both women’s heads snapped up.
The guilt vanished in a flash, replaced by the sharp hum of fierce competition.
They exchanged a brief, fiery glare before snapping their attention back to Silas.
"Give me a map," Silas ordered, extending his hand. "One of you."
Brida immediately began frantically patting down her armor, fumbling with the battered leather pouches on her hips. "Wait! It’s in my side pocket... hold on, the buckle is jammed with monster blood—"
SWOOSH!

Before Brida could even unhook her strap, Tasmin’s hand blurred. With the smooth effortless precision of an elite scout, she produced a crisp perfectly folded vellum map from her inner harness and placed it gently into Silas’s open palm.
"Here, my Lord," Tasmin murmured, offering him a sweet triumphant smile.
Silas looked down at the parchment, then looked at Tasmin. "Efficient as always. Thank you, Tasmin."
"You’re very welcome, Lord Silas," Tasmin beamed, tilting her chin up and casting a smug venomous side-eye at Brida that practically screamed words at her. ’I win this round, you clumsy ox.’
Brida ground her molars together so hard an audible crunch echoed in her jaw, but she forced herself to keep quiet.
Silas unfolded the vellum, smoothing it out across the flat surface of a limestone boulder.
The map of the Umbral Basin was covered in grid coordinates, and symbols.
Across the northwestern ridges, Mine XVIT... the impenetrable alloy deposit had already been stamped with a glowing green mark.
Silas chuckled softly under his breath, shaking his head. It was probably Eluned...

’Eluned,’ Silas thought, a fond knowing warmth settling in his chest. ’Knowing my cute competitive wife, she probably cracked that impenetrable cavern wide open with her roots, realized she stole all the work from the girls, and immediately marched the squad to the adjacent sectors to clear the unassigned nodes... She wouldn’t be able to resist showing off.’
He traced his finger across the map, moving toward the central crags where BVR Star and Brida’s outpost lay.

"Look here," Silas said, tapping three distinct circular marks clustered within a two-mile radius of their current position. "These three caverns... Sector Seven, Sector Eight, and the lower ridge of Nine. All three have been surveyed by Thora’s ledgers and they’re confirmed high-yield veins of Star-Iron and Deep-Earth Alloy."
He picked up the map, refolded it neatly, and handed it back to Tasmin.

"Here are your orders," Silas commanded, looking directly into both of their eyes. "You two will return to your squads immediately. You will link up, form a joint extraction detachment, and you will systematically clear and harvest all three of these mines before the sunset bells ring."
Both women blinked, listening intently.

"And let me make this crystal clear," Silas added. "You will mine at a normal pace... That means no Earth-Shattering Cleaves to collapse the mountain, Brida and no using chains to violently rip veins out of the bedrock, Tasmin. You will use dwarven technique, protect the crystal matrices, and guide the recruits properly. If I find out either of you brought down a cavern roof just to speed up the ledger, you are disqualified from the reward entirely. Understood?"
Both women gulped in unison, their throats bobbing as they nodded vigorously.
"Understood, my Lord!" they chorused.

"Good," Silas smirked. "Whoever logs the highest tonnage of pristine, undamaged ore in their golem’s bins by the end of the day... receives the special reward directly from me tonight, Now get moving."
Tasmin’s amber eyes flickered with a sudden practical thought. "My Lord... what if the transport bins on our Phase 2 Golems fill up completely before we finish the third mine?"
Before Silas could answer, Thora stepped forward, waving a soot-stained wrench through the air.

"If the bins fill up, you send a runner or a wolf back to the eastern foundry line!" Thora barked, puffing out her chest. "I’ve got transport carts and a spare Phase 2 chassis idling outside the gates! Just submit a formal request to Aeli and it’ll be dispatched within minutes! Don’t let empty bins be an excuse for laziness!"
"Understood!" Brida grinned, her eyes blazing with renewed determination.
Without waiting another second, Brida took two massive, sprinting steps backward, tossed her cleaver into the subterranean hole, and dove headfirst into the dark breach.
"SEE YOU AT THE FORGE, TASMIN!" Brida’s boisterous voice echoed up from the depths of the shaft!
Tasmin gasped, her jaw dropping. "You cheating, ill-mannered brute—!"
SHSHSHK.
Tasmin didn’t even bother saying goodbye.
She cursed under her breath, dissolved into a fluid wave of pitch-black mist, and surged down the shaft in hot pursuit, determined to pass the woman before she hit the lower tunnels.
Silas stood watching the empty, smoking hole in the floor for a long moment, slowly letting out a quiet wheezing breath.
He raised his arm, wiping the fresh beads of sweat from his brow.
"Gods give me strength," Silas muttered to himself. "Those two are going to take ten years off my life."
He stepped up to the edge of the jagged breach, channeled a gentle pulse of his Gold Core’s earth affinity, and stomped his boot against the stone.
KRA-CRUNCH.
The pulverized limestone and shattered shale ground together like teeth, flowing like liquid rock to seamlessly seal the breach shut.
Within seconds, the floor was flat, solid, and completely impassable once more, leaving the geode secure.
Silas turned around, only to find the fifteen recruit maidens staring at him with wide intensely expectant eyes.
Brenda was chewing her lower lip, holding her chisel against her chest, while Sarah cautiously raised her hand, her cheeks still sporting that soft rosy flush.

"Um... Lord Silas?" Sarah asked hesitantly, her voice echoing softly in the quiet cavern. "Since Lady Brida and Lady Tasmin are competing so fiercely for the reward... does that mean... is it still okay for us to keep working for a reward too? Or is the competition only between the commanders?"
A chorus of quiet hopeful murmurs rippled through the ranks of the younger girls.
Silas looked at their sweat-streaked faces, noting the blistered palms, the chalk-dusted armor, and the genuine earnest desire shining in their eyes.
He offered them a warm reassuring smile that made several of their knees wobble.

"Of course it’s still open to you," Silas said gently, his voice carrying effortlessly. "Brida and Tasmin are competing for the prize, but a territory does not run on the backs of two women alone. Blessed Land is built upon every single strike of your picks... I have plenty of rewards to give. For the girls who show the greatest discipline and harvest the cleanest yields today, I will personally ensure you receive custom rewards from my own hands."
"YES!" Brenda squealed, pumping her fist before immediately clamping both hands over her mouth in embarrassment.
"You heard the Lord!" Helen shouted, her face alight with fierce, motivated energy as she hoisted her pickaxe. "Back to the walls! Clean facets! Let’s fill the titan’s bins to the brim!"
With a unified thunderous cheer, the recruits and everyone alike threw themselves back into their work with five times the intensity of the morning.
Tink! Tink! Tink! Clang!
The music of the geode resumed with terrifying efficiency.
For the next two hours, the women worked like a well-oiled machine as slabs of porous limestone parted cleanly from the bedrock.
Fist-sized cerulean stones, brilliant emerald clusters, and deep royal amethysts were pried loose, dusted off, and stacked into gleaming pyramids across the chamber floor.
By the time the midday bells rang from Helen’s brass wrist-timer, the central dome of the geode had been completely swept clean of all exposed surface diamonds.
Thora stepped up to the massive glittering mountain of extracted wealth, wiping sweat from her brow as she signaled the entrance fissure.
"Phase One Titan!" Thora yelled. "Final sweep! Clear the floor!"
KRRRRRR-GRIND!
The colossal stone arm of the Phase 1 Titan Golem slid through the limestone gap once more.
Its massive articulated bedrock fingers scooped beneath the final enormous pile of gems, lifting hundreds of pounds of raw refracted light through the opening.
CLATTER-CRASH!
Outside in the goblin settlement, the last load poured into the titan’s reinforced alloy bins, filling the one of the main compartments to the point that it was almost overflowing.
The construct hissed, its central amber optic flashing once as it settled back into low-power idling mode.
Inside the geode, the women collapsed against the rock walls, groaning with exhausted deeply satisfied smiles.
Their leather harnesses were soaked through, their arms burned with lactic acid, and their boots were coated in glittering crystalline dust.
Silas rested his pickaxe against a stalagmite, clapping his hands together with a crisp clap.
"Alright, that’s the morning shift concluded," Silas announced with a broad smile. "Tools down, everyone. It’s lunchtime..."
A collective joyful cheer rippled through the cavern.
Silas stepped into the center of the cleared, smooth limestone floor.
He focused his mind, tapping into the spatial storage of his inventory ring.
VUUUM!
With a gentle shimmer of spatial mana, a massive thick woven picnic mat... wide enough to comfortably seat twenty people materialized in the center of the room.
It unrolled smoothly across the stone, its soft quilted surface providing a luxurious clean sanctuary from the cold gravel.
"Take off your boots if you want, sit down, and make yourselves comfortable," Silas instructed, stepping onto the mat.
The girls didn’t hesitate.

One by one, all of the primary excavation members... the recruit squad leaders Helen, Brenda, and Sarah... Catelyn and Lyra, even the Princess, Aurelia, Thora, Vala and Reina eagerly slipped off their heavy tool belts and dropped onto the soft mat with sighs of sheer, unadulterated bliss.

Thor marched over, her heavy footsteps shaking the limestone, and plopped her massive leather-clad rear directly onto the edge of the mat with her long blonde hair swaying as she looked at Silas with desperate starving eyes.
Silas chuckled, reaching back into his inventory.
He began retrieving neatly stacked, polished wooden lunch boxes... each one carefully prepared and packed before dawn by Kaelia’s master culinary team back at the Keep’s royal kitchens.
He handed the boxes out one by one.

The girls eagerly popped the lacquered lids open, revealing vibrant mouth-watering arrangements of herb-seared river trout, steaming parcels of seasoned wild rice, crisp honey-glazed root vegetables, and sweet berry tarts that filled the damp cavern with an intoxicating heavenly aroma.
"Oh, by the heavens..." Brenda moaned, taking a delicate bite of a glazed carrot. "This is incredible! It’s so sweet!"
"Kaelia’s cooking is truly a divine blessing," Aurelia murmured gracefully, using a pair of wooden utensils to sample a sliver of trout, her golden eyes fluttering with quiet appreciation.
And then, Silas turned toward the towering blonde God of Thunder.
With both hands, Silas hauled a massive two-foot-wide iron roasting bowl from his inventory, placing it directly before Thor with a heavy metallic thud.
Inside the bowl was a mountain of prime roasted wild boar.
The meat was charred to crispy, golden-brown perfection on the outside, succulent and dripping with savory, spiced juices on the inside, and garnished with thick cloves of roasted mountain garlic.
Beside the bowl, Silas set down a massive five-gallon wooden keg of Thora’s finest dark dwarven stout, its spigot practically weeping with frost.
Thor’s storm-blue eyes expanded to the size of full moons.
A single divine tear of pure joy rolled down her soot-stained cheek.
"Lord Silas..." Thor choked out, her voice trembling with reverence as she stared at the boar meat. "You... you are a true king of men and an emperor among mortals."
She threw her massive muscular arms forward, catching Silas by the shoulder and pulling him into an affectionate one-armed bear hug.
THUMP!

chapters.title: Chapter 487: Lunch Games And Watching Eyes
paragraphs: Silas was briefly smothered against her leather-strained chest, the intoxicating scent of her filling his senses before she released him, her cleavage shaking wildly with every boisterous laugh.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHA!" Thor roared, slapping Silas on the back with enough force to shatter a normal man’s clavicle. "The ale is safe! The meat is mine! Let the feast begin!"
Without waiting for utensils, Thor plunged both hands into the bowl, ripping off a three-pound roasted shank and tearing into the succulent meat with savage glorious divine enthusiasm.
Juice ran down her chin, her eyes rolling back in pure ecstasy as she popped the spigot on the keg and took a massive five-second swig of dark stout, letting out a satisfied cavern-shaking belch.

"Hey! Giantess! Mind your table manners!" Thora scowled from across the mat, though the dwarf was happily devouring her own box of salted beef and sharp cheese. "You’re spraying garlic onto the Princess’s rice!"
"Pay it no mind, Master Thora!" the Princess giggled brightly, her azure eyes sparkling as she sat with her legs tucked demurely beneath her. "It is wonderful to see Lady Thor in such high spirits!"
As the food disappeared, the atmosphere on the picnic mat transformed into a lively chaotic celebration.

"Alright, girls! Who’s up for an eating trial?!" Sarah shouted, waving a skewer of spicy spirit-peppers in the air. "The frontier wall game! Five spirit-peppers in a single bite without reaching for the water canteen! Winner gets first pick of the dessert pastries!"
"You’re on, Sarah!" Brenda barked, rolling up her sleeves with fierce freckled determination. "I ate boiled nettles for six months on the border! Your little pepper seeds can’t hurt me!"
"Count me in!" Helen grinned, leaning over the mat.
The girls cheered and clapped, banging their empty wooden cups against the stone floor as Brenda and Sarah stuffed their mouths with the bright crimson peppers.

Within three seconds, both girls’ faces turned the exact shade of ripe tomatoes, their eyes watering profusely as they chewed frantically, refusing to blink with their cheeks puffing out as the rest of the squad roared with hysterical laughter.
"Don’t swallow yet, Brenda! Hold the line!"
"Sarah’s tearing up! Sarah’s reaching for the canteen!"
"I am not!" Sarah choked out, her voice muffled around the peppers, coughing as smoke practically vented from her ears.
Silas sat back, leaning comfortably against the warm wall, watching the women laugh, tease, and shove each other playfully.
’Ah, I’m happy...’
This was what the mining, the walls, and the sovereign upgrades were all about.
Building a sanctuary where the people who bled for him could laugh like children in the middle of a hostile wasteland.
Eventually, the lunch boxes were emptied, the mat was neatly rolled up and returned to Silas’s spatial inventory, and the women strapped their heavy tool belts back onto their hips.
The playful banter faded, replaced once more by professionalism.
Silas hoisted his runic pickaxe over his shoulder, his expression turning serious as he turned toward the eastern quadrant of the geode.
"Form up on me," Silas ordered quietly. "We’re heading into the eastern alcove."
The squad immediately fell into disciplined ranks behind him, their boots crunching softly against the crystalline gravel as they navigated past the towering calcified stalagmites.
Within minutes, they stood at the lip of the sunken bowl-shaped depression Silas had scouted earlier.
The vibrant multicolored prismatic light of the main geode completely vanished here.
In its place was a heavy suffocating aura that pressed against the skin like thick humid fog.
The walls and floor of the sunken grove were completely coated in a bizarre petrified lattice of striking blood-red crystals and pure milky-white diamonds.

They didn’t grow in jagged geometric clusters like the standard gems... they twisted and wound around each other like living, petrified vines, pulsing with a slow eerie heartbeat that sent metallic hums through the air.
The hair on the back of Silas’s neck stood on end.
The entire atmosphere felt remarkably familiar.

It carried the exact same strange and volatile pressure as the lightless cavern where they had discovered that unrecorded white alloy... the one Thora had claimed naming rights over and christened Sil-Graves Silver.
"Look at the grain on these bastards..." Thora whispered, her voice dropping all mockery as she knelt at the edge of the depression.
She pressed her bare palm against a patch of dark stone near the red vines with her clean-shaven face set in deep calculating lines.
"The mana conductivity here is completely mutated. It’s dense as lead, but volatile as blasting powder."
"How do we harvest it, Thora?" Silas asked, his eyes scanning the pulsing red lattice.

"Carefully, my Lord," Thora explained, pointing with the tip of her chisel. "You don’t strike outside the bleed-line here because the white diamonds are the bleed-line... The red crystal is the core while the white diamond is the calcified mana shell. If you separate them cleanly at the junction seam, you preserve both so if you nick the red core with an improper angle, the trapped elemental charge will violently discharge."
Silas nodded, stepping down into the sunken grove. He gripped his pickaxe, looking back over his shoulder at the squad.

"Keep your eyes wide and your senses sharp," Silas warned, his voice ringing out with clarity. "Like I said earlier, caverns with this level of stagnant centuries-old elemental power are prime breeding grounds for entities. Uncontracted spirits born in places like this don’t have bodies of flesh... they manifest directly out of the mana fields. If something stirs, do not hesitate to raise the alarm."

Aurelia stepped up to his left, her golden eyes glowing with a sharp tranquil vigilance as a faint aura of Argent Flame wrapped protectively around her hands. "I will keep my senses peeled, Lord Silas... No corrupt or restless presence will escape my notice."

To his right, Thor casually stepped down into the depression, her massive dwarven pickaxe resting easily in one hand while her storm-blue eyes narrowed as microscopic arcs of blue static crackling across her knuckles.
"Aye! Fear not, Lord Silas! If a spirit dares to bare its fangs at us, I will swat it out of the air like a summer fly!"
Silas looked at both of them, offering a sincere nod. "Thank you, both of you. That’s precisely why I brought you two to this sector."
He took a slow deep breath, centering his focus.

’I’m at the second stage of Core Advancement,’ Silas thought, mentally probing the brilliant sea of power humming within his Mythic Gold Core. ’My spiritual perception has expanded tenfold since the Lord War... If there’s an elemental entity lurking in this chamber, my senses should be able to pick up its spiritual footprint just as easily as Aurelia or Thor.’
He closed his eyes, extending his internal mana outward like a delicate invisible web, sweeping across the stone, the twisting red vines, and the vaulted ceiling above.
...Nothing.
The air was heavy, the mana was dense, but there was no hostile intent as no foreign consciousness brushing against his web.
Silas opened his eyes, letting his gaze sweep the quiet alcove.
He shrugged his shoulders, rolling his wrists to loosen his grip on the tool.
"Whatever," Silas muttered under his breath, shaking off the paranoia. "Let’s get to work."
TINK!
Silas brought his pickaxe down, his wrists snapping with precision as he began carefully prying the first cluster of white diamonds away from the crimson vine.
Behind him, the girls, Aurelia, and Thora spread out along the perimeter of the depression with their tools chiming softly in the eerie gloom.
The work continued in steady silence and none of them noticed... well except Thor but even then, it was too weak for her to take seriously.
High above their heads, nestled deep within a shadowy cluster of jagged overhanging blood-red stalactites forty feet up on the cavern ceiling, something stirred.
It was not a beast of fur and bone...
It was a compact fist-sized orb of pure crimson light... an uncontracted elemental spirit.
The orb pulsed slowly, expanding and contracting with the exact heartbeat-like cadence as the crystal vines below.
Two burning pinpricks of pure, curious consciousness flickered within the center of the sphere.

Silently, without releasing a single ripple of hostile mana into the air, the crimson spirit hovered in the darkness of the ceiling, staring straight down at the black-haired Lord harvesting its sacred grove.
The rhythmic metallic chiming of dwarven pickaxes against stone continued to echo through the sunken depression of Cavern KB-22.
TINK! TINK! TINK!
Every strike was disciplined.
Following Thora’s strict guidelines, the girls worked along the perimeter of the ancient grove, carefully reading the petrified fault lines where the blood-red vines met the milky-white diamonds.
Near the eastern curve of the bowl, Sarah wiped a drop of sweat from her eyelid with the back of her leather gauntlet.
She rested her steel pickaxe against her boot, arching her back with a soft breathy groan that drew a laugh from Helen.

"My shoulders are going to be stiff for a week," Sarah murmured, rolling her neck until her joints popped. "I thought running drills in the mud with Lady Brida was hell, but this? You can’t even put your back into it... You have to snap your wrists like a seamstress."

"Stop whining and keep tapping," Helen chuckled, dislodging a clean fist-sized cluster of white diamonds that clattered neatly into her leather collection bag. "The faster we clear this alcove, the sooner we head back to the bathhouses... Master Thora said these red formations burn hotter than forge embers when they’re processed so imagine the heat in the private quarters if we put it there."

"Oh, don’t get me started on the baths," Brenda chimed in from five paces away, her freckled cheeks glowing red as she dropped another gleaming stone into her pack. "Hot mineral water up to my chin, clean linen sheets... and maybe a certain Lord checking in on the barracks to deliver those commendations he promised."
A round of soft teasing giggles rippled through the ranks.
Even Vala and Reina, working on opposite sides of the grove, shared a knowing silent smirk.

Reina was meticulously checking the fault lines with a small steel awl, while Vala used her shadow-affinity to catch falling stones before they struck the bedrock, ensuring not a single crystalline facet chipped upon landing.
GURRRRRRRR-ROOOOOM!
A low vibrating rumble like the distant roll of summer thunder shaking an imperial fortress suddenly tore through the cavern, drowning out the chiming pickaxes.
The girls froze mid-swing. Brenda gasped, almost dropping her runic chisel, while Helen snapped her spear forward with a sharp clack.
"What was that?!" Sarah yelped, her eyes darting toward the ceiling. "Did the fault lines slip?!"
Silas lowered his pickaxe, his brow furrowing as he stepped back from the wall.
His senses swept the stone floor, probing for seismic shifts or collapsing bedrock but nothing was moving as the mountain was stable.
Slowly, every pair of eyes in the sunken grove drifted toward the center of the depression.
There, perched cross-legged atop a rounded limestone boulder, was Thor.

The towering blonde God of Thunder had her pickaxe resting casually across her lap. One massive, muscular hand was pressed firmly against her stomach, which was currently letting out another series of wet seismic gurgles that vibrated the loose shale beneath her boots.
GURRR-RUMBLE!

"Didn’t you literally just eat an entire roasted boar?!" Thora shouted, her hands flying to her hips as she glared at the demigoddess with bewildered indignation. "A three-pound shank! A five-gallon keg of dark dwarven stout! You inhaled enough calories to keep a siege battalion marching for a fortnight, and your gut is already screaming like a dying hydra?!"
Thor didn’t even look ashamed.
She tilted her head, giving her flat rock-hard abdomen an affectionate pat that echoed with a dull muscular thump.
Her storm-blue eyes turned toward Silas, they were wide, innocent, and brimming with unapologetic divine hunger.

"The mortal shell burns fuel swiftly when glory is at stake, little smith!" Thor declared, her booming voice rattling the stalactites overhead. "Divine flesh requires divine sustenance! The thunder in my veins demands meat to feed the lightning! Besides, that pig was lean... A great warrior cannot subsist on a mere single beast when the mountain air is so cold and crisp! I can feel my divine essence fading away to nothingness!"

"Fading to nothingness?!" Thora sputtered, her face reddening as she gestured wildly toward Thor’s armor-straining chest and sculpted thighs. "You take up half the cavern, you overgrown blonde glutton! If you fade any more, you’ll collapse the tectonic plates!"
The Princess giggled behind her hand, her shoulders trembling with amusement, while Aurelia offered a serene patient smile from the other side of the grove.𝒻𝘳ℯℯ𝑤ℯ𝒷𝘯ℴ𝓋ℯ𝘭.𝑐ℴ𝑚
Silas let out a quiet chuckle, shaking his head.
"Don’t let her near the reserve rations, Thora. If she starts gnawing on the crates, we won’t have anything left to haul the ore."
He turned back to the rock face, hoisting his runic pickaxe once more.
Tink!
His wrists snapped with fluid precision, cleanly severing another cluster of milky-white diamonds from the blood-red vine.
But as the stone fell into his palm, that same strange prickly chill brushed against the back of his neck.
’There it is again...’ Silas thought, his eyes narrowing slightly in the gloom.
It was faint... so faint that even with his second-stage Gold Core advancement, he couldn’t pinpoint an exact physical vector.
It didn’t carry malice, nor did it possess the greasy suffocating stench of the shapeshifting beasts or the corrupt monsters of the Umbral Basin.
It felt more like a gaze.
An intense curious pair of eyes boring into his skull from somewhere overhead.

sentences.text: Silas was briefly smothered against her leather-strained chest, the intoxicating scent of her filling his senses before she released him, her cleavage shaking wildly with every boisterous laugh.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHA!" Thor roared, slapping Silas on the back with enough force to shatter a normal man’s clavicle.
"The ale is safe!
The meat is mine!
Let the feast begin!"
Without waiting for utensils, Thor plunged both hands into the bowl, ripping off a three-pound roasted shank and tearing into the succulent meat with savage glorious divine enthusiasm.
Juice ran down her chin, her eyes rolling back in pure ecstasy as she popped the spigot on the keg and took a massive five-second swig of dark stout, letting out a satisfied cavern-shaking belch.
"Hey!
Giantess!
Mind your table manners!" Thora scowled from across the mat, though the dwarf was happily devouring her own box of salted beef and sharp cheese.
"You’re spraying garlic onto the Princess’s rice!"
"Pay it no mind, Master Thora!" the Princess giggled brightly, her azure eyes sparkling as she sat with her legs tucked demurely beneath her.
"It is wonderful to see Lady Thor in such high spirits!"
As the food disappeared, the atmosphere on the picnic mat transformed into a lively chaotic celebration.
"Alright, girls!
Who’s up for an eating trial?!" Sarah shouted, waving a skewer of spicy spirit-peppers in the air.
"The frontier wall game!
Five spirit-peppers in a single bite without reaching for the water canteen!
Winner gets first pick of the dessert pastries!"
"You’re on, Sarah!" Brenda barked, rolling up her sleeves with fierce freckled determination.
"I ate boiled nettles for six months on the border!
Your little pepper seeds can’t hurt me!"
"Count me in!" Helen grinned, leaning over the mat.
The girls cheered and clapped, banging their empty wooden cups against the stone floor as Brenda and Sarah stuffed their mouths with the bright crimson peppers.

Within three seconds, both girls’ faces turned the exact shade of ripe tomatoes, their eyes watering profusely as they chewed frantically, refusing to blink with their cheeks puffing out as the rest of the squad roared with hysterical laughter.
"Don’t swallow yet, Brenda!
Hold the line!"
"Sarah’s tearing up!
Sarah’s reaching for the canteen!"
"I am not!" Sarah choked out, her voice muffled around the peppers, coughing as smoke practically vented from her ears.
Silas sat back, leaning comfortably against the warm wall, watching the women laugh, tease, and shove each other playfully.
’Ah, I’m happy...’
This was what the mining, the walls, and the sovereign upgrades were all about.
Building a sanctuary where the people who bled for him could laugh like children in the middle of a hostile wasteland.
Eventually, the lunch boxes were emptied, the mat was neatly rolled up and returned to Silas’s spatial inventory, and the women strapped their heavy tool belts back onto their hips.
The playful banter faded, replaced once more by professionalism.
Silas hoisted his runic pickaxe over his shoulder, his expression turning serious as he turned toward the eastern quadrant of the geode.
"Form up on me," Silas ordered quietly.
"We’re heading into the eastern alcove."
The squad immediately fell into disciplined ranks behind him, their boots crunching softly against the crystalline gravel as they navigated past the towering calcified stalagmites.
Within minutes, they stood at the lip of the sunken bowl-shaped depression Silas had scouted earlier.
The vibrant multicolored prismatic light of the main geode completely vanished here.
In its place was a heavy suffocating aura that pressed against the skin like thick humid fog.
The walls and floor of the sunken grove were completely coated in a bizarre petrified lattice of striking blood-red crystals and pure milky-white diamonds.

They didn’t grow in jagged geometric clusters like the standard gems... they twisted and wound around each other like living, petrified vines, pulsing with a slow eerie heartbeat that sent metallic hums through the air.
The hair on the back of Silas’s neck stood on end.
The entire atmosphere felt remarkably familiar.

It carried the exact same strange and volatile pressure as the lightless cavern where they had discovered that unrecorded white alloy... the one Thora had claimed naming rights over and christened Sil-Graves Silver.
"Look at the grain on these bastards..." Thora whispered, her voice dropping all mockery as she knelt at the edge of the depression.
She pressed her bare palm against a patch of dark stone near the red vines with her clean-shaven face set in deep calculating lines.
"The mana conductivity here is completely mutated.
It’s dense as lead, but volatile as blasting powder."
"How do we harvest it, Thora?" Silas asked, his eyes scanning the pulsing red lattice.
"Carefully, my Lord," Thora explained, pointing with the tip of her chisel.
"You don’t strike outside the bleed-line here because the white diamonds are the bleed-line...
The red crystal is the core while the white diamond is the calcified mana shell.
If you separate them cleanly at the junction seam, you preserve both so if you nick the red core with an improper angle, the trapped elemental charge will violently discharge."
Silas nodded, stepping down into the sunken grove.
He gripped his pickaxe, looking back over his shoulder at the squad.
"Keep your eyes wide and your senses sharp," Silas warned, his voice ringing out with clarity.
"Like I said earlier, caverns with this level of stagnant centuries-old elemental power are prime breeding grounds for entities.
Uncontracted spirits born in places like this don’t have bodies of flesh... they manifest directly out of the mana fields.
If something stirs, do not hesitate to raise the alarm."
Aurelia stepped up to his left, her golden eyes glowing with a sharp tranquil vigilance as a faint aura of Argent Flame wrapped protectively around her hands.
"I will keep my senses peeled, Lord Silas...
No corrupt or restless presence will escape my notice."

To his right, Thor casually stepped down into the depression, her massive dwarven pickaxe resting easily in one hand while her storm-blue eyes narrowed as microscopic arcs of blue static crackling across her knuckles.
"Aye!
Fear not, Lord Silas!
If a spirit dares to bare its fangs at us, I will swat it out of the air like a summer fly!"
Silas looked at both of them, offering a sincere nod.
"Thank you, both of you.
That’s precisely why I brought you two to this sector."
He took a slow deep breath, centering his focus.

’I’m at the second stage of Core Advancement,’ Silas thought, mentally probing the brilliant sea of power humming within his Mythic Gold Core. ’My spiritual perception has expanded tenfold since the Lord War...
If there’s an elemental entity lurking in this chamber, my senses should be able to pick up its spiritual footprint just as easily as Aurelia or Thor.’
He closed his eyes, extending his internal mana outward like a delicate invisible web, sweeping across the stone, the twisting red vines, and the vaulted ceiling above.
...Nothing.
The air was heavy, the mana was dense, but there was no hostile intent as no foreign consciousness brushing against his web.
Silas opened his eyes, letting his gaze sweep the quiet alcove.
He shrugged his shoulders, rolling his wrists to loosen his grip on the tool.
"Whatever," Silas muttered under his breath, shaking off the paranoia.
"Let’s get to work."
TINK!
Silas brought his pickaxe down, his wrists snapping with precision as he began carefully prying the first cluster of white diamonds away from the crimson vine.
Behind him, the girls, Aurelia, and Thora spread out along the perimeter of the depression with their tools chiming softly in the eerie gloom.
The work continued in steady silence and none of them noticed... well except Thor but even then, it was too weak for her to take seriously.
High above their heads, nestled deep within a shadowy cluster of jagged overhanging blood-red stalactites forty feet up on the cavern ceiling, something stirred.
It was not a beast of fur and bone...
It was a compact fist-sized orb of pure crimson light... an uncontracted elemental spirit.
The orb pulsed slowly, expanding and contracting with the exact heartbeat-like cadence as the crystal vines below.
Two burning pinpricks of pure, curious consciousness flickered within the center of the sphere.

chapters.title: Chapter 488: A Higher Spirit
paragraphs: Silas didn’t stop swinging though.
He kept his rhythm steady, allowing his mana to hum quietly beneath his skin, ready to detonate outward at the slightest provocation.
Within an hour of steady focused work, the center of the sunken depression was dominated by a massive shimmering mound of raw material.
Hundreds of pounds of blood-red crystal vines and brilliant milky-white diamonds lay stacked together.
The pulsing luminescence of the crimson formations bathed the girls’ faces in a warm ethereal glow, while the white gems scattered the light across the ceiling in brilliant dancing flecks.
Helen leaned on her pickaxe, wiping sweat from her brow as she looked down at the volume of the harvest.

"Well," Helen said, her chest heaving slightly against her leather harness, "that’s the lower shelf completely stripped. But... how in the world are we going to haul this up to the main cavern? The Phase One Golem is way too massive to squeeze down this narrow fissure."
Brenda nodded, looking back toward the winding, cramped tunnel that led to the outer goblin hollow.
"Yeah, even if we split it into the Phase Three scout units, those little quad-golems can only carry a couple of crates each. It would take twenty trips back and forth just to move this single pile."
The women turned their attention toward Thora.
"Master Thora," Sarah asked, tilting her head. "What’s the extraction protocol for this alcove? Did you bring auxiliary pulley lines?"
Thora paused.

The dwarven forge master slowly looked at the towering mountain of red and white crystals, then looked at the narrow three-foot-wide limestone throat of the tunnel, and then down at her own empty hands.
"Good question," Thora said plainly.
She turned slowly, locking her amber eyes onto Silas.
Silas blinked. He lowered his pickaxe, staring at the dwarven smith with deadpan incredulous disbelief.
"Thora," Silas murmured, his voice dropping into a flat monotone. "Don’t tell me. You didn’t have a plan for getting the payload out of this alcove, did you?"
Thora didn’t flinch.

Instead, she tilted her head to the side, poked the tip of her tongue out between her teeth, brought her clenched fist up to the side of her temple, and gave her head a light cartoonishly cute rap with her knuckle.

"Ehe~" Thora chirped, winking one amber eye. "Sorry, my Lord! My brain was so full of high-grade alloy formulas and diamond matrices that I forgot to measure the doorway! Logistics is an evolving science, you know!"
Silas stared at her, his left eye twitching violently.
Without moving his boots an inch, Silas raised his right hand, curled his thumb behind his index finger, and flicked the empty air directly toward the four-foot-tall dwarf.
POW!
He didn’t even make physical contact, but the compressed air-bullet generated by the physical power of his Gold Core shot across the five-foot gap.
CLACK!

"OWWWWW!" Thora shrieked, clutching both hands to her forehead as she stumbled backward with her boots kicking up crystalline dust. "What was that for?! You didn’t even touch me and it felt like an iron rivet! You’re abusing your chief of the forge!"
"I’m disciplining a logistics officer who didn’t measure the damn door," Silas retorted dryly, though the smirk on his lips betrayed his amusement.
Thor immediately vaulted down from her boulder with an earth-shattering thud, puffing out her massive chest.

"Fear not, Lord Silas! If the little smith’s mind has failed, divine strength shall prevail! Point me to the stone! I shall pick up the entire mountain shelf and march it to the surface upon my shoulders!"

"No, Thor, absolutely not," Silas sighed, holding up a hand to stop her before she collapsed the entire ceiling. "I appreciate the enthusiasm, but you’d punch a hole straight through the mountain and bury the diamonds in an avalanche."
Silas walked into the center of the depression, stopping right before the massive pile of harvested crystals.
He took a slow steady breath, closing his eyes as he tapped into the dense reservoir of his Mythic Gold Core.
VUUUUUUM!
A subtle pale golden halo hummed around his silhouette.
He didn’t channel the destructive fury of his fire but instead, he reached deep into the earth affinity anchored within his core, attuning his will to the limestone bedrock beneath his boots.
He raised his right foot and stomped down against the stone.
KRA-CRUNCH!
The bedrock beneath the perimeter of the crystal pile groaned in submission.
With terrifying fluidity, the solid limestone floor cracked, warped, and surged upward.
Four dense thick slabs of rock rose from the earth, interlocking seamlessly along their edges to form a massive perfectly squared storage crate roughly eight feet wide and four feet deep.

With a sweep of his arm, Silas manipulated the earth mana, causing the stone floor beneath the diamonds to tilt smoothly, sliding every single red crystal and white diamond directly into the newly forged stone crate without a single chip to their facets.𝕗𝐫𝐞𝕖𝕨𝐞𝗯𝚗𝕠𝘃𝐞𝚕.𝐜𝗼𝚖
RATTLE-CLATTER!
"There," Silas murmured, stepping up to the heavy stone crate.
He reached down with his right hand, wrapping his fingers firmly beneath the thick limestone rim.
The entire crate, loaded to the brim with hundreds of pounds of dense, mana-saturated earth ores, had to weigh well over a ton.
Yet, as Silas flexed his arm, the corded muscles of his bicep and shoulder tightened beneath his dark leather harness, veins rising against his tanned skin with effortless terrifying power.
With a single, smooth pull, Silas hoisted the massive stone crate off the ground using only his right hand, balancing the crushing weight on his palm as if it were a common wooden tray.
"I’ll carry this batch out to the main chamber," Silas instructed, turning toward the tunnel. "Keep working the lower seams and be careful around the vine roots."
"Understood, my Lord!" the girls chorused, watching his retreating form with wide, awe-struck eyes.
As Silas stepped into the shadow of the narrow passage, Aurelia’s golden eyes suddenly flicked upward toward the cavern ceiling.
High above, nestled within the dense thicket of blood-red stalactites, a soft crimson glow flared.
FZZT!
A small fist-sized orb of pure, incandescent red light detached from the stone roof.
It floated, drifting silently through the air like a drifting soap bubble, maintaining a distance of barely ten paces behind Silas’s back as he marched down the dark corridor.
Aurelia’s brow arched delicately.
’A spirit, huh?’ she thought, her lips curving into a quiet knowing smile.
She glanced sideways, looking over at Thor.

The blonde thunder god was leaning against a stalagmite, completely oblivious to the spiritual presence, staring into empty space with a thin, glossy line of drool slowly pooling at the corner of her parted lips.
’Roasted boar... crispy skin... sweet mustard...’ Thor’s internal thoughts were practically radiating from her skull like a beacon.
Aurelia shook her head, letting out a soft amused sigh.
’Was this god ever not hungry?’ she mused, turning back to her vertical limestone slab and raising her pickaxe. ’Well, Lord Silas can handle a little curiosity on his own.’
Out in the winding corridor connecting the geode to the outer goblin hollow, the air grew noticeably colder.
Silas walked with steady measured strides, his heavy boots crunching against the limestone gravel.
The massive stone crate resting on his right palm remained perfectly level, not a single diamond spilling over the rim despite the awkward narrow turns of the rock chimney.
As he reached the midpoint of the passage... right near the sharp ninety-degree bend where the natural geode light faded, a sudden sharp tingling sensation swept across the skin behind his left ear.
The temperature in the tunnel dropped by a fraction of a degree, replaced by the distinct hum of high-power elemental mana.
SWISH!
Silas’s combat instincts flared. Without breaking his stride, he snapped his head around, his blue eyes scanning the darkness behind his left shoulder.
Nothing... The corridor was empty...
FZZT!
A second later, a warm tickling draft brushed against the right side of his jaw.
Silas whipped his head forward and to the right, his jaw clenching.
Empty.
’This thing is fucking with me,’ Silas thought, his eye twitching with suppressed irritation. ’It’s fast... It’s slipping through the spatial blind spots right at the edge of my optical vision.’
He didn’t draw a blade and he didn’t drop the crate.
Silas calmly rounded the final corner, stepping out into the colossal dome-shaped hollow where the goblin settlement had once stood.
’We already widened the path before with the help of Thor so it’s a lot easier.’
The smoldering bone-fires of the dead tribe had long since turned to cold gray ash, but the wide expanse gave him plenty of room to maneuver.
Resting in the center of the hollow was the massive Phase 1 Titan Golem, its amber optics idling in low-power standby mode.
Silas approached the open space, bent his knees slightly, and lowered the heavy stone crate to the limestone bedrock with a muffled thud.

He tilted the crate forward, using a subtle pulse of earth mana to dissolve the front panel, allowing the hundreds of pounds of red crystals and white diamonds to slide smoothly into a massive glittering heap on the floor.
"Phase One Titan," Silas commanded, his voice echoing cleanly off the high granite ceiling. "Sweep and load."
KRRRRRR-GRIND!
The construct responded immediately.
Its massive stone arm, thick as an ancient oak and reinforced with plates of Deep-Earth Alloy, reached out across the cavern floor.
The articulated bedrock fingers spread wide, scooping beneath the entire pile of crimson and white ores with mechanical elegance.
The golem lifted the massive haul overhead, dumping the minerals directly into the second reinforced transport bin bolted across its back with a rolling thunderous roar.
CLATTER-CRASH!
Right beside Silas’s left ear, a tiny high-pitched hum vibrated through the air.
Silas didn’t move his neck as he merely shifted his eyes.
Floating roughly three feet off the ground, hovering entirely out in the open, was the source of his annoyance.
It was a compact fist-sized orb of pure radiant crimson light.
The sphere pulsed with a slow hypnotic rhythm, completely entranced by the sight of the colossal stone titan effortlessly moving hundreds of pounds of earth ore.
The tiny entity seemed completely spellbound, its faint light flickering with pure child-like fascination.
Silas slowly turned his head to look directly at it.
The moment their eyes met, the crimson orb froze.
The pulsing light hitched, and the spirit violently jerked backward, attempting to dart back toward the ceiling fissures—
SWOOSH!
Silas’s hand was faster.
Honed by weeks if not months of brutal combat, his right arm blurred through the air like a striking viper.
His fingers clamped shut, catching the floating orb dead-center in his palm.
"Finally," Silas smirked, his grip tightening around the smooth, weightless ball of light. "I caught you."
He raised his hand, inspecting the trapped anomaly.
"I’ve been wondering what kind of ghost was breathing down my neck all morning... So you’re the little spectator watching us from the ceiling."
The moment Silas’s calloused flesh wrapped around its form, the spirit panicked.
SZZZZZZZZZT!
The crimson orb violently heated up.
Within a fraction of a second, the surface temperature skyrocketed from a mild hum to a blistering white-hot blaze.
An inferno of bright crimson elemental fire erupted from the sphere, wrapping around Silas’s fingers and engulfing his entire right hand in roaring flames!
"Whoa—"
Silas reflexively opened his fingers, releasing his grip.
The crimson orb shot upward like a panicked firework, soaring twenty feet into the air before hovering near the granite ceiling, its light flaring erratically as if gasping for breath.
Silas raised his right hand, casually waving it through the air twice.
WHOOSH!
The flames detached from his skin, dying out in harmless wisps of gray smoke that drifted toward the darkness.
Silas looked down at his palm.
His skin wasn’t blistered and it wasn’t charred either.
There was barely a rosy flush across his calluses, which faded within seconds under the natural self-cleansing vitality of his Mythic Gold Core.
’It’s still quite weak,’ Silas analyzed, rubbing his thumb across his palm with a thoughtful hum.
His mind quickly sifted through the academic lectures he had half-listened to during his early days at Valoria Academy before the Lord War had shattered normal life.
Spirits were not monsters.

They were not born of corrupted flesh, anomalous curses, or necrotic rot. They were spontaneous manifestations of pure concentrated elemental mana that gathered in stagnant undisturbed geological formations over centuries.
Places like Cavern KB-22 where high-power Mana Diamonds and volatile crimson crystal vines grew intertwined for hundreds of years were natural cradles for elemental life.
Most spirits born in such isolation were little more than curious, instinct-driven wisps.
They possessed consciousness, but it was simple, innocent, and reactive... much like a newborn beast or a young child.
They lacked the malice of Evil Spirits, like that parasitic entity that had lurked in the dark mines to ambush Thora during the discovery of the Sil-Graves Silver alloy.
Silas tilted his chin upward, looking at the trembling crimson orb hovering near the rafters.
"You’re not trying to hurt anyone, are you?" Silas called out, his voice softening, shedding its cold combat edge. "That fire was just a panic reflex so its self-defense."
The crimson orb bobbed slightly, its erratic pulsing slowly stabilizing into a warm steady heartbeat.
It hovered in place, watching the human lord who had brushed off its hottest flames without a single blister.
Silas turned his back on the spirit, walking calmly toward the entrance of the narrow tunnel to head back to the harvesting crew.
PING!
Right before his eyes, a crisp translucent system notification flashed into existence, floating in the center of his vision.
[Ding! A Higher Spirit would like to initiate a Spirit Contract with you. Will you accept?]
[Y / N]
Silas froze mid-step.
He blinked, staring at the glowing letters hovering in the dark air.
"A Spirit Contract?" Silas murmured aloud.

sentences.text: Silas didn’t stop swinging though.
He kept his rhythm steady, allowing his mana to hum quietly beneath his skin, ready to detonate outward at the slightest provocation.
Within an hour of steady focused work, the center of the sunken depression was dominated by a massive shimmering mound of raw material.
Hundreds of pounds of blood-red crystal vines and brilliant milky-white diamonds lay stacked together.
The pulsing luminescence of the crimson formations bathed the girls’ faces in a warm ethereal glow, while the white gems scattered the light across the ceiling in brilliant dancing flecks.
Helen leaned on her pickaxe, wiping sweat from her brow as she looked down at the volume of the harvest.
"Well," Helen said, her chest heaving slightly against her leather harness, "that’s the lower shelf completely stripped.
But... how in the world are we going to haul this up to the main cavern?
The Phase One Golem is way too massive to squeeze down this narrow fissure."
Brenda nodded, looking back toward the winding, cramped tunnel that led to the outer goblin hollow.
"Yeah, even if we split it into the Phase Three scout units, those little quad-golems can only carry a couple of crates each.
It would take twenty trips back and forth just to move this single pile."
The women turned their attention toward Thora.
"Master Thora," Sarah asked, tilting her head.
"What’s the extraction protocol for this alcove?
Did you bring auxiliary pulley lines?"
Thora paused.

The dwarven forge master slowly looked at the towering mountain of red and white crystals, then looked at the narrow three-foot-wide limestone throat of the tunnel, and then down at her own empty hands.
"Good question," Thora said plainly.
She turned slowly, locking her amber eyes onto Silas.
Silas blinked.
He lowered his pickaxe, staring at the dwarven smith with deadpan incredulous disbelief.
"Thora," Silas murmured, his voice dropping into a flat monotone.
"Don’t tell me.
You didn’t have a plan for getting the payload out of this alcove, did you?"
Thora didn’t flinch.

Instead, she tilted her head to the side, poked the tip of her tongue out between her teeth, brought her clenched fist up to the side of her temple, and gave her head a light cartoonishly cute rap with her knuckle.
"Ehe~" Thora chirped, winking one amber eye.
"Sorry, my Lord!
My brain was so full of high-grade alloy formulas and diamond matrices that I forgot to measure the doorway!
Logistics is an evolving science, you know!"
Silas stared at her, his left eye twitching violently.
Without moving his boots an inch, Silas raised his right hand, curled his thumb behind his index finger, and flicked the empty air directly toward the four-foot-tall dwarf.
POW!
He didn’t even make physical contact, but the compressed air-bullet generated by the physical power of his Gold Core shot across the five-foot gap.
CLACK!
"OWWWWW!" Thora shrieked, clutching both hands to her forehead as she stumbled backward with her boots kicking up crystalline dust.
"What was that for?!
You didn’t even touch me and it felt like an iron rivet!
You’re abusing your chief of the forge!"
"I’m disciplining a logistics officer who didn’t measure the damn door," Silas retorted dryly, though the smirk on his lips betrayed his amusement.
Thor immediately vaulted down from her boulder with an earth-shattering thud, puffing out her massive chest.
"Fear not, Lord Silas!
If the little smith’s mind has failed, divine strength shall prevail!
Point me to the stone!
I shall pick up the entire mountain shelf and march it to the surface upon my shoulders!"
"No, Thor, absolutely not," Silas sighed, holding up a hand to stop her before she collapsed the entire ceiling.
"I appreciate the enthusiasm, but you’d punch a hole straight through the mountain and bury the diamonds in an avalanche."
Silas walked into the center of the depression, stopping right before the massive pile of harvested crystals.
He took a slow steady breath, closing his eyes as he tapped into the dense reservoir of his Mythic Gold Core.
VUUUUUUM!
A subtle pale golden halo hummed around his silhouette.
He didn’t channel the destructive fury of his fire but instead, he reached deep into the earth affinity anchored within his core, attuning his will to the limestone bedrock beneath his boots.
He raised his right foot and stomped down against the stone.
KRA-CRUNCH!
The bedrock beneath the perimeter of the crystal pile groaned in submission.
With terrifying fluidity, the solid limestone floor cracked, warped, and surged upward.
Four dense thick slabs of rock rose from the earth, interlocking seamlessly along their edges to form a massive perfectly squared storage crate roughly eight feet wide and four feet deep.

With a sweep of his arm, Silas manipulated the earth mana, causing the stone floor beneath the diamonds to tilt smoothly, sliding every single red crystal and white diamond directly into the newly forged stone crate without a single chip to their facets.𝕗𝐫𝐞𝕖𝕨𝐞𝗯𝚗𝕠𝘃𝐞𝚕.𝐜𝗼𝚖
RATTLE-CLATTER!
"There," Silas murmured, stepping up to the heavy stone crate.
He reached down with his right hand, wrapping his fingers firmly beneath the thick limestone rim.
The entire crate, loaded to the brim with hundreds of pounds of dense, mana-saturated earth ores, had to weigh well over a ton.
Yet, as Silas flexed his arm, the corded muscles of his bicep and shoulder tightened beneath his dark leather harness, veins rising against his tanned skin with effortless terrifying power.
With a single, smooth pull, Silas hoisted the massive stone crate off the ground using only his right hand, balancing the crushing weight on his palm as if it were a common wooden tray.
"I’ll carry this batch out to the main chamber," Silas instructed, turning toward the tunnel.
"Keep working the lower seams and be careful around the vine roots."
"Understood, my Lord!" the girls chorused, watching his retreating form with wide, awe-struck eyes.
As Silas stepped into the shadow of the narrow passage, Aurelia’s golden eyes suddenly flicked upward toward the cavern ceiling.
High above, nestled within the dense thicket of blood-red stalactites, a soft crimson glow flared.
FZZT!
A small fist-sized orb of pure, incandescent red light detached from the stone roof.
It floated, drifting silently through the air like a drifting soap bubble, maintaining a distance of barely ten paces behind Silas’s back as he marched down the dark corridor.
Aurelia’s brow arched delicately.
’A spirit, huh?’ she thought, her lips curving into a quiet knowing smile.
She glanced sideways, looking over at Thor.

The blonde thunder god was leaning against a stalagmite, completely oblivious to the spiritual presence, staring into empty space with a thin, glossy line of drool slowly pooling at the corner of her parted lips.
’Roasted boar... crispy skin... sweet mustard...’ Thor’s internal thoughts were practically radiating from her skull like a beacon.
Aurelia shook her head, letting out a soft amused sigh.
’Was this god ever not hungry?’ she mused, turning back to her vertical limestone slab and raising her pickaxe. ’Well, Lord Silas can handle a little curiosity on his own.’
Out in the winding corridor connecting the geode to the outer goblin hollow, the air grew noticeably colder.
Silas walked with steady measured strides, his heavy boots crunching against the limestone gravel.
The massive stone crate resting on his right palm remained perfectly level, not a single diamond spilling over the rim despite the awkward narrow turns of the rock chimney.
As he reached the midpoint of the passage... right near the sharp ninety-degree bend where the natural geode light faded, a sudden sharp tingling sensation swept across the skin behind his left ear.
The temperature in the tunnel dropped by a fraction of a degree, replaced by the distinct hum of high-power elemental mana.
SWISH!
Silas’s combat instincts flared.
Without breaking his stride, he snapped his head around, his blue eyes scanning the darkness behind his left shoulder.
Nothing...
The corridor was empty...
FZZT!
A second later, a warm tickling draft brushed against the right side of his jaw.
Silas whipped his head forward and to the right, his jaw clenching.
Empty.
’This thing is fucking with me,’ Silas thought, his eye twitching with suppressed irritation. ’It’s fast...
It’s slipping through the spatial blind spots right at the edge of my optical vision.’
He didn’t draw a blade and he didn’t drop the crate.
Silas calmly rounded the final corner, stepping out into the colossal dome-shaped hollow where the goblin settlement had once stood.
’We already widened the path before with the help of Thor so it’s a lot easier.’
The smoldering bone-fires of the dead tribe had long since turned to cold gray ash, but the wide expanse gave him plenty of room to maneuver.
Resting in the center of the hollow was the massive Phase 1 Titan Golem, its amber optics idling in low-power standby mode.
Silas approached the open space, bent his knees slightly, and lowered the heavy stone crate to the limestone bedrock with a muffled thud.

He tilted the crate forward, using a subtle pulse of earth mana to dissolve the front panel, allowing the hundreds of pounds of red crystals and white diamonds to slide smoothly into a massive glittering heap on the floor.
"Phase One Titan," Silas commanded, his voice echoing cleanly off the high granite ceiling.
"Sweep and load."
KRRRRRR-GRIND!
The construct responded immediately.
Its massive stone arm, thick as an ancient oak and reinforced with plates of Deep-Earth Alloy, reached out across the cavern floor.
The articulated bedrock fingers spread wide, scooping beneath the entire pile of crimson and white ores with mechanical elegance.
The golem lifted the massive haul overhead, dumping the minerals directly into the second reinforced transport bin bolted across its back with a rolling thunderous roar.
CLATTER-CRASH!
Right beside Silas’s left ear, a tiny high-pitched hum vibrated through the air.
Silas didn’t move his neck as he merely shifted his eyes.
Floating roughly three feet off the ground, hovering entirely out in the open, was the source of his annoyance.
It was a compact fist-sized orb of pure radiant crimson light.
The sphere pulsed with a slow hypnotic rhythm, completely entranced by the sight of the colossal stone titan effortlessly moving hundreds of pounds of earth ore.
The tiny entity seemed completely spellbound, its faint light flickering with pure child-like fascination.
Silas slowly turned his head to look directly at it.
The moment their eyes met, the crimson orb froze.
The pulsing light hitched, and the spirit violently jerked backward, attempting to dart back toward the ceiling fissures—
SWOOSH!
Silas’s hand was faster.
Honed by weeks if not months of brutal combat, his right arm blurred through the air like a striking viper.
His fingers clamped shut, catching the floating orb dead-center in his palm.
"Finally," Silas smirked, his grip tightening around the smooth, weightless ball of light.
"I caught you."
He raised his hand, inspecting the trapped anomaly.
"I’ve been wondering what kind of ghost was breathing down my neck all morning...
So you’re the little spectator watching us from the ceiling."
The moment Silas’s calloused flesh wrapped around its form, the spirit panicked.
SZZZZZZZZZT!
The crimson orb violently heated up.
Within a fraction of a second, the surface temperature skyrocketed from a mild hum to a blistering white-hot blaze.
An inferno of bright crimson elemental fire erupted from the sphere, wrapping around Silas’s fingers and engulfing his entire right hand in roaring flames!
"Whoa—"

The crimson orb shot upward like a panicked firework, soaring twenty feet into the air before hovering near the granite ceiling, its light flaring erratically as if gasping for breath.
Silas raised his right hand, casually waving it through the air twice.
WHOOSH!
The flames detached from his skin, dying out in harmless wisps of gray smoke that drifted toward the darkness.
Silas looked down at his palm.
