chapters.title: Chapter 489: Kael-Drin
paragraphs: He turned slowly on his heel, looking back toward the ceiling.
The crimson orb had drifted downward.
It was now hovering barely four feet off the ground, floating directly in front of him.

The light radiating from its core was pulsing with a strange brightness... an insistent and slightly indignant rhythm that looked remarkably like a small child puffing out its cheeks in a determined pout.
Silas scratched the back of his neck, his brows furrowing in genuine surprise.
’A Higher Spirit?’
The Valoria Academy texts echoed in his mind once more.
Spirits were categorized into rigid evolutionary hierarchies beginning from Lesser Spirits which are mindless formless wisps that could barely sustain a flame or a gust of wind.

After that were the Median Spirits which are semi-conscious entities capable of basic elemental manipulation and following simple commands, Higher Spirits which are fully sentient beings possessing immense elemental purity, distinct personalities, and the capacity to evolve into the higher level which was Great Spirits.

As for Great Spirits, they were very strong spirits whose powers were simply too much to be explained while Primordial Spirits were ancient spirits which had lived for a very long time and could unleash much more power than Great spirits.
The thought of Primordial Spirits sent an involuntary shudder down Silas’s spine.

His mind instantly flashed to Seraphina. That terrifying woman possessed a contracted Primordial Spirit of Fire... an apocalyptic entity whose flames burned so unfathomably hot that even the memories of her battle aura made his skin prickle with phantom heat.

’Seraphina’s fire was that hot because she held a Primordial entity,’ Silas thought, looking down at the fist-sized red orb hovering before him. ’This little thing isn’t at that level, but a Higher Spirit? Born naturally inside our territory’s diamond caverns?’
The crimson orb drifted closer. It didn’t spark, nor did it unleash its scalding heat.
Instead, two thin delicate tendrils of pure, translucent ruby mana slowly extended from the base of the sphere.
The tendrils reached out, hesitating for a fraction of a second, before gently brushing against Silas’s open palm.
Silas braced himself for a burn, but to his shock, the touch was remarkably cool.
It felt like smooth chilled glass, carrying a gentle pulse that hummed harmoniously with his own heartbeat.
A slow genuine smile spread across Silas’s face.
"Well," Silas chuckled, looking into the warm red light. "Why not? You’re certainly bold for a little cave spirit."
He leaned in slightly, his blue eyes locking onto the center of the sphere.
"Are you sure about this? Once you link with a Lord, you’re bound to Blessed Land. You’ll be working for the territory, little one."
The crimson orb bobbed vigorously. It tilted downward twice in rapid succession, executing a clean unmistakable nod.
"Smart little thing," Silas praised softly.
He raised his hand and tapped his finger against the translucent floating interface, selecting [Y].
VUUUUUUUUUUUM!
The instant his finger made contact, a dazzling pillar of pure golden mana detonated outward from Silas’s chest.
The royal radiance of his Mythic Gold Core flooded the entire cavern hollow, washing away every trace of shadow.
WHOOSH!
The crimson spirit didn’t retreat from the blinding light as it surged forward instead...

Like a falling ruby star, the orb slammed directly into the center of Silas’s chest, dissolving into a brilliant flash of liquid crimson fire that sank straight through his leather harness, through his skin, and deep into his internal mana circuits.
THUMP-THUMP!
Silas’s breath hitched.

For three long seconds, he felt a strange, thrilling pressure wrapping around his ribs... not painful, but intensely snug, as if dozens of cool, soothing crimson tendrils were weaving themselves seamlessly around his spiritual core, attuning their elemental frequencies to his own.
The pressure eased, melting into a warm comfortable hum that settled just beneath his heart.
[Ding! Spirit Contract successfully established!]
[Congratulations, Lord Silas Graves! You have formed a Bond with a Higher Elemental Spirit (Fire/Earth Variant)!]
POP!
With a soft, cheerful sound of displaced air, the spirit emerged from Silas’s sternum.
It floated in front of his face, looking largely identical to its previous form... a fist-sized sphere of radiant crimson light but there was an unmistakable shift in its aura.
Microscopic flecks of pure gold now drifted lazily within the ruby sphere which was a permanent mark of Silas’s core.
The spirit spun in a joyful celebratory circle, letting out a series of musical, chiming hums that sounded like tiny silver bells ringing in the wind.
Silas laughed, raising a finger to let the spirit rub its warm surface against his knuckle.
"Alright, if we’re partners now, you need a proper name," Silas mused, tapping his chin with his free hand. "Can’t just call you ’the red orb.’ How about... Cinder?"
The spirit spun violently to the left, letting out a flat dissonant bzzzt sound that clearly indicated disgust.
"Not a fan of Cinder? Fair enough," Silas grinned. "What about Pyro?"
Another sharp dismissive shake and the orb actually dimmed slightly, as if offended by the lack of creativity.
"Picky, aren’t you?" Silas chuckled.
He looked at the deep blood-red core of the spirit, remembering the ancient petrified crystal vines from which it had been born. "How about... Ignis? Or... Rubi?"
The spirit tilted slightly, considering it, but didn’t commit.
"Alright, one more," Silas said, his eyes gleaming. "Kael-Drin... It’s an old word for the sacred heart of the mountain fire."
The crimson orb froze.
Then, it flared with blinding ecstatic brilliance.

The tiny bell-like chiming resonated through the cavern, and the spirit began bouncing rapidly through the air, doing backflips around Silas’s head before settling happily on his right shoulder, nuzzling against his neck with a contented purr.
"Kael-Drin it is," Silas smiled, thoroughly amused. ’Proud little creature... It likes things that sound grand and ancient, huh?’
With the contract settled, Silas turned back toward the narrow passage, his newly bound companion riding securely on his shoulder.
"Come on, Kael-Drin," Silas said. "Let’s introduce you to the rest of the crew."
When Silas stepped back into the sunken depression of the diamond grove, the women were still hard at work with their pickaxes chiming against the rock face.
"Lord Silas is back!" Brenda called out, turning around with a bright smile.
Then, her eyes widened, locking onto the glowing red orb resting comfortably on his shoulder.
"Wait... what is that?!" Sarah gasped, lowering her chisel.
"Is that a spirit?!" Helen asked, taking a step forward with wide, curious eyes.
Silas chuckled, reaching up to gently tap the side of the sphere. "Girls, meet Kael-Drin. It seems our mining operation attracted a little local resident... We just formalized a Spirit Contract."

"A Spirit Contract?!" Thora’s jaw dropped, her soot-stained face cycling through pure shock before morphing into deep dwarven respect. "My Lord, you walked out to dump a load of rocks and came back with a contracted Higher Spirit?! Do you just trip over legendary blessings in your sleep?!"
Thor marched over, her heavy footsteps shaking the limestone, and bent her towering frame down until her face was barely six inches from the floating orb.

"Oho!" Thor boomed, her storm-blue eyes sparkling with delight as she poked a calloused finger toward the spirit. "A fiery little spark, aren’t you! You’ve got good spirit in your core, little one! Serve our Lord well, and I won’t eat you for breakfast!"
Kael-Drin didn’t cower. Instead, it flared its light brightly, letting out an indignant high-pitched chirp right into the thunder god’s face, completely unintimidated.
Thor threw her head back, roaring with boisterous laughter.
"GWAHAHAHA! I like this one! It has the heart of a berserker!"
The recruit maidens quickly gathered around, cooing and admiring the spirit’s radiant ruby glow.
The Princess reached out with delicate tentative fingers, giggling with pure delight as Kael-Drin gently brushed against her palm with its cool smooth tendrils.
"Alright, back to business," Silas announced, stepping into the center of the grove.

He stomped his boot once more, calling upon his earth magic to raise a massive wide stone crate from the bedrock... twice the size of the previous one, easily capable of holding the entirety of the remaining harvest.
"Let’s finish stripping this shelf," Silas ordered, hoisting his pickaxe. "We have daylight burning outside."
The women returned to the rock walls with renewed energized cheer.
Kael-Drin, eager to prove its worth to its new master, floated over to where Thora was working.
"What are you looking at, little spark?" Thora asked, wiping sweat from her brow as she held her heavy runic pickaxe.
Kael-Drin drifted down, extending two translucent red mana tendrils toward the tool.
The spirit gave the wooden handle an insistent tug, chiming softly as if demanding to hold the implement.
Thora’s face softened, a rare motherly grin breaking across her rough dwarven features.
"Oh, aren’t you precious! You want to carry Master Thora’s pickaxe? You’re too small for this, little one, but go on... show me what you’ve got!"
Chuckling, Thora handed the heavy steel tool over.
Kael-Drin didn’t try to lift the heavy iron with physical force.
Instead, it wrapped four thick dense tendrils of solidified ruby mana tightly around the shaft, effortlessly hoisting the twenty-pound pickaxe into the air!
"Well, look at that!" Thora beamed proudly, crossing her arms. "Stronger than you look—"
KRA-WHACK!
Kael-Drin didn’t measure six inches outside the bleed-line and it didn’t snap its wrists either.

Carried away by pure elemental enthusiasm, the spirit raised the pickaxe high overhead and slammed the steel spike dead-center into a protruding cluster of blood-red crystal vines with the concussive force of an explosive shell.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
A massive chunk of the wall... roughly ten feet wide violently fractured. Slabs of limestone peeled away in a massive cascade, exposing a breathtaking haul of raw diamonds.
...Along with roughly thirty percent of the precious crystal vines, which instantly destabilized and shattered into a cloud of sparkling worthless red powder that rained down over Thora’s boots.
Dead silence descended over the corner.
Kael-Drin hovered proudly in the air, pickaxe still raised, chiming happily as if expecting a gold medal.
Thora stood completely frozen.
Her pale face slowly transitioned from dwarven pride into a shade of volcanic purple that rivaled the deep-earth magma.
Her amber eyes bulged from their sockets, her fists shaking with such violent fury that her leather straps groaned.
"YOU... YOU LITTLE..." Thora’s voice strangled in her throat, her chest heaving as she fought the most agonizing internal battle of her entire life.
Every dwarven instinct screamed at her to roar at the top of her lungs, invoke a generational blood-curse, and punt the spirit across the cavern.
But as her eyes locked onto the innocent happily pulsing orb, she physically bit her lower lip, swallowing the scream until tears of pure, suppressed rage welled in the corners of her eyes.
Vala stepped out from the shadows beside her, reaching out and gently patting the trembling dwarf on the shoulder with a calm, comforting gesture.
"Breathe, Master Thora," Vala murmured soothingly. "It is a child. It knows not what it broke."

"I... I am calm..." Thora wheezed through clenched teeth, her eye twitching uncontrollably. "I am... an ocean of dwarven tranquility... Lord Silas, take your damn spark back before I forge it into a chamber pot!"
Silas quickly whistled, and Kael-Drin obediently floated over, relinquishing the pickaxe and settling contritely on his shoulder, seemingly sensing that it had crossed a very dangerous line.
The rest of the extraction went smoothly.

With everyone working in disciplined unison, the girls salvaged the remaining intact veins, carefully prying the white diamonds and crimson vines free until the entire sunken depression including the high formations clinging to the thirty-foot ceiling was completely stripped clean.
Every single scrap of the harvest was loaded into Silas’s massive stone crate, filling the container to its brim.
Silas wiped his brow, leaning against his pickaxe.
"Alright. That’s the entire grove cleared. Now... we just have to figure out how to haul this two-ton block out to the golem."
Thor stepped forward, cracking her knuckles with a confident, boisterous grin.
"Leave it to me, Lord Silas!" Thor declared. "I shall simply take the crate and teleport aboard the Titan Golem’s back!"
Silas blinked and Thora froze too.
The other women stared at her in stunned silence.
"You... you can teleport?" Silas asked, his voice deadpan.
Thor blinked her storm-blue eyes, looking at him as if he had just asked if the sky was blue.

"Yes?" Thor replied innocently. "I am the God of Thunder. The lightning rides the atmospheric currents... it strikes where it wills. Did you think I merely walked everywhere because I enjoyed the exercise?"
Before anyone could utter a single word of protest, Thor leaned down, hooked her massive muscular arms beneath the two-ton stone crate, and hoisted it effortlessly against her chest.
KRA-FLASH!
A deafening arc of brilliant blue lightning detonated in the center of the depression, smelling of scorched ozone.
When the light cleared, Thor and the two-ton crate had completely vanished from the room.
Silence stretched across the cavern.
"She... she could have just teleported the crates the entire bloody time?" Thora whispered, her voice cracking with existential exhaustion.
From the ranks, young Brenda tentatively raised her hand, breaking the silence with a soft thoughtful question.
"Um... Master Thora?" Brenda asked innocently. "Since we harvested all of these crystals... how long will it take for them to grow back? Can we come back next month?"
A chorus of soft good-natured chuckles rippled through the older veterans.
Thora slowly turned her head, fixing the freckled recruit with a flat unblinking dwarven stare.

"Crystals are not cabbages, lass," Thora stated plainly. "A high-density Mana Diamond vein takes roughly four to six centuries of subterranean tectonic compression and stagnant spiritual pressure to crystallize into physical ore..."
Brenda’s eyes widened. "Four... four hundred years?!"
"Aye," Thora sighed, turning toward the tunnel. "Which means you’re dumb for asking. Now grab your packs and move your boots!"

’Seraphina’s fire was that hot because she held a Primordial entity,’ Silas thought, looking down at the fist-sized red orb hovering before him. ’This little thing isn’t at that level, but a Higher Spirit?
Born naturally inside our territory’s diamond caverns?’
The crimson orb drifted closer.
It didn’t spark, nor did it unleash its scalding heat.
Instead, two thin delicate tendrils of pure, translucent ruby mana slowly extended from the base of the sphere.
The tendrils reached out, hesitating for a fraction of a second, before gently brushing against Silas’s open palm.
Silas braced himself for a burn, but to his shock, the touch was remarkably cool.
It felt like smooth chilled glass, carrying a gentle pulse that hummed harmoniously with his own heartbeat.
A slow genuine smile spread across Silas’s face.
"Well," Silas chuckled, looking into the warm red light.
"Why not?
You’re certainly bold for a little cave spirit."
He leaned in slightly, his blue eyes locking onto the center of the sphere.
"Are you sure about this?
Once you link with a Lord, you’re bound to Blessed Land.
You’ll be working for the territory, little one."
The crimson orb bobbed vigorously.
It tilted downward twice in rapid succession, executing a clean unmistakable nod.
"Smart little thing," Silas praised softly.
He raised his hand and tapped his finger against the translucent floating interface, selecting [Y].
VUUUUUUUUUUUM!
The instant his finger made contact, a dazzling pillar of pure golden mana detonated outward from Silas’s chest.
The royal radiance of his Mythic Gold Core flooded the entire cavern hollow, washing away every trace of shadow.
WHOOSH!
The crimson spirit didn’t retreat from the blinding light as it surged forward instead...

Like a falling ruby star, the orb slammed directly into the center of Silas’s chest, dissolving into a brilliant flash of liquid crimson fire that sank straight through his leather harness, through his skin, and deep into his internal mana circuits.
THUMP-THUMP!
Silas’s breath hitched.

For three long seconds, he felt a strange, thrilling pressure wrapping around his ribs... not painful, but intensely snug, as if dozens of cool, soothing crimson tendrils were weaving themselves seamlessly around his spiritual core, attuning their elemental frequencies to his own.
The pressure eased, melting into a warm comfortable hum that settled just beneath his heart.
[Ding!
Spirit Contract successfully established!]
[Congratulations, Lord Silas Graves!
You have formed a Bond with a Higher Elemental Spirit (Fire/Earth Variant)!]
POP!
With a soft, cheerful sound of displaced air, the spirit emerged from Silas’s sternum.
It floated in front of his face, looking largely identical to its previous form... a fist-sized sphere of radiant crimson light but there was an unmistakable shift in its aura.
Microscopic flecks of pure gold now drifted lazily within the ruby sphere which was a permanent mark of Silas’s core.
The spirit spun in a joyful celebratory circle, letting out a series of musical, chiming hums that sounded like tiny silver bells ringing in the wind.
Silas laughed, raising a finger to let the spirit rub its warm surface against his knuckle.
"Alright, if we’re partners now, you need a proper name," Silas mused, tapping his chin with his free hand.
"Can’t just call you ’the red orb.’ How about...
Cinder?"
The spirit spun violently to the left, letting out a flat dissonant bzzzt sound that clearly indicated disgust.
"Not a fan of Cinder?
Fair enough," Silas grinned.
"What about Pyro?"
Another sharp dismissive shake and the orb actually dimmed slightly, as if offended by the lack of creativity.
"Picky, aren’t you?" Silas chuckled.
He looked at the deep blood-red core of the spirit, remembering the ancient petrified crystal vines from which it had been born.
"How about...
Ignis?
Or...
Rubi?"
The spirit tilted slightly, considering it, but didn’t commit.
"Alright, one more," Silas said, his eyes gleaming.
"Kael-Drin...
It’s an old word for the sacred heart of the mountain fire."
The crimson orb froze.
Then, it flared with blinding ecstatic brilliance.

The tiny bell-like chiming resonated through the cavern, and the spirit began bouncing rapidly through the air, doing backflips around Silas’s head before settling happily on his right shoulder, nuzzling against his neck with a contented purr.
"Kael-Drin it is," Silas smiled, thoroughly amused. ’Proud little creature...
It likes things that sound grand and ancient, huh?’
With the contract settled, Silas turned back toward the narrow passage, his newly bound companion riding securely on his shoulder.
"Come on, Kael-Drin," Silas said.
"Let’s introduce you to the rest of the crew."
When Silas stepped back into the sunken depression of the diamond grove, the women were still hard at work with their pickaxes chiming against the rock face.
"Lord Silas is back!" Brenda called out, turning around with a bright smile.
Then, her eyes widened, locking onto the glowing red orb resting comfortably on his shoulder.
"Wait... what is that?!" Sarah gasped, lowering her chisel.
"Is that a spirit?!" Helen asked, taking a step forward with wide, curious eyes.
Silas chuckled, reaching up to gently tap the side of the sphere.
"Girls, meet Kael-Drin.
It seems our mining operation attracted a little local resident...
We just formalized a Spirit Contract."
"A Spirit Contract?!" Thora’s jaw dropped, her soot-stained face cycling through pure shock before morphing into deep dwarven respect.
"My Lord, you walked out to dump a load of rocks and came back with a contracted Higher Spirit?!
Do you just trip over legendary blessings in your sleep?!"
Thor marched over, her heavy footsteps shaking the limestone, and bent her towering frame down until her face was barely six inches from the floating orb.
"Oho!" Thor boomed, her storm-blue eyes sparkling with delight as she poked a calloused finger toward the spirit.
"A fiery little spark, aren’t you!
You’ve got good spirit in your core, little one!
Serve our Lord well, and I won’t eat you for breakfast!"
Kael-Drin didn’t cower.
Instead, it flared its light brightly, letting out an indignant high-pitched chirp right into the thunder god’s face, completely unintimidated.
Thor threw her head back, roaring with boisterous laughter.
"GWAHAHAHA!
I like this one!
It has the heart of a berserker!"
The recruit maidens quickly gathered around, cooing and admiring the spirit’s radiant ruby glow.
The Princess reached out with delicate tentative fingers, giggling with pure delight as Kael-Drin gently brushed against her palm with its cool smooth tendrils.
"Alright, back to business," Silas announced, stepping into the center of the grove.

He stomped his boot once more, calling upon his earth magic to raise a massive wide stone crate from the bedrock... twice the size of the previous one, easily capable of holding the entirety of the remaining harvest.
"Let’s finish stripping this shelf," Silas ordered, hoisting his pickaxe.
"We have daylight burning outside."
The women returned to the rock walls with renewed energized cheer.
Kael-Drin, eager to prove its worth to its new master, floated over to where Thora was working.
"What are you looking at, little spark?" Thora asked, wiping sweat from her brow as she held her heavy runic pickaxe.
Kael-Drin drifted down, extending two translucent red mana tendrils toward the tool.
The spirit gave the wooden handle an insistent tug, chiming softly as if demanding to hold the implement.
Thora’s face softened, a rare motherly grin breaking across her rough dwarven features.
"Oh, aren’t you precious!
You want to carry Master Thora’s pickaxe?
You’re too small for this, little one, but go on... show me what you’ve got!"
Chuckling, Thora handed the heavy steel tool over.
Kael-Drin didn’t try to lift the heavy iron with physical force.
Instead, it wrapped four thick dense tendrils of solidified ruby mana tightly around the shaft, effortlessly hoisting the twenty-pound pickaxe into the air!
"Well, look at that!" Thora beamed proudly, crossing her arms.
"Stronger than you look—"
KRA-WHACK!
Kael-Drin didn’t measure six inches outside the bleed-line and it didn’t snap its wrists either.

Carried away by pure elemental enthusiasm, the spirit raised the pickaxe high overhead and slammed the steel spike dead-center into a protruding cluster of blood-red crystal vines with the concussive force of an explosive shell.
KRA-BOOOOOOOOM!
A massive chunk of the wall... roughly ten feet wide violently fractured.
Slabs of limestone peeled away in a massive cascade, exposing a breathtaking haul of raw diamonds.
...Along with roughly thirty percent of the precious crystal vines, which instantly destabilized and shattered into a cloud of sparkling worthless red powder that rained down over Thora’s boots.
Dead silence descended over the corner.
Kael-Drin hovered proudly in the air, pickaxe still raised, chiming happily as if expecting a gold medal.
Thora stood completely frozen.
Her pale face slowly transitioned from dwarven pride into a shade of volcanic purple that rivaled the deep-earth magma.
Her amber eyes bulged from their sockets, her fists shaking with such violent fury that her leather straps groaned.
"YOU...
YOU LITTLE..." Thora’s voice strangled in her throat, her chest heaving as she fought the most agonizing internal battle of her entire life.
Every dwarven instinct screamed at her to roar at the top of her lungs, invoke a generational blood-curse, and punt the spirit across the cavern.
But as her eyes locked onto the innocent happily pulsing orb, she physically bit her lower lip, swallowing the scream until tears of pure, suppressed rage welled in the corners of her eyes.
Vala stepped out from the shadows beside her, reaching out and gently patting the trembling dwarf on the shoulder with a calm, comforting gesture.
"Breathe, Master Thora," Vala murmured soothingly.
"It is a child.
It knows not what it broke."
I am calm..." Thora wheezed through clenched teeth, her eye twitching uncontrollably.
"I am... an ocean of dwarven tranquility...
Lord Silas, take your damn spark back before I forge it into a chamber pot!"
Silas quickly whistled, and Kael-Drin obediently floated over, relinquishing the pickaxe and settling contritely on his shoulder, seemingly sensing that it had crossed a very dangerous line.
The rest of the extraction went smoothly.

With everyone working in disciplined unison, the girls salvaged the remaining intact veins, carefully prying the white diamonds and crimson vines free until the entire sunken depression including the high formations clinging to the thirty-foot ceiling was completely stripped clean.
Every single scrap of the harvest was loaded into Silas’s massive stone crate, filling the container to its brim.
Silas wiped his brow, leaning against his pickaxe.
"Alright.
That’s the entire grove cleared.
Now... we just have to figure out how to haul this two-ton block out to the golem."
Thor stepped forward, cracking her knuckles with a confident, boisterous grin.
"Leave it to me, Lord Silas!" Thor declared.
"I shall simply take the crate and teleport aboard the Titan Golem’s back!"
Silas blinked and Thora froze too.
The other women stared at her in stunned silence.
"You... you can teleport?" Silas asked, his voice deadpan.
Thor blinked her storm-blue eyes, looking at him as if he had just asked if the sky was blue.
"Yes?" Thor replied innocently.
"I am the God of Thunder.
The lightning rides the atmospheric currents... it strikes where it wills.
Did you think I merely walked everywhere because I enjoyed the exercise?"
Before anyone could utter a single word of protest, Thor leaned down, hooked her massive muscular arms beneath the two-ton stone crate, and hoisted it effortlessly against her chest.
KRA-FLASH!
A deafening arc of brilliant blue lightning detonated in the center of the depression, smelling of scorched ozone.
When the light cleared, Thor and the two-ton crate had completely vanished from the room.
Silence stretched across the cavern.
"She... she could have just teleported the crates the entire bloody time?" Thora whispered, her voice cracking with existential exhaustion.
From the ranks, young Brenda tentatively raised her hand, breaking the silence with a soft thoughtful question.
Master Thora?" Brenda asked innocently.
"Since we harvested all of these crystals... how long will it take for them to grow back?
Can we come back next month?"
A chorus of soft good-natured chuckles rippled through the older veterans.
Thora slowly turned her head, fixing the freckled recruit with a flat unblinking dwarven stare.
"Crystals are not cabbages, lass," Thora stated plainly.
"A high-density Mana Diamond vein takes roughly four to six centuries of subterranean tectonic compression and stagnant spiritual pressure to crystallize into physical ore..."
Brenda’s eyes widened.
"Four... four hundred years?!"
"Aye," Thora sighed, turning toward the tunnel.
"Which means you’re dumb for asking.
Now grab your packs and move your boots!"

chapters.title: Chapter 490: The Bust... Goddess?
paragraphs: The squad packed up their tools, laughing and teasing Brenda as they filed out of the sunken grove, making their way back through the winding limestone passage.
When they emerged into the wide dome of the former goblin hollow, Thor was already standing proudly atop the back of the Phase 1 Titan Golem.
She had dumped the massive haul of red crystals and white diamonds into the other transport bin, effortlessly tossing the heavy stone crate to the side.
Silas snapped his fingers, and before the crate could shatter against the ground, his earth magic dissolved the structure back into harmless gravel dust.
Thor leaped down from the golem, landing with a light triumphant thud.
She strode up to Silas, wiping a speck of chalk from her cheek with a wide toothy grin.
"The payload is secured, Lord Silas! Hehe~" Thor announced proudly.
Silas looked up at the towering demigoddess, offering her a genuine appreciative smile.
"Incredible work, Thor. Truly. When we get back to Blessed Land, I am personally ordering Kaelia to prepare an entire roasted ox just for you. As much meat and stout as your stomach can hold..."
Thor’s face lit up with radiant joy.
"GWAHAHAHA! You are a king among men, Silas!"
She reached out with an affectionate hand and gave him two heavy, affectionate pats on the head, ruffling his dark hair as if he were a favored younger brother.
Standing barely two paces away, the Princess instantly puffed out her cheeks, crossing her arms over her chest with a quiet indignant huff as she glared up at the blonde giantess.
Thor noticed the pout immediately.

"And a pat for our brave royal princess as well!" Thor laughed, reaching down and giving the Princess a gentle affectionate ruffle on her azure hair, which instantly broke the girl’s pout into a flustered embarrassed giggle.
"Hehehe~ You didn’t have to~"
Silas chuckled, turning toward the mouth of the cavern. "Alright, everyone. The titan is fully loaded so let’s head to the surface."
Thora stepped up to the resting Phase 1 Titan Golem, pulling a small brass control rod from her belt and tapping the chassis’s primary rune matrix.
"Phase One Titan, engage transport mobility!" Thora commanded. "Compact terrain mode! Slither protocol!"
WHIRRRR-CLANG-HISS!
The colossal construct stirred, venting a thick plume of steam from its lower conduits.
Instead of rising onto its four massive, knee-jointed legs, the golem’s chassis folded inward.

The heavy basalt plates shifted on ball-and-socket hydraulic tracks, tucking its limbs flat against its undercarriage as the central alloy spine lengthened and loosened, transforming the rigid four-legged siege engine into a dense serpent-like stone train.

Without legs to catch on the narrow limestone walls, the golem began to smoothly slither across the cavern floor, navigating the tight, twisting curves of the upward trail with shocking frictionless agility.
Within twenty minutes, the expedition group emerged from the jagged limestone maw of Cavern KB-22, stepping back out into the open air of the Umbral Basin.
The sub-zero blizzard from earlier had completely died down, leaving behind a crisp bitterly cold stillness.
The iron-gray sky hung heavy over the jagged shale ridges, and the surrounding terrain was a rugged expanse of black frost and broken volcanic rock.
Silas pulled his fur mantle tighter around his shoulders, his blue eyes scanning the jagged horizon to the north.
"The payload from KB-22 is massive," Silas noted, checking his mental map. "How about we hit that Spider’s Lair on the northern ridge before sunset? We still have a few hours of operational light..."
Thora immediately raised both hands, shaking her head vigorously.
"Out of the question, my Lord!" Thora declared firmly, pointing up at the golem.
The construct had expanded back into its standard four-legged posture, standing tall among the jagged rocks.
Thora scrambled up the side mounting rungs with practiced dwarven agility, grabbing the heavy reinforced leather tie-down straps bolted along the rim of the central transport bins.

With sharp muscular pulls, she hauled the heavy webbing across the glittering mounds of Mana Diamonds and red crystal vines, ratcheting the iron buckles down with a series of thunderous metallic clacks.

"Look at this chassis!" Thora shouted down from the golem’s back, patting the bulging leather straps. "These bins are filled to the brim! If you try to stack another five hundred pounds of raw ore on this construct, the suspension will grind against the axles! Not to mention, if we get ambushed by a pack of high-tier basin beasts on the march, we won’t be able to maneuver without risking half the haul spilling across the snow!"
She hopped down to the ground, landing with a solid thud.

"We head back to the Sovereign Distribution Nexus right now," Thora urged, wiping soot from her forehead. "We offload the payload, let the automated sorting conduits catalog the diamonds, and give the girls a hot meal... Greed on the return march is how miners end up dead, Lord Silas."
Silas looked at the bulging bins, then down at the exhausted women before nodding in agreement.
"You’re right," Silas conceded smoothly. "Logistics comes first. We head back to Blessed—"
RUSTLE!
The words died in Silas’s throat.
Barely thirty yards to their right, nestled near the edge of a snow-choked volcanic ridge, a dense thicket of deadwood pine suddenly rustled violently.
’Hostile?!’
Silas’s hand blurred with his fingers instantly locking around the hilt of his golden sword.
Beside him, Aurelia’s eyes sharpened as a faint halo of Argent Flame flickering to life at her fingertips.
Vala slipped half into the shadows, her void-iron sword drawn in a reverse grip, while Thor casually rested a hand on her belt, her storm-blue eyes narrowing into predatory slits.
FLAP-FLAP-FLAP.
From the swaying deadwood branches, a solitary, desperate shape broke through the freezing mist.
...It was a bird?
The creature was roughly the size of a mountain hawk, but its feathers were completely devoid of natural color, resembling dull shards of chipped obsidian.
It possessed an unnervingly long scythe-curved beak that looked wicked enough to shear through leather, and its beady black eyes were wide with pure terror.
The bird looked like it had been dragged through seven layers of hell.

Its plumage was ragged, crooked, and caked in frozen slush as several of its primary wing feathers were bent at agonizing angles, and its tailfeathers looked as though they had been singed by a high-altitude atmospheric explosion.
And clutched desperately within its iron-black talons was a large, perfectly flat, rectangular tablet of smooth gray slate.
FLAP... FLAP... FLUTTER!
The obsidian avian flew toward them with agonizing pathetic slowness.
Its hollow chest heaved, whistling with desperate breaths as it fought the freezing mountain drafts, its wings barely generating enough lift to keep it airborne.
As it closed the distance, the bird’s beady eyes locked onto Silas.
The Lord stood tall, draped in black furs and leather with his hand resting on a blade of pure radiant gold and his Gold Core humming with terrifying pressure.
Beside him stood the Saintess, a woman who was really strong, and an immortal God of Thunder who looked capable of swatting dragons out of the sky with a wooden spoon.
The bird’s hollow bones vibrated in paralyzing dread.

’He is going to cleave me in half,’ the bird thought in pure shrieking panic, its scythe-beak clicking erratically. ’He is going to draw that golden sword and turn me into a cloud of black feathers before my claws even touch the dirt!’
Yet, remembering the terrifying image of its frozen mistress spitting saliva craters into bedrock, the terrified avian forced its crooked wings to beat one last time.
FLUTTER-THUD!
The bird dropped out of the sky, tumbling clumsily onto the snow barely three paces in front of Silas’s boots.
It skidded across the frozen shale, ruffling its battered feathers, and immediately dropped onto its belly.

With a trembling desperate motion, the bird shoved the flat stone tablet forward across the snow, tapping the rock twice with its scythe-curved beak before bowing its crested head flat against the permafrost in an unmistakable gesture of terrified desperate supplication.
"Squawk..." the bird wheezed weakly, trembling in the cold. "Krrr-caw..."
Silas didn’t draw his sword.
He stood frozen with his hand still resting on the golden crossguard, blinking down at the shivering battered avian in complete and utter bewilderment.
Behind him, Thor tilted her head, squinting at the creature. "Is that dinner? It looks a bit stringy, but with enough mustard—"
"Quiet, Thor," Silas muttered, slowly lowering his hand from his blade.
"Lord Silas, be careful," Aurelia warned softly, stepping up beside him, her golden eyes analyzing the stone. "It carries no corrupt mana, but its origin is strange..."
"It’s just a bird," Silas said quietly.
He took two slow cautious steps forward, crunching through the snow as he knelt down on one knee before the prostrated creature.
The bird flinched, pulling its scythe-beak tight against its chest, but it didn’t flee.
Silas reached down, his leather-gloved fingers wrapping around the edges of the flat slate tablet.
He lifted the heavy stone from the snow, turning it over in his hands.
"Oh?" Silas muttered, his dark eyebrows creeping upward in surprise.
The surface of the stone wasn’t blank.
Crude and jaggedly carved into the smooth slate... clearly etched using the tip of a razor-sharp rock were distinct legible letters written in English.
Silas squinted, tilting the slate toward the dim daylight, his lips moving as he read the opening line carved into the stone.
"Dear Lord of Blessed Land... from the B... Bust Goddess...?"
Silas stopped and he blinked.
He stared at the tablet, his mind grinding to a violent screeching halt.
’...The what?’ Silas thought, his eye twitching as he looked from the stone tablet down to the shivering prostrate obsidian bird waiting desperately in the snow.

"Wait, what?" Brenda blurted from six paces back, her ash-wood spear drooping toward her boots as her freckled nose scrunched up. "A bust goddess? Like... a broken statue? Or... a woman who’s remarkably—"
"Quiet, Brenda," Helen hissed, nudging the younger recruit’s ribcage with an iron-banded elbow, though Helen’s own eyes were darting toward the slate with shameless curiosity.
The bird frantically hopped upright, flapping its ragged, singed wings in a frantic frenzy.
"Squawk! Caw-caw-caw! Krrr-clack!"
It launched into an erratic frantic routine, hopping from talon to talon in the snow before violently jabbing its wicked, hooked beak down toward the edge of the slate tablet.

It pecked the rock three times with sharp metallic dinks, then threw its head back, pointed its wing toward the vast jagged expanse of the northern peaks, and made an exaggerated panting sound while dragging its beak sideways through the slush.
Silas blinked.
He ran a calloused thumb over the jagged indentations, tracing the groove that looked less like a scripted alphabet and more like a series of violent gouges carved by desperate madness.
"Wait," Silas said slowly, leaning closer. "This doesn’t say ’Bust.’ The horizontal stroke cuts clean through the middle loop, and the bottom tail dragged outward across the grain. It says... Beast."
"Squawk!" The bird’s beady black eyes widened with tearful validation.
It nodded its crested head so violently its skull blurred, letting out an affirmative rattle that sounded like dry river stones bouncing down a copper chute.
"The Goddess of Beasts," Silas read, piecing the mangled letters together.
He tilted the stone toward the light once more, but the rest of the text was a disaster.

The lettering degraded rapidly after the greeting, turning into erratic jagged zig-zags that slashed violently across the slate, overlapping each other until the lines looked like the seismograph of an earthquake.

"How was this even written?" Silas asked, genuinely baffled, glancing from the tablet down to the ragged avian. "It looks like someone took a railroad spike, held it in a mechanical vice, and violently dragged it across the surface with an unstable drill... There’s no structural syntax here at all as half these vowels are just straight gouges."
He scanned the middle section, his vision filtering through the messy grooves.

Most of it was an unreadable smear of pulverized slate dust, but two words near the lower third had been gouged into the stone with such terrifying force that the bedrock had fractured around their margins.
TRAPPED.
And right beneath it, carved four times larger than any other word on the tablet, encircled by three frantic crooked rings.
FOOD.
The word was so brutally defined that it looked as though it had been etched with tears and concentrated hunger.
"Trapped... and food," Silas murmured with his brow arching. "Those are the only two words that were carved with any deliberate legibility."

The creature was roughly the size of a mountain hawk, but its feathers were completely devoid of natural color, resembling dull shards of chipped obsidian.
It possessed an unnervingly long scythe-curved beak that looked wicked enough to shear through leather, and its beady black eyes were wide with pure terror.
The bird looked like it had been dragged through seven layers of hell.

Its plumage was ragged, crooked, and caked in frozen slush as several of its primary wing feathers were bent at agonizing angles, and its tailfeathers looked as though they had been singed by a high-altitude atmospheric explosion.
And clutched desperately within its iron-black talons was a large, perfectly flat, rectangular tablet of smooth gray slate.
FLAP...
FLAP...
FLUTTER!
The obsidian avian flew toward them with agonizing pathetic slowness.
Its hollow chest heaved, whistling with desperate breaths as it fought the freezing mountain drafts, its wings barely generating enough lift to keep it airborne.
As it closed the distance, the bird’s beady eyes locked onto Silas.
The Lord stood tall, draped in black furs and leather with his hand resting on a blade of pure radiant gold and his Gold Core humming with terrifying pressure.
Beside him stood the Saintess, a woman who was really strong, and an immortal God of Thunder who looked capable of swatting dragons out of the sky with a wooden spoon.
The bird’s hollow bones vibrated in paralyzing dread.

’He is going to cleave me in half,’ the bird thought in pure shrieking panic, its scythe-beak clicking erratically. ’He is going to draw that golden sword and turn me into a cloud of black feathers before my claws even touch the dirt!’
Yet, remembering the terrifying image of its frozen mistress spitting saliva craters into bedrock, the terrified avian forced its crooked wings to beat one last time.
FLUTTER-THUD!
The bird dropped out of the sky, tumbling clumsily onto the snow barely three paces in front of Silas’s boots.
It skidded across the frozen shale, ruffling its battered feathers, and immediately dropped onto its belly.

With a trembling desperate motion, the bird shoved the flat stone tablet forward across the snow, tapping the rock twice with its scythe-curved beak before bowing its crested head flat against the permafrost in an unmistakable gesture of terrified desperate supplication.
"Squawk..." the bird wheezed weakly, trembling in the cold.
"Krrr-caw..."
Silas didn’t draw his sword.
He stood frozen with his hand still resting on the golden crossguard, blinking down at the shivering battered avian in complete and utter bewilderment.
Behind him, Thor tilted her head, squinting at the creature.
"Is that dinner?
It looks a bit stringy, but with enough mustard—"
"Quiet, Thor," Silas muttered, slowly lowering his hand from his blade.
"Lord Silas, be careful," Aurelia warned softly, stepping up beside him, her golden eyes analyzing the stone.
"It carries no corrupt mana, but its origin is strange..."
"It’s just a bird," Silas said quietly.
He took two slow cautious steps forward, crunching through the snow as he knelt down on one knee before the prostrated creature.
The bird flinched, pulling its scythe-beak tight against its chest, but it didn’t flee.
Silas reached down, his leather-gloved fingers wrapping around the edges of the flat slate tablet.
He lifted the heavy stone from the snow, turning it over in his hands.
"Oh?" Silas muttered, his dark eyebrows creeping upward in surprise.
The surface of the stone wasn’t blank.
Crude and jaggedly carved into the smooth slate... clearly etched using the tip of a razor-sharp rock were distinct legible letters written in English.
Silas squinted, tilting the slate toward the dim daylight, his lips moving as he read the opening line carved into the stone.
"Dear Lord of Blessed Land... from the B...
Bust Goddess...?"
Silas stopped and he blinked.
He stared at the tablet, his mind grinding to a violent screeching halt.
’...The what?’ Silas thought, his eye twitching as he looked from the stone tablet down to the shivering prostrate obsidian bird waiting desperately in the snow.
"Wait, what?" Brenda blurted from six paces back, her ash-wood spear drooping toward her boots as her freckled nose scrunched up.
"A bust goddess?
Like... a broken statue?
Or... a woman who’s remarkably—"
"Quiet, Brenda," Helen hissed, nudging the younger recruit’s ribcage with an iron-banded elbow, though Helen’s own eyes were darting toward the slate with shameless curiosity.
The bird frantically hopped upright, flapping its ragged, singed wings in a frantic frenzy.
"Squawk!
Caw-caw-caw!
Krrr-clack!"
It launched into an erratic frantic routine, hopping from talon to talon in the snow before violently jabbing its wicked, hooked beak down toward the edge of the slate tablet.

It pecked the rock three times with sharp metallic dinks, then threw its head back, pointed its wing toward the vast jagged expanse of the northern peaks, and made an exaggerated panting sound while dragging its beak sideways through the slush.
Silas blinked.
He ran a calloused thumb over the jagged indentations, tracing the groove that looked less like a scripted alphabet and more like a series of violent gouges carved by desperate madness.
"Wait," Silas said slowly, leaning closer.
"This doesn’t say ’Bust.’ The horizontal stroke cuts clean through the middle loop, and the bottom tail dragged outward across the grain.
It says...
Beast."
"Squawk!" The bird’s beady black eyes widened with tearful validation.
It nodded its crested head so violently its skull blurred, letting out an affirmative rattle that sounded like dry river stones bouncing down a copper chute.
"The Goddess of Beasts," Silas read, piecing the mangled letters together.
He tilted the stone toward the light once more, but the rest of the text was a disaster.

The lettering degraded rapidly after the greeting, turning into erratic jagged zig-zags that slashed violently across the slate, overlapping each other until the lines looked like the seismograph of an earthquake.
"How was this even written?" Silas asked, genuinely baffled, glancing from the tablet down to the ragged avian.
"It looks like someone took a railroad spike, held it in a mechanical vice, and violently dragged it across the surface with an unstable drill...
There’s no structural syntax here at all as half these vowels are just straight gouges."
He scanned the middle section, his vision filtering through the messy grooves.

Most of it was an unreadable smear of pulverized slate dust, but two words near the lower third had been gouged into the stone with such terrifying force that the bedrock had fractured around their margins.
TRAPPED.
And right beneath it, carved four times larger than any other word on the tablet, encircled by three frantic crooked rings.
FOOD.
The word was so brutally defined that it looked as though it had been etched with tears and concentrated hunger.
"Trapped... and food," Silas murmured with his brow arching.
"Those are the only two words that were carved with any deliberate legibility."

chapters.title: Chapter 491: Straight Teeth
paragraphs: The bird looked Silas dead in the eye.
It slowly lowered its head, pinched its scythe-curved beak tight, and mimed an exaggerated biting motion around an imaginary chunk of shale.
It clamped its jaws, shook its head violently from side to side like a dog tearing through sinew, and dragged its beak across the slate, grinding its lower mandible in a scraping demonstration.
Behind them, Thora stepped up, leaning her weight against the broad shaft of her dwarven pickaxe.
The smith wiped a smudge of black soot from her cheek, squinting down at the bird’s theatrical performance with a calculating, sharp dwarven eye.

"Well, stone me sideways," Thora muttered, spitting a speck of grit into the snow. "Look at the angle of those fractures, my Lord. See how the impact points lean to the left, but the exit drags curve up and out? That wasn’t carved with hands as no set of fingers swings a chisel at that downward cant."
Silas’s blue eyes flicked from the slate to the bird, and then a sudden absurd realization clicked into place.
"She held the rock in her mouth," Silas stated, deadpan. "She was biting a sharp stone and violently whipping her neck around to gouge the letters into the slate..."
The bird froze mid-peck. It stared at Silas, slowly rose to its full height, and nodded its head in slow affirmation.
’Yes... Exactly...’
"She wrote a diplomatic plea for aid... with her teeth," Silas summarized, the unorthodoxy of the situation hanging in the freezing mountain air like a brick.
"Damn," Aurelia murmured, stepping up beside Silas’s shoulder as she folded her hands over her waist.
Her golden eyes analyzed the desperate, scratched stone with deep pity.
"To be reduced to carving scripture with one’s own jaws... whoever she is, her suffering must be immense."

"Aye, or she’s just completely lost her bloody mind," Thora snorted, resting her fists on her hips. "A goddess who writes with her mouth and demands roasted meat like a tavern drunk at closing time? Sounds like a handful... We’ve already got one blonde thunder-head who eats us out of house and home so we don’t need a feral dog-goddess gnawing on the furniture in the Keep."
"Hey!" Thor yelled from the back, her voice booming over the wind as she polished off the last scrap of dried salted mutton from her pouch.
"I heard that, little smith! The divine appetite is a sign of boundless vitality! A warrior who does not eat cannot shatter mountains!"
Silas ignored the bickering, his mind shifting into the cool gears that had kept him alive for so long as he looked down at the shivering battered obsidian bird.

"Listen to me, bird," Silas said, keeping his voice level, calm, and grounded. "I can barely read ten percent of this. The intent is clear enough... someone powerful is locked down and she needs a key to break the seal, and she’s starving too but I can’t just drop what I’m doing, mount a war-pack, and charge blind into that part of the Umbral Basin based on a handful of scratches on a rock. We are in the middle of a massive territorial mobilization as Blessed Land’s entire logistics pipeline is running right now."
The bird’s crested head drooped.
Its feathers sagged, its scythe-beak hovering an inch above the permafrost in crushing defeat.
It looked as though every ounce of life had been violently siphoned out of its hollow bones.

"However," Silas continued, tucking the heavy slate tablet securely beneath his left arm, "I’m not throwing the message away. If there really is an uncontracted Goddess of Beasts entombed in this basin, I want to meet her."
His blue eyes sharpened with ambition gleaming within his pupils.
A high-tier entity commanding authority over beasts, lingering directly within the Umbral Basin?

If she was an enemy, she was an existential threat that needed to be cataloged and neutralized before she thawed out but if she was willing to bend the knee... if she was desperate enough to offer herself as a Hero just for a warm hearth and roasted meat then the strategic value to Blessed Land was immeasurable.

His cavalry corps was expanding, the Umbral Basin was infested with wild monsters, and a Beast Goddess could turn the entire natural ecosystem of the northern territory into an unassailable defensive bulwark.

"If you want this tablet back, you can take it," Silas offered, gesturing with his chin toward the stone. "Or... you can come with us. Fly south to the walls of Blessed Land and once we reach the Keep as wel as offload the mining haul, I’ll have Eluned sit down with you. She’s a Goddess herself so she understands the language of nature, plants, and beasts far better than I could ever... She can translate every single squawk in your throat and tell me exactly where your mistress is pinned."
The bird looked up as its beady black eyes blinked once and then twice.
Then, it let out a sharp chirp that sounded like a rusty latch snapping open.
It flapped its ragged wings, launching itself three feet into the air, hovering eagerly against the freezing breeze.
"Good," Silas said, nodding smoothly.

He raised his right arm, extending his forearm outward in a firm horizontal perch with the dark leather of his vambrace offering a broad stable platform... It was the classic stance of a falconer calling in a royal hunting hawk.
He kept his posture relaxed and effortlessly cool.
"Come on. Land."
The bird hovered, its wings beating rapidly against the snow as it looked at the extended leather arm then, its gaze slowly drifted upward, locking onto Silas’s face.
From the bird’s perspective, Silas did not look like a comfortable wooden perch.
Beneath his dark hair, Silas’s piercing blue eyes were narrowed in that intense look that never truly left him even if he smiled.
His Mythic Gold Core hummed with a suffocating weight that distorted the atmospheric pressure around his shoulders.

To the tiny hyper-sensitive avian creature, looking at Silas’s outstretched hand was like looking directly down the throat of an ancient golden dragon that was casually baring a double-row of serrated fangs, waiting for an excuse to snap its jaws shut.

It had spent the entirety of its life savings in pure courage just to land that stone tablet at his boots so it was not about to push its luck by sitting within arm’s reach of those dangerous Gold-Core-reinforced fingers.
Its gaze flicked frantically across the gathered group.
Aurelia? No...𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝚠𝕖𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝕖𝚕.𝚌𝗼𝗺
The Saintess was surrounded by an invisible suffocating shimmer of pure Argent Flame that smelled of divine incineration.
Vala? Absolutely not... and as for Thor? That was suicide! The blonde giant was still licking grease from her lips and eyeing its tailfeathers like a skewered appetizer.
Thora as well as terrifying. The dwarf was clutching an oversized wrench and glaring at it with deep suspicion.
Then, the bird’s eyes landed on the Princess.
The blue-haired royal woman was standing near the flank of her Blessed Wolf with her hands tucked neatly into the fur-lined cuffs of her winter mantle.
She looked soft, harmless, and remarkably pretty as her azure eyes were wide and sparkling with innocent girlish fascination the more she watched the ragged creature.
SWOOSH!

The bird banked violently to the right! It completely ignored Silas’s outstretched leather arm, dove through the freezing air like an obsidian stone, and flared its wings at the last second, coming down to make a neat delicate landing dead-center atop the Princess’s royal head.
FLUMP!
Its dark talons tangled gently into her soft azure locks.

The bird puffed out its chest, tucked its scythe-beak down against its throat, and closed its eyes, trembling with relief as it nestled comfortably into her thick, fragrant hair like an oversized nest.
"Eep!" The Princess gasped softly, her shoulders hitching upward as her face flushed a brilliant adorable crimson.
She raised two delicate gloved hands, gently patting the side of the bird’s ragged feathers.

"Oh... goodness," the Princess giggled, her blue eyes fluttering with delight as the bird let out a contented clicking sound against her crown. "It... it’s remarkably light! It feels like a little woolen hat!"
Thor leaned her massive frame forward, squinting at the bird with genuine wide-eyed amusement, letting out a booming chuckle that rattled the shale.
"Gwahaha! Well look at that! The feathered runt knows quality when it sees it! That’s a royal throne, you scruffy little parasite!"
Silas stood frozen.
His right arm remained extended horizontally in the freezing air, stiff as an iron rod and completely empty.
A gust of bitterly cold wind howled across the rocky plateau, carrying a flurry of pale snow that dusted the dark leather of his empty vambrace.
Slowly, Silas lowered his arm.
He brought his fingers together, casually brushing a speck of nonexistent dirt from the cuff of his mining tunic as his face was set in a rigid deadpan expression.

"Ahem," Silas cleared his throat, subtly rolling his shoulders as if he had intended to stretch his muscles the entire time. "Yes, naturally. The avian recognizes royal diplomacy so that’s a sound decision."
Thor didn’t let him have the victory for even half a second.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHA!"
The God of Thunder threw her head back, slapping her leather-clad thigh with enough concussive force to blast the snow away from her boots!

"Did you see that?!" Thor roared with tearful breathless glee, pointing a thick finger straight at Silas’s face. "The great Lord Of Blessed Land! Finessed! Utterly rejected by a half-starved crow! It looked at your hand, looked at your ugly scowl, and chose the soft blue hair of a maiden instead! Oh, by Odin’s beard, that is magnificent!"
A chorus of muffled trembling snickers instantly rippled through the ranks of the women.

Brenda turned her face toward the limestone cliff, biting her lip so hard it turned white, while Sarah and Helen aggressively cleared their throats, their shoulders violently shaking with suppressed laughter.
Aurelia lowered her chin with a soft graceful smile tugging at the corners of her lips as her golden eyes danced with amusement.
Silas let out a slow long-suffering sigh, closing his eyes against the cold.
’I am surrounded by comedians,’ Silas thought, though a wry smirk tugged at his mouth despite himself.
FZZT.
From the collar of his tunic, a soft crimson glow flared. Kael-Drin, the newly contracted Higher Spirit, floated upward until it hovered directly beside Silas’s left ear.

The little ruby orb pulsed brightly, chiming with an indignant defensive sequence of silver-bell tones, puffing out tiny waves of comforting warmth against Silas’s cheek as if declaring that it would never reject its master.
Silas reached up, gently tapping the side of the glowing red sphere with a gloved knuckle.
"At least someone here respects the territorial hierarchy. Good boy, Kael-Drin."
"Alright, that’s enough clowning around!" Silas commanded, raising his voice over the rising gale.
He brought two fingers to his lips and loosed a sharp piercing whistle that cut cleanly through the freezing drafts of the basin.
HOWOOOOOOOOOL!
From the jagged shale outcrops lining the perimeter of Cavern KB-22, a chorus of powerful howls answered.
Pounding across the frozen drifts with terrifying coordinated speed came the pack.
Leading the vanguard was Valkyrie, her wolf frame moving with majestic grace and her golden harness humming softly against her broad chest.
Behind her bounded the rest of the Blessed Wolves, their dense coats shaking off the accumulating frost as they fanned out in a clean disciplined perimeter around the squad.
The recruit maidens immediately moved toward their mounts, checking the tension of the girth-straps and securing their tool-sacks.
Thor, however, did not have a mount.
The God of Thunder didn’t even look at the wolves as she stepped into an open patch of clear bedrock, cracking her neck from left to right with a succession of violent deafening snaps.
Her storm-blue eyes ignited with a crackling blaze of sapphire lightning, and the air around her sculpted frame began to violently distort with raw ozone.
"Racing you back to the Keep, Silas!" Thor bellowed, her wild blonde locks whipping into a frenzy as arcs of blue static danced across her bare shoulders.
She grinned, pointing a thick finger toward Thora.
"First one through the main gates of Blessed Land takes every single keg of dark dwarven stout in the royal cellars! No limits! No bans! Winner takes all!"
"WHAT?!" Thora shrieked with her wrench flying into the air as her face turned volcanic purple. "YOU CANNOT BET MY CELLARS, YOU OVERGROWN LEAF-BRAINED BLONDE—"
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

No bans!
Winner takes all!"
"WHAT?!" Thora shrieked with her wrench flying into the air as her face turned volcanic purple.
"YOU CANNOT BET MY CELLARS, YOU OVERGROWN LEAF-BRAINED BLONDE—"
KRA-BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 492: It Was Never A Competition
paragraphs: Thor didn’t wait for the protest as she simply detonated forward.
With an apocalyptic roar of atmospheric displacement that violently shattered the sound barrier, a blinding pillar of sapphire lightning blasted downward from the gray heavens.
The concussive sonic boom blasted the snow away in a three-hundred-foot circular shockwave, knocking several women to their knees and sending loose boulders tumbling down the cliff face.
ZOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!

Like a celestial artillery shell fired from the gods, a brilliant blinding streak of golden-blue light tore across the sky, shrieking southward toward the distant horizons of Blessed Land at hypersonic velocity, leaving behind a glowing scar that sizzled in the freezing clouds.

"THAT WAS NOT EVEN A COMPETITION!" Thora screamed at the top of her lungs, shaking her fist at the empty sky, her soot-stained cheeks trembling with pure dwarven outrage. "THAT’S CHEATING! SHE USED CELESTIAL VELOCITY AGAINST QUADRUPED MOUNTS! SOMEONE SHOOT HER OUT OF THE SKY!"
Silas shook his head, dusting the fresh layer of churned snow from his shoulders as he vaulted smoothly into Valkyrie’s saddle.
"Mount up!" Silas ordered, leaning forward as the dire wolf’s muscles coiled beneath him. "We have an entire titan golem to escort so move out!"
The women scrambled into their saddles.

The Princess held the pommel of her mount with one hand while keeping her other gloved hand cupped protectively over the top of her head, ensuring the trembling obsidian bird didn’t get blown away by the gale.
Thora scrambled onto the back of her own wolf, pulling the portable control tablet... a heavy slab of slate etched with intricate pulsing blue runes from her side satchel.
She aggressively tapped the central rune with her thumb.
"Phase One Titan, engage column escort!" Thora barked into the slate. "Match cavalry stride! Forward march!"
WHIRRRR-CLANG-HISS!
Behind them, the colossal four-legged stone titan rose to its full, staggering height.

Its massive bedrock limbs drove into the frozen earth with deep thuds that shook the valley, its reinforced alloy bins bulging with thousands of pounds of pristine Mana Diamonds and blood-red crystal vines.
As the construct took its first massive step forward, its central amber optic pulsed.
The glowing optical sensor slowly tilted downward, its mechanical lens locking dead-center onto the tiny obsidian bird perched atop the Princess’s head.
The bird froze.
Its scythe-beak clicked shut and its beady black eyes widened in paralyzing horror as it took in the twelve-foot-wide stone face of an ancient siege engine staring down at it like a god of judgment.
’It’s looking at me,’ the bird’s internal thoughts shrieked in gibbering panic. ’The mountain has eyes! The mountain is going to eat me!’

With a desperate flutter, the bird abandoned the Princess’s hair, diving downward and violently burrowing its entire head into the folds of the Princess’s wool-lined lap, pulling her heavy cloak over its wings and shivering like an autumn leaf.
The Princess blinked, gently patting the trembling lump beneath her mantle.
"Oh, my... that’s new. Don’t worry, little one. It doesn’t bite! It’s just stone!"
Back on her mount, Thora was violently tapping the runes on her slate, her face split into a dark cackle.

’Take that, you scruffy feathered little squawker...’ Thora cursed internally, adjusting the golem’s optical tracking to keep its glaring gaze locked directly on the shivering bird. ’Steal the Lord’s attention from my mining reports, will you? Stare at the rock, you overgrown crow!’
With a unified roar of paws hitting permafrost, the cavalry detachment surged forward, tearing through the jagged shale canyons of the Umbral Basin, racing south toward the safety of the territory.
The late afternoon had descended into an iron-gray, suffocating gloom.
The sub-zero blizzard that had battered the central crags earlier had not vanished, instead it had settled into a persistent squall.
Heavy, wet sheets of pale snow drifted laterally across the frozen flats, burying the jagged basalt ridges beneath a thick suffocating blanket of white.
Yet, on the wrists of every single officer and squad leader deployed across the basin, a metallic chime suddenly shattered the silence of the storm.
CHIME! CHIME! CHIME!
The brass-rimmed mechanical timers... mass-produced by Thora’s foundry and bound with precise runes vibrated violently against their gauntlets.
It was the final bell.
The midday mining window was officially closed.
All territorial units were under strict orders to cease extraction immediately and initiate full-scale withdrawal toward the primary gates of Blessed Land.
Barely a mile from the towering southern palisades, emerging from the jagged snow-choked mouth of a narrow canyon, was the joint detachment of Brida and Tasmin.
Riding abreast at the head of the column with their Blessed Wolves cutting parallel trenches through the three-foot snowdrifts, were the two commanders.
Behind them marched twenty battle-hardened maidens, their leather harnesses caked in chalky stone dust and their boots stained with black frost.
Trailing behind the cavalry, their mechanical limbs moving with steady discipline, were two Phase 2 Golems.
The four-legged stone constructs carried heavy alloy bins loaded to the brim with midnight-blue Star-Iron, dense Deep-Earth Alloy, and glittering veins of raw mythril.
A recruit riding on the left flank leaned over her mount’s neck, raising her left forearm to inspect the brass face of her watch.
"Captain Brida! Captain Tasmin!" the girl called out, her voice cutting through the whistling wind. "The operational window has expired! That’s the final bell!"
Brida grunted, pulling her wolf to a momentary halt at the crest of the snowy ridge.
She adjusted the massive thick-bladed Titan’s Cleaver strapped across her back, wiping a crust of frozen sweat from her jaw.
Her amber eyes swept backward, assessing the cargo bins.

After Silas had intercepted their petty domestic dispute in the geode and laid down the law, the two women had linked their squads and systematically assaulted the three assigned sectors... Sector Seven, Sector Eight, and the lower ridge of Nine.
They had mined at a furious punishing pace.
Brida’s side had muscled their picks through the dense Deep-Earth seams with raw terrifying physical power, logging a slightly higher tonnage from the lower caverns.
But Tasmin’s squad had countered with technique, carefully extracting the high-tier, constellation-flecked Star-Iron from Mine BVR Star without shattering a single crystal lattice.
When factoring in the original spoils from the shapeshifting wolf nest, the two ledgers were practically dead-even.
There was no clear victor as the prize was hanging precariously in the balance.
Tasmin pulled her wolf up alongside Brida, her breath rising in steady controlled plumes of white mist.
Her dark leather harness was pristine compared to Brida’s battered, ichor-stained plate, but her amber eyes burned with the exact same sharp intensity.

"Well, Brida," Tasmin drawled coolly, her gloved fingers lightly tapping the pommel of her sidearm. "The ledger is balanced so the dwarven clerks will spend half the night weighing the carats before they determine a difference of ounces."
Brida slowly turned her head. A wide wolfish smirk split across her rugged soot-stained face.

"Ounces are for merchants, Tas," Brida grinned, her crimson battle-aura beginning to hum and crackle beneath the surface of her breastplate like a waking volcano. "Frontline warriors settle the score with their boots."
She pointed a heavy gauntlet straight through the falling snow.
A mile down the long sloping valley of frozen shale, the palisades of Blessed Land rose against the winter sky like an unassailable fortress.
The massive primary gates stood wide open, illuminated by the warm flickering orange glow of torches.

"First one through the timber threshold," Brida challenged, her voice booming with competitive fire. "Takes the reward... The winner gets his private quarters tonight and the loser sits in the mess hall and washes the grease off the soup kettles."
Tasmin didn’t even blink.
"You’re on, you overgrown battering ram."
BOOM!

The snow beneath their mounts exploded as both Blessed Wolves surged forward simultaneously, their muscular hindquarters driving into the permafrost with enough power to blast two twenty-foot roostertails of pulverized slush into the freezing air.
"FOLLOW THE CAPTAINS!" A woman roared from the ranks behind.
The entire twenty-woman column exploded into a dead sprint, their wolf mounts bounding through the drifts in a thundering charge.
Behind them, the two Phase 2 Golems locked their hydraulic joints, their stone pads pounding against the bedrock in rolling mechanical movements as they chased the racing cavalry.
Down the long, descending slope of the valley, Brida and Tasmin transformed the race into a fight.
"GET OUT OF MY WAY!" Brida roared.
She didn’t reach for her cleaver, Brida unhooked the heavy rune-forged buckler from her left arm and slammed it horizontally through the air.
FWOOM!

A concussive shockwave of dense red mana detonated from the rim of the shield, blasting across the five-yard gap between their mounts like a solid wall of force, meant to knock Tasmin’s wolf off balance.
SHSHSHK!
Tasmin didn’t even try to brace it.
"Predictable!" Tasmin hissed!
With a single, effortless thought, Tasmin engaged her Shadow-Submersion Drift.
Her physical body, her armor, and her massive dire wolf mount instantly dissolved, flattening into a wide two-dimensional sheet of liquid blackness that slipped beneath the snow.
The crimson shockwave screamed harmlessly over her head, obliterating a snowdrift twenty yards to the right!𝙛𝒓𝒆𝙚𝒘𝒆𝓫𝙣𝓸𝙫𝓮𝒍.𝒄𝒐𝓶
A fraction of a second later, the shadow shot forward across the frictionless permafrost, snapping back into three-dimensional reality five yards ahead of Brida.
"Eat my snow, ox!" Tasmin yelled, glancing over her shoulder with a mocking smirk!
"NOT ON YOUR LIFE!"
Brida roared, channeling her mana directly into her mount’s silver-inlaid harness. Her wolf surged with sudden explosive speed, its heavy jaws snapping at the air as it closed the gap!
As she pulled level, Brida dropped her shoulder, leaning out of the stirrups to drive her heavy steel-plated elbow straight toward Tasmin’s ribs in a brutal bone-jarring check.
CLINK-CLANK-WHIP!
Tasmin’s left hand blurred... Her weighted void-chains shot out from beneath her cloak, wrapping like striking vipers around Brida’s forearm.
Tasmin violently pulled back, using Brida’s own forward momentum to pivot as she planted her boot against the rim of Brida’s saddle, leaping into the air in a breathtaking acrobatic spin.
Her twin void-daggers flashed in reverse grips, the flat spines of the blades slapping against Brida’s heavy pauldrons with a sequence of deafening metallic clangs.
"Your balance is sloppy, Brida!" Tasmin mocked, vaulting cleanly back onto her own saddle without losing a single yard of ground.
"My balance is fine, you slippery flea!" Brida hollered, wrenching her arm free with a savage tug that snapped the dark chains back into Tasmin’s sleeve.
Across the wide valley floor, other mining detachments were converging on the gates as well.

Small squads of ten-woman harvesting teams, and supply carts were funneling down the mountain tracks, watching the two commanders tear down the center of the valley like a hurricane of red energy and black shadow.
The massive gates of Blessed Land were barely three hundred yards away.
Brida lowered her center of gravity, her eyes blazing with competitive madness as the runes on her boots ignited.
Tasmin leaned over her wolf’s neck with the liquid shadows pooling beneath its paws to eliminate all friction, preparing for the final sprint—
RUMBLE... KRA-CRUNCH!
The earth beneath the center of the valley suddenly groaned with an unfathomable seismic shudder.
"What the—" Brida’s jaw tightened.
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
From the deep bedrock directly between their mounts, the frozen earth violently ruptured outward in an explosion of pulverized shale, ice, and rich soil.
Shooting out of the ground like a colossal, breaching leviathan was a massive glowing emerald root.
The root was as thick as a watchtower, covered in smooth, moss-green bark that pulsed with green mana.
It surged forward through the air, arching over the snowdrifts like a living organic bridge, moving with the frictionless velocity of a high-speed mag-train.
And riding comfortably atop the highest curve of the massive emerald root, leaning gracefully against her wooden staff with her emerald robes billowing in the wind, was Goddess Eluned.
Surrounding the serene goddess were the women, all lounging comfortably atop the living wood and their boots dangling over the edge as if they were riding a pleasure barge down a summer river.
’Fucking hell...’
Lashed securely to the rear section of the root, resting safely within a cradle of woven branches, was an entire Phase 1 Titan Golem, its bins overflowing with gleaming slabs of virgin alloy.
Beside Eluned, Morwenna was holding onto a thick vine with one hand with her hair swaying wildly in the gale as she looked down at Brida and Tasmin with a wide shit-eating grin.
Eluned turned her head, offering the two sprinting commanders a gentle wave of her slender fingers.

"Good afternoon, little sisters!" Eluned’s voice chimed with effortless magical amplification, ringing out like sweet bells over the howling blizzard. "My squad and I have had a most productive afternoon! Do mind the drifts... the snow is quite slippery on foot!"
