chapters.title: Chapter 493: The Nexus Does It’s Job
paragraphs: "BY THE GODS!" Tasmin shrieked in horror.
"SHE HAS A LIVING TRANSPORT?!" Brida roared, her eyes bulging out of her skull! "THAT IS AN UNFAIR USE OF MAGIC!"
SWOOOOOOOSH!
The massive emerald root shot straight over their heads, clearing the remaining two hundred yards in a single gliding leap.

It gracefully touched down right before the threshold of Blessed Land, setting the cheering girls and the colossal Titan Golem down onto the gravel outside with a soft rustling sigh, arriving at the boundary a full twenty seconds before anyone else.
SKRRRR-SLIDE!
Brida and Tasmin pulled their Blessed Wolves to a violent frantic halt outside the entrance with their mounts kicking up massive waves of slush as they skidded across the road.
"WE WERE ROBBED!" Brida screamed, throwing both hands into the air as she glared at the smiling goddess. "SHE DIDN’T EVEN USE LEGS! SHE RODE A VEGETABLE!"
"That is a clear violation of everything!" Tasmin hissed, jumping down from her saddle, her face pale with bitter burning resentment. "She bypassed the entire terrain!"
"Now, now, ladies! Calm yourselves! Lower your voices!"
Stepping out from the gatehouse into the falling snow were half a dozen stout dwarven officers, led by a dwarf named Boa.
The dwarves were bundled in heavy shearling coats, holding thick brass measuring calipers, ledger slates, and clipboards.

"You lot put on a hell of a show," Bodil grunted, waving her clipboard to usher the panting women into the outer yard. "Master Thora’s already inside the logistics hub... The Lord of Blessed Land has received the preliminary extraction manifests, and he’s thoroughly pleased with every single detachment."
The girls paused with their breathing heavy, looking at the dwarf with wide eager eyes.
"Is he coming out to see us?" Brenda asked, shivering slightly in the cold.

"Aye, eventually," Bodil chuckled, rolling her shoulders. "The Lord will personally receive and review every single squad to hand out your commendations and rewards. But... and he was very specific about this, he ordered that every single woman is to take a hot bath first."
The yard went completely silent.
The twenty women from Brida and Tasmin’s squad blinked and the girls from Eluned’s detachment stopped their cheering as well as the other arriving women.
Not a single woman looked offended.
Instead, a slow wave of rosy warmth began to creep across different female faces simultaneously.
’He... he wants us to bathe first?’
Their minds instantly raced with wild unholy interpretations.
Why would their Lord specifically demand that they wash off the stone dust, soak in hot water, and cleanse their skin before he received them in private?
"Well..." Sion murmured softly, her fingers nervously twisting a lock of sweat-matted hair that was dusted with gray limestone powder.
Her cheeks turned a brilliant adorable shade of scarlet. "I... I suppose I really am quite filthy. It would be terribly rude to stand before the Lord smelling like sulfur and monster guts."
"She’s right!" another woman gasped, her eyes shining with excited energy. "I have chalk all over my thighs! I need hot water! I need that scented jasmine soap too!"
"If he’s going to inspect us," Levia whispered, practically vibrating with nervous anticipation. "I’m scrubbing until my skin is glowing!"
A chorus of breathless eager giggles rippled through the gathered army of women.

The exhaustion of eight hours of brutal labor vanished in a flash, replaced by a mad chaotic scramble as the women began dismounting, checking their mirrors, and whispering furiously among themselves about bathhouse rotations and lavender oils.
Boa shook her head with a dry knowing smirk, stepping aside.
"Open the gates properly!" Boa shouted. "Let the wolves through to the Pavilion!"
The massive gates creaked inward.

The women, leading their panting Blessed Wolves by the reins, surged into the warm torchlit interior of Blessed Land, their laughter and excited chatter echoing off the stone walls as they rushed past the Spirit Trees and toward the territory’s bathouse.
Left behind in the wide outer staging yard, standing beside the towering stone walls, was the massive fleet of heavy transport constructs.

Dozens of Phase 1 Titan Golems and Phase 2 working units stood in neat disciplined rows, their chassis caked in snow and their massive alloy bins bulging with hundreds of tons of high-grade ores, Mana Diamonds, Star-Iron, virgin alloy... and so many more.
VUUUUUUUM!
A gentle shimmer of spatial mana resonated through the falling snow.
Materializing right in the center of the staging yard was Aeliana.
The high-elf hero stood tall and immaculate, her pristine golden hair cascading down her back like liquid sunlight, completely untouched by the freezing slush.
Her striking silver-gold eyes swept across the gathered constructs, her slender hands resting lightly over the white-and-silver robes of her rank.
She brought her hands together, letting out two crisp authoritative claps.
CLAP! CLAP!
"Splendid work, everyone," Aeliana’s melodic voice rang out with crystal-clear clarity. "The field operations are concluded. Golems, execute uncoupling protocol and lower the payloads."
WHIRRRR-CLANG-HISS!
The dozens of colossal stone constructs stirred simultaneously.
Standing on their massive hind legs, the golems reached behind their shoulders with their articulated bedrock arms.
Heavy iron locking latches snapped open with the sound of cracking timber.

With terrifying precision, the constructs lifted the massive reinforced alloy storage crates... each one weighing several tons and bulging with extracted wealth cleanly off their backs, setting them down onto the frozen gravel of the staging yard in neat organized motions.
Aeliana walked gracefully along the rows of stacked crates, turning her silver-gold gaze toward Boa and the gathered dwarven logistics crew.
"Do you have the perimeter tallies secured, Master Boa?" Aeliana asked politely.
"Aye, Lady Aeliana," Boa replied, saluting with her clipboard. "All bins accounted for and the ledgers are accounted for too..."
The magic of the ledgers was that what the girls wrote was reflected in the main paper and the Boa and the rest had been tallying them since.
"The haul is ready for transit."
"Very well."
Aeliana stepped into the center of the massive grid of crates as she closed her eyes, inhaling a slow deep breath of the freezing basin air.
She raised both hands, her slender palms meeting in a single, resounding clap.
CRACK-FLASH!
A blinding dome of silver spatial mana erupted outward from her silhouette, enveloping Aeliana and every single multi-ton alloy crate in a roaring vortex of distorted space.
When the light snapped shut a microsecond later, Aeliana and hundreds of tons of raw ore had completely vanished from the staging yard, leaving behind only the cold wind and empty gravel.
Boa and the dwarven crew stood in the quiet yard, looking up at the towering silent siege constructs standing before them.
Bodil raised her portable rune slate, pressing the master rune.
"All units," Bodil commanded gruffly. "Operation concluded so deactivate!"
CLANK-HISS.
The amber lenses on every single golem flickered, dimmed, and extinguished.

The hydraulic hiss of their mana conduits died down to absolute silence as their internal cores settled into deep,dormant sleep with the massive stone bodies stiffening, deactivating, and returning to harmless unmoving pillars of mountain rock.
’It seems the changes that were made to them before being used today are working...’
Boa pocketed her slate, letting out a long foggy sigh as she looked toward the gates.

"Bloody hell..." the dwarf muttered, scratching her rough beard-line with a heavy sigh. "After a day like this... I hope the Lord’s got a few of those special rewards saved for the logistics crew too. We’re the ones who have to count every damn pebble."
Boa herself wouldn’t mind it if her mouth was full of his dick.
POP-FLASH!
Deep within the reinforced subterranean foundations of the Keep, the air inside the Sovereign Distribution Nexus twisted with a sharp spatial snap.
Aeliana materialized cleanly in the center of the polished rune-carved floor.

Surrounding her in towering, perfectly aligned rows were the dozens of massive alloy transport crates, their heavy leather tie-down straps still holding the vast mountains of raw ore securely in place.

Towering overhead were sprawling networks of brass sorting conduits, pneumatic vacuum tubes, and glowing crystalline conveyor tracks that stretched across the vaulted ceiling like the circulatory system of a modern industrial complex.

Standing near the primary control dais was Thora, her soot-stained face illuminated by the soft blue light of the central terminals and standing right beside her, leaning his forearms casually against the polished alloy railing, was Silas.
Silas had already visited the private quarters to wash off the grime of Cavern KB-22.
He was dressed in a loose comfortable dark bathrobe made of thick, midnight-blue silk, belted loosely around his waist.
His dark hair was still damp with several wet strands clinging to his forehead, and his neck and chest were clean, radiating the fresh invigorating scent of mountain pine and warm water.
Aeliana took a single step forward, and then her breath subtly hitched.
Her silver-gold eyes locked onto Silas’s damp hair, his relaxed posture, and the effortless aura of masculinity pouring off him in the warm light of the Nexus.
A delicate rosy blush instantly bloomed across the high-elf’s porcelain cheeks as she quickly averted her gaze, her small hands clasping shyly in front of her robes as she offered a deep demure bow.

"L-Lord Sy..." Aeliana stammered softly, her voice barely louder than a whisper as her heart gave an uncharacteristic fluttering leap beneath her ribs. "The... the extraction haul from all outer sectors has been successfully retrieved and secured within the Nexus perimeter."
Silas turned his head, offering her a warm and deeply appreciative smile.

"Incredible work, Aeliana," Silas praised, his voice rich and relaxed. "Your spatial precision saved us hours of dangerous surface hauling in this blizzard... You’ve done Blessed Land an immense service today."
Aeliana’s blush deepened to the very tips of her pointed ears, her lips curving into a small blissful smile.
"It... it is my honor to serve your will, my Lord."
"Alright, enough blushing and bowing!" Thora’s rough boisterous voice cut through the romantic tension like a rusty saw.
The dwarven forge master grinned, stepping up to the central control pedestal and planting her calloused hands onto the glowing master rune.

"Look alive, Lady Elf!" Thora barked proudly, her amber eyes gleaming with manic industrial excitement. "You brought the payload to the right floor! Watch what the building can do! Don’t blink, or you’ll miss the magic!"
Thora slammed her palm down against the activation rune.
KRA-VUUUUUUUUUUUM!

The entire Sovereign Distribution Nexus woke up with a small whirr as the glowing blue lines etched into the floorboards flared with blinding brilliance, washing over the dozens of multi-ton alloy crates.
SHING-SHING-SHING-SHING!
Aeliana blinked her silver-gold eyes.
In that single imperceptible fraction of a second... faster than a heart could beat, the entire room transformed.
The heavy leather straps vanished and the sealed alloy lids opened.
FZZZZZZT!
With a sound like a deck of cards being shuffled by a god, hundreds of thousands of individual minerals, gems, and metal ingots dissolved into pure shimmering light.
They were instantly dematerialized by the Nexus’s automated sorting arrays.
Aeliana gasped softly, her eyes widening as she looked up.
High above, lining the massive multi-tiered walls of the vault, thousands of reinforced storage alcoves snapped shut in rapid synchronized succession.
CLACK-CLACK-CLACK-CLACK-CLACK!
Every single mineral had been instantly analyzed, cataloged by purity, and shelved into its exact designated containment cell!
Over on the eastern wall, thousands of raw uncut Mana Diamonds from KB-22 glowed behind transparent crystal panels, neatly sorted by carat, color, and elemental affinity.
On the northern shelves, the constellation-flecked midnight-blue branches of Star-Iron rested in specialized zero-friction cradles.

And in the central high-security vault, the impenetrable slate-gray slabs of virgin alloy that Eluned had extracted from Mine XVIT sat bathed in stabilizing runic fields, their weights and molecular densities already logged into the digital tab by the counter.
On the floor of the Nexus, the dozens of massive alloy transport crates were completely empty.
...Not a single grain of dust remained on the metal.
Thora threw both hands into the air, her face split into a wild grin as she let out a roaring triumphant cackle that echoed off the ceiling.

"GWAHAHAHAHAHA!" Thora yelled at the top of her lungs, hopping from one steel-toed boot to the other with pure industrial ecstasy. "LOOK AT THAT! PERFECT RECOGNITION! ZERO LOSS! INSTANT REFINEMENT CATEGORIZATION! HA! TAKE THAT, BLESSED LAND RULES!"

chapters.title: Chapter 494: The Nexus Does It’s Job [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The mechanical majesty of the Sovereign Distribution Nexus hung in the air, illuminated by the soft glow of azure runes.
CLAP! CLAP! CLAP!
Silas brought his hands together in a slow appreciative clap.
Beside him, Aeliana stood frozen, her delicate hands raised mid-clap with her striking silver-gold eyes wide as dinner plates as she stared up at the towering multi-tiered walls of the vault.

In less than a fraction of a second, the Nexus had dematerialized hundreds of tons of high-grade ores, processed their chemical purities, and shelved every single grain of star-iron, deep-earth alloy, and uncut mana diamonds into their exact containment coordinates.

’It didn’t just sort them...’ Aeliana thought, a sudden cold panic squeezing her chest as her pointed ears twitched beneath her golden hair. ’It analyzed the spatial frequencies of thirty distinct mineral variants simultaneously. I... I can barely maintain spatial cohesion over five different mass-signatures without a bit of strain. Is... is this machine going to replace me? Am I going to be obsolete in Blessed Land?’
A warm weight suddenly settled onto the crown of her head.
Silas chuckled softly, his broad calloused hand gently ruffling the soft golden strands between her pointed ears.
The soothing warmth of his Gold Core bled into his touch, grounding her spiraling thoughts in an instant.

"Calm down, Aeli," Silas murmured with the damp ends of his dark hair brushing his collar. "No machine is taking your job... The Nexus can sort what’s already here, but it doesn’t have legs, and it certainly can’t bend space across a battlefield to pull my minerals out of a blizzard. You’re irreplaceable so don’t let a bunch of brass tubes and gears hurt your pride."
Aeliana’s breath hitched.
A furious rose bloom exploded across her porcelain cheeks, traveling all the way to the delicate tips of her ears.
She lowered her chin, staring down at the polished floorboards with her fingers nervously twisting the fabric of her fine silver-and-white robes.
’He... he saw right through me,’ she thought, her heart doing a fluttering dance against her ribs. ’To be so easily read by Lord Sy... how utterly embarrassing...’
"Alright, Thora, wipe the foam off your mouth," Silas called out, turning his amused gaze toward the primary control dais.

The dwarven forge master was still clutching the glowing master rune with both hands, her amber eyes practically vibrating in their sockets as she revelled in the industrial perfection of the facility.
"Do we have the complete inventory logged?" Silas asked, leaning his forearms casually against the polished alloy railing. "Every payload from today’s expedition?"
Silas loved this place.
He truly did.
Upgrading the Sovereign Distribution Nexus had cost a bit of UP, but standing here now, watching it operate, every single Upgrade point felt like a bargain.
It completely removed the logistical bottleneck that crippled normal territories.
There was no need for hundreds of weary clerks breaking their backs over ledgers, no tedious manual weighing of carats, and zero risk of corrupt guards skimming off the top.
The moment a payload crossed the threshold, the Nexus simply digested it, categorized it, and indexed it.
He glanced to the side of the central console where a translucent glowing blue holographic tab floated in mid-air.
The digital interface displayed a comprehensive, real-time breakdown of every single resource contained within the vault and the numbers updated in synchronized pulses.
’There are quite a lot, even some I’ve never seen before... truly the girls have outdone themselves.’
Both Silas and Thora held administrative authority over the system.
With a single flick of a finger, Silas could reroute items outside as well as Thora. He could summon whatever was stored here wherever he wanted in the territory.
Silas let out a deep satisfied sigh with a smirk tugging at his lips.

’Again, Investing UP in this place really was worth every damn dime,’ Silas thought. ’In the markets back on Earth even before I reincarnated, logistics is king... The guy who controls the supply line controls the continent and here, it’s no different. An empire that can’t catalog its own steel is an empire waiting to be dismantled.’

"Almost complete, my Lord!" Thora shouted back, wiping a speck of chalk from her brow with her sleeve with her voice echoing off the high rafters. "This is just what the squads brought through the main gate! We’ve still got several auxiliary carts sitting in the Foundry yard from yesterday’s smelting shift. My girls are hauling them over right now!"
Silas nodded thoughtfully, rubbing his chin.

"When they arrive, make sure you keep a shipment separated from the territorial reserves. Package them into reinforced containers. The moment I go back to Earth, I’m taking a batch directly to the private exchange... We need liquid capital."

"Understood!" Thora grinned, tapping a series of glyphs on the glowing terminal. "I’ll personally calibrate the containers so we’ll pack the mid-tier star-iron and those slightly flawed Mana Diamonds! Those will fetch an astronomical rate on the open market, right?!"
"Astronomical doesn’t even begin to describe it," Silas replied, his blue eyes gleaming with cold financial ambition.
He looked like a merchant.

"High-purity mana-conductive gems are becoming a scarcity on the global stage." Silas said, he wasn’t wrong... It wasn’t that it was hard after all there were territories where ore was being discovered everyday but globally, it was becoming scarce.

"From what I researched the last time I was on Earth, everybody is clawing at each other’s throats for even a handful of mana crystals to stabilize their high-tier weaponry... If I drop fifty kilos of pristine unmarred Mana Diamonds for sale, They’ll pay until their treasuries bleed dry and it’ll fund our territorial infrastructure for the next six months."
Aeliana stepped up beside Silas with her hands folding politely over her waist as she looked up at him through her long eyelashes.

"Lord Sy," Aeliana murmured softly, her melodic voice catching his attention. "If you are preparing an export shipment, I can link up with Lady Kadi. Together, we can draft a comprehensive manifest of the specialized goods and equipment we require from the human markets... supplies and agricultural seeds for the inner greenhouse wards. Anything we need."
Silas blinked, his brows furrowing slightly as the name registered in his mind.
’Kadi...’
He had originally intended to bring the sharp-tongued Sand Mage along for the morning expedition to KB-22.

Her high-velocity earth and sand manipulation would have made quick work of the loose limestone shale but early this morning, word had arrived from the residential wing that Talira had suddenly fallen violently ill.
The dragon woman had pushed her draconic threshold to its edge during that spar against Thor.
Thor’s lightning had collided with Talira’s body after all.
Eluned had already applied her divine vitality to mend the physical fractures, but Talira’s ancient lineage was stubborn.

The dragon’s internal physiology wasn’t just healing... her mana circuits were aggressively mutating, forcefully adapting to assimilate the foreign celestial thunder energy into her own draconic bloodstream.
Kadi had refused to leave her side, sitting by the bed with cold compresses and sand-barriers to keep the fluctuating temperatures from shattering the bedroom furniture.

’Dragon bodies are biological hazards,’ Silas mused inwardly, shaking his head. ’I could catch a cold and cough but when a dragon catches an energetic fever, they risk detonating an entire residential corridor with spontaneous combustion.’
"That’s a good idea, Aeli," Silas agreed, offering her a nod. "Coordinate with Kadi... Draft the procurement list so we’re ready to move the moment I want to head back."
"Right away, my Lord," Aeliana beamed, her silver-gold eyes shimmering with quiet happiness at being useful.
KRRRRRR-CLANG!
The heavy reinforced blast doors of the Sovereign Distribution Nexus hissed open, venting a pressurized cloud of cold air into the warm illuminated vault.
Marching through the threshold came half a dozen stout muscular dwarven smiths from the primary foundry.𝒇𝒓𝒆𝒆𝙬𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝒎
They were grunting under the strain hauling massive iron-banded freight crates loaded to the brim with dense freshly cooled ingots of refined Deep-Earth Alloy and shimmering chunks of raw mythril.
"Make way! Heavy haul coming through!" the lead dwarf barked.
"Bring ’em straight in, girls!" Thora yelled from the dais, waving her wrench. "Right onto the intake perimeter! Don’t drag your boots!"
The six dwarves nodded, setting their stances to hoist the multi-ton crates over the threshold line.
They took exactly two steps onto the polished stone floor.
SHING-FZZT!
A wave of azure light washed over their boots.
In that single imperceptible microsecond, the massive iron-banded crates suddenly weighed nothing at all.
The heavy ingots of Deep-Earth Alloy and mythril vanished into thin air, dematerializing with a soft musical chime.
High above, on the northern storage tiers, six heavy containment shutters snapped open and slammed shut in rapid deafening succession.
CLACK-CLACK-CLACK-CLACK-CLACK-CLACK!
Every single ingot had already been weighed, stamped, and neatly stacked into its respective alcove.
The six dwarves stood completely frozen in the center of the intake circle.

Their thick calloused hands were still curled in heavy lifting postures, clutching at empty air with their mouths hanging slack beneath their braided beards as they stared at the completely vacant floorboards.
"Every... bloody... time," the lead dwarf muttered, her raspy voice cracking as she slowly let her empty hands drop to her sides.
She blinked rapidly, shaking her head in dumbfounded bewilderment.
"I swear by the anvil... you can see it happen a hundred times, and it still feels like the stone is mocking your muscles."

"Stop standing around like stunned badgers!" Thora barked, resting her hands on her hips with a wide toothy grin. "Stack the empty crates against the western bulkhead! Then grab your ledgers and get over here to the secondary terminal! Lord Silas needs a high-tier export batch prepped for the human markets, and I’m not letting you lazy lumps slack off while the ale is still cold!"
"Y-Yes, Master Thora!" the dwarves stammered, instantly scrambling into motion.
Silas chuckled, pushing himself off the railing as he turned toward Aeliana, gesturing toward the heavy exit doors.
"Come on, Aeli," Silas said softly. "Let’s give Thora room to manage her girls."
They walked out of the humming vault, stepping into the massive corridor that led toward the Keep’s primary entrance.
Silas pushed open the heavy exterior door leading out to the covered colonnade, pausing to look out over the courtyard.
The evening had settled in full.
The iron-gray sky had darkened into a deep bruised navy, and thick heavy flakes of snow were drifting steadily from the heavens, dusting the walls around Blessed Land in a pristine blanket of white.
The biting chill of the Umbral Basin whistled through the stonework, carrying the scent of frozen pine and clean permafrost.
Silas let out a slow, frosty breath, watching the white mist plume in the cold air.
His damp hair was beginning to feel cold against his neck.

"The temperature is dropping fast tonight," Silas remarked, pulling the lapels of his midnight-blue silk bathrobe a fraction tighter around his chest. "We’re going to need the central hearths stoked before the garrison turns in..."
Aeliana stepped up beside him, the soft ethereal fragrance of star-lilies drifting off her skin.
She looked up at his handsome tired profile, her silver-gold eyes softening with sudden shy resolve.

"Lord Sy..." Aeliana whispered, her melodic voice trembling slightly with nervous warmth. "If... if you are weary from the day’s march... I can teleport you directly into the Keep. You will not have to walk through the snowy corridors."
Silas turned, meeting her gaze.
Seeing the genuine, eager desire to be helpful shining in her eyes, his lips curled into a warm gentle smile.
"I’d appreciate that, Aeli. Thank you."
He reached out, his warm calloused fingers closing gently around her slender porcelain hand.
Aeliana’s entire body gave a violent electric shudder.
’Again...’
The simple, unhurried contact sent a jolt of pure intoxicating heat straight up her arm and into her chest.
A radiant crimson blush painted her cheeks as she squeezed his fingers, her heart pounding like a war drum against her ribs.
She closed her eyes, drawing a shuddering breath.
’Spatial alignment... Keep interior... primary sanctum...’
CRACK-FLASH!
A brilliant, blinding dome of silver spatial mana enveloped them both!
Silas blinked.
One second, he was standing beneath the freezing, snow-dusted eaves of the outer colonnade, looking out over the frozen ridges of the Umbral Basin.
The next second, the freezing draft was violently replaced by a wave of thick suffocating heat.
The air was heavy with the rich mineral fragrance of spring water, mixed with the sweet delicate aroma of lavender bath oils and crushed rose petals.

Thick, swirling clouds of white steam billowed lazily through the massive arched stone chamber, clinging to the polished obsidian pillars and condensing into tiny shimmering droplets along the high vaulted ceiling.
This was the Keep’s Grand Bath.

sentences.text: The mechanical majesty of the Sovereign Distribution Nexus hung in the air, illuminated by the soft glow of azure runes.
CLAP!
CLAP!
CLAP!
Silas brought his hands together in a slow appreciative clap.
Beside him, Aeliana stood frozen, her delicate hands raised mid-clap with her striking silver-gold eyes wide as dinner plates as she stared up at the towering multi-tiered walls of the vault.

In less than a fraction of a second, the Nexus had dematerialized hundreds of tons of high-grade ores, processed their chemical purities, and shelved every single grain of star-iron, deep-earth alloy, and uncut mana diamonds into their exact containment coordinates.

’It didn’t just sort them...’ Aeliana thought, a sudden cold panic squeezing her chest as her pointed ears twitched beneath her golden hair. ’It analyzed the spatial frequencies of thirty distinct mineral variants simultaneously.
I can barely maintain spatial cohesion over five different mass-signatures without a bit of strain.
Is... is this machine going to replace me?
Am I going to be obsolete in Blessed Land?’
A warm weight suddenly settled onto the crown of her head.
Silas chuckled softly, his broad calloused hand gently ruffling the soft golden strands between her pointed ears.
The soothing warmth of his Gold Core bled into his touch, grounding her spiraling thoughts in an instant.
"Calm down, Aeli," Silas murmured with the damp ends of his dark hair brushing his collar.
"No machine is taking your job...
The Nexus can sort what’s already here, but it doesn’t have legs, and it certainly can’t bend space across a battlefield to pull my minerals out of a blizzard.
You’re irreplaceable so don’t let a bunch of brass tubes and gears hurt your pride."
Aeliana’s breath hitched.
A furious rose bloom exploded across her porcelain cheeks, traveling all the way to the delicate tips of her ears.
She lowered her chin, staring down at the polished floorboards with her fingers nervously twisting the fabric of her fine silver-and-white robes.
’He... he saw right through me,’ she thought, her heart doing a fluttering dance against her ribs. ’To be so easily read by Lord Sy... how utterly embarrassing...’
"Alright, Thora, wipe the foam off your mouth," Silas called out, turning his amused gaze toward the primary control dais.

The dwarven forge master was still clutching the glowing master rune with both hands, her amber eyes practically vibrating in their sockets as she revelled in the industrial perfection of the facility.
"Do we have the complete inventory logged?" Silas asked, leaning his forearms casually against the polished alloy railing.
"Every payload from today’s expedition?"
Silas loved this place.
He truly did.
Upgrading the Sovereign Distribution Nexus had cost a bit of UP, but standing here now, watching it operate, every single Upgrade point felt like a bargain.
It completely removed the logistical bottleneck that crippled normal territories.
There was no need for hundreds of weary clerks breaking their backs over ledgers, no tedious manual weighing of carats, and zero risk of corrupt guards skimming off the top.
The moment a payload crossed the threshold, the Nexus simply digested it, categorized it, and indexed it.
He glanced to the side of the central console where a translucent glowing blue holographic tab floated in mid-air.
The digital interface displayed a comprehensive, real-time breakdown of every single resource contained within the vault and the numbers updated in synchronized pulses.
’There are quite a lot, even some I’ve never seen before... truly the girls have outdone themselves.’
Both Silas and Thora held administrative authority over the system.
With a single flick of a finger, Silas could reroute items outside as well as Thora.
He could summon whatever was stored here wherever he wanted in the territory.
Silas let out a deep satisfied sigh with a smirk tugging at his lips.
’Again, Investing UP in this place really was worth every damn dime,’ Silas thought. ’In the markets back on Earth even before I reincarnated, logistics is king...
The guy who controls the supply line controls the continent and here, it’s no different.
An empire that can’t catalog its own steel is an empire waiting to be dismantled.’
"Almost complete, my Lord!" Thora shouted back, wiping a speck of chalk from her brow with her sleeve with her voice echoing off the high rafters.
"This is just what the squads brought through the main gate!
We’ve still got several auxiliary carts sitting in the Foundry yard from yesterday’s smelting shift.
My girls are hauling them over right now!"
Silas nodded thoughtfully, rubbing his chin.
"When they arrive, make sure you keep a shipment separated from the territorial reserves.
Package them into reinforced containers.
The moment I go back to Earth, I’m taking a batch directly to the private exchange...
We need liquid capital."
"Understood!" Thora grinned, tapping a series of glyphs on the glowing terminal.
"I’ll personally calibrate the containers so we’ll pack the mid-tier star-iron and those slightly flawed Mana Diamonds!
Those will fetch an astronomical rate on the open market, right?!"
"Astronomical doesn’t even begin to describe it," Silas replied, his blue eyes gleaming with cold financial ambition.
He looked like a merchant.
"High-purity mana-conductive gems are becoming a scarcity on the global stage." Silas said, he wasn’t wrong...
It wasn’t that it was hard after all there were territories where ore was being discovered everyday but globally, it was becoming scarce.
"From what I researched the last time I was on Earth, everybody is clawing at each other’s throats for even a handful of mana crystals to stabilize their high-tier weaponry...
If I drop fifty kilos of pristine unmarred Mana Diamonds for sale, They’ll pay until their treasuries bleed dry and it’ll fund our territorial infrastructure for the next six months."
Aeliana stepped up beside Silas with her hands folding politely over her waist as she looked up at him through her long eyelashes.
"Lord Sy," Aeliana murmured softly, her melodic voice catching his attention.
"If you are preparing an export shipment, I can link up with Lady Kadi.
Together, we can draft a comprehensive manifest of the specialized goods and equipment we require from the human markets... supplies and agricultural seeds for the inner greenhouse wards.
Anything we need."
Silas blinked, his brows furrowing slightly as the name registered in his mind.
’Kadi...’
He had originally intended to bring the sharp-tongued Sand Mage along for the morning expedition to KB-22.

Her high-velocity earth and sand manipulation would have made quick work of the loose limestone shale but early this morning, word had arrived from the residential wing that Talira had suddenly fallen violently ill.
The dragon woman had pushed her draconic threshold to its edge during that spar against Thor.
Thor’s lightning had collided with Talira’s body after all.
Eluned had already applied her divine vitality to mend the physical fractures, but Talira’s ancient lineage was stubborn.

The dragon’s internal physiology wasn’t just healing... her mana circuits were aggressively mutating, forcefully adapting to assimilate the foreign celestial thunder energy into her own draconic bloodstream.
Kadi had refused to leave her side, sitting by the bed with cold compresses and sand-barriers to keep the fluctuating temperatures from shattering the bedroom furniture.

’Dragon bodies are biological hazards,’ Silas mused inwardly, shaking his head. ’I could catch a cold and cough but when a dragon catches an energetic fever, they risk detonating an entire residential corridor with spontaneous combustion.’
"That’s a good idea, Aeli," Silas agreed, offering her a nod.
"Coordinate with Kadi...
Draft the procurement list so we’re ready to move the moment I want to head back."
"Right away, my Lord," Aeliana beamed, her silver-gold eyes shimmering with quiet happiness at being useful.
KRRRRRR-CLANG!
The heavy reinforced blast doors of the Sovereign Distribution Nexus hissed open, venting a pressurized cloud of cold air into the warm illuminated vault.
Marching through the threshold came half a dozen stout muscular dwarven smiths from the primary foundry.𝒇𝒓𝒆𝒆𝙬𝒆𝒃𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝒎
They were grunting under the strain hauling massive iron-banded freight crates loaded to the brim with dense freshly cooled ingots of refined Deep-Earth Alloy and shimmering chunks of raw mythril.

Heavy haul coming through!" the lead dwarf barked.
"Bring ’em straight in, girls!" Thora yelled from the dais, waving her wrench.
"Right onto the intake perimeter!
Don’t drag your boots!"
The six dwarves nodded, setting their stances to hoist the multi-ton crates over the threshold line.
They took exactly two steps onto the polished stone floor.
SHING-FZZT!
A wave of azure light washed over their boots.
In that single imperceptible microsecond, the massive iron-banded crates suddenly weighed nothing at all.
The heavy ingots of Deep-Earth Alloy and mythril vanished into thin air, dematerializing with a soft musical chime.
High above, on the northern storage tiers, six heavy containment shutters snapped open and slammed shut in rapid deafening succession.
CLACK-CLACK-CLACK-CLACK-CLACK-CLACK!
Every single ingot had already been weighed, stamped, and neatly stacked into its respective alcove.
The six dwarves stood completely frozen in the center of the intake circle.

Their thick calloused hands were still curled in heavy lifting postures, clutching at empty air with their mouths hanging slack beneath their braided beards as they stared at the completely vacant floorboards.
"Every... bloody... time," the lead dwarf muttered, her raspy voice cracking as she slowly let her empty hands drop to her sides.
She blinked rapidly, shaking her head in dumbfounded bewilderment.
"I swear by the anvil... you can see it happen a hundred times, and it still feels like the stone is mocking your muscles."
"Stop standing around like stunned badgers!" Thora barked, resting her hands on her hips with a wide toothy grin.
"Stack the empty crates against the western bulkhead!
Then grab your ledgers and get over here to the secondary terminal!
Lord Silas needs a high-tier export batch prepped for the human markets, and I’m not letting you lazy lumps slack off while the ale is still cold!"
"Y-Yes, Master Thora!" the dwarves stammered, instantly scrambling into motion.
Silas chuckled, pushing himself off the railing as he turned toward Aeliana, gesturing toward the heavy exit doors.
"Come on, Aeli," Silas said softly.
"Let’s give Thora room to manage her girls."

Silas pushed open the heavy exterior door leading out to the covered colonnade, pausing to look out over the courtyard.
The evening had settled in full.

chapters.title: Chapter 495: Princess’s Resolve [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: While every private suite in Blessed Land was equipped with its own luxurious en-suite washroom.
In the center of the room lay a sunken hot-springs tub... roughly thirty feet wide, carved from a single seamless block of dark volcanic bedrock.
’I still don’t know how the Upgrade System does these things but I’m not complaining...’
The crystal-clear, steaming water rippled gently with a continuous soothing hum, fed by runes that maintained a perfect muscle-melting temperature.
Silas stood at the edge of the stone basin with the warm steam instantly clinging to his damp hair and condensing on his exposed throat.
He looked down into the tub and his entire thought process ground to a screeching halt.
Sitting dead-center in the shallow submerged seating ledge of the hot spring was the Princess.
The twenty-five-year-old royal maiden was completely naked.
The crystal-clear water lapped gently at her slender waist, leaving the entirety of her upper body fully exposed to the warm misty air.
Her porcelain skin, pale as freshly fallen snow, was flushed a brilliant, dewy rose from the heat of the springs.
Her azure hair, dark and heavy with wetness, was pinned up in a loose messy royal twist, allowing long elegant tendrils to cling to the graceful curve of her slender neck and exposed collarbones.
Her shoulders were soft and narrow, descending into the delicate perfectly proportioned curves of her bosom.
She wasn’t massive like Thor, nor was she muscular like Brida either as her body possessed the exquisite timeless elegance of a sculpted marble statue.
Her waist was narrow and supple with her hips flaring into smooth shapely thighs beneath the shimmering surface of the water.
And sitting right in front of her, perched unsteadily atop a floating wooden cedar washing bucket, was the obsidian bird.
The ragged avian had its wings pinned tightly to its sides, looking like a thoroughly soaked miserable black pigeon.

Its wicked scythe-curved beak was parted slightly as the Princess gently dipped a soft linen cloth into the warm water, humming a sweet lullaby as she carefully washed the soot, frost, and dried monster grit from its ruffled tailfeathers.
"There, there, little one~" the Princess was cooing softly, her small delicate fingers smoothing down its wet plumage. "A warm bath washes away all the terrors of the mountain..."
Silas stood frozen on the tiled rim but he didn’t move, hell he barely even breathed.
Slowly, his eyes darted to the empty space directly to his right... the exact spot where Aeliana had been standing when she initiated the spatial teleportation.
There was nothing there.
Only a lingering shimmer of fading silver mana, followed by the soft distant pop of a spatial seam snapping shut.
’The hell...’ Silas’s mind screamed, his eye twitching violently as sweat broke out beneath his collar. ’Did Aeli... did she just dump me directly into the bath and immediately teleport away?!’
Silas gulped a bit.
’Was this an assassination attempt via embarrassment? A prank or a coordinated scheme to compromise my dignity?’
It made zero sense.
Aeliana was the most demure, disciplined, and fiercely loyal hero under his banner.
She wouldn’t pull a stunt like this unless—
’Wait. Did she think the bath was empty? Or did she... did she deliberately place me here?!’
Before Silas could finish unraveling the conspiracy, the water rippled.
SPLASH!
The Princess paused her humming. Feeling the sudden shift in atmospheric pressure, she casually turned her head with her deep azure eyes blinking through the swirling clouds of white steam.
Her gaze locked directly onto Silas.

She took in his tall commanding frame standing barely five paces away... his damp dark hair clinging to his forehead, his piercing blue eyes and his parted silk bathrobe revealing the hard chiseled contours of his chest.
The silence stretched.
One second... Two seconds... Three seconds...

The obsidian bird slowly turned its head, looked at Silas, looked at the naked royal woman, and immediately tucked its scythe-beak under its wet wing, utterly refusing to be an accomplice to whatever execution was about to take place.
"Uhh..." Silas finally managed to choke out, his voice cracking by a fraction of a decibel. "Princess. I... apologize. Aeliana’s spatial coordinates were... severely miscalculated."
The Princess didn’t scream.
She didn’t reach for a towel, hell she didn’t even cross her arms over her exposed chest.
Instead, a deep crimson blush swept across her porcelain face, traveling all the way from the tips of her delicate ears down to the soft swell of her bosom.
Her azure eyes fluttered, wide and shining with an intoxicating mix of breathless shock and sudden wild hope.
Her heart began to hammer against her ribs like a trapped bird.
’He’s... he’s here,’ the Princess thought, her throat suddenly parched despite being submerged in mineral water. ’Lord Silas... in the bath...’
She swallowed hard with her small hands trembling slightly beneath the surface as she looked up at him through her wet eyelashes.
A soft and surprisingly bold smile curved her rosy lips.
"Lord Silas..." the Princess whispered, her melodic voice echoing with sweet trembling clarity off the warm stone walls. "You... you do not need to apologize."
She shifted slightly on the submerged stone bench, the crystal-clear water rippling softly against her slender waist, exposing a fraction more of her smooth porcelain hips.

"I... I truly do not mind," she continued, her voice gaining an earnest courage that surprised even herself. "After all... it is because of your benevolence that I am here now. It is because of your strength that I am sheltered within Blessed Land, eating wonderful food, learning to defend myself, and experiencing the world without the suffocating chains of the real world. If... if you wish to share the waters... if you wish to bathe together... I would... I would gladly accept—"
STEP!
Before the final syllable could even cross her lips, Silas took a sharp disciplined step backward.
His hand found the heavy brass handle of the bathhouse door.
"Pardon the intrusion," Silas said with a sigh. "Enjoy your bath, Princess."
CLICK! SLAM!
The heavy oak door snapped shut, plunging the Grand Bath back into steamy quiet solitude.
The Princess sat completely motionless in the center of the steaming tub.
Her small delicate hand was still frozen mid-reach, hovering an inch above the water.
Her lips were parted, her azure eyes wide and unblinking as she stared at the solid, closed wooden door.
Drip... drip... drip...
The sound of mineral water falling from the ceiling sounded deafening in the silence.
The Princess slowly blinked.
’He... he left?’
She slowly lowered her hand, looking down at her reflection shimmering across the crystal-clear surface of the spring.
As the Princess of the human realm... a royal whose bloodline traced back through centuries of nobility, Rejection was a foreign alien concept.
’Even if I’m useless...’
Throughout her entire sheltered life, suitors had crawled across polished marble floors just to kiss the hem of her silk gowns.
’Even if I’m useless...’
Presidents and other lords had offered entire provinces, legendary artifacts, and trade monopolies simply for the honor of sharing a single midday tea with her.
Even when she was denied or faced an obstacle, she had always possessed leverage.
She had always possessed something valuable to put on the bargaining table to make an arrangement worthwhile for the other party.

When she had wanted to flee the stifling cages of Rhyx City, she had successfully bribed Thor... an immortal God of Thunder into acting as her personal escort simply by using her royal allowances to supply endless mountains of meat.
She understood transactional power and she understood value too.
’But with Silas...’
A painful agonizing squeeze tightened around the Princess’s chest.
She looked down at her bare porcelain body, her smooth shoulders, her narrow waist and her delicate curves.

’I have nothing to offer him,’ she realized, her lower lip trembling with a sudden overwhelming wave of inadequacy. ’He doesn’t need my royal titles since he is a Lord who bends a territory to his will. I already agreed to pay him money too or should I offer him more? That won’t work...’
Their arrangement was purely monetary.
’And yet...’
Her fingers subconsciously reached up, pressing against the center of her chest, right above her rapidly beating heart.
’I don’t want it to just be a contract.’
Silas was the first person in her entire existence who had ever seen her true self.
He didn’t treat her like a fragile porcelain doll meant to be traded off in a political marriage as he had hoisted her onto the back of a wolf.
He had placed a void-iron dagger in her hands, stood behind her, and taught her how to strike.
He had praised her when she had slain her first beast, laughed warmly when she discovered the hidden diamond passage, and patted her head as if she were a precious companion rather than a royal pawn.

She had experienced more joy, more freedom, and more genuine, heart-pounding exhilaration in the last seventy-two hours than in all twenty-five years of her royal life combined so she didn’t just admire him.
She was falling for him.
...Hard.
If she could explain this feeling.
The Princess slowly turned her head, looking at the soaked obsidian bird sitting on the floating cedar bucket.

"Little bird..." the Princess whispered softly, her azure eyes pooling with genuine earnest anxiety. "Tell me honestly... what should I do? How do I make him look at me? Should I... should I practice with the spear more? Should I try to be more like Lady Brida?"
The bird opened one beady black eye.
It slowly turned its crested head, looking at the Princess’s delicate, slender frame, then looked at the reinforced oak door that Silas had just vanished behind.
"Squawk," the bird croaked flatly.
It lifted a single, dripping black wing, mimed an exaggerated slashing motion across its own throat, and gave its head two slow dismissive shakes.
’Give up!!! You’re fighting a losing battle!!!’
The Princess puffed out her porcelain cheeks, her azure eyes flashing with sudden stubborn royal defiance.

"No!" the Princess declared, splashing her hands into the warm water, sending a spray of droplets across the tub. "I will not give up! I am a princess of the realm! If Lady Brida can punch through mountains to win his favor, I can learn to swing a pickaxe with proper technique! I will prove my worth to Blessed Land!"
She snatched the linen cloth from the water, furiously scrubbing the remaining soot from the bird’s wings.
"Hurry, little one! We need to finish washing!" she urged, her face determined. "Lady Eluned is back at the Keep! You need to tell your story, and I am going to be right by his side when you do!"
"Krrr-caw?!" the bird shrieked in protest as the aggressive scrubbing resumed, wishing it had chosen the freezing blizzard over royal ambition.
Meanwhile, out in the wide, carpeted corridors of the Keep’s residential wing, Silas was walking briskly as his wet hair finally beginning to air-dry against his collar.
’That was close,’ Silas thought, letting out a long breath as he rubbed his temple. ’Way too close. I don’t want any issues with the Royal family too...’
Why was this always happening to him? First it was the thing with Seraphina which he had not even settled, now he had to handle a princess too?
’Kill me now.’
He was just a commoner dammit!
FZZT!
From beneath the midnight-blue silk lapel of his bathrobe, a soft vibrant crimson light flickered to life.
With a cheerful musical chime that sounded like tiny silver bells, Kael-Drin popped out into the open air.
The fist-sized ruby orb hovered effortlessly in the warm hallway, bobbing up and down with boundless childlike curiosity.
Faint flecks of gold drifted within its translucent fiery core, pulsing in harmonious rhythm with Silas’s own heartbeat.
The little spirit drifted down the hallway, zooming toward a brass wall sconce, sniffing the unlit oil wick before doing a rapid celebratory loop-de-loop around a stone bust mounted on the wall.
Silas chuckled with the lingering tension in his chest finally melting away.
"Enjoying the new territory, Kael-Drin?" Silas asked, his voice fond as he watched the glowing orb hover around a velvet tapestry.
The spirit zipped back, hovering right before Silas’s nose, chiming with an eager high-pitched chirp that practically radiated excitement.

"Go on then," Silas smiled, waving his hand toward the sprawling corridors of the upper floor. "You can explore the Keep... Check out the architecture, meet the garrison, stretch your wings but mark this down... Do not set anything on fire. If you scorch a single rug or singe anything, I’m putting you in a cold stone jar for a week. Understood?"
Kael-Drin flared brightly, executing a crisp double-nod in mid-air.
ZOOM!

She didn’t reach for a towel, hell she didn’t even cross her arms over her exposed chest.
Instead, a deep crimson blush swept across her porcelain face, traveling all the way from the tips of her delicate ears down to the soft swell of her bosom.
Her azure eyes fluttered, wide and shining with an intoxicating mix of breathless shock and sudden wild hope.
Her heart began to hammer against her ribs like a trapped bird.
’He’s... he’s here,’ the Princess thought, her throat suddenly parched despite being submerged in mineral water. ’Lord Silas... in the bath...’
She swallowed hard with her small hands trembling slightly beneath the surface as she looked up at him through her wet eyelashes.
A soft and surprisingly bold smile curved her rosy lips.
"Lord Silas..." the Princess whispered, her melodic voice echoing with sweet trembling clarity off the warm stone walls.
"You... you do not need to apologize."
She shifted slightly on the submerged stone bench, the crystal-clear water rippling softly against her slender waist, exposing a fraction more of her smooth porcelain hips.
I truly do not mind," she continued, her voice gaining an earnest courage that surprised even herself.
"After all... it is because of your benevolence that I am here now.
It is because of your strength that I am sheltered within Blessed Land, eating wonderful food, learning to defend myself, and experiencing the world without the suffocating chains of the real world.
If... if you wish to share the waters... if you wish to bathe together...
I would...
I would gladly accept—"
STEP!
Before the final syllable could even cross her lips, Silas took a sharp disciplined step backward.
His hand found the heavy brass handle of the bathhouse door.
"Pardon the intrusion," Silas said with a sigh.
"Enjoy your bath, Princess."
CLICK!
SLAM!
The heavy oak door snapped shut, plunging the Grand Bath back into steamy quiet solitude.
The Princess sat completely motionless in the center of the steaming tub.
Her small delicate hand was still frozen mid-reach, hovering an inch above the water.
Her lips were parted, her azure eyes wide and unblinking as she stared at the solid, closed wooden door.
Drip... drip... drip...
The sound of mineral water falling from the ceiling sounded deafening in the silence.
The Princess slowly blinked.
’He... he left?’
She slowly lowered her hand, looking down at her reflection shimmering across the crystal-clear surface of the spring.
As the Princess of the human realm... a royal whose bloodline traced back through centuries of nobility, Rejection was a foreign alien concept.
’Even if I’m useless...’
Throughout her entire sheltered life, suitors had crawled across polished marble floors just to kiss the hem of her silk gowns.
’Even if I’m useless...’
Presidents and other lords had offered entire provinces, legendary artifacts, and trade monopolies simply for the honor of sharing a single midday tea with her.
Even when she was denied or faced an obstacle, she had always possessed leverage.
She had always possessed something valuable to put on the bargaining table to make an arrangement worthwhile for the other party.

When she had wanted to flee the stifling cages of Rhyx City, she had successfully bribed Thor... an immortal God of Thunder into acting as her personal escort simply by using her royal allowances to supply endless mountains of meat.
She understood transactional power and she understood value too.
’But with Silas...’
A painful agonizing squeeze tightened around the Princess’s chest.
She looked down at her bare porcelain body, her smooth shoulders, her narrow waist and her delicate curves.

’I have nothing to offer him,’ she realized, her lower lip trembling with a sudden overwhelming wave of inadequacy. ’He doesn’t need my royal titles since he is a Lord who bends a territory to his will.
I already agreed to pay him money too or should I offer him more?
That won’t work...’
Their arrangement was purely monetary.
’And yet...’
Her fingers subconsciously reached up, pressing against the center of her chest, right above her rapidly beating heart.
’I don’t want it to just be a contract.’
Silas was the first person in her entire existence who had ever seen her true self.
He didn’t treat her like a fragile porcelain doll meant to be traded off in a political marriage as he had hoisted her onto the back of a wolf.
He had placed a void-iron dagger in her hands, stood behind her, and taught her how to strike.
He had praised her when she had slain her first beast, laughed warmly when she discovered the hidden diamond passage, and patted her head as if she were a precious companion rather than a royal pawn.

She had experienced more joy, more freedom, and more genuine, heart-pounding exhilaration in the last seventy-two hours than in all twenty-five years of her royal life combined so she didn’t just admire him.
She was falling for him.
...Hard.
If she could explain this feeling.
The Princess slowly turned her head, looking at the soaked obsidian bird sitting on the floating cedar bucket.
"Little bird..." the Princess whispered softly, her azure eyes pooling with genuine earnest anxiety.
"Tell me honestly... what should I do?
How do I make him look at me?
Should I... should I practice with the spear more?
Should I try to be more like Lady Brida?"
The bird opened one beady black eye.
It slowly turned its crested head, looking at the Princess’s delicate, slender frame, then looked at the reinforced oak door that Silas had just vanished behind.
"Squawk," the bird croaked flatly.
It lifted a single, dripping black wing, mimed an exaggerated slashing motion across its own throat, and gave its head two slow dismissive shakes.
’Give up!!!
You’re fighting a losing battle!!!’
The Princess puffed out her porcelain cheeks, her azure eyes flashing with sudden stubborn royal defiance.
"No!" the Princess declared, splashing her hands into the warm water, sending a spray of droplets across the tub.
"I will not give up!
I am a princess of the realm!
If Lady Brida can punch through mountains to win his favor, I can learn to swing a pickaxe with proper technique!
I will prove my worth to Blessed Land!"
She snatched the linen cloth from the water, furiously scrubbing the remaining soot from the bird’s wings.
"Hurry, little one!
We need to finish washing!" she urged, her face determined.
"Lady Eluned is back at the Keep!
You need to tell your story, and I am going to be right by his side when you do!"
"Krrr-caw?!" the bird shrieked in protest as the aggressive scrubbing resumed, wishing it had chosen the freezing blizzard over royal ambition.
Meanwhile, out in the wide, carpeted corridors of the Keep’s residential wing, Silas was walking briskly as his wet hair finally beginning to air-dry against his collar.
’That was close,’ Silas thought, letting out a long breath as he rubbed his temple. ’Way too close.
I don’t want any issues with the Royal family too...’
Why was this always happening to him?
First it was the thing with Seraphina which he had not even settled, now he had to handle a princess too?
’Kill me now.’
He was just a commoner dammit!
FZZT!
From beneath the midnight-blue silk lapel of his bathrobe, a soft vibrant crimson light flickered to life.
With a cheerful musical chime that sounded like tiny silver bells, Kael-Drin popped out into the open air.
The fist-sized ruby orb hovered effortlessly in the warm hallway, bobbing up and down with boundless childlike curiosity.
Faint flecks of gold drifted within its translucent fiery core, pulsing in harmonious rhythm with Silas’s own heartbeat.
The little spirit drifted down the hallway, zooming toward a brass wall sconce, sniffing the unlit oil wick before doing a rapid celebratory loop-de-loop around a stone bust mounted on the wall.
Silas chuckled with the lingering tension in his chest finally melting away.
"Enjoying the new territory, Kael-Drin?" Silas asked, his voice fond as he watched the glowing orb hover around a velvet tapestry.
The spirit zipped back, hovering right before Silas’s nose, chiming with an eager high-pitched chirp that practically radiated excitement.
"Go on then," Silas smiled, waving his hand toward the sprawling corridors of the upper floor.
"You can explore the Keep...
Check out the architecture, meet the garrison, stretch your wings but mark this down...
Do not set anything on fire.
If you scorch a single rug or singe anything, I’m putting you in a cold stone jar for a week.
Understood?"
Kael-Drin flared brightly, executing a crisp double-nod in mid-air.
ZOOM!

paragraphs: The moment the command was given, the ruby orb shot down the hallway like a miniature crimson comet, leaving behind a harmless warm draft of mountain air as it disappeared around the corner.
Silas laughed softly, shaking his head.

’Once the Princess finishes washing that battered bird, we can gather in the grand study and have Eluned translate the Beast Goddess’s stone tablet...’ Silas planned mentally, navigating the wide marble staircase.
He paused at the landing of the second floor, his blue eyes drifting toward the western wing.
’Before that... I need to check on Talira. If her dragon core is still fluctuating from Thor’s lightning, I might need to channel my Gold Core’s affinity to ground the excess mana.’
He turned down the quiet carpeted hallway, stopping before the heavy oak door of the guest suite.
He didn’t knock as he gently turned the brass latch and pushed the door open, stepping silently into the dimly lit room.
Silas looked toward the massive, four-poster feather bed in the center of the room.
Lying flat on her back, sprawled out in exhaustion was Talira.
The dragon woman’s wild, crimson hair was splayed across the white pillows like a violent splash of blood.
She was dressed in loose dark linen sleeping shorts and a sleeveless undershirt, completely unconcerned with modesty.

Her skin was flushed a deep feverish bronze, and two small leathery crimson dragon wings jutting from her shoulder blades twitched rhythmically in her sleep, fluttering like the wings of a dozing bat.
And from her parted lips came a sequence of deep earth-rattling concussive snores.
HROOOOOO-SNK... WHUUUUU! HROOOOOO-SNK... WHUUUUU!
The snores weren’t quite as loud as Thor’s starving stomach rumblings, but they carried enough draconic bass to make the glass water carafe on the nightstand rattle softly against its wooden saucer.
Silas smiled wryly.
He turned his gaze toward the floor beside the bed.
Sitting on a thick sheepskin rug, her upper torso slumped forward with her face buried directly into the edge of the velvet mattress, was Kadi.
The Sand Mage had clearly collapsed from exhaustion.
Her long dark braids spilled over the duvet, her slender shoulders rising and falling in deep peaceful breaths.
A protective barrier of fine golden sand still hovered lazily around her ankles... an instinctive defensive reflex that had stayed active even while her consciousness drifted into sleep.
Silas chuckled under his breath, stepping forward with soundless deliberate steps.
"Stubborn girl," Silas whispered affectionately. "Sitting awake all day watching a snoring lizard."
She was going to be okay, Silas could see as much.
’It also seems she awakened a new affinity.’ Silas thought as small sparks of white lightning covered her. ’Maybe next time I should reincarnate as a dragon.’
He bent down, slipping one strong calloused arm beneath Kadi’s knees and the other beneath her slender waist.
With effortless strength, he lifted the sleeping mage into his arms, pulling her gently against his chest.
Kadi let out a soft sleepy whimper, her face nuzzling instinctively into the warm silk of his bathrobe, inhaling the scent of clean pine and soap but she didn’t wake.
She simply sighed, her smaller hands lightly clutching at the fabric of his lapel as her defensive sand dispersed into harmless dust.
Silas carried her out of the recovery room, using his heel to gently pull the door shut behind him to let the dragon woman sleep off her energetic fever.
He walked down the quiet corridor to Kadi’s private quarters, pushed the door open with his elbow, and carried her inside.

Silas walked over to her bed, gently lowering her onto the soft mattress as he pulled off her lightweight leather traveling boots, set them neatly by the bedstand, and drew the thick wool duvet up to her shoulders, tucking her in securely.
Silas brushed a stray dark braid away from her cheek, lingering for a brief second as a soft smile touched his lips.
"Rest well, Kadi," Silas murmured. "Thank you for looking after her."
He stepped back, quietly pulling the door shut until the brass latch clicked into place.
Silas made his way down the central corridor toward the master suite at the end of the hall.
He reached out, pushing the heavy double doors open, stepping into the warm luxurious expanse of his private chambers.
A crackling fire roared within the granite hearth, casting dancing orange shadows across the bed in the center of the room.
Sitting cross-legged in the center of the massive bed was Eluned.
The former World Spirit was clad in a loose flowing emerald-green silk nightgown that pooled around her slender thighs like liquid moss.

Her long radiant green hair cascaded down her back in stunning waves as she was humming a soft melody with her delicate pale fingers casually combing through the damp strands, working out the small tangles left behind by the mountain blizzard.
From the adjacent master bathroom, the sound of splashing water and humming pipes echoed softly.
SPLASH! HUMMMM!
Morwenna was clearly still occupying his private soaking tub, washing the salt and stone dust from her skin after Eluned had finished her own bath.
The moment Silas closed the heavy oak doors, Eluned’s humming abruptly stopped.
Her emerald eyes snapped toward the entrance.

Seeing Silas standing there... his dark hair damp, his bathrobe tied loosely around his chiseled frame and his golden ringed blue eyes soft and relaxed made a breathtaking light ignite within her gaze.
SWOOSH!
The Goddess didn’t bother climbing off the bed.
She vanished in an emerald blur and moving with the frictionless terrifying velocity of wind, she launched herself across the ten paces of open floorboards.
"Hubby!"
Silas didn’t even flinch. He planted his back foot, opened his arms, and caught her cleanly out of the air!
Her soft, fragrant body slammed against his chest, her slender arms wrapping tightly around his neck as her legs instinctively coiled around his waist.
Silas wrapped his strong arms firmly around the small of her back, holding her tight against him as she buried her face into the crook of his neck, inhaling deeply.
Before he could say a word, Eluned pulled back slightly, her emerald eyes blazing with possessive adoring heat, and captured his lips in a deep breathtaking kiss.
"Mmph~"
SMACK!
The kiss was demanding as Silas groaned softly into her mouth, his hands tightening against the silk of her waist, lifting her higher against him as he returned the kiss firmly.
When their lips finally parted with a wet breathless gasp, a thin silver strand of saliva connected them for a fleeting second before snapping in the warm hearth-light.
Silas looked down into her flushed radiant face, his lips curving into a dry fond smirk.
"Well," Silas chuckled. "Aren’t you remarkably cheeky tonight? Did the mountain air get to your head, Elu?"
Eluned pouted, her cheeks puffing out with exaggerated girlish indignation that contrasted wildly with her status as a goddess.
She reached up with both hands, aggressively rummaging her fingers through his damp dark hair, messing up the neat strands with wild affection.

"I missed you, you stubborn man," Eluned whined softly, resting her forehead against his chin, her voice dripping with sweet honey. "You left me to deal with so many girls and a foul-mouthed pirate queen all morning while you were off playing with diamonds!"
She tilted her head up, a slow lewd smirk spreading across her porcelain face.
Her emerald eyes narrowed into half-lidded crescents, brimming with ravenous desire.

"Heh~" Eluned purred, her slender hips subtly grinding against his waist through their robes, sending a violent spike of heat straight to his groin. "You set the decree, Lord Graves as the greatest harvest takes the sovereign prize."
She leaned in, her warm sweet breath brushing directly against the shell of his ear, sending shivers down his spine.

"I mined the highest tonnage in the entire territory," Eluned whispered, her voice husky and trembling with raw lust. "I shattered an impenetrable mountain with my roots and I delivered an entire Phase One Titan Golem filled to the brim with virgin alloy so... you have to give me a very, very good reward tonight~"
She swallowed hard, her throat bobbing as her imagination ran completely wild.
Her face turned a feverish shade of red as dizzy blissful smile stretched across her lips.

"And all of that reward..." Eluned breathed, her fingers digging into his shoulders with hunger. "...should be your thick, hot cum buried deep inside my fertile womb~ Every single drop~ Fill me until it leaks down my thighs, Silas... let’s make a little divine sprout tonight—"
Silas let out a rough ragged breath, his heart slamming against his ribs as blood surged furiously through his veins.
Every instinct in his body screamed at him to throw her onto the king-sized bed, tear that emerald silk to ribbons, and take her right there on the velvet sheets.
’It’s always like that with this woman...’
"Elu..." Silas groaned, his hands gripping her hips with bruising strength. "I would love nothing more than to give you that exact reward... but there are bigger fish to fry right now—"
SLAM!
The master bathroom door was violently kicked open with enough force to rattle the hinges.
"I MINED TOO, YOU GREEDY TREE-WITCH!"
Morwenna stormed out of the bathroom with her heavy boots completely absent as her bare feet slapped against the hardwood floor.
Silas and Eluned froze, their heads snapping in unison toward the sound.
Standing in the doorway with her hands planted aggressively on her hips, was the Pirate Queen.
Morwenna was naked.

Thick fragrant white soap suds covered her bronzed, athletic body in swirling patches... clinging to the hard sculpted ridges of her abdominal muscles, dripping from the swell of her sun-kissed breasts, and lathering across the wide powerful expanse of her hips and muscular thighs.
Her messy black hair was soaked, plastered flat against her back, and water dripped from the tip of her sharp chin onto the floorboards.
She looked completely furious, her amber eyes burning with fierce competitive fire as she glared at Eluned.

"You didn’t do it alone!" Morwenna barked, her voice booming through the bedroom with zero regard for modesty. "I was the one who commanded the perimeter! I was the one who mapped the secondary fissures! If she gets a reward, I’m getting—"
Morwenna suddenly stopped with her amber eyes flickered downward.
She looked at Silas, who was currently holding Eluned in a tight, waist-wrapped embrace, his dark bathrobe parted slightly and his eyes wide as he stared directly at her soap-lathered naked body.
Morwenna looked down at herself.
She saw the white suds dripping from her bare chest and she saw her completely exposed waist.
’I forgot...’
An apocalyptic shade of deep bruised purple-red instantly exploded across Morwenna’s face.
"WAIT—NO—" Morwenna’s voice hitched.
SWOOSH.
From the wide sleeves of her emerald nightgown, Eluned’s hand blurred with terrifying speed as she whipped out the rectangular runic-enchanted camera.
FLASH! CLICK-WHIRRRRR.
A blinding burst of white light illuminated the bedroom, freezing Morwenna’s horrified soap-covered wide-eyed scream in high-definition.
"YOU MOSS-COVERED BITCH!" Morwenna shrieked in mortified agony.
She threw both hands over her chest, spun on her bare heel with the agility of a cornered cat, and sprinted back into the master bathroom.
BANG! CLICK!
The bathroom door slammed shut so violently the entire wall shuddered, followed immediately by the desperate sound of the deadbolt sliding into place!

"OPEN THIS DOOR AND DELETE THAT RIGHT NOW OR I WILL SINK THIS ENTIRE KEEP INTO THE MOUNTAIN!" Morwenna screamed from behind the heavy oak with her voice muffled by the wood, practically weeping with embarrassment.
’Ah... Sink my Keep?!’
Still wrapped securely around Silas’s waist, Eluned threw her head back and let out a wild hysterical cackle.
"AHAHAHAHAHA!"
WHIRRR-ZIP!
From the lower slot of the enchanted camera, a thick glossy piece of enchanted photographic paper slid out smoothly.

The image developed in real-time, showing the fierce terrifying Pirate Queen of the seas standing completely naked, lathered in soap bubbles and her mouth open in a comically wide shriek of pure horror.
Eluned held the photograph up between her two fingers, waving it through the air to let the ink dry.𝚏𝕣𝕖𝚎𝚠𝚎𝚋𝚗𝐨𝐯𝕖𝕝.𝕔𝐨𝕞
She leaned down toward the bathroom door, shouting with mocking sisterly delight.

"Keep scrubbing, Pirate!" Eluned laughed, resting her chin comfortably on Silas’s shoulder as she tapped the photo against his chest. "You are a photo-making factory! I’m framing this one in Silas’s office!"
