She threw both hands over her chest, spun on her bare heel with the agility of a cornered cat, and sprinted back into the master bathroom.
BANG!
CLICK!
The bathroom door slammed shut so violently the entire wall shuddered, followed immediately by the desperate sound of the deadbolt sliding into place!

"OPEN THIS DOOR AND DELETE THAT RIGHT NOW OR I WILL SINK THIS ENTIRE KEEP INTO THE MOUNTAIN!" Morwenna screamed from behind the heavy oak with her voice muffled by the wood, practically weeping with embarrassment.
Sink my Keep?!’
Still wrapped securely around Silas’s waist, Eluned threw her head back and let out a wild hysterical cackle.
"AHAHAHAHAHA!"
WHIRRR-ZIP!
From the lower slot of the enchanted camera, a thick glossy piece of enchanted photographic paper slid out smoothly.

The image developed in real-time, showing the fierce terrifying Pirate Queen of the seas standing completely naked, lathered in soap bubbles and her mouth open in a comically wide shriek of pure horror.
Eluned held the photograph up between her two fingers, waving it through the air to let the ink dry.𝚏𝕣𝕖𝚎𝚠𝚎𝚋𝚗𝐨𝐯𝕖𝕝.𝕔𝐨𝕞
She leaned down toward the bathroom door, shouting with mocking sisterly delight.
"Keep scrubbing, Pirate!" Eluned laughed, resting her chin comfortably on Silas’s shoulder as she tapped the photo against his chest.
"You are a photo-making factory!
I’m framing this one in Silas’s office!"

chapters.title: Chapter 497: Framed Pictures [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The upper corridor of the Keep was whisper-quiet, insulated by heavy granite blocks and thick dark wool tapestries that swallowed the howling of the Umbral Basin’s sub-zero squalls.
Standing barely two paces outside the heavy door of Silas’s personal office, the Princess lingered.
Her damp azure hair, freshly washed and smelling faintly of sweet lilac and mineral hot springs, curled softly around her delicate shoulders.
She reached up with a pale hand, curling a lock of hair around her index finger, twisting it obsessively while her small leather-clad boots shifted against the carpet runner.
Perched securely atop her right shoulder pauldron was the obsidian bird.
The creature was barely recognizable compared to the wretched, frozen scrap of feathers that had plummeted into the snowdrifts outside Cavern KB-22.
Every single primary flight quill had been meticulously cleaned, dried, and smoothed down by the Princess’s own hands.
Its dark crystalline plumage possessed a deep obsidian sheen that caught the warm yellow light of the hallway sconces, and its wicked scythe-curved beak was tucked neatly against its chest.
It looked remarkably noble... less like an anomalous pest and more like an ancient royal familiar.
’So... how do I even go about it?’ the Princess thought, her throat suddenly parched as she chewed on her lower lip. ’How am I supposed to get closer to Lord Silas?’
Her mind wandered back to the steam-choked bath.

The raw heat that had flared in his eyes when he stood at the threshold, the sculpted lines of his chest, the hard cut of his jaw, and the agonizing heart-stopping way he had looked at her before he shut the door.
She wasn’t stupid.
In seven days, her time in Blessed Land would draw to a close.
She would have to return through the help of Thor back to Earth, stepping back into the suffocating gilded cage of high-society and global politics.

’Once the week is over and I go back... I’ll have to commission a discrete investigation,’ she mused, her azure eyes narrowing slightly in contemplation. ’I need to find out who Silas Graves truly is in the human world.’
A man with that kind of terrifying presence had to have roots somewhere.
’He must be a noble, right?’ she wondered. ’Or at least the scion of an old-money corporate dynasty or a high-ranking military house...’
He certainly possessed the striking looks for it.
The sharp high cheekbones, the flawless posture, the effortless way he held court and commanded his Heroes and even Thor without a shred of hesitation... it screamed noble.
If someone presented her with a family tree showing three centuries of Lords, she would have believed it without a second thought.
’Except...’ Her brow knit together, a subtle frown marring her porcelain forehead. ’For some reason, I doubt it.’
If Silas were a true noble... especially one hailing from the entrenched high-tier families of Earth’s modern federations, he would care about class.
He would care about decorum, lineage, social pedigree, and the rigid suffocating distance between a lord and his retainers.
True highborns didn’t swing dwarven pickaxes until their linen shirts were soaked in sweat.
They didn’t sit cross-legged on a dusty picnic mat in a subterranean cavern, laughing with their people and sharing roasted wild boar with brawlers.
Silas treated every woman under his banner with an intoxicating blend of protectiveness.
He valued competence over everything.
’And if he’s a commoner...’
A heavy freezing pit settled into the Princess’s stomach.
’This just becomes even harder.’
Her father, the King, did not care about her. Not in any way that mattered to a daughter.

She had spent twenty-five years being groomed as an ornamental bargaining chip, a political asset to be traded off to whatever territorial duke, arch-mage, or sovereign magnate offered the highest economic concession for the crown’s borders.
But while her father didn’t care about her happiness, he cared obsessively about the royal prestige.
He was not the kind of man to let a commoner touch royal blood without retribution...

If she dared to marry an unranked man from the lower rings of Earth, her father wouldn’t just disapprove... he would dispatch high-tier state assassins to quietly erase the man’s entire bloodline from the civil registry.

’Though...’ The Princess caught herself, a small breathless giggle slipping past her lips as she ran a hand through her azure locks. ’If father sent royal executioners after Silas... Silas would probably cleave them in half, feed their armor to Thora’s forge, and send the King an invoice for trespassing.’
She shook her head vigorously, banishing the dark clouds.
’All of this is getting far too serious far too fast!’
She pulled her shoulders back, inhaled the scent of clean pine lingering in the hall, and pumped her small clenched fist near her hip.
She was still riding the intoxicating high of the day’s expedition.
She had swung a pickaxe, drawn a void-iron blade, and looked monsters in the eyes without flinching.
The Princess surely wasn’t going to let fear hold her back.
CREAK!
The Princess reached out and gently pushed the heavy ironwood door inward.
The study was bathed in the warm flickering radiance of a roaring granite hearth.
Standing behind a broad desk carved from solid petrified ironwood was Silas.
He had shed his damp silk bathrobe, now dressed in a clean fitted charcoal-gray tunic cinched with a dark leather weapon belt.
His dark hair was still slightly damp, brushed casually back from his forehead, emphasizing the sharp masculine contours of his face and those penetrating golden ringed blue eyes.
He looked as effortlessly handsome as ever.
"Princess," Silas greeted her as he gestured toward the plush velvet chairs facing the desk. "Come on in... Take a seat."
Sitting casually upon the edge of the ironwood desk with one leg crossed over the other, was Eluned.
The Goddess was clad in a loose flowing emerald-green silk robe that pooled around her slender thighs like liquid moss.
Her vibrant silver green hair, shimmering with the soft luminescence of her mana, cascaded down her back in stunning waves.
Seeing the young royal enter, Eluned’s porcelain face broke into a sweet welcoming smile.
"Ah, our sweet little bluebird," Eluned purred, her melodic voice chiming like silver bells. "Come, sit down. You smell delightfully of the hot springs."
The Princess offered a relieved genuine smile, bowing her head slightly.
Eluned had been remarkably kind, patient, and maternal to her ever since she arrived in Blessed Land, providing a gentle calming presence that made the young woman feel safe.
"Thank you, Lady Eluned," the Princess said softly, stepping forward.

She walked past the hearth and pulled out one of the plush velvet chairs, smoothing her dark traveling skirt beneath her thighs as she sat down with the obsidian bird remaining perched obediently on her shoulder.
Then, she happened to look up at the stone wall directly behind Silas’s desk.
Her jaw dropped.
Her azure eyes widened to the size of full moons, and the breath violently caught in her throat.
Hanging side-by-side upon the dark granite wall, mounted in ornate, freshly carved silver frames, were two high-definition magical photographs.
The frame on the left depicted Morwenna.
The Pirate Queen was shamelessly naked, covered in thick, dripping patches of white soap suds, her mouth frozen in a wide-eyed shriek of sheer horror as she desperately clutched at her chest.
The frame on the right depicted Eluned.
The World Spirit was equally naked, lounging comfortably across a velvet chaise.

But unlike the horrified pirate, Eluned was beaming at the lens with a proud seductive smirk, puffing her ample flawless bosom out toward the frame with an arched brow, as if directly daring the viewer to reach out and touch the canvas.
GULP!
The Princess swallowed dryly, her entire face igniting into a brilliant volcanic shade of crimson that traveled all the way down to her collarbone.
"U-Um..." the Princess squeaked, her voice trembling as she pointed a shaking finger at the gallery. "L-Lady Eluned... those... those portraits..."
Eluned didn’t flinch. She simply tilted her head, letting out a soft, melodious giggle as she leaned back against Silas’s desk.

"Oh, do you like our new territorial art installation?" Eluned purred smoothly, resting her chin in her palm. "Both taken earlier this evening... A celebration of feminine vitality, wouldn’t you say? Morwenna was rather upset when I captured her lathered in suds, so she snatched my camera and spent twenty minutes stalking the hallways trying to catch me off-guard. Naturally, I don’t hide my divine gifts. When she burst in, I simply gave her a proper pose and she was so furious she almost choked on her own tongue. She still has the camera, actually. Probably lurking in the shadows waiting to take another shot."
The Princess blinked rapidly, utterly paralyzed by the casual shamelessness of high-tier entities.
Suddenly, the hairs on the back of the Princess’s neck stood on end.𝗳𝗿𝐞𝕖𝘄𝗲𝕓𝗻𝚘𝚟𝕖𝐥.𝚌𝕠𝕞
A freezing draft whispered through the heavy velvet curtains drawn across the eastern window.
The Princess’s eyes flicked to the side.
There, clinging to the exterior stone sill three stories above the courtyard, the window sash was sliding open with an agonizingly slow scrape.
Screeeeee!
A messy mop of black hair appeared over the ledge.
Slowly, carefully, Morwenna’s upper torso slid horizontally through the narrow opening.
The Pirate Queen was dressed in her dark leather breeches and a tight linen shirt, her teeth gritted in concentration.
Clutched firmly in her right hand was the enchanted runic camera, her finger hovering tensely over the shutter rune as she aimed the lens directly at Eluned’s flank.
Morwenna raised her eyes to line up the shot and her amber gaze locked directly onto Eluned.
Eluned was already standing, her emerald eyes glowing with cold amused mockery, staring right at her.
Morwenna’s jaw went slack.
"Shit." Morwenna hissed under her breath.
FWOOSH!
Eluned’s hand blurred.
A thick whip-like emerald root erupted from the floorboards, shooting across the room like a striking jade viper, aimed straight for Morwenna’s throat.
SWOOSH!
Morwenna’s reflexes kicked in as she pushed violently off the stone sill with both hands, throwing herself backward into the freezing night air!
KRA-CRACK!
The emerald root slammed into empty space, punching clean through the open window frame and obliterating the wooden shutter into kindling before whipping violently through the empty gale.
Outside in the darkness, Morwenna’s mocking laughter echoed from the lower battlements, followed by the sound of boots sliding across slate shingles.
"MISSED ME, YOU OVERGROWN DANDELION! I’LL GET YOU NEXT TIME!"
Inside the study, the emerald root retracted into the floor with a sharp hiss, leaving behind a draft of freezing basin air.
Eluned clenched her pale jaw, her perfect saintly composure cracking as she clicked her tongue in raw irritation.
"Tch. Slippery bilge-rat," Eluned cursed under her breath, brushing a stray green lock from her forehead. "I should have grown thorn-vines over her sill."
The Princess sat frozen in her velvet chair with her hands trembling in her lap, looking between the shattered window and the annoyed goddess.
"You... you two are certainly... unique characters," the Princess stuttered weakly, a bead of nervous sweat rolling down her temple.
Silas let out a massive sigh, placing both palms flat against the ironwood desk with a heavy thud.

"Alright, that’s enough," Silas commanded, his tone dropping into a cool tone that brooked no argument. "We are not having a photography war in my private office. All I want right now is to get this over and done with."
VUUUM.
Silas’s right hand flared with a soft azure light.
Tapping into his inventory, he withdrew the heavy dark slate tablet the bird had delivered earlier, setting the stone flat onto the desk between them.
He turned his blue eyes toward the Princess.

"I’ve already briefed Eluned on the basic premise," Silas explained calmly. "There’s an entity claiming to be a ’Goddess of Beasts’ trapped in the deep northern sectors of the Umbral Basin... The writing on the tablet is mostly illegible scratches, but the message is clear enough. She is imprisoned, she wants a savior, and she is demanding food so now, we need precise intelligence."
Eluned nodded in agreement, stepping around the desk.
"Yes, a trapped beast goddess who wants food," Eluned summarized smoothly. "A rather simple request, all things considered. Bring the creature forward, little one. I will access its memories."
Silas blinked, his brow furrowing slightly as he looked at her.
’You can actually do that?’ Silas thought, genuinely intrigued.
As if reading his exact internal thoughts, Eluned turned her head toward him, offering a confirming nod, though her nose wrinkled with subtle disdain.

"I can," Eluned confirmed. "Through the fundamental resonance of Nature, all living fauna carry a spiritual frequency that bridges with the world. However... monster memories are very disoriented. I truly dislike doing it. Monsters are an unnatural mutation of the pristine natural order, and sifting through their minds feels like wading through stagnant foul mud but it works."

chapters.title: Chapter 498: No Cages [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She extended her right arm, turning her pale slender palm upward toward the Princess.
"Come, little messenger."
On the Princess’s shoulder, the obsidian bird stiffened.
Its beady black eyes darted between Eluned’s glowing palm and the formerly shattered window frame where a root had just obliterated solid wood.
Its hollow chest hitched, its scythe-curved beak clicking nervously as it dug its talons into the Princess’s leather pauldron, trembling with clear hesitation.

"Go on, little bird," the Princess urged gently, raising a gloved hand to stroke its dark plumage with reassuring warmth. "Lady Eluned will not harm you... She is a benevolent woman. You flew all this way to save your mistress, didn’t you? Show her where she is."
The bird looked into the Princess’s soft azure eyes, finding a shred of comfort in her voice.
Steeling its nerve, the avian puffed out its chest, spread its dark wings, and pushed off the pauldron with a muted flutter.
FLAP-FLAP-FLAP.
It soared across the short gap, landing neatly upon Eluned’s outstretched palm.
SNAP!
The instant its iron-black talons touched her porcelain skin, Eluned’s emerald eyes flared with blinding radiant light.
CRRR-WHIP.
Microscopic, hair-thin emerald roots erupted from her fingertips, wrapping themselves tightly around the bird’s legs and winding upward across its chest and skull like a living jade cage.
The bird let out a sharp strangled squeak, its wings locking rigid as its pupils dilated into pure pinprick voids.
HUMMMMM.
The memory transfer was instantaneous.
For a single, fleeting fraction of a second, the bird felt entirely exposed as if its soul were being stripped bare under the piercing, all-seeing gaze of an ancient forest deity.
POP!
The glowing roots detached, dissolving into shimmering emerald motes that drifted harmlessly to the desk.
The bird violently jerked backward, fluttering frantically through the air before crashing into the Princess’s lap, shivering uncontrollably as it buried its head beneath her sleeve.
It had lasted only an instant, but looking up into Eluned’s green eyes now, the bird felt ten times more terror than it had ever felt before.
Just staring into those deep jade irises made it feel completely naked, as if every secret of its hollow bones had been permanently laid bare.
The emerald glow in Eluned’s eyes slowly died down.
Before Eluned could begin her report, a crisp sound across the surface of Silas’s desk.
A thick, leather-bound folder... embossed with the sigil of Blessed Land materialized atop the table with a soft spatial snap.
Silas looked down.
’Aeli...’
"The final mining ledgers," Silas murmured, pulling the folder toward him and flipping it open.
His eyes swept over the columns of dense figures, tracking the tonnage harvested across the territory.
’Ah...’ Silas thought, leaning back in his leather chair.
Tasmin and Brida had logged an undisputed draw.
Brida’s brawlers had extracted slightly more raw Deep-Earth Alloy from the lower fault lines, but Tasmin’s scouts had countered with high-carat Star-Iron and pristine void-ores.
When Thora’s automated scales factored in mineral density, rarity, and zero-defect extraction bonuses, the two squads were separated by a microscopic margin of less than three ounces.
And if one wanted to say who mined the absolute most across the entire territory?
It was Eluned’s group, dead-first by a colossal margin thanks to her World-Tree roots ripping out Mine XVIT...
And second place?
Second place belonged to Gunnhild’s group.

’Apparently Gunnhild was deployed near several interconnected surface mines,’ Silas noted, his finger tracing her squad’s entry. ’She quietly marched her unit from cavern to cavern, clearing and harvesting all of them with disciplined efficiency.’
Silas tapped his knuckles against the petrified wood, a quiet contemplative sigh escaping his lips.
’What girls actually deserve the reward then...?’
He had specifically stoked the rivalry between Tasmin and Brida so that if one of them claimed victory, he could use that reward to motivate the other to push past her limits.
But they had tied... And beyond the two commanders, what about the rest of the women?
Gunnhild’s squad had broken their backs hauling iron, while Eluned had literally brought home a mountain.
If he rewarded only one, the others would feel slighted. If he rewarded everyone, the decree lost its competitive bite.
Silas closed the ledger with a heavy thud, setting it aside.
He looked up at Eluned.
The Goddess smiled, stepping forward and resting her hands on the edge of the desk.
"I have sifted through the creature’s thoughts," Eluned reported, her tone turning smooth and informative.

She raised a pale arm, pointing through the shattered window frame toward the dark jagged peaks of the northern horizon. "In the deepest northern sectors of the Umbral Basin, within a lightless canyon, rests the woman who calls herself the Goddess of Beasts."
Eluned’s eyes narrowed slightly.
"She is completely entombed within a colossal block of Forever Ice."
Silas’s brow arched. "Forever Ice?"

"An ancient freeze," Eluned explained, crossing her arms over her chest. "It is not mundane frozen moisture... from my experience... it is a stasis boundary forged to seal divine entities. It is remarkably difficult to break, even for me. The bird’s memories show that she has been trapped in that exact position for several centuries, desperately waiting for someone with the authority to shatter the ice and set her free."
Silas paused, his tactical mind processing the timeline.
’Several centuries...?’
He had only claimed the territory recently.
That meant this trapped Goddess of Beasts had been buried beneath the permafrost long before Aeliana’s original lord had ever set foot in the Umbral Basin.
She was a relic of an ancient age, frozen in the deep dark while empires rose and fell above her head.
"Can the ice be shattered?" Silas asked.

"With your current power, Silas... yes," Eluned confirmed. "If you unleash the full concentrated authority of your Gold Core and drive your fire magic into the structural fault points, you could crack it."
"How long would it take?"

"Perhaps thirty minutes to an hour of continuous high-output bombardment," Eluned estimated. "However, Morwenna’s Tidebringer carries an armor-cleaving sea enchantment that could slice through the grain in an instant and Thor? Thor could burst it with a single, high-tier lightning strike."
Silas rubbed his chin. "I see."

"We will have to travel there in person, of course," Eluned added, an amused smirk tugging at her lips. "The Goddess has already formally agreed to submit to your banner and join Blessed Land as a registered Hero, provided she is given warm shelter and abundant food..."
Silas let out a soft, thoughtful sigh, looking out at the snowy peaks.
"When do you think we can depart?" Silas asked.
Eluned’s smile faded slightly, replaced by a stern cautionary gaze.

"That is the complication," Eluned warned, her voice dropping into a serious tone. "To reach her, we must enter the deepest sectors of the Umbral Basin. According to the bird’s flight memories, there are numerous Tier 4 monsters roaming those lightless valleys."
She paused, letting the silence hang in the warm office.
"And buried within the deepest crevasses... there are slumbering presences that radiate the suffocating pressure of Tier 5 calamities."
Silas rubbed his stubbled chin, his piercing blue eyes narrowing into a dark squint.
Tier 4 and Tier 5 monsters were extreme hazards.
A Tier 4 beast was a disaster... capable of shrugging off modern high-caliber artillery, tearing through fortified city walls, and requiring coordinated strike teams of elite combatants to suppress.
And Tier 5? That was a whole different monster.

’Those are a bit much...’ Silas thought, his pulse quickening with cold ruthless ambition rather than fear. ’Facing a Tier 5 head-on would be an nightmare but... the corpses. The high-tier cores, the hide, the blood... they would be worth an astronomical fortune.’
He nodded slowly.

"We should go," Silas agreed firmly. "It’s going to be dangerous, but we have you, Morwenna, and Thor. You’ll be able to protect the perimeter, and the bird will guide us along the safest path to bypass the sleeping titans. Right?"
Silas, Eluned, and the Princess all turned their gaze toward the small obsidian creature peeking out from beneath the Princess’s sleeve.
The bird stiffened under the collective weight of their stares. It puffed out its chest, slowly nodding its crested head in rapid affirmative clicks.

"Good," Silas said, standing up from behind the ironwood desk. "I’ll assemble a specialized strike team for this... We can’t bring a large army into a calamity zone so we’ll leave the bulk of the garrison behind to secure the territory under Gunnhild’s command."
He adjusted his leather belt, looking at Eluned.
"I also want Aeli to come along with us."
Eluned arched a delicate green brow. "Aeli? Our sweet secretary?"

"She needs the field time," Silas explained calmly. "She’s been buried in administrative work for a while. Her spatial teleportation is our ultimate escape hatch if a strong monster wakes up, and she needs to stretch her legs outside the walls."
Eluned nodded gracefully. "I will speak with the girls and prepare our kits."
"Wait!"
A small desperate voice cut through the room.
Silas and Eluned paused, looking toward the velvet chairs.
The Princess had shot up to her feet.
Her hands were balled into tight, trembling fists at her sides, her porcelain cheeks burning with a desperate flush as she looked straight into Silas’s eyes.
"Lord Silas..." the Princess pleaded softly. "Please. Let me come along with you."
Silas stared at her for a flat second as he blinked, letting out a dry incredulous breath.

"Princess," Silas said, his voice dropping into a flat unimpressed monotone. "Did you even hear a single word we just said? Tier 4 monsters... Tier 5 monsters too... That is astronomically far beyond what you need for basic combat training. You learned how to stab a monster three days ago but this is an expedition into a death-zone."
The Princess’s lower lip quivered slightly, but she refused to yield.
She puffed out her cheeks, reaching frantically into her embroidered belt pouch and pulling out a sleek, gold-embossed royal promissory slate.

"I... I will pay you more!" the Princess blurted out, holding the gold slate forward like a shield! "A hundred million credits! Two hundred million! The moment Thor takes me and I return to Earth, I will execute an immediate wire transfer directly into your account! Please, Lord Silas!"
Silas didn’t even look at the slate. He simply crossed his arms over his broad chest with his expression hardening into stone.

"Put your money away, Princess," Silas said coldly. "Our vaults are overflowing with Mana Diamonds... I don’t trade my women’s lives for paper currency so you are staying behind the walls where it’s safe."
The Princess’s chest heaved.
The sharp rejection stung, but beneath the sting was a burning desperate fire that she had never felt in her entire sheltered existence.
She took two bold, determined steps forward, stopping barely two feet from his desk.
"It is not about the money, Lord Silas," she whispered, her voice dropping its frantic edge, replaced by an earnest heart-wrenching voice that resonated through the quiet office.
’Again...’
She looked up into his piercing blue eyes, her own azure pupils wide and shimmering with raw emotion.

"All my life... I have been kept in a gilded cage," she spoke. "My father, the court ministers, the noble houses... they treated me like an ornamental doll. They told me the world was too dangerous, that I belonged behind marble pillars, waiting for someone else to decide my fate. I was never allowed to see the horizon. I was never allowed to bleed. I was never allowed to live..."
She reached up, pressing a hand firmly against her heart.

"Today... in Cavern KB-22... and since I joined Blessed Land, when I swung that pickaxe, when I stood beside your warriors, when I saw the light refracting through those raw diamonds... I felt alive for the very first time... I don’t want to hide in the Keep while you fight for the future of this territory... I want to see this world with my own eyes... I want to see the frozen goddess... I want to learn... Even if I only watch from behind your shield... please..."
She gulped.
"Do not lock me in a cage again."
The office fell into pin-drop silence as the crackling of the hearth seemed to soften.
Silas looked down at her trembling frame and he saw the genuine desperate plea in her eyes.
’Why doesn’t she just want to sit still?’
He could see the hunger of a caged bird that had finally tasted the open sky and would rather die in the wind than return to its golden bars.
He felt the rigid paranoia in his chest slowly yield, giving way to a grudging reluctant respect.
Beside him, Eluned stepped forward, a soft smile gracing her lips as she reached out and gently rested a warm hand on the Princess’s shoulder.

"Take her, Silas," Eluned murmured gently, her voice like warm honey. "I will personally weave a barrier of bark around her mount so nothing short of an apocalyptic strike will touch her skin and Thor will be riding with us... you know the blonde giant treats the little royal like her favorite sister."

chapters.title: Chapter 499: Postponed Rewards [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas let out a long defeated groan, running a calloused hand through his dark hair.
He looked down at the Princess, pointing a stern finger directly at her nose.
"If you step so much as three inches out of the formation," Silas sighed, "I am having Thor throw you five miles back to the palisades. Understood?"
The Princess’s azure eyes expanded, lighting up with a blinding, ecstatic brilliance that rivaled the finest diamonds of KB-22.
"Yes, my Lord!" she gasped, bowing deeply as she was practically vibrating with uncontainable joy. "I swear it upon my life! Thank you!"
Silas shook his head, picking up the heavy mining ledger from the desk and tucking it securely beneath his arm.
He turned, walking toward the mahogany door.
Eluned tilted her head, watching his retreating back with a slow mischievous smirk.
"Where are you off to now, my Lord?" Eluned purred.
Silas paused with his hand on the brass latch, looking back over his shoulder.
"I’m going to... uh..."
Silas stopped.

Catching the intensely lewd expectant smile spreading across the World Spirit’s porcelain lips... remembering her breathless feverish whispers from earlier about filling her womb with divine sprouts, Silas aggressively cleared his throat to keep his face deadpan.
"I’m going to dismiss the rewards giving until we get back from the northern trenches," Silas declared firmly.
Eluned’s face fell for a fraction of a second, her radiant smile withering into a comical disappointed pout.
"Aww... Silas, that’s so cruel," she whined softly.
Then, she perked right back up, her emerald eyes sparkling with renewed, shameless heat as she swayed her hips toward the desk.
"Doesn’t matter~" Eluned purred, licking her lips with sweet divine anticipation. "We can just do it tonight when you return~ With interest~"
"Sure, sure," Silas muttered dryly, rolling his eyes as he pulled the door open.
CLICK!
The heavy ironwood door clicked shut behind him.
The moment Silas stepped into the quiet corridor, the dry teasing smirk vanished from his face.
His features hardened, settling into an intensely serious burdened one as he looked down at the leather-bound ledger clutched in his hands.
He took a slow heavy breath with his fingers tightening against the binding.

’A dead tie between Brida and Tasmin,’ Silas thought, his boots carrying him toward the lower eastern wing. ’And all these girls who worked their fingers to the bone, waiting for a decree. I really don’t want to disappoint them but I have to, what can I give as a bigger reward?’
Down in the lower eastern wing of the Keep, the grand Barracks was practically bursting at its stone seams with deafening noise, roaring heat, and unrestrained celebration.on
The hall flanked by three roaring hearths and lined with long polished wooden trestle tables was packed to capacity.
Over a hundred freshly bathed women.
Their damp hair smelled of floral bath oils and lavender soap, their bruised muscles completely relaxed in loose linen tunics, leather vests, and comfortable breeches.
The atmosphere was an joyful riot.
"DRINK! DRINK! DRINK! DRINK!"
A chorus of thirty screaming recruits banged their heavy wooden tankards against the tabletops in a deafening synchronized rhythm.
THUD! THUD! THUD! THUD!
At the head of the central table, standing proudly atop a heavy wooden bench, was Brida.
The woman was dressed in an unbuttoned leather vest that showed off her chiseled abdominal muscles and broad powerful shoulders.
She held a massive two-gallon iron pitcher of dark dwarven stout high overhead, tipping the vessel back and pouring a continuous frothing cascade of ale straight down her throat.
Ale splashed across her cheeks, dripping down her strong corded neck as she chugged the entire pitcher in five terrifying seconds.
SLAM!
Brida slammed the empty iron pitcher onto the oak table with concussive force, threw her head back, and let out a deafening earth-shaking burp that echoed off the high rafters like a siege cannon.
BURRRRRRRRR-URP!
"GWAHAHAHAHAHA!" Brida roared, wiping the foam from her chin with the back of her forearm. "THAT’S HOW A VANGUARD HYDRATES! FILL IT UP AGAIN, YOU LAZY WENCHES!"
The girls screamed with laughter, banging their cups as fresh pitchers were passed down the line.
Across the room, sitting cross-legged atop an overturned supply crate near the roaring hearth, was Thor.
The God of Thunder was in a glorious state of divine bliss.
’This is how you reward one for work...’
Clutched in her massive hands was an entire roasted suckling pig, glistening with crispy skin and fragrant spices.

She tore into the succulent meat with joyous abandon, alternating between massive, three-pound bites of pork and draining entire wooden flagons of cold stout in single gulps with her booming laughter shaking the stone foundation.

"Gwahahaha! More meat! Bring more ale to the fire!" Thor bellowed merrily, her wild blonde locks swaying as she threw an empty bone over her shoulder. "This is a true hall of warriors! A grand feast for a glorious harvest!"
Nearby, Tasmin sat quietly on the edge of a bench, sipping a cup of spiced tea.
Her dark hair was neatly braided, her amber eyes watching Brida’s drunken theatricals with a mixture of dry disdain and subtle amusement.
CREAK!
At the far end of the barracks hall, the heavy iron-reinforced double doors slowly swung inward.
Silas stepped through the threshold and in his right hand, he held the leather-bound logistical ledger.
"The Lord is here..."
He didn’t need to announce his presence, everyone was already calm.
Silas simply took two steps onto the polished stone floorboards and gently pulled the heavy double doors shut behind him.
THUD!
The latch snapped into place with a crisp click and in that single, imperceptible fraction of a second... the entire room died.

The roaring cheers abruptly choked in their throats, the rhythmic banging of wooden tankards against the tabletops froze mid-strike and Brida’s wild laughter hitched with her pitcher freezing three inches from her lips.
Sarah choked on her ale, desperately clapping both hands over her mouth to keep from coughing, while Brenda’s eyes widened to the size of full moons with her back snapping straight as an iron poker.
Even Thor paused.
The God of Thunder froze mid-chew, an entire roasted pork rib hovering an inch from her mouth, her storm-blue eyes snapping toward the entrance.
Total pin-drop silence descended over the Mess hall as the only sound remaining was the soft crackle of the embers in the hearth.
Every single female eye in the room locked directly onto Silas.
They took in his tall imposing silhouette framed against the closed oak doors and they saw the dark intensity in his blue eyes.
And most importantly, they saw the heavy leather-bound folder clutched in his hand... the final stamped extraction manifests of the Umbral Basin.
The tension in the hall soared to a suffocating peak as their hearts began to hammer violently against their ribs.
...It was time.
It was time for him to announce who would get the reward!
For three long, agonizing seconds, the mess hall hung in suspended animation.
The great granite hearths still threw dancing orange light across the long wooden trestles, illuminating over a hundred pairs of eyes that were locked dead-center onto Silas Graves.
Brida stood frozen on her bench, her hand clamped around the handle of her two-gallon iron flagon with a stray globule of dark stout dangling from the tip of her freckled nose.

Three tables over, Tasmin remained perched on the edge of her seat like a primed spring, her fingers coiled around her bone-inlaid dagger hilt with her amber eyes burning through the haze of pipe smoke straight into Brida’s profile.
It was almost like she was daring her to move.
Silas broke the stillness with a slow, deliberate clearing of his throat.
He brought his knuckles to his mouth, coughing softly into his closed fist, before looking up with that calm smirk that always set the girls on edge.
"Ah..." Silas began, letting his boots carry him three paces down the center runner. "Evening, everyone."
The greeting was completely mundane.
It was practically cheerful and that, more than any roaring battle cry, made Brenda swallow her spit with an audible gulp that echoed off the timber rafters.

"I’ve spent the last half-hour reviewing the extraction ledgers with the logistics clerks," Silas continued, tapping the leather-bound folder tucked beneath his forearm. "The tonnage brought in today was unprecedented... The outer perimeter of KB-22 is hollowed out, the Star-Iron seams from BVR Star are secured, and the territory’s reserves look healthier than they have since we drove the first palisade into the shale thanks to all of you."
A collective murmur of breathless anticipation ran through the front ranks.
Brida’s eyebrows twitched upward as her chest puffed out against her loose linen tunic, practically daring Tasmin to contradict her.

"However," Silas’s tone dropped a bit, smoothing out into that unshakeable voice that meant an executive order was hitting the floor, "the territorial reward distribution... will be postponed as a whole."
WHAM!
It was like he had dropped a chunk of deep-basin glacier directly into the central fire pit.
"WHAT?!" Brida’s roar rattled the copper plates hanging from the kitchen racks.
She slammed her tankard down onto the pine table so hard the wood groaned, frothing ale splashing across the knuckles of the recruit sitting beside her.
"Postponed?! My Lord! I literally dug through three miles of solid granite with my bare elbows and a pickaxe! I have rock dust inside my ear canals that the bath couldn’t even reach!"

"Are you serious, Lord Silas?" Sarah whined from the third bench, her hands thrown dramatically into the air. "We’ve been scrubbing the limestone grit out from under our fingernails for an hour just to stand inspection!"
"My Lord, please!" another recruit called out, her cheeks still pink from the hot water. "We took the bet! And we worked for it!"
Even Tasmin’s cool facade cracked.
Her slender shoulders tensed, her dark fringe falling across her eyes as she leaned forward over the table.
"Lord Silas. The extraction criteria were explicitly defined at dawn... If the parameters have shifted, does the original wager between Brida and myself still hold?"
Silas raised both hands, palms flat, waving the room back down to a manageable simmer.

He didn’t raise his voice, but the golden shimmer of his Gold Core rippled across the cuffs of his officer’s coat, pressing down on the hall with just enough gentle weight to remind them who held the deed to the ground beneath their boots.

He paused, letting his gaze sweep across the long rows of freshly scrubbed faces.

"A scout familiar reached the Keep an hour ago... We have confirmed intelligence on an uncontracted high-tier entity trapped within the deepest northern trenches of the Umbral Basin... an ancient being who calls herself the Goddess of Beasts. She’s locked beneath a formation of Forever Ice, and her survival window is narrowing."
A hushed silence washed over the hall.
The casual bickering died instantly.

"Retrieving her isn’t an afternoon stroll," Silas continued smoothly, leaning his hip against the corner of the heavy wooden serving sideboard. "It will require an expedition deep into the unmapped dead-zones... It may take several days of high-mobility reconnaissance, heavy breaching, and severe combat. He tapped the edge of the ledger against his hip, his blue eyes flashing with a wicked spark.

Silas paused, letting the silence stretch until you could hear the fat sizzling on the hearth spit.
"The winner... will be granted the permanent right to move their quarters directly into the Keep."

sentences.text: Silas let out a long defeated groan, running a calloused hand through his dark hair.
He looked down at the Princess, pointing a stern finger directly at her nose.
"If you step so much as three inches out of the formation," Silas sighed, "I am having Thor throw you five miles back to the palisades.
Understood?"
The Princess’s azure eyes expanded, lighting up with a blinding, ecstatic brilliance that rivaled the finest diamonds of KB-22.
"Yes, my Lord!" she gasped, bowing deeply as she was practically vibrating with uncontainable joy.
"I swear it upon my life!
Thank you!"
Silas shook his head, picking up the heavy mining ledger from the desk and tucking it securely beneath his arm.
He turned, walking toward the mahogany door.
Eluned tilted her head, watching his retreating back with a slow mischievous smirk.
"Where are you off to now, my Lord?" Eluned purred.
Silas paused with his hand on the brass latch, looking back over his shoulder.
"I’m going to... uh..."
Silas stopped.

Catching the intensely lewd expectant smile spreading across the World Spirit’s porcelain lips... remembering her breathless feverish whispers from earlier about filling her womb with divine sprouts, Silas aggressively cleared his throat to keep his face deadpan.
"I’m going to dismiss the rewards giving until we get back from the northern trenches," Silas declared firmly.
Eluned’s face fell for a fraction of a second, her radiant smile withering into a comical disappointed pout.
"Aww...
Silas, that’s so cruel," she whined softly.
Then, she perked right back up, her emerald eyes sparkling with renewed, shameless heat as she swayed her hips toward the desk.
"Doesn’t matter~" Eluned purred, licking her lips with sweet divine anticipation.
"We can just do it tonight when you return~ With interest~"
"Sure, sure," Silas muttered dryly, rolling his eyes as he pulled the door open.
CLICK!
The heavy ironwood door clicked shut behind him.
The moment Silas stepped into the quiet corridor, the dry teasing smirk vanished from his face.
His features hardened, settling into an intensely serious burdened one as he looked down at the leather-bound ledger clutched in his hands.
He took a slow heavy breath with his fingers tightening against the binding.
’A dead tie between Brida and Tasmin,’ Silas thought, his boots carrying him toward the lower eastern wing. ’And all these girls who worked their fingers to the bone, waiting for a decree.
I really don’t want to disappoint them but I have to, what can I give as a bigger reward?’
Down in the lower eastern wing of the Keep, the grand Barracks was practically bursting at its stone seams with deafening noise, roaring heat, and unrestrained celebration.on
The hall flanked by three roaring hearths and lined with long polished wooden trestle tables was packed to capacity.
Over a hundred freshly bathed women.
Their damp hair smelled of floral bath oils and lavender soap, their bruised muscles completely relaxed in loose linen tunics, leather vests, and comfortable breeches.
The atmosphere was an joyful riot.
"DRINK!
DRINK!
DRINK!
DRINK!"
A chorus of thirty screaming recruits banged their heavy wooden tankards against the tabletops in a deafening synchronized rhythm.
THUD!
THUD!
THUD!
THUD!
At the head of the central table, standing proudly atop a heavy wooden bench, was Brida.
The woman was dressed in an unbuttoned leather vest that showed off her chiseled abdominal muscles and broad powerful shoulders.
She held a massive two-gallon iron pitcher of dark dwarven stout high overhead, tipping the vessel back and pouring a continuous frothing cascade of ale straight down her throat.
Ale splashed across her cheeks, dripping down her strong corded neck as she chugged the entire pitcher in five terrifying seconds.
SLAM!
Brida slammed the empty iron pitcher onto the oak table with concussive force, threw her head back, and let out a deafening earth-shaking burp that echoed off the high rafters like a siege cannon.
BURRRRRRRRR-URP!
"GWAHAHAHAHAHA!" Brida roared, wiping the foam from her chin with the back of her forearm.
"THAT’S HOW A VANGUARD HYDRATES!
FILL IT UP AGAIN, YOU LAZY WENCHES!"
The girls screamed with laughter, banging their cups as fresh pitchers were passed down the line.
Across the room, sitting cross-legged atop an overturned supply crate near the roaring hearth, was Thor.
The God of Thunder was in a glorious state of divine bliss.
’This is how you reward one for work...’
Clutched in her massive hands was an entire roasted suckling pig, glistening with crispy skin and fragrant spices.

She tore into the succulent meat with joyous abandon, alternating between massive, three-pound bites of pork and draining entire wooden flagons of cold stout in single gulps with her booming laughter shaking the stone foundation.
"Gwahahaha!
More meat!
Bring more ale to the fire!" Thor bellowed merrily, her wild blonde locks swaying as she threw an empty bone over her shoulder.
"This is a true hall of warriors!
A grand feast for a glorious harvest!"
Nearby, Tasmin sat quietly on the edge of a bench, sipping a cup of spiced tea.
Her dark hair was neatly braided, her amber eyes watching Brida’s drunken theatricals with a mixture of dry disdain and subtle amusement.
CREAK!
At the far end of the barracks hall, the heavy iron-reinforced double doors slowly swung inward.
Silas stepped through the threshold and in his right hand, he held the leather-bound logistical ledger.
"The Lord is here..."
He didn’t need to announce his presence, everyone was already calm.
Silas simply took two steps onto the polished stone floorboards and gently pulled the heavy double doors shut behind him.
THUD!
The latch snapped into place with a crisp click and in that single, imperceptible fraction of a second... the entire room died.

The roaring cheers abruptly choked in their throats, the rhythmic banging of wooden tankards against the tabletops froze mid-strike and Brida’s wild laughter hitched with her pitcher freezing three inches from her lips.
Sarah choked on her ale, desperately clapping both hands over her mouth to keep from coughing, while Brenda’s eyes widened to the size of full moons with her back snapping straight as an iron poker.
Even Thor paused.
The God of Thunder froze mid-chew, an entire roasted pork rib hovering an inch from her mouth, her storm-blue eyes snapping toward the entrance.
Total pin-drop silence descended over the Mess hall as the only sound remaining was the soft crackle of the embers in the hearth.
Every single female eye in the room locked directly onto Silas.
They took in his tall imposing silhouette framed against the closed oak doors and they saw the dark intensity in his blue eyes.
And most importantly, they saw the heavy leather-bound folder clutched in his hand... the final stamped extraction manifests of the Umbral Basin.
The tension in the hall soared to a suffocating peak as their hearts began to hammer violently against their ribs.

It was time for him to announce who would get the reward!
For three long, agonizing seconds, the mess hall hung in suspended animation.
The great granite hearths still threw dancing orange light across the long wooden trestles, illuminating over a hundred pairs of eyes that were locked dead-center onto Silas Graves.
Brida stood frozen on her bench, her hand clamped around the handle of her two-gallon iron flagon with a stray globule of dark stout dangling from the tip of her freckled nose.

chapters.title: Chapter 500: Celebration? [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Across the room, near the far corner where the former border-wall veterans clustered, two figures visibly choked.
Lupina’s bushy silver tail, which had been resting lazily over the back of her wooden stool, went rigid as a steel spear.
Her pointed wolf ears flattened completely back against her silver hair, her eyes widening until the white rings around her irises were fully visible.
Beside her, Morrighan’s dark obsidian-horned head snapped up from her wooden bowl of stew.
The demonic caster’s jaw went totally slack with a massive bead of sweat rolling down the pale, elegant slope of her throat.
They swallowed their saliva in unison and the sound was like two dry stones clicking together.
Back on the Unmovable Wall, before Silas had won them and brought them under his banner, both Lupina and Morrighan had been Heroes.
But within the absurdly stacked hierarchy of Blessed Land, where there were too many strong women including a dragon they were simply heavy troops.
They lived in the barracks and it was comfortable... luxurious, even, compared to their two prior arrangements but the Keep?
The Keep was the sanctum.
The Keep had private baths and a lot of people in it where they could learn from and grow stronger and most importantly... the Keep was where Silas slept.

It was where his scent lingered in the hallways so living there didn’t just make you an elite soldier... it put you within arm’s reach of the Lord while the rest of the territory was a bit further away..
It was an upgrade beyond measure.
"MOVE INTO THE KEEP?!" Brida’s voice cracked into a desperate feral shriek.
She practically launched herself over the bench with her boots skidding across the grease-slick floor as she closed the distance to Silas in three violent strides.
"My Lord! That’s... that’s an inner sanctum commission! You can’t just throw that out there like extra mutton! Are you serious?!"
"Dead serious," Silas smirked, not yielding an inch of ground as the towering woman loomed in front of him.

"What about the squad going north?!" Sarah shouted, scrambling to her feet with her knuckles white against the tabletop. "Who goes to the ice trench?! If they’re with you, do they get points for the monsters they kill out there?!"

"I am selecting the northern strike team personally," Silas answered, his voice firm and decisive. "It will be a lightweight rapid-response unit tailored for the extreme terrain as the rest of the garrison stays behind to secure Blessed Land’s borders, maintain the watch, and continue the mining operations in the other mines. Every beast you put down while we are gone, every crate of high-grade alloy you log with Thora’s foundry... it all counts. When I step back through those gates, the girl at the top of the board takes the room next to mine."
"HOOOOOOOOO-AH!"
The barracks detonated.
All the women threw their heads back and screamed with a wild hungry fervor that sounded more like a pack of starved winter drakes than disciplined infantry.

Mugs were slammed, fists were pumped toward the vaulted ceiling, and even the normally quiet dwarven craftswomen began furiously scribbling on their cuffs, calculating how many shifts of rock-drilling it would take to out-score someone like Brida.
Before Silas could take another step toward the exit, a shadow fell over him from behind.
CRACK-THUD!
A massive armor-plated arm... thick with sculpted divine muscles and smelling like pork grease hooked around his neck like an iron crane.
"GWAHAHAHAHAHA!"
Thor’s booming laugh hit him dead in the ear, nearly rattling his teeth in their sockets.

The God of Thunder dragged him backward against her unyielding chest with her wild blonde locks spilling over his shoulder as she brandished a foaming wooden flagon the size of an oil barrel in his face.

"Running away so soon, Silas?!" Thor bellowed, her storm-blue eyes flashing with drunken ecstasy. "You swung the pickaxe like a true master of the earth all morning, you filled the carts until the axles screamed, and now you try to slip out the back like a thief in the night?! Not in this hall! A great harvest demands a great flood! Drink with your warriors, Silas! Drink until the rafters spin!"
"Thor, wait—" Silas grunted, trying to lever his arm between his collar and her bicep. "I still have manifests to review with—"
"DRINK! DRINK! DRINK! DRINK!" the women roared in a deafening unified chant, slamming their tankards in rhythm.

"You heard the vanguard!" Thor grinned wildly, her bicep tightening as she hauled him bodily toward the central long table. "No decrees until you’ve downed your share! A lord who starves his throat while his soldiers drown theirs is no king at all!"
CREAK!
The barracks doors swung open once more, and this time, two more figures stepped through the steam.
Eluned drifted into the hall, her emerald-green silk robes swaying gracefully around her calves, looking entirely too serene for the chaos of the mess hall.

Beside her, the Princess hurried in, her cheeks still sporting a delicate rosy flush from the hot springs with her eyes darting nervously around the screaming crowd while the obsidian bird clung securely to her shoulder pauldron.
"Oh, my..." the Princess murmured, her small hands coming up to cover her mouth. "Are they... always this energetic after a shift?"
"Only when they smell blood and fresh meat, little bluebird," Eluned purred, stepping smoothly into the hall.
Before either of them could take three paces, Brida and Helen materialized out of the smoke, grabbing the Princess by her silk sleeves and Eluned by her green sashes with boisterous whoops.
"The royal guest is here! And the tree lady!" Brida hollered, steering them toward the long benches. "Get ’em a flagon! Nobody leaves this room sober tonight! Lord’s orders!"
"I never issued that order—" Silas called out from the head of the table, though his voice was instantly swallowed by a fresh wave of cheers.
Within minutes, the barracks had reached a fever pitch.
Trestle tables were dragged together, forming a massive continuous wooden ring around the central roasting hearth.
Enormous platters of spicy, pepper-crusted spirit boar, mountain tubers roasted in marrow butter, and heaps of smoked river trout were hauled from the kitchens on heavy iron trays.
The Princess sat wedged precariously between Helen and Brenda, her delicate royal skirts tucked beneath her knees.
In front of her sat a carved horn flagon brimming with golden mead.
"Come on, Your Highness!" Brenda urged, leaning over with a flushed, freckled grin. "One sip for the first goblin! Two sips for the diamond cave!"
The Princess looked at the dark amber liquid and was a bit hesitant.
’I drank a whole lot of it last night but should I do so again?’
Back home, she sipped thimble-sized crystal glasses of diluted elderberry wine at formal banquets while courtiers watched their posture.
But looking around at the women laughing, shouting, and trading scars under the warm firelight... she felt that same strange intoxicating fire bloom in her chest once again.
’Let’s just enjoy everything Blessed Land has to offer!’
She gripped the horn with both hands, brought it to her lips, and took a massive reckless gulp.
GULP! GULP! COUGH!

"Whoa!" The Princess gasped, slamming the horn down, her azure eyes watering instantly as a fiery spiced warmth exploded straight down her throat and into her stomach. "It’s... it burns! But it’s so sweet!"
"THAT’S THE SPIRIT!" the girls screamed, pounding the table until the platters rattled!
Across the table, Eluned was not faring much better.
The ancient Goddess, who normally carried herself with the untouchable divine grace of an eternal forest deity, had already drained three flagons of heavy floral berry wine.
Her porcelain cheeks had turned the brilliant, incandescent shade of a ripe summer peach.
Her emerald eyes were half-lidded, and brimming with a loose uninhibited glaze as she leaned her upper body heavily against Silas’s left arm.

"Silas..." Eluned whined softly, her voice slurred into sweet melodic mush as her slender fingers lazily traced the silver embroidery on his lapel. "The roots... the roots in the cellar are humming... did you know that? They’re humming because you’re so warm... you should come down to the roots and let me wrap you up... like a little acorn..."
"You’re completely hammered, Elu," Silas muttered dryly, though he kept his arm steady so the swaying goddess wouldn’t slide off the bench and crack her head on the stone.
’Or rather, crack the stone with her head.’

"I am not hammered," Eluned pouted, her lower lip protruding in an adorable exaggerated pout that looked thoroughly undignified for a primordial spirit. "I am... deeply attuned to the soil’s fermentation... there is a difference..."𝑓𝘳𝘦𝑒𝑤𝑒𝘣𝘯ℴ𝘷𝘦𝓁.𝑐𝑜𝑚
"GWAHAHAHA! She’s down for the count!" Thor bellowed from Silas’s right, slamming an empty flagon into the wood.
The God of Thunder had already consumed enough roasted pork to feed an entire squadron, but her storm-blue eyes were burning with hunger.
’At this rate, we’ll have to multiply our hunting.’
Thor was going to finish their reserves of food!
She leaned across the table, thrusting a thick calloused finger straight into Silas’s chest.

"You’ve been sipping that watered-down barley swill all night, Silas!" Thor accused with her wild blonde mane shaking as she grinned. "You think you can hide behind your calm face?! I see you! You haven’t swayed an inch! So you have high alcohol resistance huh?!"
Silas blinked, maintaining a perfectly serene innocent expression.
’It’s not like she’s wrong.’

The moment the fermented mash crossed his tongue, his Mythic Gold Core... acting on instinctual self-preservation naturally circulated a thin microscopic film of mana through his liver and bloodstream.
The alcohol was broken down into basic moisture and inert vapor within milliseconds of entering his stomach.
He could drink fifty gallons of pure grain alcohol and walk a straight line across a tightrope without his pulse jumping a single beat.
’I hate it a bit...’
Naturally, he had zero intention of telling her that.
"I simply possess a dignified tolerance, Thor," Silas replied smoothly, raising his horn with a relaxed shrug. "A lord must remain composed, even while his warriors drown themselves."
"LIES!" Thor roared, slapping her thigh with concussive force. "I challenge you! A true warrior’s trial! The strongest spirit in the territory!"
CLANG-RATTLE!
Right on cue, the pantry doors swung open with a violent shriek of iron hinges.
Stomping into the hall like an armored badger on a warpath was Thora.
The dwarven forge master had completely discarded her soot-stained apron, now dressed in a clean dark leather tunic with steel-reinforced cuffs.
Her beautiful face was flushed with pride, and held securely in both hands was a massive dark stoneware jug sealed with black pitch and wrapped in glowing blue cooling runes.
"Step aside! Make way for the master’s private stock!" Thora shouted, her boots thudding against the floorboards as she approached the central table.
She slammed the stoneware jug onto the oak with a hollow thud that made the grease in the platters jump.
"What is that?!" Brida asked, leaning over the table with her eyes squinting at the glowing blue runes.

"This," Thora grinned savagely, wiping her nose with the back of her wrist, "is Blessed Drink 2.0... I took the fermented mash of the deep-basin frost-berries as well as some of Eluned’s berries, filtered it through a pulverized star-iron gravel bed, and distilled it four times using the high-temperature steam exhaust from the primary foundry furnaces. It’s ninety-two percent pure spiritual alcohol or so... One drop will strip the rust off an iron wagon wheel and three swallows will put an earth-drake into a coma!"
Thor’s eyes ignited with pure unholy fire.
"POUR IT!"
"Don’t say I didn’t warn you, giantess!" Thora cackled, drawing a heavy belt dagger and slicing the wax seal with a crisp shik.
She popped the wooden cork.
FZZZZZZT.
A thick pale vapor hissed out of the neck of the jug as the air within three feet of the opening dropped by ten degrees while simultaneously smelling like it could ignite if someone struck a flint.
Thora filled two massive polished horn flagons to the brim.
The liquid inside wasn’t amber or brown... it was a clear shimmering cerulean blue that seemed to swirl with its own internal current.
Thor grabbed her horn with both hands, her massive muscles coiling.
"To the victor, Silas! No magic! No divine purification! Pure mortal grit!"
"Pure mortal grit," Silas agreed, taking up his flagon with an easy confident grip.
"THREE! TWO! ONE! CHUG!"
GLUG! GLUG! GLUG! GLUG!
Both of them tipped their horns back simultaneously.
